Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तौ काष्ठसङ्घातमथो चक्रतु स्सुमहाप्लवम्। शुष्कैर्वंशै स्समास्तीर्णमुशीरैश्च समावृतम्।।2.55.14।।
output: अथ then, तौ both of them, शुष्कै: with dry, वंशै: bamboos, समास्तीर्णम् wellspread, उशीरै: fragrant roots of Ushira bush, समावृतम् covered with, काष्टसङ्घातम् with logs of wood joined together, महाप्लवम् big float, चक्रतु: made.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 55:
ततो वेतसशाखाश्च जम्बूशाखाश्च वीर्यवान्। चकार लक्ष्मणश्छित्वा सीताया स्सुखमासनम्।।2.55.15।।
output: The valiant Lakshmana cut the stems of reeds and branches of the Jambu tree to prepare a comfortable seat for Sita (on that float).

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तत्र श्रियमिवाचिन्त्यां रामो दाशरथिः प्रियाम्। ईषत्संलज्जमानां तामध्यारोपयतप्लवम्।।2.55.16।।
output: Rama, son of Dasaratha helped his beloved (Sita), who was looking inconceivably like Lakshmi (goddess of wealth) and was feeling a little bashful while stepping on to the float.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 55:
पार्श्वे च तत्र वैदेह्या वसने भूषणानि च। प्लवे कठिनकाजं च रामश्चक्रे सहायुधैः।।2.55.17।।
output: Rama placed robes and ornaments on the float by the side of Sita and a spade and a basket along with weapons.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
आरोप्य प्रथमं सीतां सङ्घाटं परिगृह्य तौ। तत प्रतेरतुर्यत्तौ वीरौ दशरथात्मजौ।।2.55.18।।
output: Those valiant sons of Dasaratha held the float (firmly) to help Sita step on to it. Then they crossed the river carefully.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कालिन्दीमध्यमायाता सीता त्वेनामवन्दत। स्वस्ति देवि तरामि त्वां पारये न्मे पतिर्व्रतम्।।2.55.19।। यक्ष्ये त्वां गोसहस्रेण सुराघटशतेन च। स्वस्ति प्रत्यागते रामे पुरी मिक्ष्वाकुपालिताम्।।2.56.20।।
output: On reaching the middle of the river Yamuna, Sita made reverential salutations to her saying O goddess, I am crossing you, may safety be ours and may my husband fulfil his vow After Rama's (safe) return to the city (of Ayodhya) ruled by the Ikshvaku kings, I shall worship you with a thousand cows and a hundred pots of wine.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कालिन्दीमध्यमायाता सीता त्वेनामवन्दत। स्वस्ति देवि तरामि त्वां पारये न्मे पतिर्व्रतम्।।2.55.19।। यक्ष्ये त्वां गोसहस्रेण सुराघटशतेन च। स्वस्ति प्रत्यागते रामे पुरी मिक्ष्वाकुपालिताम्।।2.56.20।।
output: On reaching the middle of the river Yamuna, Sita made reverential salutations to her saying O goddess, I am crossing you, may safety be ours and may my husband fulfil his vow After Rama's (safe) return to the city (of Ayodhya) ruled by the Ikshvaku kings, I shall worship you with a thousand cows and a hundred pots of wine.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कालिन्दी मथ सीता तु याचमाना कृताञ्जलिः। तीरमेवाभिसम्प्राप्ता दक्षिणं वरवर्णिनी।।2.55.21।।
output: वरवर्णिनी lady of fair complexion, सीता Sita, कालिन्दीम् Yamuna, कृताञ्जलि: folding her  hands, याचमाना in supplication, अथ thereafter, दक्षिणं तीरमेव southern bank, अभिसम्प्राप्ता reached.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तत प्लवेनांशुमतीं शीघ्रगामूर्मिमालिनीम्। तीरजै र्बहुभिर्वृक्षै स्सन्तेरुर्यमुनां नदीम्।।2.55.22।।
output: तत: then, शीघ्रगाम् swiftflowing, ऊर्मिमालिनीम् full of waves, तीरजै: growing on the banks, बहुभि: many, वृक्षै: trees, अंशुमतीम् daughter of the Sungod, यमुनां नदीम् river Yamuna, सन्तेरु: crossed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ते तीर्णाः प्लवमुत्सृज्य प्रस्थाय यमुनावनात्। श्यामं न्यग्रोध मासेदु श्शीतलं हरितच्छदम्।।2.55.23।।
output: तीर्णा: having crossed, ते they, प्लवम् raft, उत्सृज्य after leaving, यमुनावनात् from the forest adjoining Yamuna river, प्रस्थाय after starting, हरितच्छदम् a place full of greenery, शीतलम्  cool, श्यामम् dark, न्यग्रोधम् banyan tree, असेदु: reached.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 55:
न्यग्रोधं तमुपागम्य वैदेही वाक्यमब्रवीत्। नमस्तेऽस्तु महावृक्ष पारयेन्मे पतिर्व्रतम्।।2.55.24।। कौशल्यां चैव पश्येयं सुमित्रां च यशश्विनीम्। इति सीताऽञ्जलिं कृत्वा पर्यगच्छद्वनस्पतिम्।।2.55.25।।
output: Having reached the banyan tree, Sita invoked it, saying, 'O great tree I offer you my salutations. May my husband fulfil his vow May I behold Kausalya and the illustrious Sumitra on my return. Saying so, she went round the tree offering reverential salutations with folded hands.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
न्यग्रोधं तमुपागम्य वैदेही वाक्यमब्रवीत्। नमस्तेऽस्तु महावृक्ष पारयेन्मे पतिर्व्रतम्।।2.55.24।। कौशल्यां चैव पश्येयं सुमित्रां च यशश्विनीम्। इति सीताऽञ्जलिं कृत्वा पर्यगच्छद्वनस्पतिम्।।2.55.25।।
output: वैदेही Sita, तं न्यग्रोधम् that banyan tree, उपागम्य having reached, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् said, महावृक्ष O great tree, ते to you, नम:अस्तु my salutations, मे पतिः my husband, व्रतम् vow, पारयेत् may fulfil, कौशल्यां च and Kausalya, यशश्विनीम् illustrious, सुमित्रां च also Sumitra, पश्येयम् may I behold, सीता Sita, इति in this way, अञ्जलिं कृत्वा offering reverential salutations with folded hands, वनस्पतिम् to the tree, पर्यगच्छत् went round.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 55:
अवलोक्य तत स्सीतामायाचन्तीमनिन्दिताम्। दयितां च विधेयां च रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्।।2.55.26।।
output: Beholding the obedient, blemishless, beloved Sita invoking blessings, Rama said to Lakhsmana:

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सीतामादाय गच्छत्वमग्रतो भरतानुज। पृष्ठतोऽहं गमिष्यामि सायुधो द्विपदां वर।।2.55.27।।
output: द्विपदां वर best among bipeds (men), भरतानुज brother of Bharata (Lakshmana), त्वम् you, सीताम् Sita, आदाय taking with you, अग्रत: ahead, गच्छ go, अहम् I, सायुध: armed with weapons, पृष्ठत: from behind, गमिष्यामि will follow.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 55:
यद्यत्फलं प्रार्थयते पुष्पं वा जनकात्मजा। तत्तत्प्रदद्या वैदेह्या यत्राऽस्या रमते मनः।।2.55.28।।
output: Whatever fruit or flower the daughter of Janaka asks for, get it. Whatever pleases her mind give it.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
गच्छतोऽस्तु तयोर्मध्ये बभूव जनकात्मजा। मातङ्गयोर्मध्यगता शुभा नागवधूरिव।।2.55.29।।
output: The daughter of Janaka walked between them like a sheelephant between two males.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 55:
एकैकं पादपं गुल्मं लतां वा पुष्पशालिनीम्। अदृष्टपूर्वां पश्यन्ती रामं पप्रच्छ साऽबला।।2.55.30।।
output: That gentle lady enquired of Rama about a tree or a shrub or a creeper in full bloom which she did not see before.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
रमणीयान्बहुविधान्पादपान्कुसुमोत्कटान्। सीतावचनसंरब्ध आनयामास लक्ष्मणः।।2.55.31।।
output: Cheered by Sita's indents, Lakshmana brought her various beautiful plants and stocks of flowers.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 55:
विचित्रवालुकजलां हंससारसनादिताम्। रेमे जनकराजस्य सुता प्रेक्ष्य तदा नदीम्।।2.55.32।।
output: Beholding the river Yamuna with its wonderful water and sand echoing with the cackle of swans and cranes, Sita went ecstatic.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
क्रोशमात्रं ततो गत्वा भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। बहून्मेध्यान्मृगान्हत्वा चेरतुर्यमुनावने।।2.55.33।।
output: तत: then, भ्रातरौ the two brothers, रामलक्ष्मणौ Rama and Lakshmana, क्रोशमात्रम् a krosa, गत्वा having gone, मेध्यान् suitable for sacrifice (pure), बहून् many, मृगान् deer, हत्वा having slain, यमुनावने in the forest on the bank of Yamuna, चेरतु: ate.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
विहृत्य ते बर्हिणपूगनादिते शुभे वने वानरवारणायुते। समं नदीवप्रमुपेत्य सम्मतं निवास माजग्मु रदीनदर्शनाः।।2.55.34।।
output: They reached the tableland on the bank of that river and moved in high spirit in the lovely forest resounding with cries of flocks of peacocks and teeming with monkeys and elephants. Finally they selected  a spot for their stay. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftyfifth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अथ रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामवसुप्तमनन्तरम्। प्रबोधयामास शनैर्लक्ष्मणं रघुनन्दनः।।2.56.1।।
output: अथ thereafter, रघुनन्दन: Delight of the Raghus (Rama), रात्र्याम् night, अतीतायाम् had passed, अनन्तरम् then, अवसुप्तम् sleeping, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana, शनै: gently, प्रबोधयामास awakened.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 56:
सौमित्रे श्रुणु वन्यानां वल्गु व्याहरतां स्वनम्। सम्प्रतिष्ठामहे काल प्रस्थानस्य परन्तप।।2.56.2।।
output: Listen to the songs of the forest birds, O son of Sumitra O tormentor of foes it is time we set out.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स सुप्तस्समये भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणः प्रतिबोधितः। जहौ निद्रां च तन्द्रीं च प्रसक्तं च पथि श्रमम्।।2.56.3।।
output: सुप्त: one asleep, स: लक्ष्मण: that Lakshmana, समये in time, भ्रात्रा by his brother, प्रतिबोधित: awakened, निद्रां च sleep, तन्द्रीं च and drowsiness, पथि during journey, प्रसक्तम् associated with, श्रमं च fatigue, जहौ cast off.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तत उत्थाय ते सर्वे स्पृष्ट्वा नद्या श्शिवं जलम्। पन्थानमृषिणाऽदिष्टं चित्रकूटस्य तं ययुः।।2.56.4।।
output: Then they all rose, touched the river's auspicious waters and went the way the sage had directed -- towards mount Chitrakuta.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततस्सम्प्रस्थितः काले रामस्सौमित्रिणा सह। सीतां कमलपत्राक्षीमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.56.5।।
output: तत: then, काले at the proper time, सौमित्रिणा सह along with Lakshmana, सम्प्रस्थित:  setting out, राम: Rama, कमलपत्राक्षीम् eyes like lotus petals, सीताम् addressing Sita, इदं वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 56:
आदिप्तानिव वैदेहि सर्वतः पुष्पितान्नगान्। स्वैः पुष्पैः किंशुकान् पश्य मालिनशिशिरात्यये।।2.56.6।।
output: O daughter of Videha behold these kimsuka trees in full bloom everywhere. With the passing of winter, they appear bright as though they are garlanded by their own flowers.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 56:
पश्य भल्लातकान् फुल्लान्नरै रनुपसेवितान्। फलपत्रैरवनता न्नूनं शक्ष्याम जीवितुम्।।2.56.7।।
output: Behold these bhallataka trees in full bloom though there are none to enjoy them. They are bent with fruits and leaves. Surely, we can live here. (This place is fit for our habitation).

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 56:
पश्य द्रोणप्रमाणानि लम्बमानानि लक्ष्मण। मधूनि मधुकारीभि स्सम्भृतानि नगे नगे।।2.56.8।।
output: O Lakshmana see the honeycombs of the size of wooden vessels crowded by the honeybees hanging down from every tree.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 56:
एष क्रोशति नत्यूहस्तं शिखी प्रतिकूजति। रमणीये वनोद्देशे पुष्पसंस्तरसङ्कटे।।2.56.9।।
output: In this delightful forest region strewn with fallen flowers the peacock is responding to the screaming of natyuha bird.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
मातङ्गयूथानुसृतं पक्षिसंङ्घानुनादितम्। चित्रकूटमिमं पश्य प्रवृद्धशिखरं गिरिम्।।2.56.10।।
output: मातङ्गयूथानुसृतं followed by the herds of elephants, पक्षिसंङ्घानुनादितम् with flocks of singing birds, प्रवृद्धशिखरम् with very towering peaks, इदम् this, गिरिम् mountain, पश्य see.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 56:
समभूमितले रम्ये द्रुमैर्बहुभिरावृते। पुण्ये रंस्यामहे तात चित्रकूटस्य कानने।।2.56.11।।
output: O dear this sacred forest of Chitrakuta standing on a level land is full of various trees. Let us enjoy it.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 56:
ततस्तौ पादचारेण गच्छन्तौ सह सीतया। रम्यमासेदतुश्शैलं चित्रकूटं मनोरमम्।।2.56.12।।
output: Then they both along with Sita walked to that lovely, delightful Chitrakuta mountain.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 56:
तन्तु पर्वतमासाद्य नानापक्षिगणायुतम्। बहुमूलफलं रम्यं सम्पन्नं सरसोदकम्।।2.56.13।।
output: Rama arrived at that enchanting mountain full of various kinds of birds, fruits and roots, and sweet water. (And said to Lakshmana:)

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
मनोज्ञोऽयं गिरिस्सौम्य नानाद्रुमलतायुतः। बहुमूलफलो रम्य स्स्वाजीवः प्रतिभाति मे।।2.56.14।।
output: सौम्य O gentle one, मनोज्ञ: pleasing to the heart, नानादृमलतायुत: with various kinds of trees and creepers, बहुमूलफल: with many roots and fruits, रम्य: beautiful, अयं गिरि: this mountain, स्वाजीव: a happy place to live in, मे to me, प्रतिभाति appears.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
मुनयश्च महात्मानो वसन्त्यस्मि शिलोच्चये। अयं वासो भवेत्तावदत्र सौम्य रमेमहि।।2.56.15।।
output: Great sages reside on this high mountain. Let it be our habitation and let us enjoy our life here, O handsome one

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इति सीता च रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्च कृताञ्जलिः। अभिगम्याऽश्रमं सर्वे वाल्मीकि मभिवादयन्।।2.56.16।।
output: Thus Rama, Sita and Lakshmana approached the hermitage of sage Valmiki and paid obeisance to him with folded hands.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तान्महर्षि प्रमुदितः पूजयामास धर्मवित्। अस्यतामिति चोवाच स्वागन्तु निवेद्य च।।2.56.17।।
output: The great sage Valmiki conversant with righteousness was delighted. He honoured them by extending welcome and said 'Be seated'.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततोऽब्रवीन्महाबाहुर्लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः। सन्निवेद्य यथान्याय मात्मानमृषये प्रभुः।।2.56.18।।
output: तत: then, महाबाहु: mightyarmed, प्रभु: master, लक्ष्माणाग्रज: the elder brother of Lakshmana, आत्मानम् himself, यथान्यायम् duly, ऋषये to the ascetic, सन्निवेद्य having introduced, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, अब्रवीत् said.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
लक्ष्मणाऽऽनय दारूणि दृढानि च वराणि च। कुरुष्वाऽवसथं सौम्य वासे मेऽभिरतं मनः।।2.56.19।।
output: सौम्य लक्ष्मण O handsome Lakshmana, दृढानि strong, वराणि च good, दारूणि logs of wood, आनय fetch, अवसथम् a dwelling, कुरुष्व build, मे मन: my mind, वासे in staying, अभिरतम् is eager.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सौमित्रिर्विविधान् द्रुमान्। आजहार तत श्चक्रे पर्णशालामरिन्दमः।।2.56.20।।
output: Having heard Rama, Saumitri, the subduer of enemies fetched different kinds of logs of wood, and with them made a hut and thatched it with leaves.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तां निष्ठितां बद्धकटां दृष्ट्वा रामस्सुदर्शनाम्। शुश्रूषमाणमेकाग्रमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.56.21।।
output: Rama saw the goodlooking leafhut with mats tied around as walls, and said to Lakshmana who was awaiting further command with rapt attention:

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ऐणेयं मांसमाहृत्य शालां यक्ष्यामहे वयम्। कर्तव्यं वास्तुशमनं सौमित्रे चिरजीविभिः।।2.56.22।।
output: O Lakshmana those who intend to live for long (in this hut), should pacify the deity presiding over here. Therefore, we shall bring the venison of a black antelope and make necessary offerings.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
मृगं हत्वाऽऽनय क्षिप्रं लक्ष्मणेह शुभेक्षण। कर्तव्य श्शास्त्रदृष्टो हि विधिर्धर्ममनुस्मर।।2.56.23।।
output: Slay an antelope and bring it here quickly. O Lakshmana The rites as prescribed by the scriptures will have to be carried out. You may recollect that tradition.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
भ्रातुर्वचनमाज्ञाय लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा। चकार स यथोक्तं च तं राम पुनरब्रवीत्।।2.56.24।।
output: Lakshmana, slayer of heroes on the enemy's side, understood and implemented what he was told. Rama again said to him:

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ऐणेयं श्रपयस्वैतच्छालां यक्ष्यामहे वयम्। त्वर सौम्य मुहूर्तोऽयं ध्रुवश्च दिवसोऽप्ययम्।।2.56.25।।
output: सौम्य O handsome one, एतत् this, ऐणेयम् venison, श्रपयस्व cook, वयम् we, शालाम् hut, यक्ष्यामहे will worship, अयम् this, दिवस: day, अयम् this, मुहूर्त:अपि this moment also, ध्रुवश्च is fixed, त्वर hasten.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स लक्ष्मणः कृष्णमृगं मेध्यं हत्वा प्रतापवान्। अथ चिक्षेप सौमित्रिस्समिद्धे जातवेदसि।।2.56.26।।
output: अथ then, सौमित्रि: son of Sumitra, प्रतापवान् powerful, स: लक्ष्मण: that Lakshmana, मेथ्यम् fit for offering pure, कृष्णमृगम् black antelope, हत्वा having killed, समिद्धे in a wellkindled, जातवेदसि fire, चिक्षेप offered.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तन्तु पक्वं परिज्ञाय निष्टप्तं छिन्नशोणितम्। लक्ष्मण: पुरुषव्याघ्रमथ राघवमब्रवीत्।।2.56.27।।
output: With the blood drained out of the venison, Lakshmana roasted it and cooked it well, and then said to Rama, the tiger (best) among men.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 56:
अयं सर्व: समस्ताग्ङ: श्रृत: कृष्णमृगो मया। देवतां देवसङ्काश यजस्व कुशलो ह्यसि।।2.56.28।।
output: This black antelope with all its limbs is wellcooked. O divine sire, you may make the offering to Vastu devata in which you are proficient.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 56:
राम: स्नात्वा तु नियतो गुणवान् जप्यकोविदः। सङ्ग्रहेणाकरोत् स्रवार्न मन्त्रान् सत्रावसानिकान्।।2.56.29।।
output: Virtuous Rama, who was an expert in the recitation of mantras, took his bath and his mind controlled, intoned briefly all the mantras appropriate to the completion of the ritual.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इष्ट्वा देवगणान्सर्वान्विवेशाऽवसथं शुचिः। बभूव च मनोह्लादो रामस्यामिततेजसः।।2.56.30।।
output: Sanctified with the worship of all the gods, Rama of immeasurable lustre felt a great happiness on entering the hut.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 56:
वैश्वदेवबलिं कृत्वा रौद्रं वैष्णव मेव च। वास्तुसंशमनीयानि मङ्गलानि प्रवर्तयन्।।2.56.31।। जपं च न्यायत कृत्वा स्नात्वा नद्यां यथाविधि। पापसंशमनं राम श्चकार बलिमुत्तमम्।।2.56.32।।
output: Rama, offered oblations to Visvadevas, Rudra and Visnu,  performed the auspices for the appeasement of the household deity. And having muttered japa silently in conformity with tradition, he took his ablution in the river as enjoined (by the sastras) and offered his final oblations for the expiation of his sins.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
वैश्वदेवबलिं कृत्वा रौद्रं वैष्णव मेव च। वास्तुसंशमनीयानि मङ्गलानि प्रवर्तयन्।।2.56.31।। जपं च न्यायत कृत्वा स्नात्वा नद्यां यथाविधि। पापसंशमनं राम श्चकार बलिमुत्तमम्।।2.56.32।।
output: राम: Rama, वैश्वदेवबलिम् oblations to Visvadevas (the entire pantheon of gods), रौद्रम् to Rudra, वैष्णवमेव च to Visnu, कृत्वा having offered, वास्तुसंशमनीयानि propitiation of the household deity (Vastu devata), मङ्गलानि auspices, प्रवर्तयन्  doing, न्यायत: according to precept, जपं च कृत्वा muttering the silent prayers, नद्याम् in the river, यथाविधि duly, स्नात्वा after bathing, पापसंशमनम् for the expiation of sins, उत्तमं बलिम् final oblation, चकार made.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 56:
वेदिस्थलविधानानि चैत्यान्यायतनानि च। आश्रमस्यानुरूपाणि स्थापयामास राघवः।।2.56.33।।
output: Rama, son of the Raghus, made altars in all the quarters, places of worship and sacred spots for fire befitting a hermitage.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 56:
वन्यैर्माल्यैः फलैर्मूलैः पक्वैर्मांसैर्यथाविधि। अद्भिर्जपैश्च वेदोक्तैर्दर्भैश्च ससमित्कुशैः।।2.56.34।। तौ तर्पयित्वा भूतानि राघवौ सह सीतया। तदा विविशतु श्शालां सुशुभां शुभलक्षणौ।।2.56.35।।
output: Bestowed with auspicious qualities, Rama and Lakshmana along with Sita propitiated those celestial beings with garlands of forest flowers, fruits and roots, wellcooked venison, water, muttering of prayers as expounded in the Vedas, faggots and kusa grass and entered that auspicious hermitage.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 56:
तां वृक्षपर्णच्छदनां मनोज्ञां यथाप्रदेशं सुकृतां निवाताम्। वासाय सर्वे विविशुस्समेतास्सभां यथा देवगणास्सुधर्माम्।।2.56.36।।
output: Just like the gods enter the court of Sudharma, they all stepped into the hut to dwell there. The hut was charming wellbuilt on a suitable site and protected against storm.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अनेकनानामृगपक्षिसङ्कुले विचित्रपत्रस्तबकैर्द्रुमैर्युते। वनोत्तमे व्यालमृगानुनादिते तदा विजह्रु स्सुसुखं जितेन्द्रियाः।।2.56.37।।
output: तदा then, जितेन्द्रियाः who had conquered the senses, अनेकनानामृगपक्षिसङ्कुले filled with  many varieties of animals and birds, विचित्रपुष्पस्तबकै: with bunches of bright flowers, द्रुमै with trees, युते full of, व्यालमृगानुनादिते echoing with the sounds of wild animals, वनोत्तमे in that splendid forest, सुसुखम् very happily, विजह्रु: wandered.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 56:
सुरम्यमासाद्य तु चित्रकूटं नदीं च तां माल्यवतीं सुतीर्थाम्। ननन्द हृष्टो मृगपक्षिजुष्टां जहौ च दुखं पुरविप्रवासात्।।2.35.38।।
output: Having reached the marvellous mount Chitrakuta and river Malyavati with excellent holy places and full of animals and birds, Rama shed the sorrow of his banishment from the city (of Ayodhya) and rejoiced with a gladdened heart. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे षट्पञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftysixth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of  the  holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कथयित्वा सुदुःखार्तस्सुमन्त्रेण चिरं सह। रामे दक्षिणकूलस्थे जगाम स्वगृहं गुहः।।2.57.1।।
output: रामे Rama, दक्षिणकूलस्थे had reached the southern bank (of the river), गुह: Guha, सुमन्त्रेण सह with Sumantra, चिरम् for a long while, कथयित्वा after talking, सुदुःखार्तः tormented with anguish, स्वगृहम् his home, जगाम reached.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
भरद्वाजाभिगमनं प्रयागे च सहाऽसनम्। आगिरेर्गमनं तेषां तत्रस्थैरुपलक्षितम्।।2.57.2।।
output: Positioned there, they could mark their arrival at Bharadwaja's at Prayaga, their stay (nighthalt) and their onward journey to Chitrakuta mountain.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 57:
अनुज्ञातस्सुमन्त्रोऽथ योजयित्वा हयोत्तमान्। अयोध्यामेव नगरीं प्रययौ गाढदुर्मनाः।।2.57.3।।
output: Permitted by Rama to leave, Sumantra harnessed the best of horses and set out for the city of Ayodhya with a heavy heart.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स वनानि सुगन्धीनि सरितश्च सरांसि च। पश्यन्नतिययौ शीघ्रं ग्रामाणि नगराणि च।।2.57.4।।
output: Beholding the fragrancefilled forests, rivers, lakes, villages and  towns on the way, Sumantra quickly crossed them.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तत स्सायाह्न समये तृतीयेऽहनि सारथिः। अयोध्यां समनुप्राप्य निरानन्दां ददर्श ह।।2.57.5।।
output: सारथिः charioteer, तृतीये on the third, अहनि day, सायाह्न समये at dusk, निरानन्दाम् cheerless, अयोध्याम् Ayodhya, समनुप्राप्य having reached, ददर्श ह saw.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 57:
स शून्यामिव निश्शब्दां दृष्ट्वा परमदुर्मनाः। सुमन्त्रश्चिन्तयामास शोकवेगसमाहतः।।2.57.6।।
output: Beholding the silent city, almost empty, the deeply depressed Sumantra, afflicted with gushing tears reflected:

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कच्चिन्न सगजा साऽश्वा सजना सजनाधिपा। रामसन्तापदुःखेन दग्धा शोकाग्निना पुरी।।2.57.7।।
output: Has the city along with its elephants, horses, people and its king perished in the fire of grief for Rama?

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इति चिन्तापरस्सूतो वाजिभिश्शीघ्रपातिभिः। नगरद्वारमासाद्य त्वरितः प्रविवेश ह।।2.57.8।।
output: Absorbed in these thoughts, the charioteer came to the citygate, carried by the swiftfooted horses, and quickly entered the city.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सुमन्त्रमभियान्तं तं शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। क्व राम इति पृच्छन्तस्सूतमभ्यद्रवन्नराः।।2.57.9।।
output: Meanwhile as the charioteer was moving towards the city, hundreds and thousands of men came pouring towards him enquiring, 'Where is Rama?'

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 57:
तेषां शशंस गङ्गायामहमापृच्छ्य राघवम्। अनुज्ञातो निवृत्तोऽस्मि धार्मिकेण महात्माना।।2.57.10।।
output: I took leave of the great, righteous Rama on the bank of the Ganga and have returned with his permission. (replied Sumantra).

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ते तीर्णा इति विज्ञाय बाष्पपूर्णमुखा जनाः। अहो धिगिति निश्श्वस्य हा रामेति च चुक्रुशुः।।2.57.11।।
output: Hearing that they had (the trio) crossed the river Ganga, the people, with their faces filled with tears sighed and saying 'Fie upon us Alas, Rama' cried out aloud.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
शुश्राव च वचस्तेषां बृन्दं बृन्दं च तिष्ठताम्। हतास्म खलु ये नेह पश्याम इति राघवम्।।2.57.12।।
output: ये all of us, इह here, राघवम् Rama, न पश्यामः unable to see, हताः स्म खलु indeed we are  lost (deprived), इति thus saying, बृन्दम् बृन्दम् in groups, तिष्ठताम् standing, तेषाम् their, वचः words, शुश्राव च also heard.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
दानयज्ञविवाहेषु समाजेषु महत्सु च। न द्रक्ष्यामः पुन र्जातु धार्मिकं राममन्तरा।।2.57.13।।
output: No longer will we see Rama at sacrifices, weddings, great assemblies and at places of charitable activity.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 57:
किं समर्थं जनस्यास्य किं प्रियं किं सुखावहम्। इति रामेण नगरं पितृवत्परिपालितम्।।2.57.14।।
output: Rama looked after his people like a father always thinking what was good for them, dear to them and comfortable to them.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
वातायनगतानां च स्त्रीणामन्वन्तरापणम्। रामशोकाभितप्तानां शुश्राव परिदेवनम्।।2.57.15।।
output: वातायनगतानाम् looking through the windows, स्त्रीणाम् women's, अन्वन्तरापणम् in the stalls, रामशोकाभितप्तानाम् burning with sorrow due to Rama's exile, परिदेवनम् bewailings, शुश्राव heard.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 57:
स राजमार्गमध्येन सुमन्त्रः पिहिताननः। यत्र राजा दशरथस्तदेवोपययौ गृहम्।।2.57.16।।
output: Sumantra with his face muffled, drove along the highway straight to the palace of king Dasaratha.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सोऽवतीर्य रथाच्छीघ्रं राजवेश्म प्रविश्य च। कक्ष्या स्सप्ताभिचक्राम महाजनसमाकुलाः।।2.57.17।।
output: Quickly alighting from the chariot, he entered  the king's palace and crossed the seven courtyards overcrowded with people.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 57:
हर्म्यै र्विमानैः प्रासादैरवेक्ष्याथ समागतम्। हाहाकारकृता नार्यो रामदर्शनकर्शिताः।।2.57.18।।
output: Women from mansions, sevenstoried buildings and from royal palaces, sighted him and pained at not seeing Rama cried out 'Alas, Alas'.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
आयतैर्विमलैर्नेत्रैरश्रुवेगपरिप्लुतैः। अन्योन्यमभिवीक्षन्तेऽव्यक्तमार्ततराः स्त्रियः।।2.57.19।।
output: The women in great anguish stood silently looking at one another, their large eyes flooded with overflowing tears.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततो दशरथस्त्रीणां प्रासादेभ्य स्तत स्ततः। रामशोकाभितप्तानां मन्दं शुश्राव जल्पितम्।।2.57.20।।
output: From different spots in the palace, Sumantra heard the sobs and whispers of Dasaratha's wives who were tormented with the sorrow of Rama's exile.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सह रामेण निर्यातो विना राम मिहागतः। सूतः किन्नाम कौसल्यां शोचन्तीं प्रतिवक्ष्यति।।2.57.21।।
output: रामेण सह with Rama, निर्यातः went out, विना रामम् without Rama, इह here, आगतः returned, सूतः charioteer, शोचन्तीम् worrying, कौशल्याम् Kausalya, किं नाम what can, प्रतिवक्ष्यति will he say?

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यथा च मन्ये दुर्जीवमेवं न सुकरं ध्रुवम्। आच्छिद्य पुत्रे निर्याते कौसल्या यत्र जीवति।।2.57.22।।
output: पुत्रे when the son, आच्छिद्य severing all connections, निर्याते had set out, कौसल्या Kausalya, यथा in whichever way, यत्र जीवति wherever surviving still, दुर्जीवम् it is difficult to live, मन्ये I consider, एवम् like this, सुकरम् easily, न not, ध्रुवम् certain.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 57:
सत्यरूपं तु तद्वाक्यं राज्ञ: स्त्रीणां निशामयन्। प्रदीप्तमिव शोकेन विवेश सहसा गृहम्।।2.57.23।।
output: Listening to the correct words of the king's wives, he immediately entered the palace as if in flames (of grief).

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 57:
स प्रविश्याष्टमीं कक्ष्यां राजानं दीनमातुरम्। पुत्रशोकपरिम्लानमपश्यत्पाण्डुरे गृहे।।2.57.24।।
output: On entering the eighth courtyard, he saw in a pale white chamber king Dasaratha desolate, anguished and withered with the sorrow of separation from his son.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अभिगम्य तमासीनं नरेन्द्रे मभिवाद्य च। सुमन्त्रो रामवचनं यथोक्तं प्रत्यवेदयत्।।2.57.25।।
output: Sumantra approached the king who was seated, paid obeisance to him and conveyed Rama's words verbatim.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स तूष्णीमेव तच्छ्रुत्वा राजा विभ्रान्तचेतनः। मूर्छितो न्यपतद्भूमौ रामशोकाभिपीडितः।।2.57.26।।
output: सः that, राजा king, तूष्णीमेव silently, तत् those words, श्रुत्वा having listened, विभ्रान्तचेतनः  with a bewildered mind, रामशोकाभिपीडितः tormented by the grief due to Rama's absence, मूर्छितः with senses lost, भूमौ on the ground, न्यपतत् fell.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततोऽन्तःपुरमाविद्धं मूर्छिते पृथिवीपतौ। उद्धृत्य बाहू चुक्रोश नृपतौ पतितेक्षितौ।।2.57.27।।
output: The moment the lord of the earth fell down on the ground unconscious, the women in the inner apartment burst into tears, raising their arms.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सुमित्रया तु सहिता कौसल्या पतितं पतिम्। उत्थापयामास तदा वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्।।2.57.28।।
output: तदा then, सुमित्रया सहिता together with Sumitra, कौशल्या Kausalya, पतितम् fallen on the ground, पतिम् husband, उत्थापयामास lifted him up, इदम् these, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् said.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इमं तस्य महाभाग दूतं दुष्करकारिणः। वनवासादनुप्राप्तं कस्मान्न प्रतिभाषसे।।2.57.29।।
output: O distinguished king, why are you not enquiring from the messenger about him  (Rama) who is capable of performing arduous tasks?

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अद्यैवमनयं कृत्वा व्यपत्रपसि राघव। उत्तिष्ठ सुकृतं तेस्तु शोके नस्या त्सहायता।।2.57.30।।
output: O descendant of the Raghus are you ashamed of having done an injustice? Arise. you may be a blessed one (for fulfilling your promise). If you grieve, none will help you.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 57:
देव यस्या भयाद्रामं नानुपृच्छसि सारथिम्। नेह तिष्ठिति कैकेयी विस्रब्धं प्रतिभाष्यताम्।।2.57.31।।
output: Kaikeyi for fear of whom you dare not ask the charioteer about Rama, O king is not here. You may speak to him without fear.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सा तथोक्त्वा महाराजं कौसल्या शोकलालसा। धरण्यां निपपाताऽशु बाष्पविप्लुतभाषिणी।।2.57.32।।
output: बाष्पविप्लुतभाषिणी speaking with a voice choked with tears, शोकलालसा absorbed in grief, सा कौशल्या that Kausalya, महाराजम् to the maharaja, तथा that way, उक्त्वा having said, आशु suddenly, धरण्याम् on the ground, निपपात fell down.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 57:
एवं विलपतीं दृष्ट्वा कौसल्यां पतितां भुवि। पतिं चावेक्ष्य ता स्सर्वा सुस्वरं रुरुदुः स्त्रियः।।2.57.33।।
output: All those women saw weeping Kausalya as well as their husband fallen on the ground and wailed loudly in a chorus.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 57:
तत स्तमन्तःपुरनादमुत्थितं समीक्ष्य वृद्धा स्तरुणाश्च मानवाः। स्त्रियश्च सर्वा रुरुदु स्समन्ततः पुरं तदासीत्पुनरेव सङ्कुलम्।।2.57.34।।
output: Having heard the sound emanating from the inner apartment, people, old, young and women, of the city lamented. The city was crowded again. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftyseventh sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
प्रत्याश्वस्तो यदा राजा मोहात्प्रत्यागतं पुनः। अथाऽजुहाव तं सूतं रामवृत्तान्तकारणात्।।2.58.1।।
output: Sumantra conveys the message of Rama to the wailing king and Kausalya.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अथ सूतो महाराजं कृताञ्जलिरुपस्थितः। राममेवानुशोचन्तं दुःखशोकसमन्वितम्।।2.58.2।। वृद्धं परमसन्तप्तं नवग्रहमिव द्विपम्। विनिश्वसन्तं ध्यायन्तमस्वस्थ मिव कुङञरम्।।2.58.3।।
output: Then the charioteer with folded palms approached the king who, deeply afflicted with grief and pain, was brooding over Rama alone. Aged Dasaratha was heaving deep sighs like a newlycaptured, indisposed elephant.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अथ सूतो महाराजं कृताञ्जलिरुपस्थितः। राममेवानुशोचन्तं दुःखशोकसमन्वितम्।।2.58.2।। वृद्धं परमसन्तप्तं नवग्रहमिव द्विपम्। विनिश्वसन्तं ध्यायन्तमस्वस्थ मिव कुङञरम्।।2.58.3।।
output: Then the charioteer with folded palms approached the king who, deeply afflicted with grief and pain, was brooding over Rama alone. Aged Dasaratha was heaving deep sighs like a newlycaptured, indisposed elephant.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
राजा तु रजसा सूतं ध्वस्ताङ्गं समुपस्थितम्। अश्रुपूर्णमुखं दीनमुवाच परमार्तवत्।।2.58.4।।
output: Seeing the dejected charioteer standing before him, the desolate king covered all over with dust and his face bathed in tears, said to him in extreme grief:

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
क्वनु वत्स्यति धर्मात्मा वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितः। सोऽत्यन्तसुखित स्सूत किमशिष्यति राघवः।।2.58.5।।
output: O charioteer Rama is rightous and he is acustoomed to all sorts of comfort. Taking refuge at the foot of a tree how shall he live and what shall he eat?

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
दुःखस्यानुचितो दुःखं सुमन्त्र शयनोचितः। भूमिपालात्मजो भूमौ शेते कथमनाथवत्।।2.58.6।।
output: How can the son of the guardian of the earth who is accustomed to a comfortable bed and not to undeserved suffering lie down on the ground like an orphan, O Sumantra

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 58:
यं यान्तमनुयान्ति स्म पदातिरथकुञ्जराः। स वत्स्यति कथं रामो विजनं वन माश्रितः।।2.58.7।।
output: Wherever Rama went, elephants, chariots and footsoldiers followed him. How can he (now) live in the desolate forest where he has taken refuge?

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
व्यालैर्मृगैराचरितं कृष्णसर्पनिषेवितम्। कथं कुमारौ वैदेह्या सार्धं वन मुपस्थितौ।।2.58.8।।
output: How can the two young men along with Vaidehi live in the forest infested with black cobras and wicked, wild animals?

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सुकुमार्या तपस्विन्या सुमन्त्र सह सीतया। राजपुत्रौ कथं पादैरवरुह्य रथाद्गतौ।।2.58.9।।
output: O Sumantra how did those two princes along with pitiable, delicate Sita, alight from the chariot, and enter the forest on foot?

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 58:
सिद्धार्थः खलु सूत त्वं येन दृष्टौ ममाऽत्मजौ। वनान्तं प्रविशन्तौ तावश्विनाविवमन्दरम्।।2.58.10।।
output: You are blessed indeed, O charioteer to have seen my sons entering the outskirts of the forest like Aswinis stepping into the region of the Mandara mountain.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
किमुवाच वचो रामः किमुवाच च लक्ष्मणः। सुमन्त्र वनमासाद्य किमुवाच च मैथिली।।2.58.11।।
output: Upon reaching the forest, O Sumantra what did Rama, Lakshmana and Sita say?

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
आसितं शयितं भुक्तं सूत रामस्य कीर्तय। जीविष्यामहमेतेन ययातिरिव साधुषु।।2.58.12।।
output: सूत charioteer, रामस्य Rama's, आसितम् seat, शयितम् bed, भुक्तम् food, कीर्तय describe, अहम् I, ययातिः Yayati, साधुषु इव as in the company of saints, एतेन with this, जीविष्यामि shall live.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 58:
इति सूतो नरेन्द्रेण बोधित स्सज्जमानया। उवाच वाचा राजानं स बाष्पपरिबद्धया।।2.58.13।।
output: Thus questioned by the king the charioteer, his voice choked with tears and words faltering in grief, addressed the king:

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अब्रवीन्मां महाराज धर्ममेवानुपालयन्। अञ्जलिं राघवः कृत्वा शिरसाऽभिप्रणम्य च।।2.58.14।।
output: With palms folded and head bowed, O great king Rama offered his salutations to you in confirmity with righteousness and said to me:

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सूत मद्वचनात्तस्य तातस्य विदितात्मनः। शिरसा वन्दनीयस्य वन्द्यौ पादौ महात्मनः।।2.58.15।।
output: 'Convey on my behalf, O charioteer to my illustrious father who is known for his selfknowledge, and is worthy of homage, that I am saluting his feet with my head bowed.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सर्वमन्तःपुरं वाच्यं सूत मद्वचनात्त्वया। आरोग्यमविशेषेण यथार्हं चाभिवादनम्।।2.58.16।।
output: 'On my behalf convey, O charioteer, without any distinction, my salutations to all the women befitting their status and tell them I was enquiring about their wellbeing.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
माता च मम कौसल्या कुशलं चाभिवादनम्। अप्रमादं च वक्तव्या ब्रूयाश्चैनामिदं वचः।।2.58.17।।
output: 'Convey my mother carefully my saluations and my wellbeing and tell her:

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
धर्मनित्या यथाकालमग्न्यगारपरा भव। देवि देवस्य पादौ च देववत्परिपालय।।2.58.18।।
output: देवि O mother, धर्मनित्या adhering to the righteous path, यथाकालम् in time, अग्न्यगारपरा भव perform the rituals in the chamber of sacrificial fire, देवस्य (your) lord's (king Dasaratha's), पादौ च feet also, देववत् like a god, परिपालय serve.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अभिमानं च मानं च त्यक्त्वा वर्तस्व मातृषु। अनु राजानमार्यां च कैकेयीमम्ब कारय।।2.58.19।।
output: अभिमानं च egoism, मानं च pride, मातृषु towards mothers, वर्तस्व conduct yourself, अम्ब O mother, आर्याम् venerable, कैकेयीम् Kaikeyi, राजानम् अनु welldisposed towards the king, कारय mould her.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कुमारे भरते वृत्तिर्वर्तितव्या च राजवत्। अर्थज्येष्ठा हि राजानो राजधर्ममनुस्मर।।2.58.20।।
output: 'Behave towards young Bharata as to a king. Irrespective of age, a king is a king. (Hence should be honoured). You should keep this rajadharma (royal prerogative) in mind.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 58:
भरतः कुशलं वाच्यो वाच्यो मद्वचनेन च। सर्वास्वेव यथान्यायं वृत्तिं वर्तस्व मातृषु।।2.58.21।।
output: 'Tell Bharata of my welfare and tell him on my behalf that he should honour all our mothers equally.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 58:
वक्तव्यश्च महाबाहुरिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनः। पितरं यौवराज्यस्थो राज्यस्थमनुपालय।।2.58.22।।
output: इक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनः delight of the race of Ikshvaku, महाबाहुः mightyarmed, वक्तव्यश्च deserves be told this way, यौवराज्यस्थः crowned as prince regent, राज्यस्थम् being in the kingdom, पितरम् father, अनुपालय rule the kingdom (by being obedient to him).

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अतिक्रान्तवया राजा मास्मैनं व्यवरोरुधः। कुमार राज्ये जीव त्वं तस्यैवाज्ञाप्रवर्तनात्।।2.58.23।।
output: राजा king Dasaratha, अतिक्रान्तवयाः is advanced in age, एनम् him, मा स्म व्यवरोरुधः do not restrict him, त्वम् you, तस्यैव that king's, आज्ञाप्रवर्तनात् carrying out the commands, कुमारराज्ये as prince regent, जीव live.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 58:
अब्रवीच्चापि मां भूयो भृशमश्रूणि वर्तयन्। मातेव मम माता ते द्रष्टव्या पुत्रगर्धिनी।।2.58.24।।
output: Shedding profuse tears, Rama continued, 'Look after my mother who is covetous of her son as your own mother'.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
इत्येवं मां महराज ब्रुवन्नेव महायशाः। रामो राजीवताम्राक्षो भृशमश्रूण्यवर्तयत्।।2.58.25।।
output: महाराज O king, महायशाः renowned, राजीवताम्राक्षः with red lotuslike eyes, रामः Rama, माम् to me, इत्येवम् thus, ब्रुवन्नेव while saying, भृशम् copious,  अश्रूणि tears, अवर्तयत् shed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
लक्ष्मणस्तु सुसङ्कृद्धो निश्श्वसन्वाक्यमब्रवीत्। केनायमपराधेन राजपुत्रो विवासितः।।2.58.26।।
output: लक्ष्मणस्तु Lakshmana, सुसङ्कृद्धः mighty angry, निश्श्वसन् sighing, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् said, अयम् this, राजपुत्रः king's son, केन by what, अपराधेन offence, विवासितः has been banished?

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
राज्ञा तु खलु कैकेय्या लघुत्वाश्रित्य शासनम्। कृतं कार्यमकार्यं वा वयं येनाभिपीडिताः।।2.58.27।।
output: 'The king, too, submitting to the trash command of Kaikeyi has perpetrated an act, just or unjust (he knows better), for which we are made to suffer so much.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यदि प्रव्राजितो रामो लोभकारणकारितम्। वरदाननिमित्तं वा सर्वथा दुष्कृतं कृतम्।।2.58.28।।
output: रामः Rama, लोभकारणकारितम् out of greed (for the kingdom), वरदाननिमित्तं वा or on account of the boons bestowed, प्रव्राजितः यदि if banished, सर्वथा by all means, दुष्कृतम् wicked act, कृतम् has been done.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
इदं तावद्यथाकाममीश्वरस्य कृते कृतम्। रामस्य तु परित्यागे न हेतु मुपलक्षये।।2.58.29।।
output: इदं तावत् this one, ईश्वरस्य कृते for (fear of) God, यथाकामम् this act, कृतम् done, रामस्य Rama's, परित्यागे in abandonment, हेतुम् reason, न उपलक्षये I do not see.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
असमीक्षय समारब्धं विरुद्धं बुध्दिलाघवात्। जनयिष्यति सङ्क्रोशं राघवस्य विवासनम्।।2.58.30।।
output: बुद्धिलाघवात् out of lack of intelligence, असमीक्ष्य without (proper) consideration, समारब्धम् commenced, विरुद्धम् contrary (to justice), राघवस्य Rama's, विवासनम् banishment, सङ्क्रोशम् bewailment, जनयिष्यति will produce.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अहं तावन्महाराजे पितृत्वं नोपलक्ष्ये। भ्राता भर्ता च बन्धुश्च पिता च मम राघवः।।2.58.31।।
output: अहम् I, महाराजे in that great king, पितृत्वम् fatherhood, नोपलक्ष्ये I do not see, मम to me, राघवः Rama alone, भ्राता च brother, भर्ताच also protector, बन्धुश्च friend, पिता father.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सर्वर्लोकप्रियं त्यक्त्वा सर्वलोकहिते रतम्। सर्वलोकोऽनुरज्येत कथं त्वाऽनेनकर्मणा।।2.58.32।।
output: सर्वलोकप्रियम् beloved to all, सर्वलोकहिते in the welfare of all, रतम् devoted, त्यक्त्वा after deserting, अनेन कर्मणा with this act, त्वा towards you, सर्वलोकः entire world, कथम् how, अनुरज्येत will be pleased?

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सर्वप्रजाभिरामं हि रामं प्रव्राज्य धार्मिकम्। सर्वलोकं विरुध्येमं कथं राजा भविष्यसि।।2.58.33।।
output: 'Having banished the righteous Rama, the delight of all subjects and, thereby, antagonizing the entire world, how can you claim to be their king?'

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
जानकी तु महाराज निश्श्वसन्ती मनस्विनी। भूतोपहतचित्तेव विष्ठिता विस्मृता स्मिता।।2.58.34।।
output: O great king as for that sensitive Janaki, she stood sighing, stupefied and oblivious (of the past), yet smiling as though her mind was possessed by an evil spirit.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अदृष्टपूर्वव्यसना राज्यपुत्री यशस्विनी। तेन दुःखेन रुदती नैव मां किञ्चिदब्रवीत्।।2.58.35।।
output: अदृष्टपूर्वव्यसना who had never experienced adversity, यशस्विनी celebrated, राजपुत्री that princess, तेन that, दुःखेन with sorrow, रुदती weeping, माम् to me, किञ्चित् even a little, नैव  अब्रवीत् did not at all say.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
उद्वीक्षमाणा भर्तारं मुखेन परिशुष्यता। मुमोच सहसा बाष्पं मां प्रयान्तमुदीक्ष्य सा।।2.58.36।।
output: सा she, प्रयान्तम् moving, माम् me, उदीक्ष्य having seen, परिशुष्यता with driedup, मुखेन face, भर्तारम् husband, उद्वीक्षमाणा beholding, सहसा suddenly, बाष्पम् tears, मुमोच shed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तथैव रामोऽश्रुमुखः कृताञ्जलिः स्थितोऽभवल्लक्ष्मणबाहुपालितः। तथैव सीता रुदती तपस्विनी निरीक्षते राजरथं तथैव माम्।।2.58.37।।
output: तथैव thus, रामः Rama, अश्रुमुखः with his face filled with tears, कृताञ्जलिः with folded hands, लक्ष्मणबाहुपालितः supported by the arms of Lakshmana, स्थितः अभवत् stood, तपस्विनी pitiable, सीता Sita, रुदती weeping, राजरथम् king's chariot, माम् me, निरीक्षते kept gazing.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इति ब्रुवन्तं तं सूतं सुमन्त्रं मन्त्रिसत्तमम्। ब्रूहि शेषं पुनरिति राजा वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.59.1।।
output: Sumantra describes the shadow of sorrow over Ayodhya -- withering plants and flowers, driedup ponds, immobile animals -- Dasaratha pines for Rama.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 59:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सुमन्त्रो बाष्पविक्लबः। कथयामास भूयोऽपि रामसन्देशविस्तरम्।।2.59.2।।
output: Having heard him, Sumantra, overcome with tears, related further details of Rama's message.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
जटाः कृत्वा महाराज चीरवल्कलधारिणौ। गङ्गामुत्तीर्य तौ वीरौ प्रयागाभिमुखौ गतौ।।2.59.3।।
output: महाराज O king, चीरवल्कलधारिणौ wearing the bark robes, तौ वीरौ those heroes, जटाः matted hair, कृत्वा having made, गङ्गाम् the river Ganga, उत्तीर्य having crossed, प्रयागाभिमुखौ towards Prayaga, गतौ went.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अग्रतो लक्ष्मणो यातः पालयन्रघुनन्दनम्। तांस्तथा गच्छतो दृष्ट्वा निवृत्तोऽस्म्यवशस्तदा।।2.59.4।।
output: लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, रघुनन्दनम् Rama, पालयन् protecting, अग्रतः ahead of him, यातः had gone, तथा that way, गच्छतः going, तान् him, दृष्ट्वा having seen, तदा then, अवशः helplessly, निवृत्तः अस्मि returned.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ममत्वश्वा निवृत्तस्य न प्रावर्तन्त वर्त्मनि। उष्णमश्रु प्रमुञ्चन्तो रामे सम्प्रस्थिते वनम्।।2.59.5।।
output: रामे Rama, वनम् for the forest, सम्प्रस्थिते when setting out, निवृत्तस्य when I returned, मम my, अश्वा: तु as for horses, उष्णम् hot, अश्रुप्रमुञ्चन्तः shedding tears, वर्त्मनि on the path, न प्रावर्तन्त did not proceed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
उभाभ्यां राजपुत्राभ्यामथ कृत्वाहमञ्जलिम्। प्रस्थितो रथमास्थाय तद्दुःखमपि धारयन्।।2.59.6।।
output: अथ thereafter, अहम् I, उभाभ्याम् to both, राजपुत्राभ्याम् princess, अञ्जलिम् folded palms, कृत्वा having made, तत् that, दुःखम् अपि grief, धारयन् controlling, रथम् chariot, आस्थाय ascending, प्रस्थितः set out.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 59:
गुहेन सार्धं तत्रैव स्थितोऽस्मि दिवसान्बहून्। आशया यदि मां रामः पुन श्शब्दापयेदिति।।2.59.7।।
output: There along with Guha I waited for (three) days that Rama might call me back.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
विषये ते महाराज रामव्यसनकर्शिताः। अपि वृक्षाः परिम्लानास्सपुष्पाङ्कुरकोरकाः।।2.59.8।।
output: O great king even trees with their flowers, buds and shoots throughout your empire have withered because of the calamity on Rama.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
उपतप्तोदका नद्यः पल्वलानि सरांसि च। परिशुष्कपलाशानि वनान्युपवनानि च।।2.59.9।।
output: नद्यः rivers, उपतप्तोदकाः with heated waters, पल्वलानि ponds, सरांसि च lakes, वनानि forests, उपवनानि च gardens, परिशुष्कपलाशानि have their foliage shrivelled.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
न च सर्पन्ति सत्त्वानि व्यासा न प्रचरन्ति च। रामशोकाभिभूतं तन्निष्कूजमभवद्वनम्।।2.59.10।।
output: सत्त्वानि living beings, न च सर्पन्ति are not moving, व्यालाः च wild animals also, नप्रचरन्ति not ranging, तत् वनम् that forest, रामशोकाभिभूतम् overpowered by grief on account of Rama, निष्कूजम् silent, अभवत् became.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
लीनपुष्करपत्राश्च नरेन्द्र कलुषोदकाः। सन्तप्तपद्माः पद्मिन्यो लीनमीनविहङ्गमाः।।2.59.11।।
output: नरेन्द्र O king, पद्मिन्यः lotus lakes, लीनपुष्करपत्राः च with the shrivelled blue lotus leaves submerged in water, कलुषोदकाः with waters turbid, सन्तप्तपद्माः withered lotuses, लीनमीनविहङ्गमाः devoid of fishes and birds.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 59:
जलजानि च पुष्पाणि माल्यानि स्थलजानि च। नाद्य भान्त्यल्पगन्धीनि फलानि च यथापुरम्।।2.59.12।।
output: Bunches of flowers grown in water and on land, as well as fruits with their scant fragrance do not shine as before.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 59:
अत्रोद्यानानि शून्यानि प्रलीनविहगनि च। न चाभिरामा नारामान्पश्यामि मनुजर्षभ।।2.59.13।।
output: Pleasuregardens are all deserted as the birds have vanished. O best of men, as such they do not look beautiful.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
प्रविशन्तमयोध्यां मां न कश्चिदभिनन्दति। नरा राममपश्यन्तो निश्श्वसन्ति मुहुर्मुहुः।।2.59.14।।
output: None greeted me when I entered Ayodhya, People heaved sighs repeatedly when they did not see Rama.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
देव राजरथं दृष्ट्वा विना राममिहागतम्। दुःखादश्रुमुखस्सर्वो राजमार्गगतो जनः।।2.59.15।।
output: Beholding the royal chariot arrive without Rama, all were on the highway shedding tears of anguish.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
हर्म्यैर्विमानैः प्रासादैरवेक्ष्यरथमागतम्। हाहाकारकृतानार्यो रामादर्शनकर्शिताः।।2.59.16।।
output: When the women from mansions, sevenstoried buildings and from royal palaces saw the chariot without Rama, they, overwhelmed with sorrow, cried, 'Alas, Alas'.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 59:
आयतैर्विमलैर्नेत्रैरश्रुवेगपरिप्लुतैः। अन्योन्यमभिवीक्षन्तेऽव्यक्तमार्ततराः स्त्रियः।।2.59.17।।
output: The women, with their large, bright eyes flooded with gushing tears looked in silence at one another in deep anguish.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
नामित्राणां न मित्राणामुदासीनजनस्य च। अहमार्ततया किञ्चिद्विशेषमुपलक्षये।।2.59.18।।
output: अहम् I, आर्ततया in great agony, अमित्राणाम् among those who are not friends, किञ्चित् even a little, विशेषम् diference, न उपलक्षये could not see, मित्राणाम् among friends, उदासीनजनस्य of people indifferent, न could not see.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 59:
अप्रहृष्टमनुष्या च दीननागतुरङ्गमा। आर्तस्वरपरिम्लाना विनिश्श्वसितनिस्स्वना।।2.59.19।। निरानन्दा महाराज रामप्रव्राजनातुरा। कौसल्या पुत्रहीनेव अयोध्या प्रतिभाति मा।।2.59.20।।
output: O maharaja, Ayodhya is filled with cheerless people with deep sighs, agonised voices and pale faces depressed and distressed due to Rama's exile. (Even) elephants and horses look spiritless. For me it (the city) resembles (dejected) Kausalya deprived of her son.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अप्रहृष्टमनुष्या च दीननागतुरङ्गमा। आर्तस्वरपरिम्लाना विनिश्श्वसितनिस्स्वना।।2.59.19।। निरानन्दा महाराज रामप्रव्राजनातुरा। कौसल्या पुत्रहीनेव अयोध्या प्रतिभाति मा।।2.59.20।।
output: O maharaja, Ayodhya is filled with cheerless people with deep sighs, agonised voices and pale faces depressed and distressed due to Rama's exile. (Even) elephants and horses look spiritless. For me it (the city) resembles (dejected) Kausalya deprived of her son.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सूतस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा वाचा परमदीनया। बाष्पोपहतया राजा तं सूतमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.59.21।।
output: राजा king, सूतस्य charioteer's, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, परमदीनया deeply dejected, बाष्पोपहतया choked with tears, वाचा with a voice, तं सूतम् to the charioteer, इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 59:
कैकेय्या विनियुक्तेन पापाभिजनभावया। मया न मन्त्रकुशलैर्वृद्धैस्सह समर्थितम्।।2.59.22।।
output: Incited by Kaikeyi of sinful relations and sinful motive, I did not consult expert, elderly counsellers.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
न सुहृद्भिर्नचामात्यैर्मन्त्रयित्वा न नैगमैः। मयायमर्थस्सम्मोहात् स्त्रीहेतो स्सहसा कृतः।।2.59.23।।
output: For the sake of a woman, this act was committed in great haste, without consulting friends or ministers or men of prudence.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 59:
भवितव्यतया नूनमिदं वा व्यसनं महत्। कुलस्यास्य विनाशाय प्राप्तं सूत यदृच्छया।।2.59.24।।
output: Surely it is destiny and this calamity has befallen for the wilful destruction of the (entire) race, O charioteer

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सूत यद्यस्ति ते किञ्चिन्मया तु सुकृतं कृतम्। त्वं प्रापयाऽऽशु मां रामं प्राणास्सन्त्वरयन्तिमाम्।।2.59.25।।
output: O Charioteer, if ever I have rendered you any favour, quickly  take me to Rama. My life is hastening me (fast running out).

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यद्यद्यापि ममैवाज्ञा निवर्तयतु राघवम्। न शक्ष्यामि विना रामं मुहूर्तमपि जीवितुम्।।2.59.26।।
output: If my command prevails today, Rama may be brought back. Without Rama I cannot live for a moment even.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अथवाऽपि महाबाहुर्गतो दूरं भविष्यति। मामेव रथमारोप्य शीघ्रं रामाय दर्शय।।2.58.27।।
output: अथवा or otherwise also, महाबाहुः mightyarmed, दूरम् far away, गतः भविष्यति must have gone, मामेव me alone, रथम् on the chariot, आरोप्य placing, शीघ्रम् quickly, रामाय to Rama, दर्शय show.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
वृत्तदंष्ट्रो महेष्वासः क्वासौ लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः। यदि जीवामि साध्वेनं पश्येयं सीतया सह।।2.59.28।।
output: Where is that Rama, elder brother to Lakshmana who has wellshaped teeth and wields a mighty bow? If I can see him along with Sita I will survive.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
लोहिताक्षं महाबाहुमामुक्तमणिकुण्डलम्। रामं यदि न पश्येयं गमिष्यामि यमक्षयम्।।2.59.29।।
output: लोहिताक्षम् one with redcoloured eyes, महाबाहुम् mightyarmed, आमुक्तमणिकुण्डलम् wearing earrings bedecked with gems, रामम् Rama, न पश्येयं यदि if I cannot see him, यमक्षयम् kingdom of Yama, lord of death, गमिष्यामि I will go.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अतो नु किं दुःखतरं सोऽहमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनम्। इमामवस्थामापन्नो नेह पश्यामि राघवम्।।2.59.30।।
output: इमाम् this, अवस्थाम् condition, आपन्नः having reached, सः अहम् such me, इक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम्  Delight of the Ikshvakus, राघवम् Rama, इह now, न पश्यामि see not, अतः than this, दुःखतरम् greater sorrow,  किं नु what more.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
हा राम रामानुज हा हा वैदेहि तपस्विनि। न मां जानीत दुःखेन म्रियमाणतमनाथवत्।।2.59.31।।
output: Ah Rama, Ah Lakshmana, Ah unfortunate Vaidehi, you do not know that I am dying  like an orphan because of my grief.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 59:
स तेन राजा दुःखेन भृशमर्पितचेतनः। अवगाढस्सुदुष्पारं शोकसागरमब्रवीत्।।2.59.32।।
output: The king whose mind was extremely enfeebled due to grief and who was immersed in a sea of tears which he was unable to cross continued:

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
रामशोकमहाभोगस्सीताविरहपारगः। श्वसितोर्मि महावर्तो बाष्पफेनजालाविलः।।2.59.33।। बाहुविक्षेपमीनौघो विक्रन्दित महास्वनः। प्रकीर्णकेशशैवालः कैकेयीबडबामुखः।।2.59.34।। ममाश्रुवेगप्रभवः कुब्जावाक्यमहाग्रहः। वरवेलो नृशंसाया रामप्रव्राजनायतः।।2.59.35।। यस्मिन्बत निमग्नोऽहं कौसल्ये राघवं विना। दुस्तरो जीवता देवि मयाऽयं शोकसागरः।।2.59.36।।
output: देवि O queen, कौशल्ये Kausalya, अहम् I, यस्मिन् in which, निमग्नः immersed, (असौ this, शोकसागरः ocean of sorrow), रामशोकमहाभोगः sorrow due to Rama's separation as its breadth, सीताविरहपारगः Sita's separation as its other shore, श्वसितोर्मिमहावर्तः sighs as its turbulent waves and whirlpools, बाष्पफेनजलाविलः tears as its foam and turbid waters, बाहुविक्षेपमीनौघः waving of the arms as fishes, विक्रन्दितमहास्वनः cries of agony as its roar, प्रकीर्णकेशशैवालः dishevelled hair as its moss, कैकेयीबडबामुखः Kaikeyi as mouth of Badaba mythical seamare, मम to me, अश्रुवेगप्रभवः source of copious tears, कुब्जावाक्यमहाग्रहः the words of hunchback (Manthara) as monstrous crocodiles, नृशंसायाः cruel, वरवेल boons as shores, रामप्रव्राजनायतः exile of Rama as its expanse, अयम् this, शोकसागरः sea of sorrow, राघवं विना without Rama, मया by me, जीवता with my life, दुस्तरः difficult to cross, बत on what a pity

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 59:
रामशोकमहाभोगस्सीताविरहपारगः। श्वसितोर्मि महावर्तो बाष्पफेनजालाविलः।।2.59.33।। बाहुविक्षेपमीनौघो विक्रन्दित महास्वनः। प्रकीर्णकेशशैवालः कैकेयीबडबामुखः।।2.59.34।। ममाश्रुवेगप्रभवः कुब्जावाक्यमहाग्रहः। वरवेलो नृशंसाया रामप्रव्राजनायतः।।2.59.35।। यस्मिन्बत निमग्नोऽहं कौसल्ये राघवं विना। दुस्तरो जीवता देवि मयाऽयं शोकसागरः।।2.59.36।।
output: O queen Kausalya, I am completely immersed in this ocean of sorrow. The misfortune due to Rama's separation is its breadth. Sita's separation is the other end of the shore. Sighs are its turbulent waves and whirlpools. Tears are its foam and turbid waters. Waving of arms is its fishes. Cries of agony are its roars. My dishevelled hair is its moss. Kaikeyi is the mouth of Badaba. My copious tears are its source. Words of the hunchback (Manthara) are the monstrous crocodiles. The cruel boons to Kaikeyi are its shores. Without Rama I cannot cross  this sea of sorrow alive. Ah, what a pity

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 59:
रामशोकमहाभोगस्सीताविरहपारगः। श्वसितोर्मि महावर्तो बाष्पफेनजालाविलः।।2.59.33।। बाहुविक्षेपमीनौघो विक्रन्दित महास्वनः। प्रकीर्णकेशशैवालः कैकेयीबडबामुखः।।2.59.34।। ममाश्रुवेगप्रभवः कुब्जावाक्यमहाग्रहः। वरवेलो नृशंसाया रामप्रव्राजनायतः।।2.59.35।। यस्मिन्बत निमग्नोऽहं कौसल्ये राघवं विना। दुस्तरो जीवता देवि मयाऽयं शोकसागरः।।2.59.36।।

Sighs are its turbulent waves and whirlpools. Tears are its foam and turbid waters. Waving of arms is its fishes. Cries of agony are its roars. My dishevelled hair is its moss. Kaikeyi is the mouth of Badaba. My copious tears are its source. Words of the hunchback (Manthara) are the monstrous crocodiles. The cruel boons to Kaikeyi are its shores. Without Rama I cannot cross  this sea of sorrow alive. Ah, what a pity

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 59:
रामशोकमहाभोगस्सीताविरहपारगः। श्वसितोर्मि महावर्तो बाष्पफेनजालाविलः।।2.59.33।। बाहुविक्षेपमीनौघो विक्रन्दित महास्वनः। प्रकीर्णकेशशैवालः कैकेयीबडबामुखः।।2.59.34।। ममाश्रुवेगप्रभवः कुब्जावाक्यमहाग्रहः। वरवेलो नृशंसाया रामप्रव्राजनायतः।।2.59.35।। यस्मिन्बत निमग्नोऽहं कौसल्ये राघवं विना। दुस्तरो जीवता देवि मयाऽयं शोकसागरः।।2.59.36।।
output: O queen Kausalya, I am completely immersed in this ocean of sorrow. The misfortune due to Rama's separation is its breadth. Sita's separation is the other end of the shore. Sighs are its turbulent waves and whirlpools. Tears are its foam and turbid waters. Waving of arms is its fishes. Cries of agony are its roars. My dishevelled hair is its moss. Kaikeyi is the mouth of Badaba. My copious tears are its source. Words of the hunchback (Manthara) are the monstrous crocodiles. The cruel boons to Kaikeyi are its shores. Without Rama I cannot cross  this sea of sorrow alive. Ah, what a pity

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अशोभनं योऽहमिहाद्य राघवं दिदृक्षमाणो न लभे सलक्ष्मणम्। इतीव राजा विलपन्महायशाः पपात तूर्णं शयने समूर्छितः।।2.59.37।।
output: यः he who, अहम् I, अद्य now, दिदृक्षमाणः wishing to see, सलक्ष्मणम् with Lakshamana, राघवम् Rama, इह here, न लभे unable to get them, अशोभनम् inauspicious, इतीव in this way, महायशाः of great reknown, सः राजा that king, विलपन् lamenting, मूर्छितः lying unconcsious, तूर्णम् immediately, शयने on the bed, पपात fell.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इति विलपति पार्थिवे प्रणष्टे करुणतरं द्विगुणं च रामहेतोः। वचनमनुनिशम्य तस्य देवी भयमगमत्पुनरेव राममाता।।2.59.38।।
output: Wailing, Dasaratha fell unconscious. He was doubly grieved due to his yearning for Rama. Rama's mother was seized with fear hearing those lamentations. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends  the fiftyninth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततो भूतोपसृष्टेव वेपमाना पुनः पुनः। धरण्यां गतसत्त्वेव कौसल्या सूतमब्रवीत्।।2.60.1।।
output: ततः thereafter, कौशल्या Kausalya, भूतोपसृष्टेव as if possessed by an evil spirit, वेपमाना trembling, गतसत्त्वेव like one who has his senses lost, पुनः पुनः again and again, धरण्याम् on the floor, सूतम् to the  charioteer (Sumantra), अब्रवीत् said.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
नय मां यत्र काकुत्स्थस्सीता यत्र च लक्ष्मणः। तान्विना क्षणमप्यत्र जीवितुं नोत्सहेह्यहम्।।2.60.2।।
output: Take me where Rama, Sita and Lakshmana are. I do not wish to live even for a moment without them.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
निवर्तय रथं शीघ्रं दण्डकान्नय मामपि। अथ तान्नानुगच्छामि गमिष्यामि यमक्षयम्।।2.60.3।।
output: 'Turn back your chariot immediately and take me to the Dandaka forest. If I do not follow them, I shall enter the world of Yama'.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
बाष्पवेगोपहतया स वाचा सज्जमानया। इदमाश्वासयन्देवीं सूतः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्।।2.60.4।।
output: सः सूतः that charioteer, बाष्पवेगोपहतया prevented by fastflowing tears, सज्जमानया faltering, वाचा with words, देवीम् to Kausalya, आश्वसयन् consoling, प्राञ्जलिः with folded palms, इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 60:
त्यज शोकं च मोहं च सम्भ्रमं दुःखजं तथा। व्यवधूय च सन्तापं वने वत्स्यति राघवः।।2.60.5।।
output: Abandon your tears, delusion and despair arising out of sorrow. Rama is going to live in the forest, brushing aside all agony.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 60:
लक्ष्मणश्चापि रामस्य पादौ परिचरन्वने। आराधयति धर्मज्ञः परलोकं जितेन्द्रियः।।2.60.6।।
output: Selfcontrolled Lakshmana, aware of his duty, serves Rama in the forest. By this he is securing his next world.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 60:
विजनेऽपि वने सीता वासं प्राप्य गृहेष्विव। विस्रम्भं लभतेऽभीता रामे सन्न्यस्तमानसा।।2.60.7।।
output: Sita with her mind fixed on Rama is living confidently in that desolate forest without any fear as if it were her home.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 60:
नास्या दैन्यं कृतं किञ्चित्सुसूक्ष्ममपि लक्ष्यते। उचितेव प्रवासानां वैदेही प्रतिभाति मा।।2.60.8।।
output: I could not see even the slightest depression in Sita as if she was accustomed to staying away from home.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
नगरोपवनं गत्वा यथा स्मरमते पुरा। तथैव रमते सीता निर्जनेषु वनेष्वपि।।2.60.9।।
output: Earlier, just as Sita used to revel in the gardens of the city, so does she now in those desolate forests.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
बालेव रमते सीताऽबालचन्द्रनिभानना। रामा रामे ह्यधीनात्मा विजनेऽपि वने सती।।2.60.10।।
output: Charming Sita whose face resembles the full Moon, with her mind fixed on Rama, is enjoying even the desolate forest like a child.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तद्गतं हृदयं ह्यस्यास्तदधीनं च जीवितम्। अयोध्यापि भवेऽत्तस्या रामहीना तदा वनम्।।2.60.11।।
output: अस्याः her, हृदयम् heart, तद्गतम् united with Rama, जीवितं च life also, तदधीनम् under his control, अयोध्यापि even Ayodhya too, रामहीना without Rama, तदा then, तस्याः to her, वनम् forest, भवेत् would have become.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
परिपृच्छति वैदेही ग्रामांश्च नगराणि च। गतिं दृष्ट्वा नदीनां च पादपान्विविधानपि।।2.60.12।। रामं हि लक्ष्मणं वापि पृष्ट्वा जानाति जानकी। अयोध्या क्रोशमात्रे तु विहारमिव संश्रिता।।2.60.13।।
output: Seeing villages, cities, trees of different kinds and courses of rivers, Sita is enquiring from Rama or Lakshmana about them. She feels as though she is sporting in the pleasuregarden just a krosa from Ayodhya.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
परिपृच्छति वैदेही ग्रामांश्च नगराणि च। गतिं दृष्ट्वा नदीनां च पादपान्विविधानपि।।2.60.12।। रामं हि लक्ष्मणं वापि पृष्ट्वा जानाति जानकी। अयोध्या क्रोशमात्रे तु विहारमिव संश्रिता।।2.60.13।।
output: अयोध्या क्रोशमात्रे at the distance of a krosa from Ayodhya, विहारम् pleasuregarden, संश्रिता इव as if sporting, वैदेही Sita, ग्रामांश्च villages, नगराणि च cities,नदीनाम् rivers', गतिं च   courses, विविधान् different kinds of, पादपानपि trees also, दृष्ट्वा seeing, रामम् to Rama, परिपृच्छति enquiring, लक्ष्मणं वापि or Lakshmana, पृष्ट्वा asking, जानाति knowing.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इदमेव स्मराम्यस्यास्सहसैवोपजल्पितम्। कैकेयी संश्रितं वाक्यं नेदानीं प्रतिभाति मा।।2.60.14।।
output: Sita did say something about Kaikeyi, but now I do not remember what.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 60:
ध्वंसयित्वा तु तद्वाक्यं प्रमादात्पर्युपत्स्थितम्। ह्लादनं वचनं सूतो देव्या मधुरमब्रवीत्।।2.60.15।।
output: Diverting the context of what he uttered inadvertently relating to Kaikeyi, the charioteer said pleasing words of consolation to Kausalya.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अध्वना वातवेगेन सम्भ्रमेणाऽऽतपेन च। न विगच्छति वैदेह्याश्चन्द्रांशु सदृशी प्रभा।।2.60.16।।
output: वैदेह्याः Sita's, चन्द्रांशु सदृशी resembling the beams of the Moon, प्रभा lustre, अध्वना on the way, वातवेगेन or by the speed of the wind, सम्भ्रमेण or due to haste, आतपेन च or due to scorching heat also, न विगच्छति does not fade.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सदृशं शतपत्रस्य पूर्णचन्द्रोपमप्रभम्। वदनं तद्वदान्याया वैदेह्या न विकम्पते।।2.60.17।।
output: वदान्यायाः of that munificent, वैदेह्याः Sita, शतपत्रस्य a hundredpetalled lotus, सदृशम् similar to, पूर्णचन्द्रोपमप्रभम् like the splendour of the full Moon, तत् वदनम् that countenance, न विकम्पते does not change at all.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 60:
अलक्तरसरक्ताभावलक्तरसवर्जितौ। अद्यापि चरणौ तस्याः पद्मकोशसमप्रभौ।।2.60.18।।
output: Her feet, now devoid of lacdye, still look red like lac and shine like the lotus bud.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
नूपुरोद्घुष्टहेलेव खेलं गच्छति भामिनी। इदानीमपि वैदेही तद्रागान्नयस्त भूषणा।।2.60.19।।
output: भामिनी damsel (Sita), नूपुरोद्घुष्ट हेलेव tinkling anklets proclaiming dalliance, खेलम् (as if) playing, गच्छति going, वैदेही Sita, इदानीमपि even now, तद्रागात् due to affection for Rama, नयस्तभूषणा cast off the ornaments.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 60:
गजं वा वीक्ष्य सिंहं वा व्याघ्रं वा वनमाश्रिता। नाऽहारयति सन्त्रासं बाहू रामस्य संश्रिता।।2.60.20।।
output: Though in the forest, Sita, under the protection of Rama's arms, is afraid of neither elephants nor lions nor tigers.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 60:
न शोच्यास्ते न चात्मनश्शोच्यो नापि जनाधिपः। इदं हि चरितं लोके प्रतिष्ठास्यति शाश्वतम्।।2.60.21।।
output: You need not lament for them or for yourself or for the king. This story of Rama will endure permanently in the world.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
विधूय शोकं परिहृष्टमानसा महर्षियाते पथि सुव्यवत्स्थिताः। वनेरता वन्यफलाशनाः पितुश्शुभां प्रतिज्ञां परिपालयन्ति ते।।2.60.22।।
output: ते they, शोकम् grief, विधूय shaking off, परिहृष्टमानसाः with cheerful hearts, महर्षियाते  established by maharshis, पथि in the path, सुव्यवत्स्थिताः firmly fixed, वने in the forest, रताः  are enjoying, वन्यफलाशनाः subsisting on forest fruits, पितुः father's, शुभाम् auspicious, प्रतिज्ञाम् promise, परिपालयन्ति are upholding.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 60:
तथापि सूतेन सुयुक्तवादिना निवार्यमाणा सुतशोककर्शिता। न चैव देवी विरराम कूजितात्प्रियेति पुत्रेति च राघवेति च।।2.60.23।।
output: Though Sumantra was speaking with befitting words to prevent Kausalya from weeping over her son which had enfeebled her, she did not stop crying, 'O my beloved', 'O my son', 'O Rama'. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे षष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtieth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
वनं गते धर्मपरे रामे रमयतां वरे। कौसल्या रुदती स्वार्ता भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.61.1।।
output: Kausalya condemns Dasaratha's action -- Dasaratha loses his senses out of intense grief.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 61:
यद्यपि त्रिषु लोकेषु प्रथितं ते महद्यशः। सानुक्रोशो वदान्यश्च प्रियवादी च राघवः।।2.61.2।।
output: Your great fame has spread all over the three worlds. People know you as compassionate, generous and sweetspeaking scion of the Raghus.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कथं नरवरश्रेष्ठ पुत्रौ तौ सह सीतया। दुःखितौ सुखसंवृद्धौ वने दुःखं सहिष्यतः।।2.61.3।।
output: O Dasaratha, the best among kings, how will your two sons and Sita brought up in great comfort now tolerate the hardships of forest life?

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सा नूनं तरुणी श्यामा सुकुमारी सुखोचिता। कथमुष्णं च शीतं च मैथिली प्रसहिष्यते।।2.61.4।।
output: तरुणी young, श्यामा in the prime of life, सुकुमारी delicate, सुखोचिता accustomed to comfort, सा मैथिली that Sita, उष्णं च heat, शीतं च cold, नूनम् surely, कथम् how?, प्रसहिष्यते will bear.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 61:
भुक्त्वाऽशनं विशालाक्षी सूपदं शान्वितं शुभम्। वन्यं नैवारमाहारं कथं सीतोपभोक्ष्यते।।2.61.5।।
output: How can the largeeyed Sita having enjoyed delicious food mixed with condiments and soup now partake the food prepared with wild grains?

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा शुभमनिन्दिता। कथं क्रव्यादसिंहानां शब्दं श्रोष्यत्यशोभनम्।।2.61.6।।
output: How can the blameless Sita, used to the soft sound of songs and musical instruments hear the frightful roars of lions and other carnivorous animals?

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
महेन्द्रध्वजसङ्काशः क्व नु शेते महाभुजः। भुजं परिघसङ्काशमुपधाय महाबलः।।2.61.7।।
output: महेन्द्रध्वजसङ्काशः resembling mighty Indra's banner, महाभुजः longarmed one, महाबलः mighty, परिघसङ्काशम् like a sword, भुजम् arm, उपधाय using as a pillow, क्व where, शेते नु is he sleeping?

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
पद्मवर्णं सुकेशान्तं पद्मनिश्श्वासमुत्तमम्। कदा द्रक्ष्यामि रामस्य वदनं पुष्करेक्षणम्।।2.61.8।।
output: पद्मवर्णम् lotuslike complexion, सुकेशान्तम् having beautiful hairends, पद्मनिश्श्वासम् breath of lotus fragrance, पुष्करेक्षणम् eyes like blue lotus, उत्तमम् excellent, रामस्य वदनम् Rama's countenance, कदा when, द्रक्ष्यामि shall I behold?.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 61:
वज्रसारमयं नूनं हृदयं मे न संशयः। अपश्यन्त्या न तं यद्वै फलतीदं सहस्रधा।।2.61.9।।
output: No doubt my heart must be made of thunderbolt, since unable to see Rama it does not split into a thousand pieces.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यत्त्वयाऽकरुणं कर्म व्यपोह्य मम बान्धवाः। निरस्ताः परिधावन्ति सुखार्हाः कृपणा वने।।2.61.10।।
output: (O king) It is because of your heartless action, my Rama and my relatives who deserve to enjoy pleasures at this age have been banished and are miserably wandering in wilderness.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यदि पञ्चदशे वर्षे राघवः पुनरेष्यति। जह्याद्राज्यं च कोषं च भरतो नोपलक्षयते।।2.61.11।।
output: Even if Rama returns in the fifteenth year, it is unlikely that Bharata will give up the kingdom and royal treasury (in favour of Rama).

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 61:
भोजयन्ति किल श्राद्धे केचित्स्वानेव बान्धवान्। ततः पश्चात्समीक्षन्ते कृतकार्या द्विजर्षभान्।।2.61.12।।
output: Some first feed their own relatives in shraddha ceremony and thereafter look for the best of brahmins to feed.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तत्र ये गुणवन्तश्च विद्वांसश्च द्विजातयः। न पश्चात्तेऽभिमन्यन्ते सुधामपि सुरोपमाः।।2.61.13।।
output: The godlike brahmins who are virtuous and learned will not accept the food after others have partaken even if it is ambrosia.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 61:
ब्राह्मणेष्वपि तृप्तेषु पश्चाद्भोक्तुं द्विजर्षभाः। नाभ्युपैतुमलं प्राज्ञा श्शृङ्गच्छेदमिवर्षभाः।।2.61.14।।
output: The bulls (best) among the wise brahmins would not like to accept the food after it is tasted by other brahmins, just as bulls dislike their horns being shorn.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
एवं कनीयसा भ्रात्रा भुक्तं राज्यं विशाम्पते। भ्राता ज्येष्ठो वरिष्ठश्च किमर्थं नावमंस्यते।।2.61.15।।
output: विशाम्पते O Lord of the world (Dasaratha), एवम् likewise, ज्येष्ठः eldest, वरिष्ठश्च most distinguished one, भ्राता brother, कनीयसा by the younger, भ्रात्रा brother, भुक्तम् enjoyed, राज्यम् kingdom, किमर्थम् why, नावमंस्यते will not disdain.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
न परेणाऽहृतं भक्ष्यं व्याघ्रः खादितुमिच्छति। एवमेतन्नरव्याघ्रः परलीढं न मन्यते।।2.61.16।।
output: व्याघ्रः tiger, परेण by some other animal, आहृतम् procured, भक्ष्यम् food, खादितुम् to eat,        न  इच्छति does not like, एवं in the same way, नरव्याघ्रः the (best) among men (Rama), एतत् परलीढम् enjoyed by others, न मन्यते will not accept.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 61:
हविराज्यं पुरोडाशाः कुशा यूपाश्च खादिराः। नैतानि यातयामानि कुर्वन्ति पुनरध्वरे।।2.61.17।।
output: Havis, sacrificial offerings like ghee, cakes, kusha grass, and sacrificial posts made from khadira wood, once used in the sacrifice cannot be used again.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तथा ह्यात्तमिदं राज्यं हृतसारां सुरामिव। नाभिमन्तुमलं रामो नष्टसोममिवाध्वरम्।।2.61.18।।
output: तथा in the same way, रामः Rama, आत्तम् enjoyed by others, इदं राज्यम् this kingdom, हृतसाराम् its essence taken away, सुरामिव like liquour, नष्टसोमम् like the run out soma juice, अध्वरमिव like a sacrifice, अभिमन्तुम् to accept, नालम् should not.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 61:
न चेमां धर्षणां राम सङ्गच्छेदत्यमर्षणः। दारयेन्मन्दरमपि स हि क्रुद्धश्शितैश्शरैः।।2.61.19।।
output: Rama, highly determined will not suffer this indignity. If enraged, he can split open even mount Mandara with his sharp arrows.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
त्वां तु नोत्सहते हन्तुं महात्मा पितृगौरवात्। ससोमार्कग्रहगणं नभस्ताराविचित्रितम्।।2.61.20।। पातयेद्योदिवं क्रुद्धस्सत्वां न व्यतिवर्तते। प्रक्षोभयेद्वारये द्वा महीं शैलशताचिताम्।।2.61.21।।
output: Out of respect for his father magnanimous Rama is not inclined to kill you. He has not defied the anger, the Sun, the Moon and the sky looking wonderful with stars can be pulled down. He will not even shake or break the earth surrounded by hundreds of mountains.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 61:
त्वां तु नोत्सहते हन्तुं महात्मा पितृगौरवात्। ससोमार्कग्रहगणं नभस्ताराविचित्रितम्।।2.61.20।। पातयेद्योदिवं क्रुद्धस्सत्वां न व्यतिवर्तते। प्रक्षोभयेद्वारये द्वा महीं शैलशताचिताम्।।2.61.21।।
output: Out of respect for his father magnanimous Rama is not inclined to kill you. He has not defied the anger, the Sun, the Moon and the sky looking wonderful with stars can be pulled down. He will not even shake or break the earth surrounded by hundreds of mountains.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 61:
नैवं विधमसत्कारं राघवो मर्षयिष्यति। बलवानिव शार्दूलो वालधेरभिमर्शनम्।।2.61.22।।
output: A powerful tiger will not allow its tail to be twisted. In the same way Rama also will not tolerate an insult of this sort.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 61:
नैतस्य सहिता लोका भयं कुर्युर्महामृथे। अधर्मंत्विह धर्मात्मा लोकं धर्मेण योजयेत्।।2.61.23।।
output: Even if all the worlds were to unite and fight against him, he will not fear. This righteous Rama will reestablish justice in this unrighteous world.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
नन्वसौ काञ्चनैर्बाणैर्महावीर्यो महाभुजः। युगान्त इव भूतानि सागरानपि निर्दहेत्।।2.61.24।।
output: Valiant and mightyarmed Rama, with his golden shafts can annihilate all living beings and oceans like at the time of  deluge everything is consumed in fire.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 61:
स तादृशस्सिंहबलो वृषभाक्षो नरर्षभः। स्वयमेव हतः पित्रा जलजेनात्मजो यथा।।2.61.25।।
output: Such Rama, the best among men, powerful like a lion, with eyes fierce like that of a bull has been destroyed by his own father just as the big fish destroys its own offsprings.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 61:
द्विजातिचरितो धर्मश्शास्त्रदृष्टस्सनातनः। यदि ते धर्मनिरते त्वया पुत्रे विवासिते।।2.61.26।।
output: You have banished your son who is devoted to righteousness. Is it in accordance with the scriptures and the eternal tradition followed by the twiceborn?

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
गतिरेका पतिर्नार्या द्वितीया गतिरात्मजः। तृतीया ज्ञातयो राजंश्चतुर्थी नेह विद्यते।।2.61.27।।
output: राजन् O king, नार्याः for a woman,पतिः husband, एका one, गतिः refuge, आत्मजः son, द्वितीया गतिः second refuge, ज्ञातयः relatives, तृतीया third, चतुर्थी fourth, इह in this world, न विद्यते does not exist.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
एवं तु क्रुद्धया राजा राममात्रा सशोकया। श्रावितः परुषं वाक्यं चिन्तयामास दुःखितः।।2.62.1।।
output: क्रुद्धया in anger, सशोकया afflicted with sorrow, राममात्रा by Rama's mother, एवम् in that way, परुषम् harsh, वाक्यम् words, श्रावितः was forced to hear, राजा king, दुःखितः distressed, चिन्तयामास sadly reflected.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 62:
चिन्तयित्वा स च नृपो मुमोह व्याकुलेन्द्रियः। अथ दीर्घीण कालेन संज्ञामाप परन्तपः।।2.62.2।।
output: The king (Dasaratha) tormentor of enemies, for a while, lost his consciousness, his senses bewildered. After a long time he regained his senses.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 62:
स संज्ञामुपलभ्यैव दीर्घमुष्णं च निश्श्वसन्। कौसल्यां पार्श्वतो दृष्ट्वा पुन श्चिन्तामुपागमत्।।2.62.3।।
output: When he regained his senses, the king heaved deep, hot sighs. Seeing Kausalya by his side he relapsed into a state of anxiety.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तस्य चिन्तयमानस्य प्रत्याभात्कर्म दुष्कृतम्। यदनेन कृतं पूर्वमज्ञानाच्छब्दवेधिना।।2.62.4।।
output: चिन्तयमानस्य as he was thinking, तस्य his, पूर्वम् formerly, अनेन by such, शब्दवेधिना Capable of hitting the target by following the sound, अज्ञानात् without knowledge, यत् which, कृतम् has been committed, दुष्कृतम् sinful, कर्म act, प्रत्यभात् flashed back.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अमनास्तेन शोकेन रामशोकेन च प्रभुः। द्वाभ्यामपि महाराज श्शोकाभ्यामन्वतप्यत।।2.62.5।।
output: The great king, the lord with a broken heart started regretting deeply about both the grievous acts he had committed previously (one is shooting at the son of a sage and the other, banishing Rama).

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 62:
दह्यामान स्सशोकाभ्यां कौसल्यामाह भूपतिः। वेपमानोऽञ्जलिं कृत्वा प्रसादार्थमवाङ्मुखः।।2.62.6।।
output: Consumed by the double sorrow, the king trembling, with head down and folding his hands said to Kausalya in order to appease her:

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
प्रसादये त्वां कौसल्ये रचितोऽयं मयाऽञ्जलिः। वत्सला चानृशंसा च त्वं हि नित्यं परेष्वपि।।2.62.7।।
output: O Kausalya I entreat you with folded palms. Be merciful. Forever affectionate, you are not cruel even towards your enemies.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
भर्ता तु खलु नारीणां गुणवान्निर्गुणोऽपि वा। धर्मं विमृशमानानां प्रत्यक्षं देवि दैवतम्।।2.62.8।।
output: O Devi for women who have regard for righteousness, a husband, whether virtuous or not, is a god incarnate.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सा त्वं धर्मपरा नित्यं दृष्टलोक परावरा। नार्हसे विप्रियं वक्तुं दुखिःताऽपि सुदुःखितम्।।2.62.9।।
output: You always adhere to righteousness. You have seen both the extremes (good and bad) of this world. Athough you yourself are in grief it does not behove you to speak unpleasant words to one who is suffering from a greater grief.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 62:
तद्वाक्यं करुणं राज्ञः श्रुत्वा दीनस्य भाषितम्। कौसल्या व्यसृजद्बाष्पं प्रणालीव नवोदकम्।।2.62.10।।
output: Kausalya heard the pitiable words uttered by the king who was in a wretched condition. She shed tears like a water channel discharging fresh rainwater.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सा मूर्ध्निबध्वा रुदती राज्ञः पद्ममिवाञ्जलिम्। सम्भ्रमादब्रवीत् त्रस्ता त्वरमाणाक्षरं वचः।।2.62.11।।
output: Frightened Kausalya, weeping and raising her palms folded like lotus on to her head,  and charged with emotions said with stumbling syllables:

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
