output: भरतस्य Bharata's, वचः words, श्रुत्वा having heard, शस्त्रपाणयः with weapons in their hands, शूराः valiant, पुरुषाः men, तत् that, वनम् forest, विविशुः entered, ततः then, धूमम् smoke, ददृशुश्च observed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ते समालोक्य धूमाग्रमूचुर्भरतमागताः। नामनुष्ये भवत्यग्नि र्व्यक्तमत्रैव राघवौ।।2.93.22।।
output: ते they, धूमाग्रम् column of smoke, समालोक्य having seen, भरतम् to Bharata, आगताः returned, ऊचुः communicated, अमनुष्ये in a place bereft of men, अग्नि: fire, न भवति  cannot exist, व्यक्तम् clearly, राघवौ Rama and Lakshmana, अत्रैव are here only.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अथ नाऽत्र नरव्याघ्रौ राजपुत्रौ परन्तपौ। अन्ये रामोपमा स्सन्ति व्यक्तमत्र तपस्विनः।।2.93.23।।
output: अथ otherwise, नरव्याघ्रौ tigers among men, परन्तपौ subduers of enemies, राजपुत्रौ princes, अत्र न if they are not here, अत्र here, रामोपमाः resembling Rama, अन्ये other, तपस्विनः सन्ति ascetics are there, व्यक्तम् evident.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतस्तेषां वचनं साधुसम्मतम्। सैन्यानुवाच सर्वांस्तानमित्रबलमर्दनः।।2.93.24।।
output: अमित्रबलमर्दनः who crushes the hostile armies, भरतः Bharata, तेषाम् their, साधुसम्मतम् acceptable to the pious, तत् वचनम् those words, श्रुत्वा having heard, सर्वान् entire, तान् सैन्यान् to that entire army, उवाच said.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यत्ता भवन्तस्तिष्ठन्तु नेतो गन्तव्यमग्रतः। अहमेव गमिष्यामि सुमन्त्रो गुरुरेव च।।2.93.25।।
output: All of you carefully watch here. Do not proceed any further. Sumantra, the preceptor and myself shall go forward.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
एवमुक्ता स्ततस्सर्वे तत्र तस्थुः समन्तः। भरतो यत्र धूमाग्रं तत्र दृष्टिं समादधात्।।2.93.26।।
output: At this command, all of them halted. Then Bharata fixed his gaze on the source of the smoke.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
व्यवस्थिता या भरतेन सा चमूर्निरीक्षमाणाऽपि च भूमिमग्रतः। बभूव हृष्टा न चिरेण जानती प्रियस्य रामस्य समागमं तदा।।2.93.27।।
output: The army thus halted by Bharata, gazing at the space before them rejoiced at the thought that not long before they would rejoin their beloved Rama. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे त्रिनवतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the ninetythird sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
दीर्घकालोषित स्तस्मिन्गिरौ गिरिवनप्रियः। वैदेह्याः प्रियमाकाङ्क्षन्स्वं च चित्तं विलोभयन्।।2.94.1।। अथ दाशरथिश्चित्रं चित्रकूटमदर्शयत्। भार्याममरसङ्काश श्शचीमिव पुरन्दरः।।2.94.2।।
output: अथ thereafter, अमरसङ्काशः one who resembles the gods, गिरिवनप्रियः one fond of mountains and forests, तस्मिन् in that, गिरौ on the mountain, दीर्घकालोषितः who had been living for a long time, दाशरथिः Rama, वैदेह्याः Sita's, प्रियम् pleasure, आकाङ्क्षन् desiring, स्वम् own, चित्तम् mind, विलोभयन् to please, चित्रम् wonderful, चित्रकूटम् Chitrakuta mountain, भार्याम् to his consort, पुरन्दरः Indra (breaker of fortresses), शचीमिव like Sachi, अदर्शयत् showed.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 94:
दीर्घकालोषित स्तस्मिन्गिरौ गिरिवनप्रियः। वैदेह्याः प्रियमाकाङ्क्षन्स्वं च चित्तं विलोभयन्।।2.94.1।। अथ दाशरथिश्चित्रं चित्रकूटमदर्शयत्। भार्याममरसङ्काश श्शचीमिव पुरन्दरः।।2.94.2।।
output: Rama, resembling the gods, who had been living there for long developed a liking for the mountains and forests. With a desire to please Sita and his own mind, he showed her the wonderful Chitrakuta mountain as Indra did to his wife Sachi.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 94:
न राज्याद्भ्रंशनं भद्रे न सुहृद्भिर्विनाभवः। मनो मे बाधते दृष्ट्वा रमणीयमिमं गिरिम्।।2.94.3।।
output: O gentle one, when I behold this lovely mountain, neither the expulsion from the kingdom nor being away from friends pains my mind.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
पश्येममचलं भद्रे नानाद्विजगणायुतम्। शिखरैः खमिवोद्विद्धैर्धातुमद्भिर्विभूषितम्।।2.94.4।।
output: भद्रे O auspicious one, नानाद्विजगणायुतम् abounding in flocks of birds of every kind, खम् the sky, उद्विद्धैरिव as if piercing, धातुमद्भि: with minerals, शिखरैः peaks, विभूषितम् adorned, इमम् this, अचलम् mountain, पश्य you may see.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 94:
केचिद्रजतसङ्काशाः केचित्क्षतजसंनिभाः। पीतमाञ्जिष्टवर्णाश्च केचिन्मणिवरप्रभाः।।2.94.5।। पुष्यार्ककेतकाभाश्च केचिज्ज्योतीरसप्रभाः। विराजन्तेऽचलेन्द्रस्य देशा धातुविभूषिताः।।2.94.6।।
output: This mountain with its peaks is adorned with various minerals. Some of the regions have the radiance of silver and bronze, some look bloodred or maddercrimson, some sparkle like the rarest of gems while others shine like topaz or crystal or a flower of ketaka plant or shimmer like stars and quicksilver.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 94:
केचिद्रजतसङ्काशाः केचित्क्षतजसंनिभाः। पीतमाञ्जिष्टवर्णाश्च केचिन्मणिवरप्रभाः।।2.94.5।। पुष्यार्ककेतकाभाश्च केचिज्ज्योतीरसप्रभाः। विराजन्तेऽचलेन्द्रस्य देशा धातुविभूषिताः।।2.94.6।।
output: This mountain with its peaks is adorned with various minerals. Some of the regions have the radiance of silver and bronze, some look bloodred or maddercrimson, some sparkle like the rarest of gems while others shine like topaz or crystal or a flower of ketaka plant or shimmer like stars and quicksilver.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 94:
नानामृगगणद्वीपितरर्क्ष्वृक्षगणैर्वुतः। अदुष्टैर्भात्ययं शैलो बहुपक्षिसमायुतः।।2.94.7।।
output: This mount Chitrakuta is swarmed by flocks of birds and herds of several kinds of animals like tigers, panthers and bears of every kind giving up their cruel nature.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
आम्रजम्ब्वसनैर्लोध्रैः प्रियालैः पनसैर्धवैः। अङ्कोलैर्भव्यतिनिशैर्बिल्वतिन्दुक वेणुभिः।।2.94.8।। काश्मर्यरिष्टवरुणैर्मधूकैस्तिलकैस्तथा। बदर्यामलकैर्नीपैर्वेत्रधन्वनबीजकैः।।2.94.9।। पुष्पवद्भिः फलोपेतैश्छायावद्भिर्मनोरमैः। एवमादिभिराकीर्णः श्रियं पुष्यत्ययं गिरिः।।2.94.10।।
output: This mountain is spread over with various kinds of flowering trees and trees laden with fruits, shady and enchanting, mango, roseapples, asanas, lodhras, priyalas, jackfruit trees, dhavas, ankolas, lovely tinisas, bilva trees, tinduka and bamboo, kashmaya, arishta and varuna, madhukas, tilaka trees, badari and myrobalan trees, nipa trees, cane, danvas, and promegranate trees, the mountain looks splendid.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
आम्रजम्ब्वसनैर्लोध्रैः प्रियालैः पनसैर्धवैः। अङ्कोलैर्भव्यतिनिशैर्बिल्वतिन्दुक वेणुभिः।।2.94.8।। काश्मर्यरिष्टवरुणैर्मधूकैस्तिलकैस्तथा। बदर्यामलकैर्नीपैर्वेत्रधन्वनबीजकैः।।2.94.9।। पुष्पवद्भिः फलोपेतैश्छायावद्भिर्मनोरमैः। एवमादिभिराकीर्णः श्रियं पुष्यत्ययं गिरिः।।2.94.10।।
output: अयं गिरिः this mountain, पुष्पवद्भिः covered with flowers, फलोपेतैः laden with fruits, छायावद्भिः shady, मनोरमैः enchanting, आम्रजम्ब्वसनैः mango, roseapples, asana trees, लोध्रैः lodhra trees, प्रियालैः priyala trees, पनसैः jackfruit trees, धवैः dhava trees, अङ्कोलैः ankola trees, भव्यतिनिशैः lovely tinisa trees, बिल्वतिन्दुकवेणुभिः bilva trees, tinduka and bamboo, काश्मर्यारिष्टवरुणैः kashmaya, arishta and varuna तथा similarly,मधूकैः madhuka trees, तिलकैः tilaka trees, बदर्यामलकै: badari and myrobalan trees, नीपैः kodamva trees, वेत्रधन्वनबीजकैः cane, danvas, and promegranates, एवमादिभि: with these kinds of trees, आकीर्णः spread over, श्रियम् splendour, पुष्यति enhancing.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
आम्रजम्ब्वसनैर्लोध्रैः प्रियालैः पनसैर्धवैः। अङ्कोलैर्भव्यतिनिशैर्बिल्वतिन्दुक वेणुभिः।।2.94.8।। काश्मर्यरिष्टवरुणैर्मधूकैस्तिलकैस्तथा। बदर्यामलकैर्नीपैर्वेत्रधन्वनबीजकैः।।2.94.9।। पुष्पवद्भिः फलोपेतैश्छायावद्भिर्मनोरमैः। एवमादिभिराकीर्णः श्रियं पुष्यत्ययं गिरिः।।2.94.10।।
output: This mountain is spread over with various kinds of flowering trees and trees laden with fruits, shady and enchanting, mango, roseapples, asanas, lodhras, priyalas, jackfruit trees, dhavas, ankolas, lovely tinisas, bilva trees, tinduka and bamboo, kashmaya, arishta and varuna, madhukas, tilaka trees, badari and myrobalan trees, nipa trees, cane, danvas, and promegranate trees, the mountain looks splendid.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
शैलप्रस्थेषु रम्येषु पश्येमान् रोमहर्षणान्। किन्नरान् द्वन्द्वशो भद्रे रममाणान्मनस्विनः।।2.94.11।।
output: भद्रे O auspicious one, रम्येषु in the beautiful, शैलप्रस्थेषु on the plateau, द्वन्द्वशः in pair, रममाणान् sporting, रोमहर्षणान् thrilling, मनस्विनः highspirited, इमान् these, किन्नरान् kinneras, पश्य behold.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
शाखावसक्तान् खड्गांश्च प्रवराण्यम्बराणि च। पश्य विद्याधरस्त्रीणां क्रीडोद्धेशान्मनोरमान्।।2.94.12।।
output: विद्याधरस्त्रीणाम् by Vidyadhara women, शाखावसक्तान् hanging from the branches, खड्गांश्च  swords, प्रवराणि best, अम्बराणि च garments, मनोरमान् captivating, क्रीडोद्धेशान् sporting retreats, पश्य behold.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 94:
जलप्रपातैरुद्भेदैर्निष्यन्दैश्च क्वचित्क्वचित्। स्रवद्भिर्भात्ययं शैल स्स्रवन्मद इव द्विपः।।2.94.13।।
output: Behold a waterfall here and a fountain there gushing from the earth and in other places, the mountain looks like an elephant rutting ichor.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
गुहासमीरणो गन्धान्नानापुष्पभवान्वहन्। घ्राणतर्पणमभ्येत्य कं नरं न प्रहर्षयेत्।।2.94.14।।
output: The breeze from the caves carrying the fragrance of many flowers is satisfying the sense of smell. Who will not find it delightful?

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यदीह शरदोऽनेकास्त्वया सार्धमनिन्दिते। लक्ष्मणेन च वत्स्यामि न मां शोकः प्रधक्ष्यति।।2.94.15।।
output: अनिन्दिते O flawless one, त्वया with you, लक्ष्मणेन च सार्धम् and in the company Lakshmana, इह here, अनेकाः many, शरदः autumns, वत्स्यामि यदि if I am to live, माम् me, शोकः grief, न प्रधक्ष्यति will not consume.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
बहुपुष्पफले रम्ये नानाद्विजगणायुते। विचित्रशिखरे ह्यस्मिन्रतवानस्मि भामिनि।।2.94.16।।
output: भामिनि O lovely Sita, बहुपुष्पफले laden with abundance of flowers and fruits, नानाद्विजगणायुते flocked by different kinds of birds, विचित्रशिखरे on enchanting mountain peaks, रम्ये delightful, अस्मिन् on this mountain, रतवान् अस्मि हि I am fond of.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 94:
अनेन वनवासेन मया प्राप्तं फलद्वयम्। पितुश्चानृणता धर्मे भरतस्य प्रियं तथा।।2.94.17।।
output: By living in the forest I have achieved a twofold benefitdischarge of debt of my father with regard to righteousness and causing happiness to Bharata.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 94:
वैदेहि रमसे कच्चिच्चित्रकूटे मया सह। पश्यन्ती विविधान्भावान्मनोवाक्कायसम्मतान्।।2.94.18।।
output: O Sita, are you enjoying by being with me here on this Chitrakuta and observing various objects gratifying to the body, mind and speech?

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इदमेवामृतं प्राहू राज्ञि राजर्षयः परे। वनवासं भवार्थाय प्रेत्य मे प्रपितामहाः।।2.94.19।।
output: My greatgrandfathers and ancient royal sages used to say that living in the forest is like enjoying nectar for a king for the best existence after death.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
शिला श्शैलस्य शोभन्ते विशाला श्शतशोऽभितः। बहुला बहुलैर्वर्णैर्नीलपीतसितारुणैः।।2.94.20।।
output: बहुलैः several, नीलपीतसितारुणैः blueblack, yellow, white and red, वर्णैः colours, बहुलाः many, विशालाः massive, शैलस्य mountain's, शिलाः rocks, शतशः in hundreds, अभितः on all sides, शोभन्ते are looking splendid.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
निशिभान्त्यचलेन्द्रस्य हुताशनशिखा इव। ओषध्यः स्वप्रभालक्ष्म्या भ्राजमाना स्सहस्रशः।।2.94.21।।
output: स्वप्रभालक्ष्म्या with the splendour of their own lustre, भ्राजमानाः illuminating, सहस्रशः in thousands, अचलेन्द्रस्य of this lord of the hills (Chitrakuta's), ओषध्यः herbs, निशि in the night, हुताशनशिखा इव like flames of fire, भान्ति shine.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
केचित् क्षयनिभा देशाः केचिदुद्यानसन्निभाः। केचिदेकशिला भान्ति पर्वतस्यास्य भामिनि।।2.94.22।।
output: O lovely Sita Some regions of the mountain look like dwellingplaces, some others are like flowergardens and some are shining like a single rock.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 94:
भित्त्वेव वसुधां भाति चित्रकूटस्समुत्थितः। चित्रकूटस्य कूटोऽसौ दृश्यते सर्वत श्शुभः।।2.94.23।।
output: This Chitrakuta mountain stands erect as if it has arisen by splitting open the earth and its peak looks graceful from every side.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कुष्ठस्थगरपुन्नाग भूर्जपत्रोत्तरच्छदान्। कामिनां स्वास्तरान्पश्य कुशेशयदलायुतान्।।2.94.24।।
output: Behold those excellent couches of lovers spread with leaves of kustha, sthagara, punnaga and bhurja and covered with lotus petals.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
मृदिताश्चापविद्धाश्च दृश्यन्ते कमलस्रजः। कामिभिर्वनिते पश्य फलानि विविधानि च।।2.94.25।।
output: O Lady, behold those lotus garlands crushed and cast aside by lovers and also many fruits (tasted by them and) lying there.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
वस्वौकसारां नलिनीमत्येतीवोत्तरान्कुरून्। पर्वतश्चित्रकूटोऽसौ बहुमूलफलोदकः।।2.94.26।।
output: This Chitrakuta mountain, with abundance of roots, fruits and water surpasses in beauty Vasvaukasara, the capital city of Kubera or Nalini, his celestial garden or the land of Uttarakuru.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इमं तु कालं वनिते विजह्रिवांस्त्वया च सीते सह लक्ष्मणेन च। रतिं प्रपत्स्ये कुलधर्मवर्धनीं सतां पथि स्वैर्नियमैः परैः स्थितः।।2.94.27।।
output: O my beloved Sita, by spending time with you and Lakshmana following the path of the virtuous with utmost restraint and by enhancing the righteousness of my race, I shall obtain great felicity. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे चतुर्नवतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the ninetyfourth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 95:
अथ शैलाद्विनिष्क्रम्य मैथिलीं कोसलेश्वरः। अदर्शयच्छुभजलां रम्यां मन्दाकिनीं नदीम्।।2.95.1।।
output: Then Rama, the lord of Kosala, descended from the mountain and showed Sita the charming river Mandakini of sacred waters.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 95:
अब्रवीच्च वरारोहां चारुचन्द्रनिभाननाम्। विदेहराजस्य सुतां रामो राजीवलोचनः।।2.95.2।।
output: Lotus-eyed Rama said to the heavy-hipped daughter of the king of Videha, whose face resembled the beautiful Moon.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 95:
विचित्रपुलिनां रम्यां हंससारससेविताम्। कमलैरुपसम्पन्नां पश्य मन्दाकिनीं नदीम्।।2.95.3।।
output: Look at this enchanting river Mandakini with its variegated sandbanks frequented by geese and swans and adorned with lotuses.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
नानाविधैस्तीररुहै र्वृतां पुष्पफलद्रुमैः। राजन्तीं राजराजस्य नलिनीमिव सर्वतः।।2.95.4।।
output: See this river sparkling with trees of every kind laden with fruits and flowers growing on its banks. Everywhere it resembles the lake Nalini of Kubera.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
मृगयूथनिपीतानि कलुषाम्भांसि साम्प्रतम्। तीर्थानि रमणीयानि रतिं सञ्जनयन्ति मे।।2.95.5।।
output: The herds of deer have just drunk water by descending down the landing places and the waters are still turbid. This sight produces great pleasure in me.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 95:
जटाजिनधराः काले वल्कलोत्तरवाससः। ऋषय स्त्ववगाहन्ते नदीं मन्दाकिनीं प्रिये।।2.95.6।।
output: O my beloved rishis with matted locks and wearing deer skins and bark of trees as upper cloth bathe in the river Mandakini for performing morning ablutions in time.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
आदित्यमुपतिष्ठन्ते नियमादूर्ध्वबाहवः। एते परे विशालाक्षि मुनय स्संशितव्रताः।।2.95.7।।
output: विशालाक्षि O largeeyed Sita, संशितव्रताः of rigid austerities, एते परे some other, मुनयः ascetics, नियमात् according to tradition, ऊर्ध्वबाहवः lifting up their arms, आदित्यम्  Sungod, उपतिष्ठन्ते are worhipping.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
मारुतोद्धूतशिखरैः प्रनृत्त इव पर्वतः। पादपैः पत्रपुष्पाणि सृजद्भिरभितो नदीम्।।2.95.8।।
output: With the trees whose tops are swayed by the wind, the mountain was as if dancing, shedding leaves and flowers all around the river.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
चिन्मणिनिकाशोदां क्वचित्पुलिनशालिनीम्। क्वचित्सिद्धजनाकीर्णां पश्य मन्दाकिनीं नदीम्।।2.95.9।।
output: Behold this river Mandakini whose waters here are transparent like crystals, there sparkling with sand dunes and elsewhere crowded with siddhas.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 95:
निर्धूतान्वायुना पश्य विततान्पुष्पसञ्चयान्। पोप्लूयमानानपरान्पश्य त्वं जलमध्यगान्।।2.95.10।।
output: Look at the scattered heaps of flowers shaken off by the wind and large quantities of flowers floating on the waters.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तांश्चातिवल्गुवचसो रथाङ्गाह्वयना द्विजाः। अधिरोहन्ति कल्याणि निष्कूजन्त श्शुभा गिरः।।2.95.11।।
output: O my auspicious Sita, sweetvoiced Chakravaka birds singing in most pleasant tones are alighting on those heaps of flowers.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
दर्शनं चित्रकूटस्य मन्दाकिन्याश्च शोभने। अधिकं पुरवासाच्च मन्ये तव च दर्शनात्।।2.95.12।।
output: My lovely Sita, I consider watching this mount Chitrakuta and river Mandakini in your presence more delightful than living in Ayodhya.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
विधूतकलुषै स्सिद्धैस्तपोदमशमान्वितैः। नित्यविक्षोभितजलां विगाहस्व मया सह।।2.95.13।।
output: विधूतकलुषैः cleansed of sins, तपोदमशमान्वितैः endowed with asceticism, selfrestraint and  tranquillity, सिद्धैः with siddhas, नित्यविक्षोभितजलाम् with perpetually agitated waters, मया सह with me, विगाहस्व enter.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सखीवच्च विगाहस्व सीते मन्दाकिनीं नदीम्। कमलान्यवमज्जन्ती पुष्कराणि च भामिनि।।2.95.14।।
output: भामिनि O lovely, सीते Sita, कमलानि red lotuses, पुष्कराणि च white lotuses, अवमज्जन्ती  submerging, सखीवत् like a friend, मन्दाकिनीं नदीम् Mandakini river, विगाहस्व you may enter.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
त्वं पौरजनवद्व्यालानयोध्यामिव पर्वतम्। मन्यस्व वनिते नित्यं सरयूवदिमां नदीम्।।2.95.15।।
output: O my lovely lady Always think this river Mandakini as Sarayu and this mount Chitrakuta as Ayodhya and these wild animals as its inhabitants.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
लक्ष्मणश्चापि धर्मात्मा मन्निदेशे व्यवस्थितः। त्वं चानुकूला वैदेहि प्रीतिं जनयथो मम।।2.95.16।।
output: वैदेहि O Sita, धर्मात्मा righteous, लक्ष्मणश्चापि Lakshmana also, मन्निदेशे at my command, व्यवस्थितः obedient, त्वं च you also, अनुकूला agreeable, मम to me, प्रीतिम् pleasure, जनयथः are causing.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 95:
उपस्पृशंस्त्रिषवणं मधुमूलफलाशनः। नायोध्यायैन राज्याय स्पृहयेऽद्य त्वया सह।।2.95.17।।
output: Bathing thrice in your company at the time of prayers and partaking honey, roots and fruits, I do not yearn either for Ayodhya or for the kingdom.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 95:
इमांहि रम्यां मृगयूथशालिनीं निपीततोयां गजसिंहवानरैः। सुपुष्पितां पुष्पभरैरलङ्कृतां नसोऽस्ति य स्स्यान्न गतक्लम स्सुखी।।2.95.18।।
output: With this enchanting Mandakini teeming with herds of deer, whose waters are drunk by elephants, lions and monkeys, decorated with heaps of flowers fallen from the trees in full bloom, who will not feel happy and free from fatigue.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
इतीव रामो बहुसङ्गतं वचः प्रियासहाय स्सरितं प्रति ब्रुवन्। चचार रम्यं नयनाञ्जनप्रभं स चित्रकूटं रघुवंशवर्धनः।।2.95.19।।
output: रघुवंशवर्धनः perpetuator of Raghu dynasty, सः रामः that Rama, इतीव in this manner, सरितं प्रति about Mandakini river, बहु at length, सङ्गतम् appropriate, वचः words, ब्रुवन् speaking,  प्रियासहायः in the company of his beloved, नयनाञ्जनप्रभम् resembling collyrium in hue, रम्यम् delightful, चित्रकूटम् Chitrakuta, चचार wandered about.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तां तथा दर्शयित्वा तु मैथिलीं गिरिनिम्नगाम्। निषसाद गिरिप्रस्थे सीतां मांसेन छन्दयन्।।2.96.1।।
output: Rama hears the sounds of the army approaching the hermitage -- alerts Lakshmana to make sure -- recognition of the army as that of Bharata's -- Lakshmana mistakes Bharata's intentions.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
इदं मेध्यमिदं स्वादु निष्टप्तमिदमग्निना। एवमास्ते स धर्मात्मा सीतया सह राघवः।।2.96.2।।
output: धर्मात्मा righteous, स राघवः that Rama, इदम् this, मेध्यम् sacred meat, इदम् this, स्वादु is savoury, इदम् this one, अग्निना with fire, निष्टप्तम् roasted, एवम् uttering this way, सीतया सह in the company of Sita, आस्ते was seated.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तथा तत्राऽसतस्तस्य भरतस्यौपयायिनः। सैन्यरेणुश्च शब्दश्च प्रादुरास्तां नभस्पृशौ।।2.96.3।।
output: तथा thus, तस्य that Rama, तत्र there, आसतः while sitting, उपयायिनः approaching, भरतस्य Bharata's, सैन्यरेणुश्च dust raised by the army, शब्दश्च and tumult, नभस्पृशौ both reaching the sky, प्रादुरास्ताम् was generated.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 96:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे त्रस्ता श्शब्देन महता ततः। अर्दिता यूथपा मत्ता स्सयूथा दुद्रुवुर्दिशः।।2.96.4।।
output: Meanwhile, the mighty leaders of the elephantherds were agitated, and frightened by the loud noise, fled away from there in different directions.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स तं सैन्यसमुद्धूतं शब्दं शुश्राव राघवः। तां श्च विप्रद्रुतान्सर्वान्यूथपानन्ववैक्षत।।2.96.5।।
output: सः राघवः that Rama, सैन्यसमुद्बूतम् generated by the army, तं शब्दम् that sound, शुश्राव heard, विप्रद्रुतान् fleeing, तान् those, सर्वान् all, यूथपान् च leaders of herds, अन्ववैक्षत saw.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तांश्च विद्रुवतो दृष्ट्वा तं च श्रुत्वा च निस्वनम्। उवाच राम स्सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणं दीप्ततेजसम्।।2.96.6।।
output: रामः Rama, विद्रुवतः running, तान् them, दृष्ट्वा having seen, तम् them, निस्वनं also sound, श्रुत्वा having heard, दीप्ततेजसम् blazing with energy, सौमित्रिम् son of Sumitra, लक्ष्मणम् addressing Lakshmana, उवाच said.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
हन्त लक्ष्मण पश्येह सुमित्रासुप्रजास्त्वया। भीमस्तनितगम्भीरस्तुमुलः श्रूयते स्वनः।।2.96.7।।
output: हन्त Oh what a wonder, लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, सुमित्रा Sumitra, त्वया by you, सुप्रजाः has a worthy son, इह here, भीमस्तनितगम्भीरः fearful rumbling of clouds, तुमुलः tumultous, स्वनः sound, इह here, श्रूयते is being heard, पश्य see.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
गजयूथानि वाऽरण्ये महिषा वा महावने। वित्रासिता मृगा स्सिंहै स्सहसा प्रद्रुता दिशः।।2.96.8।।
output: अरण्ये in the forest, गजयूथानि herds of elephants, महावने in the great woods, महिषाः वा buffaloes, मृगाः wild beasts, वित्रासिताः frightened, सिंहैः by lions, सहसा quickly, दिशः in directions, प्रद्रुताः running.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 96:
राजा वा राजपुत्रो वा मृगयामटते वने। अन्यद्वा श्वापदं किञ्चित्सौमित्रे ज्ञातुमर्हसि।।2.96.9।।
output: O Lakshmana, do ascertain if any king or prince has come for hunting or whether any ferocious animal has entered this forest, shouldn't you?

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सुदुश्चरो गिरिश्चायं पक्षिणामपि लक्ष्मण। सर्वमेतद्यथातत्त्वमचिरात् ज्ञातुमर्हसि।।2.96.10।।
output: लक्ष्मण O Lakshmana, अयम् this, गिरिः mountain, पक्षिणामपि even to birds, सुदुश्चरः is highly inaccessible, एतत् सर्वम् all this, यथातत्त्वम् exactly, अचिरात् quickly, ज्ञातुम् to know, अर्हसि ought to.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स लक्ष्मण स्सन्त्वरित स्सालमारुह्य पुष्पितम्। प्रेक्षमाणो दिश स्सर्वाः पूर्वां दिशमुदैक्षत।।2.96.11।।
output: Lakshmana hurriedly climbed a flowering sala tree, surveyed in all directions and fixed his gaze on the east.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
उदङ्मुखः प्रेक्षमाणो ददर्श महतीं चमूम्। रथाश्वगजसम्बाधां यत्तैर्युक्तां पदातिभिः।।2.96.12।।
output: Turning his face to the north, he beheld a vast army consisting of chariots, elephants and horses and a wellequipped infantry.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तामश्वगजसम्पूर्णां रथध्वजविभूषिताम्। शशंस सेनां रामाय वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्।।2.96.13।।
output: अश्वगजसम्पूर्णाम् full of horses and elephants, रथध्वजविभूषिताम् decorated with chariotbannars, तां सेनाम् of the army, रामाय to Rama, शशंस informed, इदम् these, वचनं च words also, अब्रवीत् said.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अग्निं संशमयत्वार्य स्सीता च भजतां गुहाम्। सज्यं कुरुष्व चापं च शरांश्च कवचं तथा।।2.96.14।।
output: आर्यः O noble one, अग्निम् sacredfires (Agnihotra), संशमयतु put off, सीता च Sita also, गुहाम् cave, भजताम् let take refuge, चापम् bow, सज्यम् with string, कुरुष्व make ready, तथा so also, शरांश्च arrows also, कवचम् armour (put on).

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तं रामः पुरुषव्याघ्रो लक्ष्मणं प्रत्युवाच ह। अङ्गावेक्षस्व सौमित्रे कस्येमां मन्यसे चमूम्।।2.96.15।।
output: Rama the best among men replied to Lakshamana, Oh, Lakshmana, look properly and tell me to whom do you think this army might belong

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 96:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण लक्ष्मणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। दिधक्षन्निव तां सेनां रुषितः पावको यथा।।2.96.16।।
output: Hearing the words of Rama, enraged Lakshmana, like a flaming fire as if he would reduce the army to ashes, replied:

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 96:
सम्पन्नं राज्यमिच्छंस्तु व्यक्तं प्राप्याभिषेचनम्। आवां हन्तुं समभ्येति कैकेय्या भरतस्सुतः।।2.96.17।।
output: It is evident that Kaikeyi's son Bharata, who has been consecrated, is coming to slay both of us desiring the prosperous kingdom (to be without obstacles).

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
एष वै सुमहाञ्छ्रीमान्विटपी सम्प्रकाशते। विराजत्युद्गतस्कन्धं कोविदारध्वजो रथे।।2.96.18।।
output: एषः this, सुमहान् lofty, श्रीमान् majestic, उद्गतस्कन्धः atop with large trunk, विटपी tree, सम्प्रकाशते रथे on chariot, कोविदारध्वजः with his standard bearing the emblem of Kovidara tree, विराजति shining brilliantly.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
असौ हि सुमहास्कन्धो विटपी च महाद्रुमः। विराजते महासैन्ये कोविदारध्वजो रथे।।2.96.19।।
output: सुमहास्कन्धः of very large trunk, विटपी च spread with many branches, असौ this, महाद्रुमः large tree, कोविदारध्वजः standard of Kovidara, रथे on chariot, महासैन्ये in large army, विराजते is shining brilliantly.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
भजन्त्येते यथाकाममश्वानारुह्य शीघ्रगान्। एते भ्राजन्ति संहृष्टा गजानारुह्य सादिनः।।2.96.20।।
output: These men mounted on swiftlymoving horses are following the post. The riders of elephants  mounted on the elephants look cheerful.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 96:
गृहीतधनुषौ चावां गिरिं वीर श्रयावहै। अथवेहैव तिष्ठाव स्सन्नद्धावुद्यतायुधौ।।2.96.21।।
output: O mighty warrior, let both of us take up the bows and station ourselves on this mountain or we shall stay here itself armed with weapons fully prepared for the battle.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अपि नौ वशमागच्छेत्कोविदारध्वजो रणे। अपि द्रक्ष्यामि भरतं यत्कृते व्यसनं महत्।।2.96.22।। त्वया राघव सम्प्राप्तं सीतया च मया तथा।
output: राघव O Rama, रणे in battle, कोविदारध्वजः Kovidara banner, नौ our, वशम् possession, अप्यागच्छेत् will it come, यत्कृते on whose account, त्वया by you, सीतया by Sita, तथा also, मया च by me, महत् great, व्यसनम् calamity, सम्प्राप्तम् has befallen, such, भरतम् Bharata, अपि द्रक्ष्यामि can I see.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 96:
यन्निमित्तं भवान्राज्याच्छ्युतो राघव शाश्वतात्।।2.96.23।। सम्प्राप्तोऽयमरिर्वीर भरतो वध्य एव मे।
output: O that mighty warrior Bharata, on whose account you have been banished from the perpetual kingdom, comes here as a foe and as for me, he deserves to be slain.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
भरतस्य वधे दोषं नाहं पश्यामि राघव। पूर्वापकारिणं हत्वा न ह्यधर्मेण युज्यते।।2.96.24।।
output: राघव O Rama, भरतस्य Bharta's, वधे in slaying, अहम् I, दोषम्  wrong, न पश्यामि do not see, पूर्वापकारिणम् one who has done harmful act earlier, हत्वा in slaying, अधर्मेण with unrighteousness, न युज्यते is not attached.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
पूर्वापकारी भरतस्त्यक्तधर्मश्च राघव। एतस्मिन्निहते कृत्स्नामनुशाधि वसुन्धराम्।।2.96.25।।
output: राघव O Rama, भरतः Bharata, पूर्वापकारी had done harm earlier, त्यक्तधर्मश्च abandoned righteousness, एतस्मिन् when such a person, निहते after having been slain कृत्स्नाम् the whole, वसुन्धराम् earth, अनुशाधि you shall rule.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अद्य पुत्रं हतं संख्ये कैकेयी राज्यकामुका। मया पश्येत्सुदुःखार्ता हस्तिभग्नमिव द्रुमम्।।2.96.26।।
output: Let that Kaikeyi, greedy for the kingdom, see in great anguish her son who shall be slain by me today in a battle like a tree felled by an elephant.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कैकेयीं च वधिष्यामि सानुबन्धां सबान्धवाम्। कलुषेणाद्य महता मेदिनी परिमुच्यताम्।।2.96.27।।
output: सानुबन्धाम् with her attendants, सबान्धवाम् with her relations, कैकेयीं च also Kaikeyi, वधिष्यामि will slay, अद्य today, मेदिनी the earth, महता by a great, कलुषेण of the sin, परिमुच्यताम् let it  be cleansed.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अद्येमं संयतं क्रोधमसत्कारं च मानद। मोक्ष्यामि शत्रुसैन्येषु कक्षेष्विव हुताशनम्।।2.96.28।।
output: O protector of honour, today I shall vent my suppressed anger and dishonour on the enemy's army like a fire on the thicket.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अद्यैतच्छित्रकूटस्य काननं निशितै श्शरैः। छिन्दञ्चत्रुशरीराणि करिष्ये शोणितोक्षितम्।।2.96.29।।
output: Today I shall rend the bodies of enemies with my sharpened arrows and spatter the forest of Chitrakuta mountain with their blood.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
शरैर्निर्भिन्नहृदयान्कुञ्जरांस्तुरगांस्तथा। श्वापदाः परिकर्षन्तु नरांश्च निहतान्मया।।2.96.30।।
output: Let the wild beasts drag away the elephants, horses and men to be killed by me with their hearts transfixed with my arrows.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 96:
शराणां धनुषश्चाहमनृणोऽस्मिन्महावने। ससैन्यं भरतं हत्वा भविष्यामि न संशयः।।2.96.31।।
output: Having slain Bharata and his army in this great forest, I shall doubtless discharge my debt to my arrows and bow. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे षण्णवतितमस्सर्गः। Thus ends the ninetysixth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सुसंरब्धं तु सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणं क्रोधमूर्छितम्। रामस्तु परिसान्त्व्याथ वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्।।2.97.1।।
output: Rama's correction of Lakshmana's judgement -- Bharata's army encamped round Chitrakuta.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
किमत्र धनुषा कार्यमसिना वा सचर्मणा। महेष्वासे महाप्राज्ञे भरते स्वयमागते।।2.97.2।।
output: महेष्वासे of great strength, महाप्राज्ञे sagacious, भरते Bharata, स्वयम् himself, अत्र here, आगते has come, धनुषा with bow, सचर्मणा with shield, असिना वा or with sword, किं कार्यम् where is the need?

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
पितुस्सत्यं प्रतिश्रुत्य हत्वा भरतमागतम्। किं करिष्यामि राज्येन सापवादेन लक्ष्मण।।2.97.3।।
output: O Lakshmana, having sworn that I would make father's word true, what shall I do with the kingdom earned slanderously by slaying Bharata who has come (to see me)?

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यद्द्रव्यं बान्धवानां वा मित्राणां वा क्षये भवेत्। नाहं तत्प्रतिगृह्णीयां भक्षान्विषकृतानिव।।2.97.4।।
output: I shall never accept any wealth obtained by destroying kith and kin or friends which is akin to taking food prepared with poison.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
धर्ममर्थं च कामं च पृथिवीं चापि लक्ष्मण। इच्छामि भवतामर्थे एतत् प्रतिशृणोमि ते।।2.97.5।।
output: O Lakshmana, on the oath of righteousness, I wish wealth and pleasure as well as this kingdom for the sake of you all.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
भ्रात्रूणां संग्रहार्थं च सुखार्थं चापि लक्ष्मण। राज्यमप्यहमिच्छामि सत्येनाऽयुधमालभे।।2.97.6।।
output: O Lakshmana, I desire this kingdom only for the unity and happiness of my brothers. I swear on the weapon I hold.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
नेयं मम मही सौम्य दुर्लभा सागराम्बरा। न हीच्छेयमधर्मेण शक्रत्वमपि लक्ष्मण।।2.97.7।।
output: सौम्य O gentle, लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, सागराम्बरा with the sea as garment, इयम् this, मही earth, मम to me, दुर्लभा difficult, न not, अधर्मेण unrighteously, शक्रत्वमपि even Indrahood, न इच्छेयं हि I do not desire.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 97:
यद्विना भरतं त्वां च शत्रुघ्नं चापि मानद। भवेन्मम सुखं किञ्चिद्भस्म तत्कुरुतां शिखी।।2.97.8।।
output: O protector of honour even if there were to be some happiness which I could enjoy without you, Bharata, and Satrughna, let it be reduced to ashes by fire.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
मन्येऽहमागतोऽयोध्यां भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः। मम प्राणात्प्रियतरः कुलधर्ममनुस्मरन्।।2.97.9।। श्रुत्वा प्रव्राजितं मां हि जटावल्कलधारिणम्। जानक्यासहितं वीर त्वया च पुरुषर्षभ।।2.97.10।। स्नेहेनाऽक्रान्तहृदय श्शोकेनाकुलितेन्द्रियः। द्रष्टुमभ्यागतो ह्येष भरतो नान्यथाऽगतः।।2.97.11।।
output: O best among men, O valiant one I think Bharata who is affectionate towards his brothers and who is dearer to me than my life, must have returned to Ayodhya and has heard that I had been exiled along with you and Janaki, wearing barks and matted locks. Remembering the duties of the race with an afflicted mind and with agitated senses he has come here to see me. He has not come with any other intention.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
मन्येऽहमागतोऽयोध्यां भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः। मम प्राणात्प्रियतरः कुलधर्ममनुस्मरन्।।2.97.9।। श्रुत्वा प्रव्राजितं मां हि जटावल्कलधारिणम्। जानक्यासहितं वीर त्वया च पुरुषर्षभ।।2.97.10।। स्नेहेनाऽक्रान्तहृदय श्शोकेनाकुलितेन्द्रियः। द्रष्टुमभ्यागतो ह्येष भरतो नान्यथाऽगतः।।2.97.11।।
output: O best among men, O valiant one I think Bharata who is affectionate towards his brothers and who is dearer to me than my life, must have returned to Ayodhya and has heard that I had been exiled along with you and Janaki, wearing barks and matted locks. Remembering the duties of the race with an afflicted mind and with agitated senses he has come here to see me. He has not come with any other intention.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 97:
मन्येऽहमागतोऽयोध्यां भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः। मम प्राणात्प्रियतरः कुलधर्ममनुस्मरन्।।2.97.9।। श्रुत्वा प्रव्राजितं मां हि जटावल्कलधारिणम्। जानक्यासहितं वीर त्वया च पुरुषर्षभ।।2.97.10।। स्नेहेनाऽक्रान्तहृदय श्शोकेनाकुलितेन्द्रियः। द्रष्टुमभ्यागतो ह्येष भरतो नान्यथाऽगतः।।2.97.11।।
output: O best among men, O valiant one I think Bharata who is affectionate towards his brothers and who is dearer to me than my life, must have returned to Ayodhya and has heard that I had been exiled along with you and Janaki, wearing barks and matted locks. Remembering the duties of the race with an afflicted mind and with agitated senses he has come here to see me. He has not come with any other intention.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अम्बां च कैकयीं रुष्य परुषं चाप्रियं वदन्। प्रसाद्य पितरं श्रीमार्नाज्यं मे दातुमागतः।।2.97.12।।
output: Auspicious Bharata, angry with Kaikeyi and having spoken to her unpleasant, bitter words and having propitiated our father, has come here to offer me the kingdom.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
प्राप्तकालं यदेषोऽस्मान्भरतो द्रष्टुमिच्छति। अस्मासु मनसाऽप्येष नाप्रियं किञ्चिदाचरेत्।।2.97.13।।
output: एषः भरतः this Bharata, अस्मान् us, यत् द्रष्टुम् इच्छति should he desire to see, प्राप्तकालम् this is appropriate time, एषः he, अस्मासु in us, मनसा अपि even by thought, किंचित् even a little, अप्रियम् harm, नाचरेत् will not do.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
विप्रियं कृतपूर्वं ते भरतेन कदा नु किम्। ईदृशं वा भयं तेऽद्य भरतं योऽत्र शङ्कसे।।2.97.14।।
output: अत्र here, यः such you, अद्य now, भरतम् about Bharata, शङ्कसे you suspect, ते to you, भरतेन by Bharata, कदा नु at any time anything, किम् विप्रियम् anything disagreeable, ईदृशम् such, भयं वा or fear, कृतपूर्वम् has been done in the past.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 97:
न हि ते निष्ठुरं वाच्यो भरतो नाप्रियं वचः। अहं ह्यप्रियमुक्त स्स्यां भरतस्याप्रिये कृते।।2.97.15।।
output: You must not speak any harsh or unpleasant words against Bharata. If you do, they will be deemed to be directed against me.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कथं नु पुत्राः पितरं हन्युः कस्यां चिदापदि। भ्राता वा भ्रातरं हन्यात्सौमित्रे प्राणमात्मनः।।2.97.16।।
output: Whatever be the calamity, O Lakshmana, how will sons slay their father, or a brother kill his own brother who is as dear to him as his own life?

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यदि राज्यस्य हेतोस्त्वमिमां वाचं प्रभाषसे। वक्ष्यामि भरतं दृष्ट्वा राज्यमस्मै प्रदीयताम्।।2.97.17।।
output: राज्यस्य हेतोः for the sake of a  kingdom, त्वम् you, इमां वाचम् these words, प्रभाषसे यदि if you are saying  भरतम् Bharata, दृष्टवा seeing, अस्मै for him, राज्यम् kingdom, प्रदीयताम् be given, वक्ष्यामि I shall tell.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 97:
उच्यमानोऽपि भरतो मया लक्ष्मण तद्वचः। राज्यमस्मै प्रयच्छेति बाढमित्येव वक्ष्यति।।2.97.18।।
output: O Lakshmana if I earnestly exhort Bharata to offer this kingdom to you, then on hearing those words, he would say, 'Certainly so'.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 97:
तथोक्तो धर्मशीलेन भ्रात्रा तस्य हिते रतः। लक्ष्मणः प्रविवेशेव स्वानि गात्राणि लज्जया।।2.97.19।।
output: Having heard the words uttered by his brother, Rama of virtuous disposition, Lakshmana who was devoted to his brother's welfare, shrank.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 97:
तद्वाक्यं लक्ष्मण श्श्रुत्वा व्रीलितः प्रत्युवाच ह। त्वां मन्ये द्रष्टुमायातः पिता दशरथ स्स्वयम्।।2.97.20।।
output: Hearing the words of Rama, Lakshmana was abashed and said I think it is our father, king Dasaratha who has come here personally to see you.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
व्रीलितं लक्ष्मणं दृष्ट्वा राघवः प्रत्युवाच ह। एष मन्ये महाबाहुरिहास्मान्द्रष्टुमागतः।।2.97.21।।
output: Observing Lakshmana's abashment, Rama said I think the mightyarmed king Dasaratha has come to see all of us here.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अथवा नौ ध्रुवं मन्ये मन्यमान स्सुखोचितौ। वनवासमनुध्याय गृहाय प्रतिनेष्यति।।2.97.22।।
output: अथवा or rather, नौ both of us, सुखोचितौ accustomed to comforts, मन्यमानः treating, वनवासम् dwelling in the forest, अनुध्याय having thought of, गृहाय to home, प्रतिनेष्यति take back, ध्रुवम् this is certain, मन्ये I think.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
इमां वाप्येष वैदेहीमत्यन्तसुखसेविनीम्। पिता मे राघव श्श्रीमान्वनादादाय यास्यति।।2.97.23।।
output: मे पिता my father, श्रीमान् prosperous, एषः राघवः this Raghava, अत्यन्त सुखसेविनीम् brought up in every luxury, इमाम् this lady, वैदेहीम् वा or princess Vaidehi, वनात् from the forest, आदाय यास्यति will take her back.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 97:
एतौ तौ सम्प्रकाशेते गोत्रवन्तौ मनोरमौ। वायुवेगसमौ वीर जवनौ तुरगोत्तमौ।।2.97.24।।
output: O valiant warrior, you can see those two splendid horses of high pedigree, charming, swift and equal to wind in speed are shining (in the army).

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स एष सुमहाकायः कम्पते वाहिनीमुखे। नागश्शत्रुञ्जयो नाम वृद्धस्तातस्य धीमतः।।2.97.25।।
output: सुमहाकायः huge, शत्रुञ्जयः named Satrunjaya, धीमतः of the sagacious, तातस्य father's, सः that, वृद्धः aged, नागः elephant, एषः here it is, वाहिनीमुखे at the head of the army, कम्पते moving about.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 97:
न तु पश्यामि तच्छत्रं पाण्डुरं लोकसत्कृतम् | पितुर्दिव्यं महाबाहो संशयो भवतीह मे।।2.97.26।।
output: I do not see, O long-armed one! that splendid white canopy of my father, well-respected by men. And this gives rise to doubts in my mind.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
वृक्षाग्रादवरोह त्वं कुरु लक्ष्मण मद्वचः। इतीव रामो धर्मात्मा सौमित्रिं तमुवाच ह।।2.97.27।।
output: लक्ष्मण O Lakshmana, त्वम् you, वृक्षाग्रात् from the tree top, अवरोह climb down, मद्वचः my words, कुरु follow, इतीव thus, धर्मात्मा the righteous one, रामः Rama, तं सौमित्रम् to that Lakshmana, उवाच ह said.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अवतीर्य तु सालाग्रात्तस्मात्स समितिञ्जयः। लक्ष्मणः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा तस्थौ रामस्य पार्श्वतः।।2.97.28।।
output: समितिञ्जयः conqueror of the enemy, सः लक्ष्मणः that Lakshmana, तस्मात् सालाग्रात् from the top of that sala tree, अवतीर्य having descended, प्राञ्जलिः भूत्वा with folded palms, रामस्य Rama's, पार्श्वतः by the side of, तस्थौ stood.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
भरतेनापि सन्दिष्टा सम्मर्दो न भवेदिति। समन्तात्तस्य शैलस्य सेना वासमकल्पयत्।।2.97.29।।
output: सम्मर्दः crowding, न भवेत् let it not happen, इति thus, भरतेनापि by Bharata also, सन्दिष्टा instructed, सेना army, तस्य शैलस्य that mountain's, समन्तात् around, आवासम् encampment, अकल्पयत् made.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 97:
अध्यर्धमिक्ष्वाकुचमूर्योजनं पर्वतस्य सा। पार्श्वे न्यविशदावृत्य गजवाजिरथाकुला।।2.97.30।।
output: Bharata's army full of horses, elephants and chariots covering a distance of more than one and a half yojanas encamped by the side of the mountain.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 97:
सा चित्रकूटे भरतेन सेना धर्मं पुरस्कृत्य विधूय दर्पम्। प्रसादनार्थं रघुनन्दनस्य विराजते नीतिमता प्रणीता।।2.97.31।।
output: The army brought by Bharata, the great moralist, was shining around Chitrakuta mountain following dharma, and casting off all pride, in order to please Rama. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तनवतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the ninetyseventh sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
निवेश्य सेनां तु विभुः पद्भ्यां पादवतां वरः। अभिगन्तुं स काकुत्थ्समियेष गुरुवर्तकम्।।2.98.1।।
output: विभुः the lord, पादवताम् among the bipeds, वरः best, सः that Bharata, सेनाम् army, निवेश्य after encamping, गुरुवर्तकम् devoted the preceptor (father), काकुत्थ्सम् Rama, पद्भ्याम् on foot, अभिगन्तुम् to approach, इयेष wished.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
निविष्टमात्रे सैन्ये तु यथोद्देशं विनीतवत्। भरतो भ्रातरं वाक्यं शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.98.2।।
output: सैन्ये army, यथोद्देशम् in assigned places, निविष्टमात्रे after encamping, भरतः Bharata, भ्रातरम् brother, शत्रुघ्नम् to Satrughna, इदम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 98:
क्षिप्रं वनमिदं सौम्य नरसङ्घै स्समन्ततः। लुब्धैश्च सहितैरेभि स्त्वमन्वेषितुमर्हसि।।2.98.3।।
output: O dear Satrughna, you should explore this forest quickly along with groups of our people and  hunters as well.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
गुहो ज्ञातिसहस्रेण शरचापासिधारिणा। समन्वेषतु काकुत्स्थमस्मिन् परिवृतस्स्वयम्।।2.98.4।।
output: गुहः Guha, शरचापासिधारिणा armed with bows, arrows and swords, ज्ञातिसहस्रेण with a thousand kinsmen, परिवृतः surrounded by, स्वयम् himself, अस्मिन् in this forest, काकुत्स्थम् Rama, समन्वेषतु explore.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अमात्यै स्सह पौरैश्च गुरुभिश्च द्विजातिभिः। वनं सर्वं चरिष्यामि पद्भ्यां परिवृत स्स्वयम्।।2.98.5।।
output: स्वयम् I myself, अमात्यैः सह with counsellors, पौरैश्च with citizens, गुरुभिश्च with preceptors, द्विजातिभिः with brahmins, परिवृतः surrounded by, सर्वम् entire, वनम् forest, पद्भ्याम् on foot, चरिष्यामि I shall move about.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यावन्न रामं द्रक्ष्यामि लक्ष्मणं वा महाबलम्। वैदेहीं च महाभागां न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति।।2.98.6।।
output: 'I shall not rest in peace until I see Rama, powerful Lakshmana and illustrious princess of Videha (Sita).

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 98:
यावन्न चन्द्रसङ्काशं द्रक्ष्यामि शुभमाननम्। भ्रातुः पद्मपलाशाक्षं न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति।।2.98.7।।
output: I shall not attain peace until I see my brother, Rama whose auspicious countenance looks radiant as the Moon and whose eyes as lotuspetals.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यावन्न चरणौ भ्रातुः पार्थिवव्यञ्जनान्वितौ। शिरसा धारयिष्यामि न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति।।2.98.8।।
output: भ्रातुः brother's, पार्थिवव्यञ्जनान्वितौ bearing the signs of royalty, चरणौ feet, यावत् till such time, शिरसा with the head, न धारयिष्यामि I will not carry, मे to me, शान्ति: peace, न भविष्यति  shall not come.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यावन्न राज्ये राज्यार्हः पितृपैतामहे स्थितः। अभिषेकजलक्लिन्नो न मे शान्तिर्भविष्यति।।2.98.9।।
output: राज्यार्हः one who is worthy of this kingdom, अभिषेकजलक्लिन्नः wet with the holy waters of consecration, पितृपैतामहे pertaining to our father and forefathers, राज्ये in the kingdom, यावत् till such time, न स्थितः is not established, मे my, शान्तिः peace, न भविष्यति shall not attain.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सिद्धार्थः खलु सौमित्रिर्यश्चन्द्रविमलोपमम्। मुखं पश्यति रामस्य राजीवाक्षं महाद्युति।।2.98.10।।
output: यः who, चन्द्रविमलोपमम् like the spotless Moon, राजीवाक्षम् whose eyes resemble red lotuses, महाद्युति of great effulgence, रामस्य Rama's, मुखम् countenance, पश्यति beholds, सौमित्रिः Lakshmana, सिद्दार्थः खलु blessed indeed.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कृतकृत्या महाभागा वैदेही जनकात्मजा। भर्तारं सागरान्तायाः पृथिव्या यानुगच्छति।।2.98.11।।
output: Sita, the illustrious daughter of Janaka and princess of Videha, has accomplished her purpose by following Rama, the lord of this earth bounded by the ocean.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सुभगश्चित्रकूटोऽसौ गिरिराजोपमो गिरिः। यस्मिन्वसति काकुत्स्थः कुबेर इव नन्दने।।2.98.12।।
output: काकुत्स्थ: Rama, यस्मिन् on which, कुबेरः Kubera, the lord of wealth, नन्दने इव like in the Nandana garden, वसति staying, असौ such, गिरिराजोपमः comparable to the king of the mountains, Himavan, चित्रकूटः गिरिः Chitrakuta mountain, सुभगः is fortunate.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कृतकार्यमिदं दुर्गं वनं व्यालनिषेवितम्। यदध्यास्ते महातेजा राम श्शस्त्रभृतां वरः।।2.98.13।।
output: Fortunate is this inaccessible forest which is inhabited by wild animals to have become the dwelling place of the most radiant Rama, the foremost among the wielders of weapons.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 98:
एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा भरतः पुरषर्षभः। पद्भ्यामेव महाबाहुः प्रविवेश महाद्वनम्।।2.98.14।।
output: Having said thus, the best of men, mightyarmed and highly energetic Bharata entered the great forest on foot.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स तानि द्रुमजालानि जातानि गिरिसानुषु। पुष्पिताग्राणि मध्येन जगाम वदतां वरः।।2.98.15।।
output: वदताम् among the eloquent, वर: best, सः that, गिरिसानुषु on mountain slopes, जातानि growing, पुष्पिताग्राणि tops of trees in bloom, तानि those, द्रुमजालानि मध्येन through the midst of multitude of trees, जगाम went.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स गिरेश्चित्रकूटस्य सालमासाद्य पुष्पितम्। रामाश्रमगतस्याग्नेर्ददर्श ध्वजमुच्छ्रितम्।।2.98.16।।
output: सः that, चित्रकूटस्य गिरेः atop Chitrakuta mountain, पुष्पितम् flowering, सालम् sala trees, असाद्य having reached, रामाश्रमगतस्य in Rama's hermitage, अग्नेः of the burning fire, उच्छ्रितं lofty, ध्वजम् banner of smoke, ददर्श beheld.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 98:
तं दृष्ट्वा भरत श्रीमान्मुमोद सह बान्धवः। अत्र राम इति ज्ञात्वा गतः पारमिवाम्भसः।।2.98.17।।
output: On seeing the smoke, majestic Bharata in the company of relatives concluded that Rama was staying there and rejoiced like a man who had reached the other bank of the river.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 98:
स चित्रकूटे तु गिरौ निशम्यव रामाश्रमं पुण्यजनोपपन्नम्। गुहेन सार्धं त्वरितो जगाम पुनर्निवेश्यैव चमूं महात्मा।।2.98.18।।
output: Having heard of Rama's hermitage on the Chitrakuta mountain inhabited by pious men, magnanimous Bharata, commanded his army to stay at a distance, and quickly proceeded with Guha. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टनवतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the ninetyeighth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
निविष्टायां तु सेनायामुत्सुको भरतस्तदा। जगाम भ्रातरं द्रष्टुं शत्रुघ्नमनुदर्शयन्।।2.99.1।।
output: Bharata sees Rama seated in the hermitage with matted hair and bark robes with Sita nearby -- Bharata's lamentation.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ऋषिं वसिष्ठं सन्दिश्य मातृ़र्मे शीघ्रमानय। इति त्वरितमग्रे स जगाम गुरुवत्सलः।।2.99.2।।
output: Bharata, deeply devoted towards elders, indicated to sage Vasistha to bring along the mothers, and  proceeded ahead quickly.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सुमन्त्रस्त्वपि शत्रुघ्नमदूरादन्वपद्यत। रामदर्शनजस्तर्षो भरतस्येव तस्य च।।2.99.3।।
output: सुमन्त्रस्त्वपि Sumantra on his part, शत्रुघ्नम् to Satrughna, अदूरात् not far from, अन्वपद्यत  followed, रामदर्शनजः arising from seeing Rama, तर्षः overeager, तस्य च for him also, भरतस्येव is like that of Bharata.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
गच्छन्नेवाथ भरतस्तापसालय संस्थिताम्। भ्रातुः पर्णकुटीं श्रीमानुटजं च ददर्श ह।। 2.99.4।।
output: While walking, Bharata beheld a hut made of leaves looking like a hermit's cottage.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
शालायास्त्वग्रत स्तस्या ददर्श भरत स्तदा। काष्ठानि चावभग्नानि पुष्पाण्युपचितानि च।।2.99.5।।
output: तदा then, भरतः Bharata, तस्याः शालायाः that leafy hut's, अग्रतः in front of, अवभग्नानि shattered, काष्ठानि logs of wood, उपचितानि plucked, पुष्पाणि च also flowers, ददर्श beheld.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स लक्ष्मणस्य रामस्य ददर्शाऽश्रममीयुषः। कृतं वृक्षेष्वभिज्ञानं कुशचीरैः क्वचित्क्वचित्।।2.99.6।।
output: सः he, आश्रमम् hermitage, ईयुषः of a man proceeding towards, लक्ष्मणस्य Lakshmana's, रामस्य Rama's, क्वचित् क्वचित् here and there, वृक्षेषु on trees, कुशचीरैः with kusa grass and strips of bark, कृतम् rendered, अभिज्ञानम् as a sign to ascertain, ददर्श beheld.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ददर्श वने तस्मिन्महत स्सञ्चयान्कृतान्। मृगाणां महिषाणां च करीषै शशीतकारणात्।।2.99.7।।
output: He also beheld large heaps of dried cakes of dung of buffaloes and deer for use against cold in the forest.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 99:
गच्छन्नेव महाबाहुर्द्युतिमान्भरत स्तदा। शत्रुघ्नं चाब्रवीद्धृष्टस्तानमात्यांश्च सर्वशः।।2.99.8।।
output: Walking on, the longarmed, effulgent and delighted Bharata said to Satrughna and the ministers surrounding him:

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
मन्ये प्राप्ताः स्म तं देशं भरद्वाजो यमब्रवीत्। नातिदूरे हि मन्येऽहं नदीं मन्दाकिनीमितः।।2.99.9।।
output: यम् about which, भरद्वाजः Bharadwaja, अब्रवीत् had spoken, तं देशम् that region, प्राप्ताः स्म  we must have reached, मन्ये I think, मन्दाकिनीं नदीं Mandakini river, इतः from here, नातिदूरे not far, अहम् I, मन्ये think.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
उच्चैर्बद्धानि चीराणि लक्ष्मणेन भवेदयम्। अभिज्ञानकृतः पन्था अकाले गन्तुमिच्छता।।2.99.10।।
output: Here are long bark garments fastened on lofty places as marks of identification left by Lakshmana, to locate the path at odd times which may be needed while going out.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 99:
इदं चोदात्तदन्तानां कुञ्जराणां तरस्विनाम्। शैलपार्श्वे परिक्रान्तमन्योन्यमभिगर्जताम्।।2.99.11।।
output: This must be the place on the hillside on which mighty tuskers wander about trumpeting and charging at one another.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यमेवाधातुमिच्छन्ति तापसा स्सततं वने। तस्यासौ दृश्यते धूम स्सङ्कुलः कृष्णवर्त्मनः।।2.99.12।।
output: वने in the forest, तापसाः ascetics, सततम् always, यमेव only whom, आधातुम् to maintain, इच्छन्ति wishing, तस्य that, कृष्णवर्त्मनः of blacktrailed fires, असौ this, सङ्कुलः thick, धूमः smoke, दृश्यते is seen.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अत्राहं पुरुषव्याघ्रं गुरुसत्कारकारिणम्। आर्यं द्रक्ष्यामि संहृष्टो महर्षिमिव राघवम्।।2.99.13।।
output: I shall see here with a delighted heart the venerable Rama, the best of men, who renders great hospitality (to elders) and who resembles a maharshi.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 99:
अथ गत्वा मुहूर्तन्तु चित्रकूटं स राघवः। मन्दाकिनीमनुप्राप्तस्तं जनं चेदमब्रवीत्।।2.99.14।।
output: Bharata walked for a short distance towards mount Chitrkuta when he reached river Mandakini. And then said to his ministers:

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 99:
जगत्यां पुरषव्याघ्र आस्ते वीरासने रतः। जनेन्द्रो निर्जनं प्राप्य धिङ्मे जन्म सजीवितम्।।2.99.15।।
output: Rama, the lord of men, a tiger among men, is sitting on the ground in a 'heroic' (yogic) posture in this secluded forest. O fie upon my birth and my life

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
मत्कृते व्यसनं प्राप्तो लोकनाथो महाद्युतिः। सर्वान्कामान्परित्यज्य वने वसति राघवः।।2.99.16।।
output: लोकनाथः lord of the world, महाद्युतिः effulgent, राघवः Rama, मत्कृते on my account, व्यसनम्  calamity, प्राप्त: has faced, सर्वान् all, कामान् desires, परित्यज्य renouncing, वने in the forest, वसति is living.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
इति लोकसमाक्रुष्टः पादेष्वद्य प्रसादयन्। रामस्य निपतिष्यामि सीताया लक्ष्मणस्य च।।2.99.17।।
output: इति thus, लोकसमाक्रुष्टः reviled by the world, अद्य now, प्रसादयन् seeking the grace, रामस्य Rama's, सीतायाः Sita's, लक्ष्मणस्य च and Lakshmana's, पादेषु at the feet, निपतिष्यामि shall fall down.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 99:
एवं संविलपं स्तस्मिन्वने दशरथात्मजः। ददर्श महतीं पुण्यां पर्णशालां मनोरमाम्।।2.99.18।। सालतालाश्वकर्णानां पर्णैर्बहुभिरावृताम्। विशालां मृदुभिस्तीर्णां कुशैर्वेदिमिवाध्वरे।।2.99.19।। शक्रायुधनिकाशैश्च कार्मुकैर्भारसाधनैः। रुक्मपृष्ठैर्महासारै श्शोभितां शत्रुबाधकैः।।2.99.20।। अर्क रश्मि प्रतीकाशैर्घोरैस्तूणीगतैश्शरैः। शोभितां दीप्तवदनै स्सर्पैर्भोगवतीमिव।।2.99.21।। महारजतवासोभ्यामसिभ्यां च विराजिताम्। रुक्मबिन्दुविचित्राभ्यां चर्मभ्यां चापि शोभिताम्।।2.99.22।। गोधाङ्गुळित्रैरासक्तैश्चित्रैः काञ्चनभूषितैः। अरिसंघैरनाधृष्यां मृगै स्सिंहगुहा मिव।।2.99.23।।
output: Lamenting in this way Bharata beheld in that forest an excellent, sacred and enchanting hut covered with a lot of leaves of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees like a sacrificial altar spread with soft kusa grass. Goldplated bows that resembled the thunderbolt of Indra, powerful and capable of achieving great targets and oppressing the enemies, adorned the hut. Arrows glittering like the rays of the Sun, were dreadful, with blazing heads and stored in quivers adorned it like the hooded serpents illumining the city of Bhogavati (in the nether world). A pair of swords in scabbards made of excellent silver, two shields of different colours with golden spots, fingerguards made of skin of iguana decorated with gold were hanging there. It was impregnable to enemy hordes like the cave of a lion to the deer.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
एवं संविलपं स्तस्मिन्वने दशरथात्मजः। ददर्श महातीं पुण्यां पर्णशालां मनोरमाम्।।2.99.18।। सालतालाश्वकर्णानां पर्णैर्बहुभिरावृताम्। विशालां मृदुभिस्तीर्णां कुशैर्वेदिमिवाध्वरे।।2.99.19।। शक्रायुधनिकाशैश्च कार्मुकैर्भारसाधनैः। रुक्मपृष्ठैर्महासारै श्शोभितां शत्रुबाधकैः।।2.99.20।। अर्क रश्मि प्रतीकाशैर्घोरैस्तूणीगतैश्शरैः। शोभितां दीप्तवदनै स्सर्पैर्भोगवतीमिव।।2.99.21।। महारजतवासोभ्यामसिभ्यां च विराजिताम्। रुक्मबिन्दुविचित्राभ्यां चर्मभ्यां चापि शोभिताम्।।2.99.22।। गोधाङ्गुळित्रैरासक्तैश्चित्रैः काञ्चनभूषितैः। अरिसंघैरनाधृष्यां मृगै स्सिंहगुहा मिव।।2.99.23।।
output: Lamenting in this way Bharata beheld in that forest an excellent, sacred and enchanting hut covered with a lot of leaves of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees like a sacrificial altar spread with soft kusa grass. Goldplated bows that resembled the thunderbolt of Indra, powerful and capable of achieving great targets and oppressing the enemies, adorned the hut. Arrows glittering like the rays of the Sun, were dreadful, with blazing heads and stored in quivers adorned it like the hooded serpents illumining the city of Bhogavati (in the nether world). A pair of swords in scabbards made of excellent silver, two shields of different colours with golden spots, fingerguards made of skin of iguana decorated with gold were hanging there. It was impregnable to enemy hordes like the cave of a lion to the deer.

output: एवम् in that way, संविलपन् lamenting, दशरथात्मजः son of Dasaratha (Bharata), तस्मिन् वने in that forest, महतीम् great, पुण्याम् sacred, मनोरमाम् enchanting, सालतालाश्वकर्णानाम् of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees, बहुभिः by abundance of, मृदुभिः by soft, पर्णैः with leaves, आवृताम् covered, अध्वरे in the sacrifice, कुशैः with kusa grass, तीर्णाम् spread over, विशालाम् spacious, वेदिमिव like altar, शक्रायुधनिकाशैः resembling the thunderbolt of Indra, भारसाधनैः capable of achieving targets, रुक्मपृष्ठैः goldplated, महासारै: by powerful, शत्रुबाधकैः oppressing the enemies, कार्मुकैः with bows, शोभिताम् glittering, सर्पैः with serpents, भोगवतीम् इव like Bhogavati, अर्करश्मिप्रतीकाशैः like the rays of the Sun, घोरैः by dreadful, दीप्तवदनैः with tips blazing, तूणीगतैः stored in quivers, शरैः with arrows, शोभिताम् adorned with, महारजतवासोभ्याम् scabbards made of silver, असिभ्याम् with a pair of swords, विराजिताम् was shining, रुक्मबिन्दुविचित्राभ्याम् of different colours with golden spots, चर्मभ्याम् with shields, ताम् all of them, काञ्चनभूषितैः decorated with gold, चित्रैः different kinds, आसक्तै: hung, गोधाङ्गुलित्रैः fingerguards made of skin of iguana, मृगैः with the deer, सिंहगुहामिव like the cave of a lion, अरिसङ्घै: with hordes of enemies, अनाधृष्याम् impregnable, पर्णशालाम् hut made of leave, तस्मिन् वने in that forest, ददर्श saw.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 99:
प्रागुदक्प्रवणां वेदिं विशालां दीप्तपावकाम्। ददर्श भरतस्तत्र पुण्यां रामनिवेशने।।2.99.24।।
output: Bharata beheld at Rama's residence a sacred and spacious altar sloping to the northeast, with a burning fire upon it.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 99:
निरीक्ष्य स मुहूर्तं तु ददर्श भरतो गुरुम्। उटजे राममासीनं जटामण्डलधारिणम्।।2.99.25।।
output: Bharata looked around for a moment and saw his esteemed brother Rama seated in that thatched cottage wearing matted locks of hair.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 99:
तं तु कृष्णाजिनधरं चीरवल्कलवाससम्। ददर्श राममासीनमभितः पावकोपमम्।।2.99.26।। सिंहस्कन्धं महाबाहुं पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणम्। पृथिव्यास्सागरान्तायाः भर्तारं धर्मचारिणम्।।2.99.27।। उपविष्टं महाबाहुं ब्रह्माणमिव शाश्वतम्। स्थण्डिले दर्भसंस्तीर्णे सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च।।2.99.28।।
output: He saw Rama, lord of the oceanbound earth, seated like blazing fire, clad in antelope skin and garment of bark, with long arms and shoulders like a lion and eyes like white lotuses. The mightyarmed warrior seemed like Brahma, the creator and the eternal, protector of righteousness. Accompanied by Sita and Lakshmana Rama sat on the bare ground strewn with darbha grass.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:

output: कृष्णाजिनधरम् clad in antelope skin, चीरवल्कलवासम् dressed in garments made of bark, अभितः near him, पावकोपमम् resembling blazing fire, आसीनम् seated, सिंहस्कन्दम् with his  shoulders like that of a lion, महाबाहुम् longarmed, पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणम् with eyes like white lotus, सागरान्तायाः bounded by the ocean, पृथिव्याः of the earth, भर्तारम् the lord, धर्मचारिणम् follower of righteouness, तं रामम् that Rama, ददर्श saw, महाबाहुम् of longarmed one, शाश्वतम् eternal, ब्रह्माणमिव like the creator Brahma, सीतया with Sita, लक्ष्मणेन along with Lakshmana, दर्भसंस्तीर्णे on the ground strewn with darbha grass, स्थण्डिले on the bare ground, उपविष्टम् seated.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तं दृष्ट्वा भरत श्श्रीमान् दुःखशोकपरिप्लुतः। अभ्यधावत धर्मात्मा भरतः कैकेयी सुतः।।2.99.29।।
output: Beholding Rama, Bharata the majestic and righteous son of Kaikeyi overwhelmed with grief and distress rushed towards him.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 99:
दृष्ट्वैव विललापाऽर्तो बाष्पसन्दिग्धया गिरा। अशक्नुवन् धारयितुं धैर्याद्वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.99.30।।
output: On seeing Rama, Bharata could not control his grief with patience and lamented in great anguish and with words choked with tears said:

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
य स्संसदि प्रकृतिभिर्भवेद्युक्त उपासितुम्। वन्यैर्मृगैरुपासीन स्सोऽयमास्ते ममाग्रजः।।2.99.31।।
output: My elder brother who deserves to be attended by ministers and other subjects in the royal assembly sits here today in the forest surrounded by wild beasts.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
वासोभिर्बहुसाहस्रैर्यो महात्मा पुरोचितः। मृगाजिने सोऽयमिह प्रवस्ते धर्ममाचरन्।।2.99.32।।
output: यः महात्मा that magnanimous (Rama), पुरा formerly, बहुसाहस्रैः with many thousands, वासोभिः with clothes, उचितः was accustomed, सः such, अयम् now, धर्मम् righteousness, आचरन् practising, मृगाजिने two deer kins, प्रवस्ते is wearing.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 99:
अधारयद्यो विविधाश्चित्रास्सुमनसस्तदा। सोऽयं जटाभारमिमं वहते राघवः कथम्।।2.99.33।।
output: How is it that Rama who used to wear variegated flowers formerly, now bears these heavy matted locks?

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यस्य यज्ञैर्यथादिष्टैर्युक्तो धर्मस्य सञ्चयः। शरीरक्लेशसम्भूतं स धर्मं परिमार्गते।।2.99.34।।
output: That Rama, who in accordance with tradition deserves accredition of religious merit through sacrifices now seeks it through mortification of body.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
चन्दनेन महार्हेण यस्याङ्गमुपसेवितम्। मलेन तस्याङ्गमिदं कथमार्यस्य सेव्यते।।2.99.35।।
output: How is it that the body of my venerable brother which was once smeared with expensive, fragrant sandal paste is now covered with dust?

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
मन्निमित्तमिदं दुःखं प्राप्तो रामः सुखोचितः। धिग्जीवितं नृशंसस्य मम लोकविगर्हितम्।।2.99.36।।
output: सुखोचितः accustomed to comforts, रामः Rama, मन्निमित्तम् on my account, इदं दुःखम् this misfortune, प्राप्तः has obtained, नृशंसस्य of a cruel one, मम my, लोकविगर्हितम् condemned by the world, जीवितम् धिक् fie on my life.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इत्येवं विलपन्दीनः प्रस्विन्नमुखपङ्कजः। पादावप्राप्य रामस्य पपात भरतो रुदन्।।2.99.37।।
output: Thus Bharata lamented in misery and with his lotuslike countenanace sweating  before reaching Rama's feet fell down, crying in distress.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
दुःखाभितप्तो भरतो राजपुत्रो महाबलः। उक्त्वाऽर्येति सकृद्दीनं पुनर्नोवाच किञ्चन।।2.99.38।।
output: Mighty prince Bharata, oppressed with grief, could only say, O Arya (venerable one) And in distress could not speak any more.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
बाष्पाभिहतकण्ठश्च प्रेक्ष्य रामं यशस्विनम्। आर्येत्येवाभिसङ्क्रुश्य व्याहर्तुं नाशकत्तदा।।2.99.39।।
output: यशस्विनम् glorious, रामम् Rama, प्रेक्ष्य on seeing, बाष्पाभिहतकण्ठश्च with choked throat, अथ then, आर्येत्येव O Arya, सङ्क्रुश्य crying out, तदा thereafter, व्याहर्तुम् to talk further, नाशकत् was not able.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
शत्रुघ्नश्चापि रामस्य ववन्दे चरणौ रुदन्। तावुभौ स समालिङ्ग्य रामश्चाश्रूण्यवर्तयत्।।2.99.40।।
output: शत्रुघ्नश्चापि Satrughna too, रुदन् weeping, रामस्य Rama's, चरणौ feet, ववन्दे prostrated, सः रामश्च that Rama also, तौ उभौ the two of them, समालिङ्ग्य having embraced, अश्रूणि  tears, अवर्तयत् shed.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 99:
ततस्सुमन्त्रेण गुहेन चैव समीयतु राजसुतावरण्ये। दिवाकरश्चैव निशाकरश्च यथाऽम्बरे शुक्रबृहस्पतिभ्याम्।।2.99.41।।
output: Thereafter, princes Rama and Lakshmana joined Sumantra and Guha in the forest like the Sun and the Moon meeting the planets Sukra and Brihaspati in the sky.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तान्पार्थिवान्वारणयूथपाभान्समागतां स्तत्र महत्यरण्ये। वनौकसस्तेऽपि समीक्ष्य सर्वेऽप्यश्रूण्यमुञ्चन्प्रविहाय हर्षम्।।2.99.42।।
output: ते सर्वे they all, वनौकसः inhabitants of the forest, तत्र there, महति in great, अरण्ये in the forest, समागतान् united, वारणयूथपाभान् with the effulgence of mighty leaders of elephant herds, तान् पार्थिवान् those kings, समीक्ष्य on seeing, हर्षम् delight, प्रविहाय having forsaken, अश्रूणि tears, अमुञ्चन् shed.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
जटिलं चीरवसनं प्राञ्जलिं पतितं भुवि। ददर्श रामो दुर्दर्शं युगान्ते भास्करंयथा।।2.100.1।।
output: Rama beheld Bharata with matted locks and robes of bark fallen down on the ground with folded hands like the Sun at the time of dissolution of the world. It was really difficult to look at him.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कथंचिदभिविज्ञाय विवर्णवदनं कृशम्। भ्रातरं भरतं रामः परिजग्राह बाहुना।।2.100.2।।
output: Rama found it extremely difficult to recognise Bharata with his emaciated body and pallid face. He held him in his arms and lifted him.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
आघ्राय रामस्तं मूर्ध्नि परिष्वज्य च राघवः। अङ्के भरतमारोप्य पर्यपृच्छत्समाहितः।।2.100.3।।
output: राघवः born in the race of Raghu, रामः Rama, तं भरतम् to that Bharata, मूर्ध्नि on the forehead, आघ्राय having kissed, परिष्वज्य च and also embracing, अङ्के on his lap, आरोप्य making him sit, समाहितः with composed mind, पर्यपृच्छत् enquired.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
क्व नु तेऽभूत्पिता तात यदरण्यं त्वमागतः। न हि त्वं जीवतस्तस्य वनमागन्तुमर्हसि।।2.100.4।।
output: तात O dear, त्वम् you, आरण्यम् to the forest, यत् आगतः now that you have come, ते पिता our father, क्व नु where, अभूत् was he, तस्य he, जीवतः while living, त्वम् you, वनम् to the forest, आगन्तुम् to come, न अर्हसि हि does not behove you.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
चिरस्य बत पश्यामि दूराद्भरतमागतम्। दुष्प्रतीकमरण्येऽस्मिन् किं तात वनमागतः।।2.100.5।।
output: अस्मिन् अरण्ये to this forest, दूरात् from a distance, आगतम् have come, दुष्प्रतीकं of emaciated limbs, भरतम् Bharata, चिरस्य after a long time, पश्यामि I see, बत it is a pity, तात dear brother, वनम् to the forest, किम् why, आगतः did you come?

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कच्चिद्धारयते तात राजा यत्त्वमिहाऽगतः। कच्चिन्न दीन स्सहसा राजा लोकान्तरं गतः।।2.100.6।।
output: तात dear child, त्वम् you, इह now, यत् आगतः that you have come here, राजा king Dasaratha, कच्चिद्दारयते Is he surviving, I trust so?, राजा king Dasaratha, दीनः dejected, सहसा immediately, लोकान्तरम् to the other world, न गतः कच्चित् I hope he did not depart.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चित्सौम्य न ते राज्यं भ्रष्टं बालस्य शाश्वतम्। कच्चिच्छुश्रूषसे तात पितरं सत्यविक्रमम्।।2.100.7।।
output: O gentle one, being young and inexperienced, I trust, you have not forfeited the kingdom for ever. Dear child, I trust, you are looking after father whose prowess is his truthfulness.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कच्चिद्धशरथो राजा कुशली सत्यसंङ्गरः। राजसूयाश्वमेधानामाहर्ता धर्मनिश्चयः।।2.100.8।।
output: सत्यसंङ्गरः who is true to his promise, राजसूयाश्वमेधानाम् Rajasuya and Ashwamedha sacrifices, आहर्ता performer, धर्मनिश्चयः firm adherent of righteousness, राजा दशरथः king Dasaratha, कच्चित् कुशली I trust he is in good health.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स कच्चिद्ब्राह्मणो विद्वान् धर्मनित्यो महाद्युतिः। इक्ष्वाकूणामुपाध्यायो यथावत्तात पूज्यते।।2.100.9।।
output: O dear child I trust, the family preceptor of the Ikshvakus, Vasistha, the brahmin (versed in the Vedas), who is learned, ever fixed in virtues and effulgent is being honoured as usual.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
सा तात कच्चित्कौसल्या सुमित्रा च प्रजावती। सुखिनी कच्चिदार्या च देवी नन्दति कैकयी।।2.100.10।।
output: Dear child I trust, Kausalya and Sumitra, mothers of an excellent progeny are happy. I trust, the noble queen Kaikeyi is happy too.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चिद्विनयसम्पन्नः कुलपुत्रो बहुश्रुतः। अनसूयुरनुद्रष्टा सत्कृतस्ते पुरोहितः।।2.100.11।।
output: I trust, you continue to honour the family priest (Suyajna, son of Vasistha) who is endowed with modesty, born of high family, conversant in scriptures, free from envy and who can give you directions with regard to your duties.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चिदग्निषु ते युक्तो विधिज्ञो मतिमानृजुः। हुतं च होष्यमाणं च काले वेदयते सदा।।2.100.12।।
output: I trust, the sagacious priest who knows ritual precepts, who is upright and is employed to take care of your sacred fires, informs you always regarding what was offered and what is to be offered as oblation at appropriate time.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कच्चिद्देवान्पित्रून् मातृ़र्गुरून्पितृसमानपि। वृद्धांश्च तात वैद्यांश्च ब्राह्मणांश्चाभिमन्यसे।।2.100.13।।
output: तात dear, देवान् gods, पित्रून् fathers, मात़ृ़: mothers, गुरून् teachers, पितृसमानपि relations equal to your father, वृद्धांश्च aged people, वैद्यांश्च physicians, ब्राह्मणांश्च brahmins, अभिमन्यसे कच्चित् I trust you are paying homage.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
इष्वस्त्रवरसम्पन्नमर्थशास्त्र विशारदम्। सुधन्वानमुपाध्यायं कच्चित्त्वं तात मन्यसे।।2.100.14।।
output: I hope you treat with respect Sudhanva who is equipped with the most formidable arrows and other weapons propelled by mantras and a master in the science of statecraft.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कच्चिदात्मसमा श्शूरा श्श्रुतवन्तो जितेन्द्रियाः। कुलीनाश्चेङ्गितज्ञाश्च कृतास्ते तात मन्त्रिणः।।2.100.15।।
output: I hope, dear brother, you have appointed men who are brave, learned, selfcontrolled, of noble birth and skilled in guessing from hints.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
मन्त्रो विजयमूलं हि राज्ञां भवति राघव। सुसंवृतो मन्त्रधरैरमात्यै श्शास्त्रकोविदैः।।2.100.16।।
output: O Bharata the wellguarded advice of ministers, learned in scriptures and capable of proper counselling, is the root of victory for kings, specially when the advice is kept in confidence.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कच्चिन्निद्रावशं नैषीः कच्चित् कालेऽवबुध्यसे। कच्चिच्चापररात्रेषु चिन्तियस्यर्थनैपुणम्।।2.100.17।।
output: I trust you are not under the grip of sleep but wake up at appropriate times, I hope you always think of the means of judicious statecraft during the last part of the night.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कच्चिन्मन्त्रयसे नैकः कच्चिन्न बहुभिस्सह। कच्चित्ते मन्त्रितो मन्त्रो राष्ट्रं न परिधावति।।2.100.18।।
output: I hope you neither decide alone nor discuss with many. I trust a decision once made by you is not leaked in the kingdom.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कच्चिदर्थं विनिश्चित्य लघुमूलं महोदयम्। क्षिप्रमारभसे कर्तुं न दीर्घयसि राघव।।2.100.19।।
output: राघव O Bharata, लघुमूलम् with a little effort, महोदयम् yielding great result, अर्थम् an endeavour, विनिश्चित्य having determined, क्षिप्रम् quickly, कर्तुम् to execute, आरभसे कच्चित्  are commencing, न दीर्घयसि are not postponing unduly.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कच्चित्तु सुकृतान्येव कृतरूपाणि वा पुनः। विदुस्ते सर्वकार्याणि न कर्तव्यानि पार्थिवाः।।2.100.20।।
output: पार्थिवाः other kings, सुकृतान्येव wellaccomplished acts only, पुनः again, कृतरूपाणि वा or almost accomplished, ते your, सर्वकार्याणि all those endeavours, विदुः कच्चित् are informed,  कर्तव्यानि endeavours intended to be performed in future, न are not revealed.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चिन्नतर्कैर्युक्त्या वा ये चाप्यपरिकीर्तिताः। त्वया वा तवामात्यैर्बुध्यते तात मन्त्रितम्।।2.100.21।।
output: Dear brother, I hope others are not able to understand your determination or those of your ministers, either by conjecture or by inference or through other means without being revealed either by you or by your ministers.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चित्सहस्रान्मूर्खाणामेकमिच्छसि पण्डितम्। पण्डितो ह्यर्थकृच्छ्रेषु कुर्यान्निश्रेयसं महत्।।2.100.22।।
output: I hope by setting aside a thousand fools, you prefer a single wise man. A wise man will be of immense help in difficult situations.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सहस्राण्यपि मूर्खाणां युद्युपास्ते महीपतिः। अथवाप्ययुतान्येव नास्ति तेषु सहायता।।2.100.23।।
output: Even if the king seeks the assistance from thousands or tens of thousands of fools, they cannot render any help to him.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
एकोऽप्यमात्यो मेधावी शूरो दक्षो विचक्षणः। राजानं राजपुत्रं वा प्रापयेन्महतीं श्रियम्।।2.100.24।।
output: A single clearsighted minister who is prudent, brave and skilful can bring about great prosperity to a king or a prince.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चिन्मुख्या महात्स्वेव मध्यमेषु च मध्यमाः। जघन्याश्च जघन्येषु भृत्याः कर्मसु योजिताः।।2.100.25।।
output: I hope you have employed highly competent servants for important tasks, mediocre servants in mediocre tasks and low people in inferior tasks.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अमात्यानुपधातीतान्पितृपैतामहाञ्छुचीन्। श्रेष्ठांछ्रेष्ठेषुकच्चित्वं नियोजयसि कर्मसु।।2.100.26।।
output: I hope you are assigning ministers, who are unyielding to bribery and other temptations, holding positions hereditarily and who are full of integrity and eminence, with superior tasks.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चिन्नोग्रेण दण्डेन भृशमुद्वेजितप्रजम्। राष्ट्रं तवानुजानन्ति मन्त्रिणः कैकयीसुत।।2.100.27।।
output: Are not the citizens of your kingdom agitated at severe punishment meted out to them reproaching your ministers?

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कच्चित्त्वां नावजानन्ति याजकाः पतितं यथा। उग्रप्रतिग्रहीतारं कामयानमिव स्त्रियः।।2.100.28।।
output: याजकाः performers of sacrifice, उग्रप्रतिग्रहीतारम् accepting unmerited charity, पतितं यथा like an outcaste, स्त्रियः women, कामयानम् इव to a lustful one, त्वाम् you, नावजानन्ति कच्चित् hope they are not insulting you.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
उपायकुशलं वैद्यं भृत्यसंदूषणे रतम्। शूरमैश्वर्यकामं च यो न हन्ति स हन्यते।।2.100.29।।
output: A learned person but skilled in contrivances, a warrior with passion for wealth and a man ever engaged in corrupting the minds of servants must be slain. A king who does not kill them is himself killed in due course.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चिद्धृष्टश्च शूरश्च मतिमान् धृतिमान् शुचिः। कुलीनश्चानुरक्तश्च दक्षस्सेनापतिः कृतः।।2.100.30।।
output: I trust you have appointed a man who is cheerful, brave, sagacious, steadfast, honest, of a good family, loyal and efficient as the army chief.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
बलवन्तश्च कच्चित्ते मुख्या युध्दविशारदाः। दृष्टापदाना विक्रान्तास्त्वया सत्कृत्यमानिताः।।2.100.31।।
output: I trust you honour and respect those prominent soldiers who are courageous, powerful, skilled in war and who have proven heroic exploits.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कच्चिद्बलस्य भक्तं च वेतनं च यथोचितम्। सम्प्राप्तकालं दातव्यं ददासि न विलम्बसे।।2.100.32।।
output: बलस्य of the army, दातव्यम् to be given, भक्तं च food (rations), यथोचितम् suitable, वेतनं च wages, सम्प्राप्तकालम् in due time, ददासि कच्चित् I trust you are paying, न विलम्बसे not delaying.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कालातिक्रमणाच्चैव भक्तवेतनयोर्भृताः। भर्तुः कुप्यन्ति दुष्यन्ति सोऽनर्थ स्सुमहान् स्मृतः।।2.100.33।।
output: It has been mentioned in the scriptures that if provisions and wages are not paid in stipulated time, the dependent attendants will be incensed with their masters and will turn hostile and become corrupt, leading to great calamity.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चित्सर्वेऽनुरक्तास्त्वां कुलपुत्राः प्रधानतः। कच्चित्प्राणां स्तवार्थेषु सन्त्यजन्ति समाहिताः।।2.100.34।।
output: I hope all men of a good family, especially those who belong to our race, are loyal to you and are ready to sacrifice their lives for your cause.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चिज्जानपदो विद्वान्दक्षिणः प्रतिभानवान्। यथोक्तवादी दूतस्ते कृतो भरत पण्डितः।।2.100.35।।
output: O Bharata, I hope you have chosen as your envoy an expert born in your own country, wellinformed, skilful and quick to understand one who repeats and reports (exactly) what has been told.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कच्चिदष्टादशान्येषु स्वपक्षे दश पञ्च च। त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरविज्ञातैर्वेत्सि तीर्थानि चारकैः।।2.100.36।।
output: I hope you collect information (of their secret efforts) intelligently through unrecognisable spies with three of them closely watching each of the eighteen officials (there are eighteen categories of officials in a kingdom) of the enemy's side and fifteen (officials) on your side.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कच्चिद्व्यपास्तानहितान्प्रतियातांश्च सर्वदा। दुर्बलाननवज्ञाय वर्तसे रिपुसूदन।।2.100.37।।
output: O slayer of foes, I hope you are always alert about your foes who were defeated by you and have come back. You should not ignore your enemies thinking they are weak.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कच्चिन्न लौकायतिकान्ब्राह्मणांस्तात सेवसे।। अनर्थकुशला ह्येते बालाः पण्डितमानिनः।।2.100.38।।
output: Dear brother, I hope you do not serve those brahmins who are atheists, who foolishly think of this world alone and fancy themselves as learned. They only bring disasters.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
धर्मशास्त्रेषु मुख्येषु विद्यमानेषु दुर्बुधाः। बुद्धिमान्वीक्षिकीं प्राप्य निरर्थं प्रवदन्ति ते।।2.100.39।।
output: दुर्बुधाः these superficial fellows, मुख्येषु among the principal, धर्मशास्त्रेषु in scriptures, विद्यमानेषु while existing, आन्वीक्षिकीम् relating to the science of logic, बुद्धिम् intelligence, प्राप्य having obtained, निरर्थम् futile, प्रवदन्ति argue.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
वीरैरध्युषितां पूर्वमस्माकं तात पूर्वकैः। सत्यनामां दृढ द्वारां हस्त्यश्वरथसङ्कुलाम्।।2.100.40।। ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्वैश्यै स्स्वकर्मनिरतैस्सदा। जितेन्द्रियैर्महोत्साहैर्वृतामार्यै स्सहस्रशः।।2.100.41।। प्रासादैर्विविधाकारैर्वृतां वैद्यजनाकुलाम्। कच्चित्सुमुदितां स्फीतामयोध्यां परिरक्षसि।।2.100.42।।
output: My dear brother I trust you are protecting the (impregnable) city of Ayodhya worthy of its name, formerly defended by our heroic ancestors, with its sturdy gates, its elephants, horses and chariots, its thousands of venerable, selfcontrolled and highly energetic brahmins, kshatriyas and vaisyas engaged in their respective professions, filled with palaces of various kinds, abounding in learned people and a prosperous city where everything is available in abundance.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
