वीरैरध्युषितां पूर्वमस्माकं तात पूर्वकैः। सत्यनामां दृढ द्वारां हस्त्यश्वरथसङ्कुलाम्।।2.100.40।। ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्वैश्यै स्स्वकर्मनिरतैस्सदा। जितेन्द्रियैर्महोत्साहैर्वृतामार्यै स्सहस्रशः।।2.100.41।। प्रासादैर्विविधाकारैर्वृतां वैद्यजनाकुलाम्। कच्चित्सुमुदितां स्फीतामयोध्यां परिरक्षसि।।2.100.42।।
output: My dear brother I trust you are protecting the (impregnable) city of Ayodhya worthy of its name, formerly defended by our heroic ancestors, with its sturdy gates, its elephants, horses and chariots, its thousands of venerable, selfcontrolled and highly energetic brahmins, kshatriyas and vaisyas engaged in their respective professions, filled with palaces of various kinds, abounding in learned people and a prosperous city where everything is available in abundance.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
वीरैरध्युषितां पूर्वमस्माकं तात पूर्वकैः। सत्यनामां दृढ द्वारां हस्त्यश्वरथसङ्कुलाम्।।2.100.40।। ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्वैश्यै स्स्वकर्मनिरतैस्सदा। जितेन्द्रियैर्महोत्साहैर्वृतामार्यै स्सहस्रशः।।2.100.41।। प्रासादैर्विविधाकारैर्वृतां वैद्यजनाकुलाम्। कच्चित्सुमुदितां स्फीतामयोध्यां परिरक्षसि।।2.100.42।।
output: My dear brother I trust you are protecting the (impregnable) city of Ayodhya worthy of its name, formerly defended by our heroic ancestors, with its sturdy gates, its elephants, horses and chariots, its thousands of venerable, selfcontrolled and highly energetic brahmins, kshatriyas and vaisyas engaged in their respective professions, filled with palaces of various kinds, abounding in learned people and a prosperous city where everything is available in abundance.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कच्चिच्चैत्यशतैर्जुष्ट स्सुनिविष्टजनाकुलः। देवस्थानैः प्रपाभिश्च तटाकैश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.43।। प्रहृष्टनरनारीकस्समाजोत्सवशोभितः। सुकृष्टसीमा पशुमान्हिंसाभिः परिवर्जितः।।2.100.44।। अदेवमातृको रम्य श्श्वापदैः परिवर्जितः। परित्यक्तो भयैस्सर्वैः खनिभिश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.45।। विवर्जितो नरैः पापैर्मम पूर्वै स्सुरक्षितः। कच्चिज्जनपदस्स्फीतः सुखं वसति राघव।।2.100.46।।
output: राघव O Bharata, चैत्यशतैः by hundreds of sanctuaries near villages, जुष्ट: furnished,  सुनिविष्टजनाकुलः filled with people where life is made comfortable, देवस्थानैः with shrines, प्रपाभिश्च with centres for providing water, तटाकैश्च with tanks, उपशोभितः graced with, सुकृष्टसीमा wellploughed land, पशुमान् with excellent cattle, हिंसाभिः with violence, परिवर्जितः abandoned, अदेवमातृकः not dependant on rain, रम्यः enchanting, श्वापदैः with wild animals, परिवर्जितः devoid of, सर्वैः by all kinds, भयैः of fears, परित्यक्तः expelled, खनिभिश्च with mines, उपशोभितः adorned with, पापैः by sinful, नरैः with people, विवर्जितः deserted,  मम my, पूर्वैः by ancestors, सुरक्षितः wellprotected, जनपद: country, स्फीतः कच्चित् I trust is prosperous, सुखम् comfortably, वसति कच्चित् I hope they are living.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कच्चिच्चैत्यशतैर्जुष्ट स्सुनिविष्टजनाकुलः। देवस्थानैः प्रपाभिश्च तटाकैश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.43।। प्रहृष्टनरनारीकस्समाजोत्सवशोभितः। सुकृष्टसीमा पशुमान्हिंसाभिः परिवर्जितः।।2.100.44।। अदेवमातृको रम्य श्श्वापदैः परिवर्जितः। परित्यक्तो भयैस्सर्वैः खनिभिश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.45।। विवर्जितो नरैः पापैर्मम पूर्वै स्सुरक्षितः। कच्चिज्जनपदस्स्फीतः सुखं वसति राघव।।2.100.46।।
output: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कच्चिच्चैत्यशतैर्जुष्ट स्सुनिविष्टजनाकुलः। देवस्थानैः प्रपाभिश्च तटाकैश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.43।। प्रहृष्टनरनारीकस्समाजोत्सवशोभितः। सुकृष्टसीमा पशुमान्हिंसाभिः परिवर्जितः।।2.100.44।। अदेवमातृको रम्य श्श्वापदैः परिवर्जितः। परित्यक्तो भयैस्सर्वैः खनिभिश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.45।। विवर्जितो नरैः पापैर्मम पूर्वै स्सुरक्षितः। कच्चिज्जनपदस्स्फीतः सुखं वसति राघव।।2.100.46।।
output: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कच्चिच्चैत्यशतैर्जुष्ट स्सुनिविष्टजनाकुलः। देवस्थानैः प्रपाभिश्च तटाकैश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.43।। प्रहृष्टनरनारीकस्समाजोत्सवशोभितः। सुकृष्टसीमा पशुमान्हिंसाभिः परिवर्जितः।।2.100.44।। अदेवमातृको रम्य श्श्वापदैः परिवर्जितः। परित्यक्तो भयैस्सर्वैः खनिभिश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.45।। विवर्जितो नरैः पापैर्मम पूर्वै स्सुरक्षितः। कच्चिज्जनपदस्स्फीतः सुखं वसति राघव।।2.100.46।।
output: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कच्चित्ते दयितास्सर्वे कृषिगोरक्षजीविनः। वार्तायां संश्रितस्तात लोको हि सुखमेधते।।2.100.47।।
output: I trust all those men who live on agriculture and cattlerearing are favourable to you. The world's prosperity, dear brother, grows on the profession of cattle rearing.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तेषां गुप्तिपरीहारैः कच्चित्ते भरणं कृतम्। रक्ष्या हि राज्ञा धर्मेण सर्वे विषयवासिनः।।2.100.48।।
output: गुप्तिपरीहारैः by affording protection and through prevention of adversities, तेषाम् their, भरणम् maintenance, ते to you (by you), कृतं कच्चित् has been done, I hope, राज्ञा by the king, विषयवासिनः those living in the country, सर्वे all, धर्मेण with righteousness, रक्ष्याः हि are  required to be protected.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चिस्त्रिय स्सान्त्वयसि कच्चित्ताश्च सुरक्षिताः। कच्चिन्न श्रद्धास्यासां कच्चिद्गुह्यं न भाषसे।।2.100.49।।
output: I trust, you keep the women pacified and wellprotected, you do not believe their words and do not divulge any secrets to them.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कच्चिन्नागवनं गुप्तं कच्चित्ते सन्ति धेनुकाः। कच्चिन्न गणिकाश्वानां कुञ्जराणां च तृप्यसि।।2.100.50।।
output: I trust, you protect the habitat of elephants and you have a large number of milch cows. I trust you are not contented with the existing number of female and male elephants and horses.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चिद्दर्शयसे नित्यं मनुष्याणां विभूषितम्। उत्थायोत्थाय पूर्वाह्णे राजपुत्र महापथे।।2.100.51।।
output: O prince, I trust, you rise early daily and present yourself welladomed to the people on the thoroughfare.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कच्चिन्न सर्वे कर्मान्ताः प्रत्यक्षास्तेऽविशङ्कया। सर्वे वा पुनरुत्सृष्टा मध्यमेवात्र कारणम्।।2.100.52।।
output: All the servants, I trust, do not present themselves to you directly. At the same time they do not remain out of sight with fear at a distance. The middle course is the best way for the welfare of every one.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कच्चित्सर्वाणि दुर्गाणि धनधान्यायुधोदकैः। यन्त्रैश्च परिपूर्णानि तथा शिल्पिधनुर्धरैः।।2.100.53।।
output: सर्वाणि all, दुर्गाणि the forts, धनधान्यायुधोदकैः with wealth, grains, weapons and water, यन्त्रैश्च with ammunitions or machines of war, तथा similarly, शिल्पिधनुर्धरैः with craftsmen and archers, परिपूर्णानि कच्चित् are adequately provided, I trust.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
आयस्ते विपुलः कच्चित्कच्चिदल्पतरो व्ययः। अपात्रेषु न ते कच्चित्कोशो गच्छति राघव।।2.100.54।।
output: राघव O Bharata, ते your, आयः revenues, विपुलः कच्चित् are abundant, I trust, व्ययः expenditure, अल्पतरः कच्चित् is much less, I hope, ते your, कोशः treasury, अपात्रेषु to  undeserving people, न गच्छति कच्चित् does not pass, I trust.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
देवतार्थे च पित्रर्थेब्राह्मणाभ्यागतेषु च। योधेषु मित्रवर्गेषु कच्चिद्गच्छति ते व्ययः।।2.100.55।।
output: I trust, you are spending only on gods, ancestors, brahmins, guests, warriors and hosts of friends.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चिदार्यो विशुद्धात्मा क्षारित श्चापरकर्मणा। अपृष्ट श्शास्त्रकुशलैर्न लोभाद्वध्यते शुचिः।।2.100.56।।
output: I trust a man who is honest, purehearted and venerable, falsely accused of adultery is not slain out of avarice without consulting experts in scriptures.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
गृहीतश्चैव पृष्टश्च काले दृष्टस्सकारणः। कच्चिन्न मुच्यते चोरो धनलोभान्नरर्षभ।।2.100.57।।
output: O best among men I trust that a thief, caught redhanded and interrogated and has sufficient proof is not set free, out of greed for money.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
व्यसने कच्चिदाढ्यस्य दुर्गतस्य च राघव। अर्थं विरागाः पश्यन्ति तवामात्या बहुश्रुताः।।2.100.58।।
output: O Bharata, I trust that your ministers are wellinformed and look into all matters in times of hardship pertaining to whether a man is rich or poor without any bias to either.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यानि मिथ्याभिशस्तानां पतन्त्यश्रूणि राघव। तानि पुत्रान्पशून्घ्नन्ति प्रीत्यर्थमनुशासतः।।2.100.59।।
output: राघव Bharata, मिथ्याभिशस्तानाम् of those who are falsely accused, यानि अश्रूणि those tears, पतन्ति fall, तानि they, प्रीत्यर्थम् for the sake of pleasure, अनुशासतः one who commands,  पुत्रान्पशून् his sons and cattle, घ्नन्ति they will destroy.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कच्चिद्वृद्धांश्च बालांश्च वैद्यामुख्यांश्च राघव। दानेन मनसा वाचा त्रिभिरेतैर्बुभूषसे।।2.100.60।।
output: O Bharata, I trust you wish to thrive by treating the old, children and foremost of learned people with the three expedients namely gifts, affection and kind words.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चिद्गुरूंश्च वृद्धांश्च तापसान् देवतातिथीन्। चैत्यांश्च सर्वान्सिध्दार्थान्ब्राह्मणांश्च नमस्यसि।।2.100.61।।
output: I trust you pay homage to the preceptors, the aged ones, ascetics, gods and guests, to shrines and to accomplished brahmins.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चिदर्थेन वा धर्ममर्थं धर्मेण वा पुनः। उभौ वा प्रीतिलोभेन कामेन च न बाधसे।।2.100.62।।
output: I trust, righteousness for the sake of prosperity or prosperity for the sake of righteousness or both for the sake of sensual pleasure are not thwarted by you.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कच्चिदर्थं च धर्मं च कामं च जयतां वर। विभज्य काले कालज्ञ सर्वान्वरद सेवसे।।2.100.63।।
output: जयताम् among the victorious, वर best, कालज्ञ one having the knowledge of time, वरद granter of boons (best of men), धर्मंच righteousness, कामंच legitimate pleasure, सर्वान् all of them, काले proper time, विभज्य dividing time for each, सेवसे कच्चित् I trust you are attending.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चित्ते ब्राह्मणा श्शर्म सर्वशास्त्रार्थकोविदाः। आशंसन्ते महाप्राज्ञ पौरजानपदैस्सह।।2.100.64।।
output: O highly sagacious Bharata, those brahmins who can comprehend the meaning of all scriptures along with the inhabitants of the city and country, I trust, are seeking your happiness.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
नास्तिक्यमनृतं क्रोधं प्रमादं दीर्घसूत्रताम्। अदर्शनं ज्ञानवतामालस्यं पञ्चवृत्तिताम्।।2.100.65।। एकचिन्तनमर्थानामनर्थज्ञैश्च मन्त्रणम्। निश्चितानामनारम्भं मन्त्रस्यापरिरक्षणम्।।2.100.66।। मङ्गलाद्यप्रयोगं च प्रत्युत्थानं च सर्वतः। कच्चित्वं वर्जयस्येतान्राजदोषांश्चतुर्दश।।2.100.67।।
output: नास्तिक्यम् atheism, अनृतम् falsehood, क्रोधम् anger, प्रमादम् inattention, दीर्घसूत्रताम्   procrastination, ज्ञानवताम् wise people's, अदर्शनम् evasion, आलस्यम् indolence, पञ्चवृत्तिताम् gratification of all five senses, अर्थानाम् relating to the affairs (of the kingdom), एकचिन्तनम् thinking alone, अनर्थज्ञैः by those proficient in worthless acts, मन्त्रणम् consultation, निश्चितानाम् of acts decided upon, अनारम्भम् not to implement, मन्त्रस्य counsel, अपरिरक्षणम् not protecting, मङ्लादि beginning of an auspicious note and the like, अप्रयोगं च not to practise, सर्वतः on all sides, प्रत्युत्थानं च attacking all the enemies at a time, एतान् all these, चतुर्दश fourteen, राजदोषान् defects of the king, त्वम् you, वर्जयसि कच्चित् I trust you eschew.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
नास्तिक्यमनृतं क्रोधं प्रमादं दीर्घसूत्रताम्। अदर्शनं ज्ञानवतामालस्यं पञ्चवृत्तिताम्।।2.100.65।। एकचिन्तनमर्थानामनर्थज्ञैश्च मन्त्रणम्। निश्चितानामनारम्भं मन्त्रस्यापरिरक्षणम्।।2.100.66।। मङ्गलाद्यप्रयोगं च प्रत्युत्थानं च सर्वतः। कच्चित्वं वर्जयस्येतान्राजदोषांश्चतुर्दश।।2.100.67।।
output: I trust you eschew the fourteen faults of kings, like atheism, falsehood, anger, inattention, procrastination, evading the wise, indolence, gratification of all five senses, planning alone in the affairs of the kingdom, consultation with people who are proficient in worthless acts, failure to implement decisious, inability to keep the counsel secret and omission of auspicious practices and setting out against all the enemies at a time.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
नास्तिक्यमनृतं क्रोधं प्रमादं दीर्घसूत्रताम्। अदर्शनं ज्ञानवतामालस्यं पञ्चवृत्तिताम्।।2.100.65।। एकचिन्तनमर्थानामनर्थज्ञैश्च मन्त्रणम्। निश्चितानामनारम्भं मन्त्रस्यापरिरक्षणम्।।2.100.66।। मङ्गलाद्यप्रयोगं च प्रत्युत्थानं च सर्वतः। कच्चित्वं वर्जयस्येतान्राजदोषांश्चतुर्दश।।2.100.67।।
output: I trust you eschew the fourteen faults of kings, like atheism, falsehood, anger, inattention, procrastination, evading the wise, indolence, gratification of all five senses, planning alone in the affairs of the kingdom, consultation with people who are proficient in worthless acts, failure to implement decisious, inability to keep the counsel secret and omission of auspicious practices and setting out against all the enemies at a time.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
दशपञ्चचतुर्वर्गान्सप्तवर्गं च तत्त्वतः। अष्टवर्गं त्रिवर्गं च विद्यास्तिस्रश्च राघव।।2.100.68।। इन्द्रियाणां जयं बुद्ध्या षाड्गुण्यं दैवमानुषम्। कृत्यं विंशतिवर्गं च तथा प्रकृतिमण्डलम्।।2.100.69।। यात्रादण्डविधानं च द्वियोनी सन्धिविग्रहौ। कच्चिदेतान्महाप्राज्ञ यथावदनुमन्यसे।।2.100.70।।
output: महाप्राज्ञः O highly sagacious, राघवः Bharata, दशपञ्चचतुर्वर्गान् the fifteen of the fourfold  divisions, सप्तवर्गं च the seven divisions, अष्टवर्गम् the eight divisions, त्रिवर्गं च the three  divisions, तिस्र: three, विद्याः च kinds of knowledge, इन्द्रियाणाम् of the senses, जयम् victory over, षाडगुण्यम् six qualities, दैवमानुषम् evils arising from destiny and human agency, कृत्यम् kritya, विंशतिवर्गं च division of twenty, तथा similarly, प्रकृतिमण्डलम् Prakriti and Mandalas, यात्रादण्डविधानं च practices of yatra and chastisement, द्वियोनिः two sources of, सन्धि विग्रहौ peace and war, तत्त्वतः the true nature, बुध्द्या by intellect, एतान् alone, यथावत् appropriately, अनुमन्यसे कच्चित् I trust you follow.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
दशपञ्चचतुर्वर्गान्सप्तवर्गं च तत्त्वतः। अष्टवर्गं त्रिवर्गं च विद्यास्तिस्रश्च राघव।।2.100.68।। इन्द्रियाणां जयं बुद्ध्या षाड्गुण्यं दैवमानुषम्। कृत्यं विंशतिवर्गं च तथा प्रकृतिमण्डलम्।।2.100.69।। यात्रादण्डविधानं च द्वियोनी सन्धिविग्रहौ। कच्चिदेतान्महाप्राज्ञ यथावदनुमन्यसे।।2.100.70।।
output: महाप्राज्ञः O highly sagacious, राघवः Bharata, दशपञ्चचतुर्वर्गान् the fifteen of the fourfold  divisions, सप्तवर्गं च the seven divisions, अष्टवर्गम् the eight divisions, त्रिवर्गं च the three  divisions, तिस्र: three, विद्याः च kinds of knowledge, इन्द्रियाणाम् of the senses, जयम् victory over, षाडगुण्यम् six qualities, दैवमानुषम् evils arising from destiny and human agency, कृत्यम् kritya, विंशतिवर्गं च division of twenty, तथा similarly, प्रकृतिमण्डलम् Prakriti and Mandalas, यात्रादण्डविधानं च practices of yatra and chastisement, द्वियोनिः two sources of, सन्धि विग्रहौ peace and war, तत्त्वतः the true nature, बुध्द्या by intellect, एतान् alone, यथावत् appropriately, अनुमन्यसे कच्चित् I trust you follow.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
दशपञ्चचतुर्वर्गान्सप्तवर्गं च तत्त्वतः। अष्टवर्गं त्रिवर्गं च विद्यास्तिस्रश्च राघव।।2.100.68।। इन्द्रियाणां जयं बुद्ध्या षाड्गुण्यं दैवमानुषम्। कृत्यं विंशतिवर्गं च तथा प्रकृतिमण्डलम्।।2.100.69।। यात्रादण्डविधानं च द्वियोनी सन्धिविग्रहौ। कच्चिदेतान्महाप्राज्ञ यथावदनुमन्यसे।।2.100.70।।
output: O highly sagacious Bharata, I trust, having understood their true nature you are appropriately following the ten, five and four divisions, the seven divisions, the eight divisions, the three divisions, three kinds of knowledge, victory over the senses, the six qualities, evils arising from destiny and human agency, kritya, division of twenty, similarly Prakriti and Mandalas and two sources of Yatra and chastisement and of peace and war.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
मन्त्रिभिस्त्वं यथोद्दिष्टैश्चतुर्भिस्त्रिभिरेव वा। कच्चित्समस्तैर्व्यस्तैश्च मन्त्रं मन्त्रयसे मिथः।।2.100.71।।
output: त्वम् you, यथोद्दिष्टैः as adumbrated in sacred texts, चतुर्भिः by four, त्रिभिरेव वा or three, मन्त्रिभिः with counsellors, समस्तै: together, व्यस्तैश्च separately with each one, मिथ: in secrecy, मन्त्रम्  counsel, मन्त्रयसे कच्चित् I trust you deliberate.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चित्ते सफला वेदाः कच्चित्ते सफलाः क्रियाः। कच्चित्ते सफला दाराः कच्चित्ते सफलं श्रुतम्।।2.100.72।।
output: I trust, the Vedas you have studied are fruitful, the acts which you commenced are productive, your wife is fruitful (blessed with a son) and the scriptures you studied are useful.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कच्चिदेषैव ते बुद्धिर्यथोक्ता मम राघव। आयुष्या च यशस्या च धर्मकामार्थ संहिता।।2.100.73।।
output: O Bharata, I trust your intellect is in conformity with what I said conducive to long life, and fame in accordance with righteousness, (legitimate) pleasure and prosperity.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
यां वृत्तिं वर्तते तातो यां च नः प्रपितामहाः। तां वृत्तिं वर्तसे कच्चिद्याच सत्पथगा शुभा।।2.100.74।।
output: I trust, you walk the auspicious path of truth (virtue) followed by our father and forefathers.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 100:
कच्चित्स्वादु कृतं भोज्यमेको नाश्नासि राघव। कच्चिदाशंसमानेभ्यो मित्रेभ्य स्सम्प्रयच्छसि।।2.100.75।।
output: O Bharata, I trust you do not partake delicious food all by yourself, and you share it with your friends when they want it.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
राजा तु धर्मेण हि पालयित्वा महामतिर्दण्डधरः प्रजानाम्। अवाप्य कृत्स्नां वसुधां यथावदितश्च्युत स्स्वर्गमुपैति विद्वान्।।2.100.76।।
output: महामति: one who has great wisdom, विद्वान् learned man, राजा तु as for the king, कृत्स्नां entire, वसुधाम् earth, अवाप्य having acquired, प्रजानाम् for people, दण्डधरः holding Danda in hand, यथावत् in accordance with tradition, धर्मेण righteously, पालयित्वा having ruled, इतः  from here, च्युतः having been released, स्वर्गम् heaven, उपैति हि will ascend.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह। किं मे धर्माद्विहीनस्य राजधर्मः करिष्यति।।2.101.1।।
output: रामस्य Rama's, वचनम् words, श्रुत्वा on listening, भरतः Bharata, प्रत्युवाच ह replied, धर्मात् from righteousness, विहीनस्य devoid of, मे to me, राजधर्मः royal duties, किं करिष्यति of what use  to me.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
शाश्वतोऽयं सदा धर्मः स्थितोऽस्मासु नरर्षभ। ज्येष्ठेे पुत्रे स्थिते राजा न कनीयान् भवेन्नृपः।।2.101.2।।
output: नरर्षभ best of men, अयम् this one, शाश्वतः ancient, धर्मः righteousness, अस्मासु in our race, सदा always, स्थितः exists, राजन् O king, ज्येष्ठपुत्रे the eldest son, स्थिते is there, कनीयान् younger one, नृपः king, न भवेत् can never become.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स समृद्धां मया सार्धमयोध्यां गच्छ राघव। अभिषेचयचात्मानं कुलस्यास्य भवाय नः।।2.101.3।।
output: राघव Rama, सः he, मया सार्धम् with me, समृद्धाम् prosperous, अयोध्याम् to Ayodhya, गच्छ return, नः for us, अस्य कुलस्य for this race, भवाय for the good of, आत्मानम् yourself, अभिषेचय  coronated.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
राजानं मानुषं प्राहु र्देवत्वे सम्मतो मम। यस्य धर्मार्थसहितं वृत्तमाहुरमानुषम्।।2.101.4।।
output: Other think the king to be a human, but to me, he is divine since his conduct and the statecraft are superhuman as they are in conformity with righteousness.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
केकयस्थे च मयि तु त्वयि चारण्य माश्रिते। दिवमार्यो गतो राजा यायजूक: सतां मतः।।2.101.5।।
output: While I was in Kekaya and you took refuge in the forest, venerable king (Dasaratha), who was always engaged in sacrifices and was held in high esteem by the virtuous, ascended to heaven.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
निष्क्रान्तमात्रे भवति ससीते सहलक्ष्मणे। दुःखशोकाभिभूतस्तु राजा त्रिदिवमभ्यगात्।।2.101.6।।
output: As soon as you set out for the forest along with Sita and Lakshmana, the king, overwhelmed with grief, attained heaven.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 101:
उत्तिष्ठ पुरुषव्याघ्र क्रियतामुदकं पितुः। अहं चायं च शत्रुघ्नः पूर्वमेव कृतोदकौ।।2.101.7।।
output: Arise, O best of men and offer libations to our father. I and Satrughna have already done so.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
प्रियेण किल दत्तं हि पितृलोकेषु राघव। अक्षय्यं भवतीत्याहुर्भवांश्चैव पितुः प्रियः।।2.101.8।।
output: O son of Raghu's race, it is said that whatever is offered by a dear son becomes eternal in the world of manes. You alone are the beloved son of our father.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 101:
त्वामेव शोचंस्तव दर्शनेप्सुस्त्वय्येव सक्तामनिवर्त्य बुद्धिम्। त्वया विहीन स्तव शोकमग्नस्त्वां संस्मरन्नस्तमितः पिता ते।।2.101.9।।
output: Your father, deprived of you, brooding over you, wishing to behold you, unable to divert his mind fixed on you, remembering you alone and immersed in sorrow departed (from this world). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोत्तर शततम स्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundredone sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तां श्रुत्वा करुणां वाचं पितुर्मरणसंहिताम्। राघवो भरते नोक्तां बभूव गतचेतनः।।2.102.1।।
output: राघवः one born in the race of the Raghus (Rama), भरतेन by Bharata, उक्ताम् uttered, पितुः father's, मरणसंहिताम्  union with death, करुणाम् pitiable, तां those, वाचम् words, श्रुत्वा on hearing, गत चेतनः unconscious, बभूव became.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तं तु वज्रमिवोत्सृष्टमाहवे दानवारिणा वाग्वज्रंभरते नोक्त ममनोज्ञं परन्तपः।।2.102.2।। प्रगृह्य रामो बाहू वैपुष्पिताग्रो यथा द्रुमः। वने परशुना कृत्तस्तथा भुवि पपात ह।।2.102.3।।
output: परन्तपः destroyer of enemies, रामः Rama, आहवे in the battle, दानवारिणा by the enemy of demons (Indra), उत्सृष्टम् hurled, वज्रमिव like thunderbolt, अमनोज्ञम् unpleasant, भरतेन by Bharata, उक्तम् spoken, तम् that, वाग्वज्रम् thunderlike words, बाहू both arms, प्रगृह्य stretching forth, वने in the forest, परशुना by an axe, कृत्तः severed, पुष्पिताग्रः with flowering tops, द्रुमः tree, यथा as, तथा like that, भुवि on the ground, पपात ह fell down.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तं तु वज्रमिवोत्सृष्टमाहवे दानवारिणा वाग्वज्रंभरते नोक्त ममनोज्ञं परन्तपः।।2.102.2।। प्रगृह्य रामो बाहू वैपुष्पिताग्रो यथा द्रुमः। वने परशुना कृत्तस्तथा भुवि पपात ह।।2.102.3।।
output: On hearing the thunderlike words spoken by Bharata afflicting the mind, like the thunderbolt hurled by Indra (enemy of demons) in a battle, Rama, the scorcher of enemies, stretching forth both his arms, fell down on the ground like a tree with flowering tops severed by an axe in the forest.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तं तु वज्रमिवोत्सृष्टमाहवे दानवारिणा वाग्वज्रंभरते नोक्त ममनोज्ञं परन्तपः।।2.102.2।। प्रगृह्य रामो बाहू वैपुष्पिताग्रो यथा द्रुमः। वने परशुना कृत्तस्तथा भुवि पपात ह।।2.102.3।।
output: परन्तपः destroyer of enemies, रामः Rama, आहवे in the battle, दानवारिणा by the enemy of demons (Indra), उत्सृष्टम् hurled, वज्रमिव like thunderbolt, अमनोज्ञम् unpleasant, भरतेन by Bharata, उक्तम् spoken, तम् that, वाग्वज्रम् thunderlike words, बाहू both arms, प्रगृह्य stretching forth, वने in the forest, परशुना by an axe, कृत्तः severed, पुष्पिताग्रः with flowering tops, द्रुमः tree, यथा as, तथा like that, भुवि on the ground, पपात ह fell down.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 102:
तथा हि पतितं रामं जगत्यां जगतीपतिम्। कूलघातपरिश्रान्तं प्रसुप्तमिव कुञ्जरम्।।2.102. 4।। भ्रातरस्ते महेष्वासं सर्वतश्शोककर्शितम्। रुदन्तस्सह वैदेह्या सिषिचुस्सलिलेन वै।।2.102.5।।
output: Those brothers on all sides, with Sita lamenting, sprinkled water on Rama, the great archer and lord of the earth who, afflicted with grief, had fallen down on the ground, and was lying like an elephant exhausted from repeatedly striking a river bank.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स तु संज्ञां पुनर्लब्ध्वा नेत्राभ्यामस्रमुत्सृजन्। उपाक्रामत काकुत्स्थ कृपणं बहु भाषितुम्।।2.102.6।।
output: सः काकुत्स्थ that Rama, पुनः again, संज्ञाम् consciousness, लब्ध्वा regaining, नेत्राभ्याम् from eyes, अस्रम् tears, उत्सृजन् shedding, कृपणम् piteously, बहु excessively, भाषितुम् to speak, उपाक्रामत started.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स रामस्स्वर्गतं श्रुत्वा पितरं पृथिवीपतिम्। उवाच भरतं वाक्यं धर्मात्मा धर्मसंहितम्।।2.102.7।।
output: On hearing that his father, king Dasaratha, the lord of the world had attained heaven, righteous Rama said to Bharata in conformty with his rightful conduct.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
किं करिष्याम्ययोध्यायां ताते दिष्टां गतिं गते। कस्तां राजवराध्दीनामयोध्यां पालयिष्यति।।2.102.8।।
output: ताते father, दिष्टां गतिम् the path ordained by the gods, अयोध्यायाम् in Ayodhya, किं करिष्यामि what shall I do, राजवरात् by the best of kings, हीनाम् deprived, ताम् अयोध्याम् that Ayodhya, कः who, पालयिष्यति will rule.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
किं नु तस्य मया कार्यं दुर्जातेन महात्मनः। यो मृतो मम शोकेन मया चापि न संस्कृतः।।2.102.9।।
output: यः that king Dasaratha, मम शोकेन of grief on account of me, मृतः died, मया by me, न संस्कृतश्चापि the last rites could not be performed, तस्य for him, महात्मनः for that  magnanimous one, दूर्जातेन of unlucky birth, मया by me, किं नु कार्यम् of what use?

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 102:
अहो भरत सिद्धार्थो येन राजा त्वयाऽनघ। शत्रुघ्नेन च सर्वेषु प्रेतकृत्येषु सत्कृतः।।2.102.10।।
output: O irreproachable Bharata, it is gratifying that you and Satrughna are indeed fortunate to have fulfilled your cherished desire since the king was wellhonoured by you with all the obsequial rites.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
निष्प्रधानामनेकाग्रां नरेन्द्रेण विनाकृताम्। निवृत्तवनवासोऽपि नायोध्यां गन्तु मुत्सहे।।2.102.11।।
output: Even after the completion of my exile I do not wish to return to Ayodhya which is directionless, bereft of its chief, the king.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
समाप्तवनवासं मामयोध्यायां परन्तप। कोऽनु शासिष्यति पुनस्ताते लोकान्तरं गते।।2.102.12।।
output: परन्तप O subduer of enemies, Bharata, ताते with father, लोकान्तरम् to the other world, गते having gone to, समाप्तवनवासम् on completion the exile, माम् me, पुनः again, अयोध्याम् in Ayodhya, कः who, अनुशासिष्यति guide.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
पुरा प्रेक्ष्य सुवृत्तं मां पिता यान्याह सान्त्वयन्। वाक्यानि तानि श्रोष्यामि कुतश्श्रोत्रसुखान्यहम्।।2.102.13।।
output: पुरा in the past, पिता father, माम् me, सुवृत्तम् good conduct, प्रेक्ष्य on seeing, सान्त्वयन् comforting, यानि वाक्यानि such words, आह used to say, श्रोत्र सुखा pleasant to the ears, तानि those words, कुतः from whom, श्रोष्यामि I can hear.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
एवमुक्त्वा स भरतं भार्यामभ्येत्य राघवः। उवाच शोकसन्तप्तः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्।।2.102.14।।
output: सः राघवः that Rama, भरतम् to Bharata, एवम् in this way, उक्त्वा having said, पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम् her face looking like the full Moon, भार्याम् wife, अभ्येत्य having approached, शोकसन्तप्तः  overhelmed with grief, उवाच said.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सीते मृतस्ते श्वशुरः पित्रा हीनोऽसि लक्ष्मण। भरतो दुःखमाचष्टे स्वर्गतं पृथिवीपतिम्।।2.102.15।।
output: O Sita, your fatherinlaw is dead. O Lakshmana, you are deprived of your father. Bharata is relating to me the sad news that king Dasaratha has attained his heavenly abode.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 102:
ततो बहुगुणं तेषां बाष्पं नेत्रेष्वजायत। तथा ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे कुमाराणां यशस्विनाम्।।2.102.16।।
output: While the scion of the Kakutsthas was saying thus, copious tears welled up from the eyes of all those illustrious sons of Dasaratha.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततस्ते भ्रातर  स्रव्रॆ भृशमाश्वास्य दु:खितम्। अब्रुवन् जगतीभर्तुः क्रियतामुदकं पितुः।।2.102.17।।
output: All the brothers, having consoled Rama as best they could, told him, Let the libations be offered to our father, the protector of the world.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 102:
सा सीता स्वर्गतं श्रुत्वा श्वशुरं  तं महानृपम्। नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्या शशाकेक्षितुं प्रियम्।।2.102.18।।
output: On hearing that her fatherinlaw, king Dasaratha, had attained heaven, Sita, her eyes filled with tears could not look at her husband in the face.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 102:
सान्त्वयित्वा तु तां रामो रुदन्तीं जनकात्मजाम्। उवाच लक्ष्मणं तत्र दुःखितो दुःखितं वचः।।2.102.19।।
output: Having consoled Sita, daughter of Janaka, griefstricken Rama said to Lakshmana who was also distressed with grief.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
आनयेङ्गुदिपिण्याकं चीरमाहर चोत्तरम्। जलक्रियार्थं तातस्य गमिष्यामि महात्मनः।।2.102.20।।
output: इङ्गुदिपिण्याकम् oil cake of Ingudi fruit, आनय bring, उत्तरम् upper, चीरं च bark garment, आहर fetch, महात्मनः of the magnanimous, तातस्य father's, जलक्रियार्थम् to offer libations of water, गमिष्यामि I shall go.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सीता पुरस्ताद्व्रजतु त्वमेनामभितो व्रज। अहं पश्चाद्गमिष्यामि गतिर्ह्येषा सुदारुणा।।2.102.21।।
output: सीता Sita, पुरस्तात् in front, व्रजतु let her proceed, एनाम् अभितः ahead of her, त्वम् you, व्रज go, अहम् I, पश्चात् behind, गमिष्यामि shall go, एषा this, गतिः procession in mourning, सुदारुणा हि is terrible indeed.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततो नित्यानुगस्तेषां विदितात्मा महामतिः। मृदुर्दान्तश्च कान्तश्च रामे च दृढभक्तिमान्।।2.102.22।। सुमन्त्र स्तैर्नृपसुतैस्सार्धमाश्वस्य राघवम्। अवातारयदालम्ब्य नदीं मन्दाकिनीं शिवाम्।।2.102.23।।
output: Thereafter, their constant follower Sumantra who was conversant in spiritual knowledge, a highminded person, softnatured, selfcontrolled, tranquilminded and staunchly devoted to Rama consoled him. Holding the hands of the princes, Sumantra helped their descent into the auspicious river Mandakini for taking bath.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 102:
ततो नित्यानुगस्तेषां विदितात्मा महामतिः। मृदुर्दान्तश्च शान्तश्च रामे च दृढभक्तिमान्।।2.102.22।। सुमन्त्रस्तैर्नृपसुतैः सार्धमाश्वास्य राघवम्। अवातारयदालम्ब्य नदीं मन्दाकिनीं शिवाम्।।2.102.23।।
output: Thereafter, their constant follower Sumantra who was conversant in spiritual knowledge, a highminded person, softnatured, selfcontrolled, tranquilminded and staunchly devoted to Rama consoled him. Holding the hands of the princes, Sumantra helped their descent into the auspicious river Mandakini for taking bath.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ते सुतीर्थां ततः कृच्छ्रादुपागम्य यशस्विनः। नदीं मन्दाकिनीं रम्यां सदा पुष्पितकाननाम्।।2.102.24।। शीघ्रस्रोतसमासाद्य तीर्थं शिवमकर्दमम्। सिषिचु स्तूदकं राज्ञे तत एतद् भवत्विति।।2.102.25।।
output: The illustrious brothers approached with great difficulty the swiftflowing and enchanting river Mandakini which had convenient descent and endowed with forests always in bloom. They descended at an auspicious place that was not slushy and offered libations of water saying 'O father, let these offerings be yours'.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 102:
ते सुतीर्थां ततः कृच्छ्रादुपागम्य यशस्विनः। नदीं मन्दाकिनीं रम्यां सदा पुष्पितकाननाम्।।2.102.24।। शीघ्रस्रोतसमासाद्य तीर्थं शिवमकर्दमम्। सिषिचु स्तूदकं राज्ञे तातैतत्ते भवत्विति।।2.102.25।।
output: The illustrious brothers approached with great difficulty the swiftflowing and enchanting river Mandakini which had convenient descent and endowed with forests always in bloom. They descended at an auspicious place that was not slushy and offered libations of water saying 'O father, let these offerings be yours'.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 102:
प्रगृह्य च महीपालो जलपूरितमञ्जलिम्। दिशं याम्यामभिमुखो रुदन्वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.102.26।।
output: Rama, the ruler of the earth, held water with both palms cupped and, facing the south, the direction of Yama (the god of death) said these words, sobbing:

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
एतत्ते राजशार्दूल विमलं तोयमक्षयम्। पितृलोकगत स्याद्य मद्दत्तमुपतिष्ठतु।।2.102.27।।
output: राजशार्दूल O best of kings, पितृलोकगतस्य one who has attained the world of the ancestors, ते to you, अद्य now, मद्दत्तम् offered by me, एतत् this, विमलम् pure, तोयम् water, अक्षयम्  inexhaustible, उपतिष्ठतु let it reach you.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततो मन्दाकिनीतीरात्प्रत्युत्तीर्य स राघवः। पितुश्चकार तेजस्वी निर्वापं भ्रातृभि सह।।2.102.28।।
output: ततः then, तेजस्वी powerful, राघवः scion of the Raghu race (Rama), मन्दाकिनीतीरात् from the bank the river Mandakini, प्रत्युत्तीर्य climbing up, भ्रातृभि: सह with his brothers, पितुः for the departed father, निवापम् offerings of pinda ( balls of rice or flour), चकार made.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ऐङ्गुदं बदरीमिश्रं पिण्याकं दर्भसंस्तरे। न्यस्य रामस्सदुःखार्तो रुदन्वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.102.29।।
output: Placing the balls of ingudi pulp mixed with badari fruit on a spread of darbha grass, Rama, was overcome with grief and weeping, said:

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इदं भुङ्क्ष्वमहाराज प्रीतो यदशना वयम्। यदन्नः पुरुषो भवति तदन्ना स्तस्य देवताः।।2.102.30।।
output: O great king, we offer you such food as we partake now. Be pleased to accept it. For,  his gods are offered the food a man takes.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तत स्तेनैव मार्गेण प्रत्युत्तीर्य सरित्तटात्। आरुरोह नरव्याघ्रो रम्यसानुं महीधरम्।।2.102.31।।
output: Rama, the tiger among men, ascending the riverbank and proceeding on the same path (he had come), climbed the (Chitrakuta) mountain of charming slopes.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततः पर्णकुटीद्वारमासाद्य जगतीपतिः। परिजग्राह बाहुभ्यामुभौ भरतलक्ष्मणौ।।2.102.32।।
output: ततः then, जगतीपतिः lord of the earth (Rama), पर्णकुटीद्वारम् the door of leafhut, आसाद्य  having reached, बाहुभ्याम् with his arms, भरतलक्ष्मणौ Bharata and Lakshmana, उभौ both, परिजग्राह took hold of.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तेषां तु रुदतां शब्दात् प्रतिशब्दोऽभवद् गिरौ। भ्रातॄणां सह वैदेह्या सिंहानां नर्दतामिव।।2.102.33।।
output: The mountain echoed with the sound of lamentations of all the brothers along with Sita which resembled the roar of lions.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
महाबलानां रुदतां कुर्वतामुदकं पितुः। विज्ञाय तुमुलं शब्दं त्रस्ता भरत सैनिकाः।।2.102.34।
output: The soldiers of Bharata were alarmed on hearing the tumultuous sounds raised by those mighty brothers offering libations of water and lamenting.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अब्रुवंश्चापि रामेण भरत संगतो ध्रुवम्। तेषामेव महान् श‌ब्द: शोचतां पितरं मृतम्।।2.102.35।।
output: भरतः Bharata, रामेण with Rama, सङ्गतः joined, घृवम् this is certain, मृतम् deceased, पितरम् about father, शोचताम् lamenting, तेषामेव their only, महान् loud, शब्दः noise, अब्रुवन् च अपि they said.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 102:
अथ वासान्परित्यज्य तं सर्वेऽभिमुखास्स्वनम्। अप्येकमनसो जग्मुर्यथास्थानं प्रधाविताः।।2.102.36।।
output: Then all of them left their camps with one single thought (of seeing Rama) in their minds and ran in the direction from where that sound emanated.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
हयैरन्ये गजैरन्ये रथैरन्ये स्वलङ्कृतैः। सुकुमारा स्तथैवान्ये पद्भिरेव नरा ययुः।।2.102.37।।
output: अन्ये some, हयैः on horses, अन्ये गजैः some on elephants, सुकुमाराः delicate men, अन्ये others, स्वलङ्कृतैः welldecorated, रथैः on chariots, तथैव similarly, अन्ये other, नराः men, पद्भिरेव on foot, ययुः went.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 102:
अचिरप्रोषितं रामं चिरविप्रोषितं यथा। द्रष्टुकामो जनः सर्वो जगाम सहसाऽऽश्रमम्।।2.102.38।।
output: The whole multitude of people at once rushed towards the hermitage wishing to see Rama as if he had left long ago though he had gone on exile very recently.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 102:
भ्रातृ़णां त्वरितास्ते तु द्रष्टुकामा स‌मागमम्। ययुर्बहुविधैर्यानै: खुरनेमिस्वनाकुलैः।।2.102.39।।
output: Eager to see the union of brothers, all those people went by every sort of vehicle filled with the sounds of hooves and wheels.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सा भूमिर्बहुभिर्यानैः रथ‌नेमिसमाहता। मुमोच तुमुलं शब्दं द्यौरिवाभ्रसमागमे।।2.102.40।।
output: The earth crushed by several vehicles, hooves (of horses) and wheels (of chariots) emitted tumultuous sounds like the sky in the gathering stormclouds.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तेन वित्रासिता नागाः करेणुपरिवारिताः। आवासयन्तो गन्धेन जग्मुरन्यद्वनं ततः।।2.102.41।।
output: Frightened by the sound, the elephants followed by their females, spreading all the way the odour of the ichor, moved to other forests.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 102:
वराह वृकसङ्घाश्च महिषा: सृमरास्तथा । व्याघ्रगोकर्णगवया वित्रेसुः पृषतै स‌ह।।2.102.42।।
output: Hearing that sound, hosts of boars and deer, buffaloes, serpents and apes, tigers, antelopes with ears like the cows', gavayas as well as dappled antelopes were all frightened.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
रथाङ्गसाह्वा नत्यूहा हंसाः कारण्डवाः परे। तथा पुंस्कोकिलाः क्रौञ्चा विसंज्ञा भेजिरे दिशः।।2.102.43।।
output: Ducks, watercranes, geese, karandavas, cranes, male cuckoos and kraunchas fled senselessly in different directions.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 102:
तेन शब्देन वित्रस्तैराकाशं पक्षिभिर्वृतम्। मनुष्यैरावृता भूमिरुभयं प्रबभौ तदा।।2.102.44।।
output: The sky was filled with birds frightened by the sound and the earth covered with people. Both looked extremely beautiful.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततस्तं पुरषव्याघ्रं यशस्विनमकल्पषम्। आसीनं स्थण्डिले रामं ददर्श सहसा जनः।।2.102.45।।
output: All at once the people saw the illustrious Rama, the best of men, and the subduer of enemies squatting on the bare earth.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
विगर्हमाणः कैकेयीं मन्थरासहितामपि। अभिगम्य जनो रामं बाष्पपूर्णमुखोऽभवत्।।2.102.46।।
output: जनः all men, मन्थरासहिताम् including Manthara, कैकेयीम् Kaikeyi, विगर्हमाणः censuring, रामम्  to Rama, अभिगम्य having reached, बाष्पपूर्णमुखः with face filled with tears, अभवत् became.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तान्नरान्बाष्पपूर्णाक्षान्समीक्ष्याथ सुदुःखितान्। पर्यष्वजत धर्मज्ञः पितृवन्मातृवच्च सः।।2.102.47।।
output: Thereafter, beholding those people deeply afflicted, their eyes full of tears, Rama embraced them as if they were his own father and mother.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स तत्र कांश्चित्परिषस्वजे नरान्नरास्तु केचित्तु तमभ्यवादयन्। चकार सर्वान्सवयस्यबान्धवान्यथार्ह मासाद्य तदा नृपात्मजः।।2.102.48।।
output: सः Rama, तत्र there, कांश्चित् some, नरान् men, परिषस्वजे embraced, केचित्तु as for some, नराश्च men, तम् that Rama, अभ्यवादयन् paid obeisance, तदा then, सः that, नृपात्मजः king's son, सर्वान् all of them, आसाद्य having reached, वयस्यबान्धवान् friends and relations, यथार्हम् as deserved, चकार made.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 102:
स तत्र तेषां रुदतां महात्मनां भुवं च खं चानुनिनादयन्स्वनः। गुहा गिरीणां च दिशश्च सन्ततं मृदङ्गघोषप्रतिमः प्रशुश्रुवे।।2.102.49।।
output: The weeping and the tumult of those magnanimous people made the earth, sky, mountaincaves and all quarters reverberate incessantly like the beating of drums. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे द्व्युत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundred and second sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
वसिष्ठः पुरतः कृत्वा दारान्दशरथस्य च। अभिचक्राम तं देशं रामदर्शनतर्षितः।।2.103.1।।
output: वसिष्ठः Vasistha, दशरथस्य Dasaratha's, दारान् wives, पुरतः in front of, कृत्वा having placed,  रामदर्शनतर्षितः longing to see Rama, तं देशम् that place, अभिचक्राम set out on foot.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
राजपत्न्यश्च गच्छन्त्यो मन्दं मन्दाकिनीं प्रति। ददृशु स्तत्र तत् तीर्थं रामलक्ष्मणसेवितम्।।2.103.2।।
output: The wives of the king while proceeding slowly towards the river Mandakini beheld the bathing place frequented by Rama and Lakshmana.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कौसल्या बाष्पपूर्णेन मुखेन परिशुष्यता। सुमित्रामब्रवीद्दीना याश्चान्या राजयोषितः।।2.103.3।।
output: कौसल्या Kausalya, बाष्पपूर्णेन filled with tears, परिशुष्यता emaciated, मुखेन with her countenance, दीना in desolation, सुमित्राम् to Sumitra, याः अन्याः the other, राजयोषितः to wives of the king, अब्रवीत् said.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
इदं तेषामनाथानां क्लिष्टमक्लिष्टकर्मणाम्। वने प्राक्कलनं तीर्थं ये ते निर्विषयीकृताः।।2.103.4।।
output: इदम् this one, ये ते those, निर्विषयीकृताः expelled from the country, तेषाम् their, आक्लिष्टकर्मणाम् men performing deeds with untiring energy, अनाथानाम् unfortunate ones, क्लिष्टम् sufferings, प्राक्कलनम् to the east of, वने in the forest, तीर्थम् sacred place.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इत स्सुमित्रे पुत्रस्ते सदा जलमतन्द्रितः। स्वयं हरति सौमित्रिर्मम पुत्रस्य कारणात्।।2.103.5।।
output: O Sumitra, your son Lakshmana, free from laziness, always carries water from here for the sake of my son.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
जघन्यमपि ते पुत्रः कृतवान् न तु गर्हितः। भ्रातुर्यदर्थरहितं सर्वं तद् गर्हितंं गुणैः।।2.103.6।।
output: Your son, though engaged in servile tasks (like bringing water), is not to be held contemptible because all the services intended for the benefit of his brother are prompted by virtue.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अद्यायमपि ते पुत्रः क्लेशानामतथोचितः। नीचानर्थ समाचारं सज्जं कर्म प्रमुञ्चतु।।2.103.7।।
output: क्लेशानाम् of suffering, अतथोचितः unaccustomed, अयम् this, ते पुत्रः अपि your son also, अद्य now, नीचानर्थसमाचारम् mean and distressing, सज्जम् commenced, कर्म work, this service, प्रमुञ्चतु cease to perform.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
दक्षिणाग्रेषु दर्भेषु सा ददर्श महीतले। पितुरिङ्गुदिपिण्याकं न्यस्तमायतलोचना।।2.103.8।।
output: That largeeyed Kausalya beheld the cakes of ingudi pulp placed by Rama for his father on a spread of darbha grass whose blades pointed toward the south.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 103:
तं भूमौ पितुरार्तेन न्यस्तं रामेण वीक्ष्य सा। उवाच देवी कौसल्या सर्वा दशरथस्त्रियः।।2.103.9।।
output: Seeing the pinda (edible offering made to the departed soul) placed on the ground for his father by the distressed Rama, queen Kausalya, addressing all the wives of Dasaratha, said:

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
इदमिक्ष्वाकुनाथस्य राघवस्य महात्मनः। राघवेण पितुर्दत्तं पश्यतैतद्यथाविधि।।2.103.10।।
output: राघवेण by Rama, इक्ष्वाकुनाथस्य for the sake of lord of the Ikshvaku race, महात्मनः of the magnanimous, पितुः father, राघवस्य for Dasaratha, यथाविधि according to tradition, दत्तम् given, इदम् this pinda, पश्यत look at.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तस्य देवसमानस्य पार्थिवस्य महात्मनः। नैतदौपयिकं मन्ये भुक्तभोगस्य भोजनम्।।2.103.11।।
output: I do not think that this is an appropriate food for that godlike and great lord of the earth who enjoyed all luxury.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
चतुरन्तां महीं भुक्त्वा महेन्द्रसदृशो विभुः। कथमिङ्गुदिपिण्याकं स भुक्ते वसुधाधिपः।।2.103.12।।
output: महेन्द्रसदृशः resembling Indra, विभुः king, सः वसुधाधिपः that lord of the earth, चतुरन्ताम् with four corners, महीम् the earth, भुक्त्वा having enjoyed, इङ्गुदिपिण्याकम् the cake of pulp of ingudi, कथम् how, भुक्ते can he eat?

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 103:
अतो दुःखतरं लोके न किञ्चित्प्रतिभाति मा। यत्र रामः पितुर्दद्यादिङ्गुदिक्षोदमृद्धिमान्।।2.103.13।।
output: Rama (who was once) highly prosperous, had to offer the cake of ingudi pulp to his father. Nothing appears more painful to me than this in this world.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 103:
रामेणेङ्गुदिपिण्याकं पितुर्दत्तं समीक्ष्य मे। कथं दुःखेन हृदयं न स्फोटति सहस्रधा।।2.103.14।।
output: Seeing the offering of cake of ingudi pulp by Rama to his father, how is it that my heart does not break into a thousand pieces in sorrow?

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
श्रुतिस्तु खल्वियं सत्या लौकिकी प्रतिभाति मा। यदन्नः पुरुषो भवति तदन्नास्तस्य देवताः।।2.103.15।।
output: पुरुषः man, यदन्नः भवति whatever is his food, तस्य his, देवताः gods, तदन्नाः they have the same food, इयम् this, लौकिकी wellknown in the world, श्रुतिस्तु saying, सत्या as truthful, मा about (to) me, प्रतिभाति खलु occurs to me.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 103:
एवमार्तां सपत्न्यस्ता जग्मुराश्वास्य तां तदा। ददृशुश्चाश्रमे रामं स्वर्गच्युतमिवामरम्।।2.103.16।।
output: The cowives, having thus consoled the distressed Kausalya, went to the hermitage. There they beheld Rama who looked like a god dislodged from heaven.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 103:
सर्वभोगैः परित्यक्तं रामं सम्प्रेक्ष्य मातरः। आर्ता मुमुचुरश्रूणि सस्वरं शोककर्शिताः।।2.103.17।।
output: Beholding Rama devoid of all luxury, his mothers afflicted with grief, and overcome with sorrow, cried aloud, tears streaming down.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तासां रामस्समुत्थाय जग्राह चरणान् शुभान्। मात्रूणां मनुजव्याघ्रस्सर्वासां सत्यसङ्गरः।।2.103.18।।
output: मनुजव्याघ्रः best among men, सत्यसङ्गरः true to his promise, रामः Rama, समुत्थाय having risen, सर्वासाम् to all, तासां मात्रूणाम् of those mothers, शुभान् auspicious, चरणान् feet, जग्राह clasped.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ताः पाणिभि स्सुखस्पर्शैर्मृद्वङ्गुलितलै श्शुभैः। प्रममार्जू रजः पृष्ठाद्रामस्यायतलोचनाः।।2.103.19।।
output: Those largeeyed queens, their palms with delicate fingers and with auspicious hands with a pleasant touch, wiped the dust from the back of his body.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 103:
सौमित्रिरपि ता स्सर्वा मातृ़स्सम्प्रेक्ष्य दुःखितः। अभ्यवादयतासक्तं शनै रामादनन्तरम्।।2.103.20।।
output: On seeing his mothers, Lakshmana, too, was overcome with grief and with devotion followed Rama and slowly bowed to them with reverence.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 103:
यथा रामे तथा तस्मिन्सर्वा ववृतिरे स्त्रियः। वृत्तिं दशरथाज्जाते लक्ष्मणे शुभलक्षणे।।2.103.21।।
output: All the queens treated Lakshmana, born of Dasaratha and endowed with auspicious qualities, with the same love as they did to Rama.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 103:
सीताऽपि चरणांस्तासामुपसङ्गृह्य दुःखिता। श्वश्रूणामश्रुपूर्णाक्षी सा बभूवाग्रतः स्थिता।।2.103.22।।
output: Sita, too, overcome with grief, grasped the feet of her mothersinlaw and stood before them, her eyes full of tears.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तां परिष्वज्य दुःखार्तां माता दुहितरं यथा। वनवासकृशां दीनां कौसल्या वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.103.23।।
output: Like a mother to her daughter, Kausalya embraced the wretched Sita, who was afflicted with sorrow, and emaciated due to her stay in the forest, and said to her:

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
विदेहराजस्य सुता स्नुषा दशरथस्य च। रामपत्नी कथं दुःखं सम्प्राप्ता निर्जने वने।।2.103.24।।
output: विदेहराजस्य of the king of Videha, सुता daughter, दशरथस्य Dasaratha's, स्नुषा daughterinlaw, रामपत्नी Rama's wife, निर्जने in desolation, वने  in the forest, कथम् how, दुःखम्  grief, सम्प्राप्ता had undergone.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
पद्ममातपसन्तप्तं परिक्लिष्टमिवोत्पलम्। काञ्चनं रजसा ध्वस्तं क्लिष्टं चन्द्रमिवाम्बुदैः।।2.103.25।। मुखं ते प्रेक्ष्य मां शोको दहत्यग्निरिवाऽश्रयम्। भृशं मनसि वैदेहि व्यसनारणिसम्भवः।।2.103.26।।
output: O Sita, after looking at your countenance, which is like a lotus, scorched by the sunshine, or like a withered waterlily or gold defiled by dust or the Moon obscured by the clouds, the fire of sorrow is burning my mind. The grief in my mind is like fire kindled from the arani (sacrificial faggots) that consumes its own souree. (On a circular wood piece, a wooden stick is placed and churned to produce fire specially in sacrifices is called arani.)

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 103:
पद्ममातपसन्तप्तं परिक्लिष्टमिवोत्पलम्। काञ्चनं रजसा ध्वस्तं क्लिष्टं चन्द्रमिवाम्बुदैः।।2.103.25।। मुखं ते प्रेक्ष्य मां शोको दहत्यग्निरिवाऽश्रयम्। भृशं मनसि वैदेहि व्यसनारणिसम्भवः।।2.103.26।।
output: O Sita, after looking at your countenance, which is like a lotus, scorched by the sunshine, or like a withered waterlily or gold defiled by dust or the Moon obscured by the clouds, the fire of sorrow is burning my mind. The grief in my mind is like fire kindled from the arani (sacrificial faggots) that consumes its own souree. (On a circular wood piece, a wooden stick is placed and churned to produce fire specially in sacrifices is called arani.)

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ब्रुवन्त्यामेवमार्तायां जनन्यां भरताग्रजः। पादावासाद्य जग्राह वसिष्ठस्य च राघवः।।2.103.27।।
output: आर्तायां while in anguish, जनन्याम् mother, एवम् in this way, ब्रुवन्त्याम् while speaking, भरताग्रजः Bharata's elder brother, राघवः Rama, आसाद्य having approached, वसिष्ठस्य Vasistha, पादौ feet, जग्राह clasped.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 103:
पुरोहितस्याग्निसमस्य वै तदा बृहस्पतेरिन्द्रमिवामराधिपः। प्रगृह्य पादौ सुसमृद्धतेजसस्सहैव तेनोपविवेश राघवः।।2.103.28।।
output: Rama touched the feet of the family priest Vasistha, a man equivalent to effulgent fire like Indra, the lord of the gods, does to Brihaspati and sat down along with him.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 103:
ततो जघन्यं सहितै स्समन्त्रिभिः पुरप्रधानैश्च सहैव सैनिकैः। जनेन धर्मज्ञतमेन धर्मवानुपोपविष्टो भरत स्तदाऽग्रजम्।।2.103.29।।
output: After Vasistha and Rama sat down, righteous Bharata sat close to his elder brother. Behind him sat his companions, leading citizens, soldiers and righteous men.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
उपोपविष्ट स्तु तदा स वीर्यवांस्तपस्विवेषेण समीक्ष्य राघवम्। श्रिया ज्वलन्तं भरतः कृताञ्जलिर्यथा महेन्द्रः प्रयतः प्रजापतिम्।।2.103.30।।
output: वीर्यवान् extremely powerful, सः that, भरतः Bharata, तपस्विवेषेण dressed as an ascetic, श्रिया with majesty, ज्वलन्तम् radiating, राघवम् Rama, प्रयतः purified by religious austerities, महेन्द्रः great Indra, प्रजापतिं यथा like Brahma, the creator, समीक्ष्य having looked at, कृताञ्जलिः with folded palms, तदा then, उपोपविष्टः तु sat next to him.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
किमेष वाक्यं भरतोऽद्य राघवं प्रणम्य सत्कृत्य च साधु वक्ष्यति। इतीव तस्यार्यजनस्य तत्त्वतो बभूव कौतूहलमुत्तमं तदा।।2.103.31।।
output: All noble people were truly filled with great curiosity as to what Bharata was going to speak, after paying his homage and honouring Rama.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स राघव स्सत्यधृति श्च लक्ष्मणो महानुभावो भरत श्च धार्मिकः। वृताः सुहृद्भि श्च विरेजुरध्वरे यथा सदस्यै स्सहितास्त्रयोऽग्नयः।।2.103.32।।
output: सत्यधृतिः steadfast in truth, सः राघवश्च that Rama, महानुभावः a man of great dignity, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, धार्मिकः practising righteouness, भरतश्च Bharata as well, सुहृद्भिः by their friends, वृताः surrounded by, अध्वरे in the sacrifice, सदस्यैः with the officiating priests  सहिताः along with, त्रयः the three, अग्नयः यथा like fires, विरेजुः were resplendent.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तं तु राम स्समाश्वास्य भ्रातरं गुरवत्सलम्। लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे।।2.104.1।।
output: Bharata beseeches Rama repeatedly -- Rama justifies his obedience to his father's command.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 104:
किमेतदिच्छेयमहं श्रोतुं प्रव्याहृतं त्वया। यस्मात्त्वमागतो देशमिमं चीरजटाजिनः।।2.104.2।।
output: I want to hear what brought you to this region with your barkrobes, matted locks and antelope skin.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यन्निमित्तमिमं देशं कृष्णाजिनजटाधरः। हित्वा राज्यं प्रविष्टस्त्वं तत्सर्वं वक्तुमर्हसि।।2.104.3।।
output: त्वम् you, राज्यम् kingdom, हित्वा leaving, कृष्णाजिनजटाधरः wearing deer skin and matted hair, किन्निमित्तम् for what reason, इमं देशम् this region, प्रविष्टः have entered, तत् that, सर्वम् everything, वक्तुम् to tell, अर्हसि behoves you.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 104:
इत्युक्तः कैकयीपुत्रः काकुत्स्थेन महात्मना। प्रगृह्य बलवद्भूयः प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.104.4।।
output: Thus enquired by the magnanimous Rama, Bharata, joining his palms tightly, replied:

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
आर्यं तातः परित्यज्य कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। गत: स्वर्ग महाबाहुः पुत्रशोकाभिपीडितः।।2.104.5।।
output: महाबाहुः mightyarmed, तातः father, आर्यं my esteemed brother, परित्यज्य having abandoned, सुदुष्करम् impossible to perform, कर्म task, कृत्वा having done, पुत्रशोकाभिपीडितः tortured by the grief due to separation from his son, स्वर्गम् heaven, गतः went.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स्त्रिया नियुक्तः कैकेय्या मम मात्रा परन्तप। चकार सा महत्पापमिदमात्मयशोहरम्।।2.104.6।।
output: परन्तप O tormentor of enemies, Rama, मम my, मात्रा mother, स्त्रिया woman, कैकेय्या by Kaikeyi, नियुक्तः instigated, आत्मयशोहरम् destroying his reputation, सुमहत् great, इदं पापम् this sin, चकार commited.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सा राज्यफलमप्राप्य विधवा शोककर्शिता। पतिष्यति महाघोरे निरये जननी मम।।2.104.7।।
output: मम my, जननी mother, सा that lady, राज्यफलम् fruit of kingodm, अप्राप्य without acquiring, विधवा widow, शोककर्शिता formented with grief, महाघोरे dreadful, निरये hell, पतिष्यति will fall.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तस्य मे दासभूतस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि। अभिषिञ्चस्व चाद्येव राज्येन मघवानिव।।2.104.8।।
output: It behoves you to grant  me a favour. I am like your servant. Now get yourself coronated in the kingdom like Indra.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 104:
इमाः प्रकृतय स्सर्वा विधवा मातरश्च याः। त्वत्सकाशमनुप्राप्ता प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि।।2.104.9।।
output: All these subjects and your widowed mothers have come to you. It behoves you to grant them this favour.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तदानुपूर्व्या युक्तं च युक्तं चात्मनि मानद। राज्यं प्राप्नुहि धर्मेण सकामान्सुहृदः कुरु।।2.104.10।।
output: मानद O bestower of honour, तत् for that reason, आनुपूर्व्या by succession, युक्तम् appropriate, आत्मनि in you, युक्तं च is appropriate, राज्यम् kingdom, धर्मेण righteously, प्राप्नुहि you may obtain, सुहृदः friends, सकामान् having fulfilled their desire, कुरु make them.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
भवत्वविधवा भूमि स्समग्रा पतिना त्वया। शशिना विमलेनेव शारदी रजनी यथा।।2.104.11।।
output: Like an autumnal night with the immaculate Moon, let this entire earth cease to be a widow by securing you as her lord.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 104:
एभिश्च सचिवैस्सार्धं शिरसा याचितो मया। भ्रातु  शिष्यस्य दासस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि।।2.104.12।।
output: With my head bowed down, I beseech you along with all these ministers to show favour to me who is your brother, disciple and slave.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तदिदं शाश्वतं पित्र्यं सर्वं प्रकृतिमण्डलम्। पूजितं पुरुषव्याघ्र नातिक्रमितुमर्हसि।।2.104.13।।
output: O best among men, it does not behove you to transgress the prayers of the whole order of subjects and ministers to assume this hereditary and perpetual order.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 104:
एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहु स्सबाष्पः कैकयीसुतः। रामस्य शिरसा पादौ जग्राह भरत: पुन:।।2.104.14।।
output: Having said thus, the mightyarmed Bharata, in accordance with tradition, grasped with tearful eyes the feet of Rama again with his head.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तं मत्तमिव मातङ्गं निःश्वसन्तं पुन पुनः। भ्रातरं भरतं रामः परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत्।।2.104.15।।
output: रामः Rama, पुनः पुनः repeatedly, निःश्वसन्तम् heaving sighs, मत्तम् in rut, मातङ्गम् इव  resembling an elephant, भ्रातरम् brother, तं भरतम् that Bharata, परिष्वज्य embracing, इदम् this word, अब्रवीत् said.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 104:
कुलीन:सत्त्वसम्पन्नस्तेजस्वी चरितव्रतः। राज्यहेतोः कथं पापमाचरेत्त्वद्विधो जनः।।2.104.16।।
output: How can a man like you, born of a noble race, endowed with energy, powerful and adherent to vows, commit a sin for the sake of a kingdom?

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
न दोषं त्वयि पश्यामि सूक्ष्ममप्यरिसूदन। न चापि जननीं बाल्यात्त्वं विगर्हितुमर्हसि।।2.104.17।।
output: O destroyer of enemies, I do not find even slightest fault with you. Like a child, it does not behove you to reproach your mother.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 104:
कामकारो महाप्राज्ञ गुरूणां सर्वदाऽनघ। उपपन्नेषु दारेषु पुत्रेषु च विधीयते।।2.104.18।।
output: O sagacious and sinless one, it is laid down (in sastras) that elders when married can always act at their free will towards their wives and sons.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 104:
वयमस्य यथा लोके सङ्ख्याता: सौम्य साधुभिः। भार्याः पुत्राश्च शिष्याश्च त्वमनुज्ञातुमर्हसि।।2.104.19।।
output: O handsome one, you should treat us the way the virtuous treat their wives, sons and disciples in this world.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
वने वा चीरवसनं सौम्य कृष्णाजिनाम्बरम्। राज्ये वाऽपि महाराजो मां वासयितुमीश्वरः।।2.104.20।।
output: सौम्य O handsome one, चीरवसनम् dressed in bark robes, कृष्णाजिनाम्बरम् with antelope skin as garment, माम् me, महाराजः the maharaja (Dasaratha), वने वा either in the forest, राज्ये वापि or in the kingdom, वासयितुम् to accommodate me,  ईश्वरः is competent.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यावत पितरि धर्मज्ञे गौरवं लोकसत्कृतम्। तावद्धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ जनन्यामपि गौरवम्।।2.104.21।।
output: धर्मभृताम् among the protectors of righteousness, श्रेष्ठ best, धर्मज्ञे conversant with the ways of righteousness, पितरि in father, लोकसत्कृतम् revered by the world, यावत् how much, गौरवम् honour, जनन्यामपि even for mother, तावत् that much, गौरवम् honour, should be shown.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
एताभ्यां धर्मशीलाभ्यां वनं गच्छेति राघव। मातापितृभ्यामुक्तोऽहं कथमन्यत्समाचरे।।2.104.22।।
output: राघव O Bharata, धर्मशीलाभ्याम् of righteous conduct, एताभ्याम् by these two, मातापितृभ्याम् by the father and mother, वनम् to forest, गच्छ go, इति thus, उक्तः having been told, अहम् I, अन्यत् other than this, कथम् how, समाचरेत् can act?

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 104:
त्वया राज्यमयोध्यायां प्राप्तव्यं लोकसत्कृतम्। वस्तव्यं दण्डकारण्ये मया वल्कलवाससा।।2.104.23।।
output: You shall rule the kingdom wellhonoured by the people in Ayodhya and I shall live in Dandaka forest wearing bark as garments.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
एवं कृत्वा महाराजो विभागं लोकसन्निधौ। व्यादिश्य च महातेजा दिवं दशरथो गतः।।2.104.24।।
output: महाराजः great king, महातेजाः of great splendour, दशरथः Dasaratha, लोकसन्निधौ in the presence of people, एवम् in this way, विभागम् apportionment, कृत्वा having  made, व्यादिश्य च having commanded, दिवम् to heaven, गतः went.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 104:
स च प्रमाणं धर्मात्मा राजा लोकगुरुस्तव। पित्रा दत्तं यथाभागमुपभोक्तुं त्वमर्हसि।।2.104.25।।
output: The proclamation of that righteous king revered by the world shall be your guide. You should enjoy that portion bestowed by father.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
चतुर्दश समास्सौम्य दण्डकारण्यमाश्रितः। उपभोक्ष्ये त्वहं दत्तं भागं पित्रा महात्मना।।2.104.26।।
output: सौम्य O handsome one, अहं तु as for myself, चतुर्दश fourteen, समाः years, दण्डकारण्यम् Dandaka forest, आश्रितः taking refuge, महात्मना magnanimous, पित्रा by father, दत्तम् bestowed, भागम् portion, उपभोक्ष्ये I will enjoy.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यदब्रवीन्मां नरलोकसत्कृतः पिता महात्मा विबुधाधिपोपमः। तदेव मन्ये परमात्मनो हितं न सर्वलोकेश्वर भावमप्ययम्।।2.104.27।।
output: नरलोकसत्कृतः honoured by the men of the world, पिता father, महात्मा highsouled, विबुधाधिपोपमः equal to the king of the gods, यत् whatever, अब्रवीत् said, माम् to me, तदेव that only, परमात्मन: the ulitimate, हितं good, मन्ये I regard it, सर्वलोकेश्वर: the will of the lord of all the worlds, भावमप्ययम् न should not be allowed to vanish.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
ततः पुरुषसिंहानां वृतानां तै स्सुहृद्गणैः। शोचतामेव रजनी दुःखेन व्यत्यवर्तत।।2.105.1।।
output: That night passed off painfully for the four lion like brothers as they lamented, surrounded by their hosts of friends.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
रजन्यां सुप्रभातायां भ्रातरस्ते सुहृद्वृताः। मन्दाकिन्यां हुतं जप्यं कृत्वा राममुपागमन्।।2.105.2।।
output: When the night dawned, those brothers surrounded by their friends made (morning) ablutions and, after the prayers, returned to Rama.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तूष्णीं ते समुपासीना न कश्चित्किञ्चिदब्रवीत्। भरतस्तु सुहृन्मध्ये रामं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.105.3।।
output: ते they, तूष्णीम् silently, समुपासीनाः sat togethr, कश्चित् any one, किञ्चित् a little, न अब्रवीत्  did not speak, भरतस्तु Bharata on his part, सुहृन्मध्ये from among the friends, रामम् addressing Rama, वचनम् these words, अब्रवीत् said.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सान्त्विता मामिका माता दत्तं राज्यमिदं मम। तद्ददामि तवैवाहं भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यमकण्टकम्।।2.105.4।।
output: This kingdom was given to me for the satisfaction of my mother. I am bestowing it back on you. Enjoy it without any obstacles.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
महतेवाम्बुवेगेन भिन्नस्सेतुर्जलागमे। दुरावारं त्वदन्येन राज्यखण्डमिदं महत्।।2.105.5।।
output: जलागमे during the rainy season, महता great, अम्बुवेगेन by the surge of waters, भिन्नः burst  सेतुः इव like a dyke, इदम् this, महत् vast, राज्यखण्डम् kingdom, त्वदन्येन other than yourself, दुरावारम्  insupportable.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
गतिं खर इवाश्वस्य तार्क्ष्यस्येव पतत्रिणः। अनुगन्तुं न शक्तिर्मे गतिं तव महीपते।।2.105.6।।
output: O lord of the earth as an ass cannot follow the pace of a horse or a bird, the pace of Tarkshya (Garuda), I do not have the capability to follow you.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
सुजीवं नित्यशस्तस्य यः परैरुपजीव्यते। राम तेन तु दुर्जीवं यः परानुपजीवति।।2.105.7।।
output: O Rama, the life of a man on whom others depend for their sustenance is a happy life and the life of one who depends on others for his own mintenance is miserable.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यथा तु रोपितो वृक्षः पुरुषेण विवर्धितः। ह्रस्वकेण दुरारोहो रूढस्कन्धो महाद्रुमः।।2.105.8।। स यदा पुष्पितो भूत्वा फलानि न विदर्शयेत्। स तां नानुभवेत्प्रीतिं यस्य हेतोः प्ररोपितः।।2.105.9।। एषोपमा महाबाहो तमर्थं वेत्तु मर्हसि। यदि त्वमस्मान्वृषभो भर्ता भृत्यान्न शाधि हि।।2.105.10।।
output: O mightyarmed Rama, a man plants a tree, rears it till it grows into such a large tree with a big trunk that it becomes difficult for a dwarf to climb. When the tree flowers but does not bear fruit, the man who planted it gets no pleasure out of the purpose for which the tree was planted. Being a mighty protector, do not chastise us who are your servants. This is a simile. You may better comprehend its implications. (The meaning of the simile is that if you do not assume the throne, the desire of our father, who nurtured you right from your childhood and hoped that one day you will become king and rule the people, will be in vain.)

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यथा तु रोपितो वृक्षः पुरुषेण विवर्धितः। ह्रस्वकेण दुरारोहो रूढस्कन्धो महाद्रुमः।।2.105.8।। स यदा पुष्पितो भूत्वा फलानि न विदर्शयेत्। स तां नानुभवेत्प्रीतिं यस्य हेतोः प्ररोपितः।।2.105.9।। एषोपमा महाबाहो तमर्थं वेत्तु मर्हसि। यदि त्वमस्मान्वृषभो भर्ता भृत्यान्न शाधि हि।।2.105.10।।
output: महाबाहो O mightyarmed one, वृषभः mighty, भर्ता protector, त्वम् you, भृत्यान् servants, अस्मान् us, न शाधि हि if you do not rule, पुरुषेण by a man, रोपितः planted, विवर्धितः reared, ह्रस्वकेण  by a dwarf  दुरारोहः difficult to climb, रूढस्कन्दः with a big trunk, महाद्रुमः large tree, वृक्षः tree, यदा when, पुष्पितः भूत्वा it having blossomed, फलानि fruit, यथा as, न विदर्शयेत् does not bear, यस्य हेतोः for such purpose, प्ररोपितः it has been planted, सः he, तां प्रीतिम् that pleasure, नानुभवेत् does not feel, एषा this one, उपमा simile, तम् अर्थम् its meaning, वेत्तुम् know, अर्हसि behoves you.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
श्रेणयस्त्वां महाराज पश्यन्त्वग्य्राश्च सर्वशः। प्रतपन्तमिवादित्यं राज्ये स्थित मरिन्दमम्।।2.105.11।।
output: महाराज O great king, राज्ये in the kingdom, स्थितम् installed, अरिन्दमम् subduer of enemies, त्वाम् you, अग्य्राः leading, श्रेणयः guilds of traders, etc, सर्वशः all over, प्रतपन्तम्  with resplendence, आदित्यम् इव like Sun, पश्यन्तु let them see.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
तवानुयाने काकुत्स्थ मत्ता नर्दन्तु कुञ्जराः। अन्तःपुरगता नार्यो नन्दन्तु सुसमाहिताः।।2.105.12।।
output: O Rama, let the elephants following you, intoxicated with ichor, be heard trumpeting. Let the women of the inner apartment rejoice with composed minds (when they hear of your return).

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
तस्य साध्वित्यमन्यन्त नागरा विविधा जनाः। भरतस्य वच श्श्रुत्वा रामं प्रत्यनुयाचतः।।2.105.13।।
output: Hearing the words of Bharata beseeching Rama to return, various classes of people of the city of Ayodhya, in approbation exclaimed well said.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
तमेवं दुःखितं प्रेक्ष्य विलपन्तं यशस्विनम्। रामः कृतात्मा भरतं समाश्वासयदात्मवान्।।2.105.14।।
output: Having seen the illustrious Bharata lamenting that way, Rama, a man of firm determination and selfpossession, consoled him thus:

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
नाऽत्मनः कामकारोऽस्ति पुरुषोऽयमनीश्वरः। इतश्चेतरतश्चैनं कृतान्तः परिकर्षति।।2.105.15।।
output: A man is neither independent nor competent to do any act on his free will. Fate pulls him this way or the other.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सर्वे क्षयान्ताः निचयाः पतनान्ता समुच्छ्रयाः। संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम्।।2.105.16।।
output: सर्वे all, निचयाः accumulations of wealth, क्षयान्ताः deplete at the end, समुच्छ्रयाः elevated positions, पतनान्ताः degrade at the end, संयोगाः union, विप्रयोगान्ताः end in separation, जीवितम् life, मरणान्तम् has death at the end.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यथा फलानां पक्वानां नान्यत्र पतनाद्भयम्। एवं नरस्य जातस्य नान्यत्र मरणाद्भयम्।।2.105.17।।
output: The only fear of a ripened fruit is the fear of falling down (from the tree). In the same way every man who is born has no other fear except the fear of death.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यथाऽगारं दृढस्थूणं जीर्णं भूत्वाऽवसीदति। तथैव सीदन्ति नरा जरामृत्युवशं गताः।।2.105.18।।
output: Even a house constructed with sturdy pillars gets dilapidated and ultimately decays. In the same way people under the sway of old age and death are destroyed (at last).

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अत्येति रजनी या तु सा न प्रतिनिवर्तते। यात्येव यमुना पूर्णा समुद्रमुदकाकुलम्।।2.105.19।।
output: या such, रजनी night, अत्येति passes off, सा that one, न प्रतिनिवर्तते does not return, पूर्णा filled with waters, यमुना river Yamuna, उदकाकुलम् waterfilled, समुद्रम् to the ocean, यात्येव flows forever.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
अहोरात्राणि गच्छन्ति सर्वेषां प्राणिनामिह। अायूंषि क्षपयन्त्याशु ग्रीष्मे जलमिवांशवः।।2.105.20।।
output: The passing days and nights quickly decrease the life span of all living beings in this world, like sunrays drying up the water in summer.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
आत्मानमनुशोच त्वं किमन्यमनुशोचसि। आयुस्ते हीयते यस्य स्थितस्य च गतस्य च।।2.105.21।।
output: स्थितस्य च whether you stand, गतस्य च or moving, यस्य whosoever, आयुः life span, हीयते decreases, आत्मानम् about you, त्वम् you, अनुशोच grieve, अन्यम् about others, किम् why, अनुशोचसि are you grieving?

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
सहैव मृत्युर्व्रजति सह मृत्युर्निषीदति। गत्वासुदीर्घमध्वानं सहमृत्युर्निवर्तते।।2.105.22।।
output: Death follows a man wherever he goes. When he sits, death sits with him. Even after travelling a very long distance, the man returns along with death.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
गात्रेषु वलयः प्राप्ता श्श्वेताश्चैव शिरोरुहाः। जरया पुरुषो जीर्णः किं हि कृत्वा प्रभावयेत्।।2.105.23।।
output: Wrinkels form on the body and hair turns grey in old age. In this way, decayed with age, what can a man do to have control over death.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
नन्दन्त्युदित आदित्ये नन्दन्त्यस्तमितेऽहनि। आत्मनो नावबुध्यन्ते मनुष्या जीवितक्षयम्।।2.105.24।।
output: People rejoice when the Sun rises and rejoice when the Sun sets. But they are unaware of the decline of the life span of their own.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
हृष्यन्त्यृतुमुखं दृष्ट्वा नवं नवमिहागतम्। ऋतूनां परिवर्तेन प्राणिनां प्राणसङ्क्षयः।।2.105.25।।
output: ऋतुमुखम् setting of a season, दृष्ट्वा having seen, इह now, नवं नवम् something new             (flowers and fruits), आगतम् have arrived, हृष्यन्ति feel delighted, ऋतूनाम् of seasons, परिवर्तेन by changes, प्राणिनाम् of living beings', प्राणसङ्क्षयः life span decreases.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
यथा काष्ठं च काष्ठं च समेयातां महार्णवे। समेत्य च व्यपेयातां कालमासाद्य कञ्चन।।2.105.26।। एवं भार्याश्चपुत्राश्च ज्ञातयश्च धनानि च। समेत्य व्यवधावन्ति ध्रुवो ह्येषां विनाभवः।।2.105.27।।
output: In a mighty ocean, two pieces of logs meet one another, float together and in due course get separated. In the same way wives, sons, relatives and riches remain together for some time and thereafter get separated. Their separation is certain.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यथा काष्ठं च काष्ठं च समेयातां महार्णवे। समेत्य च व्यपेयातां कालमासाद्य कञ्चन।।2.105.26।। एवं भार्याश्चपुत्राश्च ज्ञातयश्च धनानि च। समेत्य व्यवधावन्ति ध्रुवो ह्येषां विनाभवः।।2.105.27।।
output: In a mighty ocean, two pieces of logs meet one another, float together and in due course get separated. In the same way wives, sons, relatives and riches remain together for some time and thereafter get separated. Their separation is certain.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
नात्र कश्चिद्यथाभावं प्राणी समभिवर्तते। तेन तस्मिन्न सामर्थ्यं प्रेतस्या स्त्यनुशोचतः।।2.105.28।।
output: अत्र then in this world, कश्चित् प्राणी any living being, यथाभावम् as one likes, न समभिवर्तते does not go, तेन therefore, प्रेतस्य for the dead, अनुशोचतः for one who grieves, तस्मिन् in the matter of death, सामर्थ्यम् capability, नास्ति not there.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यथा हि सार्थं गच्छन्तं ब्रूयात्कश्चित्पथि स्थितः। अहमप्यागमिष्यामि पृष्ठतो भवता मिति।।2.105.29।। एवं पूर्वैर्गतो मार्गः पितृपैतामहो ध्रुवः। तमापन्नः कथं शोचेद्यस्य नास्ति व्यतिक्रमः।।2.105.30।।
output: Like a man standing on the wayside says to a passing caravan, 'I am following you', and follows them, the road taken by our fathers and forefathers is certain for every one and cannot be violated by a person treading that path. (So) why should a man grieve?

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
यथा हि सार्थं गच्छन्तं ब्रूयात्कश्चित्पथि स्थितः। अहमप्यागमिष्यामि पृष्ठतो भवता मिति।।2.105.29।। एवं पूर्वैर्गतो मार्गः पितृपैतामहो ध्रुवः। तमापन्नः कथं शोचेद्यस्य नास्ति व्यतिक्रमः।।2.105.30।।
output: Like a man standing on the wayside says to a passing caravan, 'I am following you', and follows them, the road taken by our fathers and forefathers is certain for every one and cannot be violated by a person treading that path. (So) why should a man grieve?

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
वयसः पतमानस्य स्रोतसो वाऽनिवर्तिनः। आत्मा सुखे नियोक्तव्यस्सुखभाजः प्रजाः स्मृताः।।2.105.31।।
output: Like the flow of water which never reverts to its source, age passes. Therefore, a man must employ his self in righteous acts that bring him happiness. By doing so, it is said, people will always be happy.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
धर्मात्मा स शुभैः कृत्स्नैः क्रतुभिश्चाप्तदक्षिणैः। स्वर्गं दशरथः प्राप्तः पिता नः पृथिवीपतिः।।2.105.32।।
output: Our righteous father and lord of the earth, Dasaratha, attained heaven by giving abundant charities and performing several sacrifices in accordance with tradition.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
भृत्यानां भरणात्सम्यक्प्रजानां परिपालनात्। अर्थादानाच्च धर्मेण पिता न स्त्रिदिवंगतः।।2.105.33।।
output: Our father nourished his dependents, splendidly governed his subjects and accepted  wealth through righteous ways. Because of these pious acts, he could go to heaven.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कर्मभि स्तु शुभैरिष्टैः क्रतुभिश्चाप्तदक्षिणैः। स्वर्गं दशरथः प्राप्तः पिता नः पृथिवीपतिः।।2.105.34।।
output: नः our, पिता father, पृथिवीपतिः lord of the earth, दशरथः Dasaratha, शुभैः auspicious, कर्मभिः  with acts, आप्तदक्षिणैः with abundant charities, इष्टैः offerings of, क्रतुभिश्च with sacrifices, स्वर्गम् heaven, प्राप्तः reached.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
इष्ट्वा बहुविधैर्यज्ञैर्भोगां श्चावाप्य पुष्कलान्। उत्तमं चायुरासाद्य स्वर्गतः पृथिवीपतिः।।2.105.35।।
output: पृथिवीपतिः lord of the earth, बहुविधैः by several kinds of, यज्ञैः with sacrifices, इष्ट्वा having performed, पुष्कलान् abundance of, भोगान् pleasures, अवाप्य च having enjoyed, उत्तमम् excellent, आयुश्च life also, आसाद्य having obtained , स्वर्गतः went to heaven.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
आयुरुत्तममासाद्य भोगानपि च राघवः। स न शोच्यः पिता तात स्वर्गत स्सत्कृत स्सताम्।।2.105.36।।
output: O dear our father, king Dasaratha, who was honoured by the virtuous and enjoyed the best of pleasures attained heaven after a long life. Therefore, he is not to be grieved over.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स जीर्णं मानुषं देहं परित्यज्य पिता हि नः। दैवीमृद्धिमनुप्राप्तो ब्रह्मलोकविहारिणीम्।।2.105.37।।
output: नः our, पिता father, सः king Dasaratha, जीर्णम् wornout, मानुषं देहम् mortal body, परित्यज्य  having abandoned, ब्रह्मलोकविहारिणीम् wandering in the world of Brahma, दैवीम् divine,  ऋद्धिम् treasure, अनुप्राप्तः हि obtained.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तं तु नैवंविधः कश्चित्प्राज्ञ श्शोचितुमर्हति। तत्विधो मद्विधश्चापि श्रुतवान्बुद्धिमत्तरः।।2.105.38।।
output: No one like you or me should ever mourn about this highly sagacious and learned king who was proficient in scriptural knowledge.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
एते बहुविधा शोका विलापरुदिते तथा। वर्जनीया हि धीरेण सर्वावस्थासु धीमता।।2.105.39।।
output: A wise man, holding on to his fortitude in all circumstances, should avoid such occasions of grief, these words of lamentation and this crying.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स स्वस्थो भव मा शोचेर्यात्वा चावसतां पुरीम्। तथा पित्रा नियुक्तोऽसि वशिना वदतां वर।।2.105.40।।
output: O foremost of the eloquent, compose yourself. Do not grieve. Return to the city (Ayodhya) and reside there. You have been commanded so by our father who was a man of selfcontrol.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यत्राहमपि तेनैव नियुक्तः पुण्यकर्मणा। तत्रैवाहं करिष्यामि पितुरार्यस्य शासनम्।।2.105.41।।
output: अहमपि I also, पुण्यकर्मणा by a man of sacred deeds, तेनैव by him (king Dasaratha), यत्र  wherever one, नियुक्तः have been commanded, तत्रैव that one only, आर्यस्य noble, पितुः father's, शासनम् order, करिष्यामि shall do.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
न मया शासनं तस्य त्यक्तुं न्याय्य मरिन्दम। स त्वयापि सदा मान्यं स वै बन्धु स नः पिता।।2.105.42।।
output: O subduer of enemies, I cannot violate the order of the king. You also must respect it for he is our father and friend indeed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तद्वचः पितुरेवाहं सम्मतं धर्मचारिणः। कर्मणा पालयिष्यामि वनवासेन राघव।।2.105.43।।
output: राघव O Bharata, तत् therefore, अहम् I, धर्मचारिणः of the champion of righteousness, पितुः father's, सम्मतम् acceptable, वचः एव word only, वनवासेन by dwelling in the forest, कर्मणा by that act, पालयिष्यामि I will obey.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
धार्मिकेणानृशंसेन नरेण गुरुवर्तिना। भवितव्यं नरव्याघ्र परलोकं जिगीषता।।2.105.44।।
output: O best of men, if a man aspires to conquer the higher world, he should remain  virtuous, compassionate and obedient to his preceptors.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 105:
आत्मानमनुतिष्ठत्वं स्वभावेन नरर्षभ। निशाम्यतु शुभं वृत्तं पितुर्दशरथस्य नः।।2.105.45।।
output: O best of men, having seen the auspicious life of our father Dasaratha and his conduct, you also stick to your own duty.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं महात्मा पितुर्निदेश प्रतिपालनार्थम्। यवीयसं भ्रातरमर्थवच्च प्रभुर्मुहूर्ताद्विरराम रामः।।2.105.46।।
output: Rama, the magnanimous lord, addressed his younger brother Bharata with words full of significance, saying, Obey father's command and remained silent in a moment. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चोत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the one hundredfifth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
