हरींश्चापिहनियिष्यामिसंयुगेसमवास्थिवान् । असाधारणमिच्छामिनदातुंमहद्यशः ।।6.63.51।।
output: "I will remain steady in the battlefield and devour monkeys also. I wish to confer an unusual and great glory on you."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तदिचेन्द्राद्भयं राजन्यदि चापिस्वयम्भुवः । ततोऽहंनाशयिष्यामिनैशंतमइवांशुमान् ।।6.63.52।। अपिदेवाश्शयिष्यन्तेक्रुद्धेमयिमहीतले ।
output: "Even if there is fear of Indra and Brahma that haunts you, I shall destroy them away like the sun dispels darkness. Devas will fall flat on earth when I am enraged."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यमं च शमयिष्यामिभक्षयिष्यामिपावकम् ।।6.63.53।। आदित्यंपातयिष्यामिसनक्षत्रंमहीतले ।
output: "I shall quell Lord Yama also, devour fire god, make the Sun including stars fall on earth."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 63:
शतक्रतुंवधिष्यामिपास्यामिवरुणालयम् ।।6.63.54।। पर्वतांश्चूर्णयिष्यामिदारयिष्यामिमेदिनीम् ।
output: "I shall kill Indra who has done a hundred sacrifices, drink up the ocean the abode of Varuna, crush the mountains totally, and break the earth."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
दीर्घकालंप्रसुप्तस्यकुम्भकर्णस्यविक्रमम् ।।6.63.55।। अद्यपश्यन्तुभूतानिभक्ष्यमाणानिसर्वशः । नन्विदंत्रिदिवंसर्वमाहारस्य न पूर्यते ।।6.63.56।।
output: अद्य now, सर्वशः all over, भक्ष्यमाणानि will be eaten, भूतानि beings, दीर्घकालम् for long time, प्रसुप्तस्य has been sleeping, कुम्भकर्णस्य Kumbhakarna's, विक्रमम् prowess, पश्यन्तु will see, इदम् now, सर्वम् all, त्रिदिवम् three worlds (earth, heaven and intermediate region), आहारस्य food, न पूर्यतेननु my stomach will not be filled.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
दीर्घकालंप्रसुप्तस्यकुम्भकर्णस्यविक्रमम् ।।6.63.55।। अद्यपश्यन्तुभूतानिभक्ष्यमाणानिसर्वशः । नन्विदंत्रिदिवंसर्वमाहारस्य न पूर्यते ।।6.63.56।।
output: " All beings all over will be eaten now. For a long time Kumbhakarna was sleeping. Now you will see that the food of all the three worlds, earth, heaven and intermediate region will not be enough to fill my stomach."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
वधेनतेदाशरथेःसुखार्हंसुखंसमाहर्तुमहंव्रजामि । निहत्यरामंसहलक्ष्मणेनखादामिन्हरियूथमुख्यान् ।।6.63.57।।
output: दाशरथेः son of Dasaratha, वधेन destruction of, ते you, सुखावहम् worthy of happiness, सुखम् for your happiness, समहर्तुम् will collect, अहम् I, व्रजामि in the battlefield, लक्ष्मणेनसह along with Lakshmana, रामम् Rama, निहत्य on killing, सर्वान् all, हरियूथमुख्यान् Vanara leaders, खादामि will devour.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तदुक्तमतिकायस्यबलिनोबाहुशालिनः । कुम्भकर्णस्यवचनंश्रुत्वोवाचमहोदरः ।।6.64.1।।
output: अतिकायस्य of massive body, बलिनः mighty, बाहुशालिनः of wellformed shoulders, कुम्भकर्णस्य Kumbhakarna's, उक्तम् spoken, तत् that, वचनम् words, आकर्ण्य having heard, महोदरः Mahodara, उवाच said.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कुम्भकर्णकुलेजातोधृष्टःप्राकृतदर्शनः । अवलिप्तो न शक्नोषिकृत्यंसर्वत्रवेदितुम् ।।6.64.2।।
output: कुम्भकर्ण Kumbhakarna, कुले noble, जातः race, धृष्टः seeing, प्राकृतदर्शनः insolent, अवलिप्तः of low intellect, सर्वत्र all aspects कृत्यम् actions, वेदितुम् knowledge, नशक्नोषि not know what should be done.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कुम्भकर्णकुलेजातोधृष्टःप्राकृतदर्शनः । अवलिप्तो न शक्नोषिकृत्यंसर्वत्रवेदितुम् ।।6.64.2।।
output: "Kumbhakarna! Although you are born of noble race, you are insolent, seeing your low intellect in all aspects you have no knowledge of what should be done or not to be done."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 64:
स्थानंवृद्धिं च हानि च देशकालविभागवित् । आत्मनश्चपरेषां च बुध्यतेराक्षसर्षभः ।।6.64.4।।
output: "Ravana, a bull among Rakshasas is conversant with rules of time and place and knows his own enemies, his progress and decline also."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 64:
यत्तुशक्यंबलवताकर्तुंप्राकृतबुद्धिना । अनुपासितवृद्धेनकःकुर्यात्तादृशंनरः ।।6.64.5।।
output: " A strong person of unsophisticated intellect, who is progressive, a knower of everything will do such a task which is not possible to do?"

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यांस्तुधर्मार्थकामांस्त्वंब्रवीषिपृथगाश्रयान् । अवबोद्धुंस्वभावेतान्नहिलक्षणमस्तितान् ।।6.64.6।।
output: त्वम् you, यान् such, धर्मार्थकामान् virtue worldly gain and sensuous pleasures, पृथगाश्रयान् separately as incompatible, ब्रवीषि told, तान् such qualities, स्वभावेन in their true nature, अवबोद्धुम् known, लक्षणम् qualities, नास्तिहि not exist.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कर्मचैवहिसर्वेषांकारणानांप्रयोजकम् । श्रेयःपापीयसांचात्रफलंभवतिकर्मणाम् ।।6.64.7।।
output: सर्वेषाम् for all, कारणानाम् means, कर्मचै action alone, प्रयोजकंहि happiness, अत्र and that, पापीयसाम् sinful, कर्मणां च actions also, श्रेयः good, फलम् result, भवति will accrue.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
निश्श्रेयसफलावेवधर्मार्थावितरावपि । अधर्मानर्थयोःप्राप्तिःफलं च प्रत्यवायिकम् ।।6.64.8।।
output: धर्मार्थौ virtues and worldly pleasures, इतरौअपि even other, निश्श्रेयसफलौएव only give benefit, अधर्मानर्थयोः if done in unrighteous manner with disinterest, प्रत्यवायिकम् other than prosperity, फलं च the result also, प्राप्तम् will give.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 64:
ऐहलौकिकपारक्यंकर्मपुम्भिर्निषेव्यते । कर्माण्यपितुकल्यानिलभतेकाममास्थितः ।।6.64.9।।
output: " All beings reap the fruit of their actions in this world as well as in other worlds. He, who remains to be pleasure seeking, devoted to actions will receive blessings and attain pleasures in this life only (not here after)."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 64:
तत्रक्लुप्तमिदंराज्ञाहृदिकार्यंमतं च नः । शत्रौहिसाहसंयत्स्यात्किमिवात्रापनीयते ।।6.64.10।।
output: " At that time the king intended in his heart (to abduct Sita), and we approved his action, and it was done. What is wrong in doing such a courageous action against an enemy?"

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
एकस्यैवाभियानेतुहेतुर्यःकथितस्त्वया । तत्राप्यनुपपन्नंतेवक्ष्यामियदसाधु च ।।6.64.11।।
output: "You have set out alone (for war) and the reason adduced by you is ill conceived and improper. I shall tell you."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
येनपूर्वंजनस्थानेबहवोऽतिबलाहताः । राक्षसाराघवंतंत्वंकथमेकोजयिष्यसि ।।6.64.12।।
output: पूर्वम् in the past, जनस्थाने Janasthana, येन he who, अतिबलाः exceeding might, बहवः many, राक्षसाः Rakshasas, हताः killed, तम् him, राघवम् Raghava, त्वम् you, एकः single handed, कथम् how, जयिष्यसि won.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
येपुरानिर्जितास्तेनजनस्थानेमहौजसः । राक्षसांस्तान्पुरेसर्वान्भीतानद्यापिपश्यसि ।।6.64.13।।
output: पुरा earlier, जनस्थाने at Janasthana, महौजसः highly energetic, ये those, निर्जिताः won, भीतान् scared, सर्वान् all, तान् राक्षसान् those Rakshasas, अद्यापि even now, पुरे earlier, पश्यसि look.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 64:
तंसिंहमिवसङ्क्रुद्धंरामंदशरथात्मजम् । सर्पंसुप्तमिवबुद्ध्यप्रबोधयितुमिच्छसि ।।6.64.14।।
output: "Do you desire to awaken Rama, who is like an enraged lion knowingly, who is like a sleeping snake?"

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ज्वलन्तंतेजसानित्यंक्रोधेन च दुरासदम् । कस्तंमृत्युमिवासह्यमासादयितुमर्हति ।।6.64.15।।
output: तेजसा burning, नित्यम् ever, ज्वलन्तम् burning, क्रोधेन in anger, दुरासदम् difficult to encounter, मृत्युमिव like spirit of death, असह्यम् unbearable, तम् him, कः who, आसादयितुम् approach, अर्हति be able.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 64:
संशयस्थमिदंसर्वंशत्रोःप्रतिसमासने । एकस्यगमनंतत्र न हिमेरोचतेभृशम् ।।6.64.16।।
output: "Face to face with the enemy this total army will be in danger. You're going alone is certainly not desirable."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 64:
हीनार्थस्तुसमृद्धार्थंकोरिपुंप्राकृतंयथा । निश्चित्यजीवितत्यागेवशमानेतुमिच्छति ।।6.64.17।।
output: "How can a weak person desire to go to the enemy who is rich in resources, determined to sacrifice his life several times and submit himself?"

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यस्यनास्तिमनुष्येषुसदृशोराक्षसोत्तम । कथमाशंससेयोद्धुंतुल्येनेन्द्रविवस्वतोः ।।6.64.18।।
output: राक्षसोत्तम best of Rakshasas, यस्य his, सदृशः great, मनुष्येषु of all the human beings, नास्ति not, इन्द्रविवस्वतोः Indra and Sun god, तुल्येन equal, योद्धुम् in war, कथम् how, आशंससे enter into combat.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
एवमुक्त्वातुसम्रब्दःकुम्भकर्णंमहोदरः । उवाचरक्षसांमध्येरावणंलोकरावणम् ।।6.64.19।।
output: महोदरः Mahodara, रक्षसाम् Rakshasas, मध्ये midst, सम्रब्दम् agitated, कुम्भकर्णम् to Kumbhakarna, एवम् in this way, उक्त्वा having spoken, लोकरावणम् one who makes people cry, रावणम् Ravana, उवाच replied.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
लब्ध्वापुनस्त्वंवैदेहींकिमर्थंसम्प्रजल्पसि । यदीच्छसितदासीतावशगातेभविष्यति ।।6.64.20।।
output: "Having got Vaidehi, why are you talking like that? Sita will submit to you if you desire."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
दृष्टःकश्चदुपायोमेसीतोपस्थानकारकः । रुचितश्चेत्स्वयाबुध्याराक्षसेन्द्र तंशृणु ।।6.64.21।।
output: "O King of Rakshasas! A means of bringing her round is known to me. Listen, think over with your intellect."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 64:
अहंद्विजिह्वस्सम्ह्रादीकुम्भकर्णोवितर्दनः । पञ्चरामवधायैतेनिर्यान्त्वित्यवघोषय ।।6.64.22।।
output: "You pronounce that I, Dwijihva, Samhradri, Kumbhakarna and Vitardana, five of us will go forth to kill Rama."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततोगत्वावयंयुद्धंदास्यामस्तस्ययत्नतः । जेष्यामोयदितेशत्रून्नोपायैःकृत्यमस्तिनः ।।6.64.23।।
output: "Thereafter, proceeding forth we shall try to win your enemy. If we win, there will be no purpose for you to do any action."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अथजीवतिनश्शत्रुर्वयं च कृतसम्युगाः । ततस्तदभिपत्स्यामोमनसायत्समीक्षितम् ।।6.64.24।।
output: थ if, नः not, शत्रुः enemy, जीवति survives, कृतसम्युगाः in the combat, वयं च we too, ततः that, मनसा mind, यत् like that, समीक्षितम् will review, तदभिपत्स्यामः we will see.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
वयंयुद्धादिहेष्यामोरुधिरेणसमुक्षिताः । विदार्यस्वतनुंबाणैरामनामाङ्कितैश्शितैः ।।6.64.25।।
output: वयम् we, रामनामाङ्कितैः marked with Rama's name, बाणैः arrows, शितैः torn, स्वतनुम् our bodies, विदार्य cruelly, रुधिरेण blood, समुक्षिताः wounded, युद्धात् from war, इहे here, एष्यामः will come.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
भक्षितोराघवोऽस्माभिर्लक्ष्मणश्चेतिवादिनः । तवपादौग्रहीष्यामस्त्वंनःकामंप्रपूरय ।।6.64.26।।
output: अस्माभिः we too, राघवः Raghava, लक्ष्मणश्च Lakshmana's, भक्षितः devoured, इति thus, वादिनः saying, तव your, पादौ feet, ग्रहीष्यावः holding, त्वम् your, नः not, कामम् desires, प्रपूरय grant.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततोऽवघोषयपुरेगजस्कन्धेनपार्थिव । हतोरामस्सहभ्रात्राससैन्यइतिसर्वतः ।।6.64.27।।
output: "Thereafter mounted on elephant backs all over the city will make a rakshasa pronounce that Rama accompanied by his brother are killed."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
प्रीतोनामततोभूत्वाभृत्यानांत्वमरिन्दम । भोगांश्चपरिवारांश्चकामांश्चवसुदापय ।।6.64.28।।
output: "O tamer of enemies! In the name of expression of happiness, thereafter gift items of enjoyment to the attendants, and companions and granting wealth as per their desire.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 64:
ततोमाल्यानिवासांसिवीराणामनुलेपनम् । पेयं च बहुयोधेभ्यस्स्वयं च मुदितःपिब ।।6.64.29।।
output: "Thereafter give your warriors, garlands, cosmetics and many drinks and drink yourself happily."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततोऽस्मिन् बहुलीभूतेकौलीनेसर्वतोगते । भक्षितस्ससुहृद्रामोराक्षसैरितिविश्रुते ।।6.64.30।। प्रविश्याश्वास्यचापित्वंसीतांरहसिसान्त्वय । धनधान्यैश्चकामैश्चरत्नैश्चानांप्रलोभय ।।6.64.31।।
output: ततः thereafter, ससुहृत् Lakshmana and friends, रामः Rama, राक्षसैः Rakshasas, भक्षितः devoured, इति this, अस्मिन् other, बहुलीभूते spread, कौलीने sc and al, सर्वतोग e very where, विश्रुते widely, त्वम् you, प्रविश्य entering, सीताम् to Sita, आश्वास्य consoling, रहसि privately, सान्त्वय restoring confidence, एनाम् in that way, धनधान्यैश्च grain and wealth, कामैश्च tempting, रत्नैश्च gems, प्रलोभय conciliate.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 64:
ततोऽस्मिन् बहुलीभूतेकौलीनेसर्वतोगते । भक्षितस्ससुहृद्रामोराक्षसैरितिविश्रुते ।।6.64.30।। प्रविश्याश्वास्यचापित्वंसीतांरहसिसान्त्वय । धनधान्यैश्चकामैश्चरत्नैश्चानांप्रलोभय ।।6.64.31।।
output: Thereafter, when the scandal that Rama and Lakshmana with all his friends have been devoured is widely spread everywhere, approaching Sita privately, restoring confidence and consoling her, tempt her with offering wealth, grain and gems and conciliate.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 64:
अनयोपधयाराजन् भयशोकानुबन्धया । अकामात्वद्वशंसीतानष्टनाथाभविष्यति ।।6.64.32।।
output: "O King! By conjuring her like this, helpless Sita overtaken by fear and sorrow having lost her husband will submit to you in spite of no desire to you."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ञ्जनीयम्हिभर्तारंविनष्टमवगम्यसा । नैराश्यात् स्त्रीलघुत्वाच्चत्वद्वशंप्रतिपत्स्यते ।।6.64.33।।
output: सा she, रञ्जनीयम् charming, भर्तारम् husband, विनष्टम् ceased, अवगम्य thinking, नैराश्यात् with no alternative, स्त्रीलघुत्वाच्च fickle being woman, त्वद्वशम् accept, प्रतिपत्स्यते your dependence.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सापुरासुखसम्वृद्धासुखार्हादुःखकर्शिता । त्वय्यधीनंसुखंज्ञात्वासर्वथोगमिष्यति ।।6.64.34।।
output: पुरा in the past, सुखसम्वृद्धा grew up with much comfort, सुखार्हा deserved felicity, दुःखकर्शिता tormented with grief, सा she, सुखम् happiness, त्वयि you alone, अधीनम् desperate, ज्ञात्वा knowing, सर्वधा always, उपगमिष्यति will submit to your will.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
एतत्सुनीतंममदर्शनेनरामंहिदृष्टवैभवेदनर्धः । इहैवतेसेत्स्यतिमोत्सुकोभूर्महानयुद्धेनसुखस्यलाभः ।।6.64.35।।
output: "To me this is the best course. As soon as you see Rama, do not be eager for war. It is meaningless. Great gain will accrue to you from here."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 64:
अदृष्टसैन्योह्यनवाप्तसंशयोरिपूनयुद्धेनजयन् जनाधिप । यशश्चपुण्यं च महन्महीपतेश्रशियं च कीर्तिं च चिरं ।।6.64.36।।
output: "O Lord of the people! If a king conquers his enemy without any loss of army, without facing any dangerand without war, such a mighty ruler of the earth will indeed earn fame and merit and attain prosperity." ।।इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेचतुष्षष्टितमस्सर्गः।। This is the end of the sixty fourth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स तथोक्तस्तुनिर्भर्त्स्यकुम्भकर्णोमहोदरम् । अब्रवीद्राक्षसश्रेष्ठंभ्रातरंरावणंततः ।।6.65.1।।
output: तथा in that way, उक्तः having said, कुम्भकर्णः Kumbhakarna, महोदरम् to Mahodara, निर्भर्त्स्य warned, ततः then, राक्षसश्रेष्ठम् foremost of Rakshasas, रावणम् to Ravana, अब्रवीत् spoke.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सोऽहंतवभयंघोरंवधात्तस्यदुरात्मनः । रामस्याद्यप्रमार्जामिनिर्वैरोहिसुखीभव ।।6.65.2।।
output: सःअहम् you, my, दुरात्मनः cruel minded, तस्यरामस्य that Rama's, वधात् with killing, तव your, घोरम् dreadful, भयम् fear, अद्य now, प्रमार्जामि will get rid of, निर्वैरः enmity, सुखी happily, भव you be.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
गर्जन्ति न वृथाशूरानिर्जलाइवतोयदाः । पश्यसम्पद्यमानंतुगर्जितंयुधिकर्मणा ।।6.65.3।।
output: "Warriors will not roar wastefully like waterless clouds. You will see me roaring after having completed the action."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
न मर्षयन्तिचात्मानंसम्भावयतिनात्मना । अदर्शयित्वाशूरास्तुकर्मकुर्वन्तिदुष्करम् ।।6.65.4।।
output: "Warriors do not tolerate even when glorified. They never praise themselves. They accomplish difficult deeds without displaying them."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
विक्लबानामबुद्धीनांराज्ञापण्डितमानिनाम् । श्रृण्वतासदितमिदंत्वाद्विधानांमहोदर ।।6.65.5।।
output: महोदर Mahodara, विक्लबानाम् cowardly, पण्डितमानिनाम् devoid of intellect, अबुद्धीनाम् not knowing anything, त्वद्विधानाम् as if knowing, श्रृण्वता on hearing, इदं this, सादितम् appeal.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
युद्धेकापुरुषैर्नित्यंभवद्भिःप्रियवादिभि: । राजानमनुगच्छद्भिःसर्वंकृत्यमोद्धिसादितम् ।।6.65.6।।
output: "You, who always fear in combat, are talking pleasingly to the king , going after him happily brought the matter to this state."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
राजशेषाकृतालङ्काक्षीणःकोशोबलंहतम् । राजानमिममासाद्यसुहृचचिह्नममित्रकम् ।।6.65.7।।
output: "The king is left alone in Lanka, which is divested of its wealth, and treasury reduced, and the army destroyed by unfriendly people pretending as good friends around him."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
एषनिर्याम्यहंयुद्धमुद्यतश्शत्रुनिर्जये । दुर्नयंभवतामद्यसमीकर्तुंमिहाहवे ।।6.65.8।।
output: "I am setting out in this manner to the battlefield, to overpower the enemies in the battle in order to redeem the mistakes done by all of you."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
एवमुक्तवतोवाक्यंकुम्भकर्णस्यधीमतः । प्रत्युवाचततोवाक्यंप्रहसन्राक्षसाधिपः ।।6.65.9।।
output: Wise Kumbhakarna having spoken in that way, the Rakshasa king, Ravana laughed and replied in this way.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
महोदरोऽयंरामात्तुपरित्रस्तो न संशयः । न हिरोचयतेतात युद्धंयुद्धविशारद ।।6.65.10।।
output: "O dear! You are an expert in war! This Mahodara is terrified at Rama. He is not desiring war. There is no doubt."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कश्चिन्मेत्वत्समोनास्तिसौहृदेनबलेन च । गच्छशत्रुवधायत्वंकुम्भकर्णजयाय च ।।6.65.11।।
output: कुम्भकर्ण Kumbakarna, सौहृदेन with friendly feeling at heart, बलेन च mighty, त्वत्समः equal to you, कश्चित् indeed, नास्ति not, त्वम् you, शत्रुवधाय by killing the enemy, जयाय च victorious, गच्छ will go.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तस्मात्तुशत्रुनाशार्थंभवान्सम्बोधितोमया । अयंहिकालस्सुहृदांराक्षसानामरिन्दम ।।6.65.12।।
output: "You are difficult to encounter. You have awakened for the sake of putting an end to the enemy. It is a momentous period for the Rakshasas, O tamer of enemies."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तद्गच्छशूलमादायपाशहस्तइवान्तकः । वानरान्राजपुत्रौ च भक्ष्यादित्यतेजसा ।।6.65.13।।
output: "Therefore, taking up trident holding the noose in hand like the God of Death proceed to devour the monkeys as well as the two princes shining like the Sun."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
समालोक्यतुतेरूपंविद्रविष्यन्तिवानराः । रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चापिहृदयेप्रस्फुटिष्यतः ।।6.65.14।।
output: "Seeing your form, the Vanaras will run away, Rama and Lakshmana's heart will break."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
एवमुक्त्वामहातेजाःकुम्भकर्णंमहाबलम् । पुनर्जातमिवात्मानंमेनेराक्षसपुङ्गवः ।।6.65.15।।
output: The highly energetic king of Rakshasas having spoken like that to mighty Kumbhakarna, felt as if he had taken birth again.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
कुम्भकर्णबलाभिज्ञोजानंस्तस्यपराक्रमम् । बभूवमुदितोराजाशशाङ्कइवनिर्मलः ।।6.65.16।।
output: The king who knew the valour and mighty strength of Kumbhakarna remained happy like the moon.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इत्येवमुक्तःसम्हृष्टोनिर्जगाममहाबलः । राज्ञस्तुवचनंश्रुत्वाकुम्भकर्णस्समुद्यत:।। 6.65.17।।
output: The king having spoken these words, mighty Kumbhakarna, pleased with the king's words set forth to fight.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
आददेनिशितंशूलंवेगाच्छत्रुनिबर्हणम् । सर्वकालायसंदीप्तंतप्तकाञ्चनभूषणम् ।।6.65.18।।
output: The destroyer of enemies, hurriedly seized a whetted flaming iron dart, embellished with polished gold.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इन्द्राशनिसमंभीमंवज्रप्रतिमगौरवम् । देवदानवगन्धर्वयक्षपन्नगसूदनम् ।।6.65.19 ।। रक्तमाल्यंमहाधामंस्वतश्चोद्गतपावकम् । आदायनिशितंशूलंशत्रुशोणितरञ्जितम् ।।6.65.20।। कुम्भकर्णोमहातेजारावणंवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
output: The dart was like Indra's thunderbolt in form and was equal to thunderbolt, capable of destroying Devas, Danavas, Gandharvas, Yakshas and Pannagas, was like rising fire shining like the face of an enemy. It was sharp, wreathed in garlands of red colour and emitting flame. Kumbhakarna wielding the dart said.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
इन्द्राशनिसमंभीमंवज्रप्रतिमगौरवम् । देवदानवगन्धर्वयक्षपन्नगसूदनम् ।।6.65.19 ।। रक्तमाल्यंमहाधामंस्वतश्चोद्गतपावकम् । आदायनिशितंशूलंशत्रुशोणितरञ्जितम् ।।6.65.20।। कुम्भकर्णोमहातेजारावणंवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
output: महातेजाः highly energetic, कुम्भकर्णः Kumbhakarna, इन्द्राशनिसमभीमम् equal to Indra in prowess, वज्रप्रतिमगौरवम् like Indra's thunderbolt in form, देवदानवगन्धर्वयक्षपन्नगसूदनम् Devas, Danavas, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Pannagas,, रक्तमाल्यमहाधाम wearing red coloured garland s, स्वतः himself, उद्गतपावकम् like the rising fire, शत्रुशोणितरञ्चितम् shining like the face of enemy, निशितम् sharp, शूलम् trident, आदाय wielding, रावणम् Ravana, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
गमिष्याम्यहमेकाकीतिष्ठत्विहबलंमम ।।6.65.21।। अद्यतान् क्षुभितान् क्रुद्धोभक्षयिष्यामिवानरान् ।
output: Enraged and angry Kumbhakarna said, "I will proceed now. Let my army remain here. I will consume them on keys today."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
कुम्भकर्णवचश्श्रुत्वारावणोवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।।6.65.22।। सैन्यैःपरिवृतोगच्छशूलमुद्गतपाणिभिः ।
output: Hearing Kumbhakarna's words Ravana said," Go with trident, sword and iron bar in hand surrounded by the army."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
वानराहिमहात्मानश्शीघ्रास्सव्यवसायिनः ।।6.65.23।। एकाकिनंप्रमत्तंवानयेयुद्धशनैःक्ष्यम् ।
output: महात्मानः gigantic, शीघ्रा: endowed with speed, सुव्यवसायिनः full of determination, वानराः Vanaras, एकाकिनम् alone, प्रमत्तंवा not alert, दशनैः with teeth, क्ष्यम् destroy.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तस्मात्परमदुर्धर्षै: सैन्यैःपरिवृतोव्रज ।।6.65.24।। रक्षसामहितंसर्वंशत्रुपक्षंनिषूदय ।
output: तस्मात् therefore, सैन्यैः army, परिवृतः surrounded, परमदुर्धर्षै: extremely difficult to encounter, रक्षसाम् for Rakshasas, अहितम् not favourable, सर्वम् all, शत्रुपक्षम् enemy side, निषूदय destroy.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अथासनात्समुत्पत्यस्रजं मणिकृतान्तराम् ।।6.65.25।। आबबन्धमहातेजाःकुम्भकर्णस्यरावणः ।
output: अथ and then, महातेजाः extremely brilliant, रावणः Ravana, आसनात् from the seat, समुत्पत्य got up, मणिकृतान्तराम् encrusted with gems, स्रजम् garland of flowers, कुम्भकर्णस्य Kumbhakarna's, आबबन्ध adorned.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अङ्गदान्यङ्गुलीवेष्टान्वराण्याभरणानि च ।।6.65.26।। हारं च श्शिसङ्काशमाबबन्दमहात्मनः ।
output: Then Ravana placed armlets, rings, exquisite ornaments, garland s of pearls like moonlight on Kumbhakarna's neck.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
दिव्यानि च सुगन्धीनिमाल्यदामानिरावणः ।।6.65.27।। श्रोत्रिचासञ्जयामासश्रीमतीचास्यकुण्डले ।
output: रावणः Ravana, अस्य his, श्रोत्रे crown, च also, दिव्यानि wonderful, सुगन्धीनि fragrant, माल्यदामानि garlands, श्रीमति prosperous, कुण्डले च ear rings, असञ्जयामास suspended.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
काञ्चनाङ्गदकेयूरोनिष्काभरणभूषितः ।।6.65.28।। कुम्भकर्णोबृहत्कर्णस्सुहुतोऽग्निरिवाबभौ ।
output: Adorned with armlets studded with gems and golden ornaments on his distinguished large ears, Kumbhakarna shone like fire.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
श्रोणीसूत्रेणमहतामेचकेनव्यराजत ।।6.65.29।। अमृतोत्पादनेनद्धोभुजङ्गेनेवमन्दरः ।
output: Adorned with a huge dark girdle, Kumbhakarna seemed like a bright jewel like Mount Mandara used for churning nectar of immortality fastened by Vasuki.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
स काञ्चनंभारसहंनिवातंविद्युत्प्रभंदीप्तमिवात्मभासा । आबध्यमानःकवचंरराजसन्ध्याभ्रसम्वीतराजः ।।6.65.30।।
output: Kumbhakarna decked in heavy golden shield (impenetrable by any weapon) and difficult to break, seemed like the lightning with self effulgence, glowing like fire, shone like the evening twilight around the mountain peak.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सर्वाभरणसर्वाङ्गश्शूलपाणिस्सराक्षसः । त्रिविक्रमकृतोत्साहोनारायणइवाबभौ ।।6.65.31।। भ्रातरंसम्परिष्वज्यकृत्वाचापिप्रदक्षिणम् । प्रणम्यशिरसातस्मैसम्प्रतस्थेमहाबलः ।।6.65.32।।
output: Decked with ornaments on all his limbs, with pike in hand, the Rakshasa was like Narayana ready to take three strides to cover the universe. Endowed with great strength, embraced his brother, went round in reverence bowing down his head and sallied forth.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सर्वाभरणसर्वाङ्गश्शूलपाणिस्सराक्षसः । त्रिविक्रमकृतोत्साहोनारायणइवाबभौ ।।6.65.31।। भ्रातरंसम्परिष्वज्यकृत्वाचापिप्रदक्षिणम् । प्रणम्यशिरसातस्मैसम्प्रतस्थेमहाबलः ।।6.65.32।।
output: सर्वाभरण decked with ornaments on all his limbs, सर्वाङ्ग all limbs, श्शूलपाणिस्स pike in hand, राक्षसः the Rakshasa, त्रिविक्रमकृतोत्साहो ready to take his three strides, नारायणइवाबभौ like Narayana, महाबलः endowed with great strength, भ्रातरम् brother, सम्परिष्वज्य embracing, प्रदक्षिणम् going round, कृत्वा having done चापि also, तस्मै his, शिरसा head, प्रणम्य bowing down in reverence, सम्प्रतस्थे sallied forth.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
निष्पतन्तंमहाकायंमहानादंमहाबलम् । तमाशीर्भिःप्रशस्ताभिःप्रेषयामासरावणः ।।6.65.33।।
output: Kumbhakarna, of huge body, of loud voice and highly capable having been dismissed by Ravana, went with the great army after benediction and started observing.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैस्सैन्यैश्चापिवरायुथैः । तंगजैश्चतुरङ्गैश्चस्यन्दनैश्चाम्बुदस्वनैः ।।6.65.34।। अनुजग्मुर्महात्मानं रथिनो रथिनां वरम् ।
output: Many great warriors seated on the best of chariots, with best of weapons amidst noise of conchs and drums, elephants, horses also and thunder like chariot warriors, started to proceed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सर्पैरुष्ट्रैःखरैरश्वैस्सिम्हद्विपमृगद्विजैः । अनुजग्मुश्चतंघोरंकुम्भकर्णंमहाबलम् ।।6.65.35।।
output: घोरम् dreadful, महाबलम् mighty, तम् them, कुम्भकर्णम् Kumbhakarna, सर्पैः serpents, उष्ट्रैः camels, खरै: donkeys, अश्वै: horses, सिम्हद्विपमृगद्विजैः lions, antelopes, birds, अनुजग्मुः followed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स पुष्पवर्षैरवकीर्यमाणोधृतातपत्रःशितशूलपाणिः । मदोत्कटःशोणितगन्धमत्तोविनिर्ययौदावनदेवशत्रुः ।।6.65.36।।
output: धृतातपत्रः determined and eager, शितशूलपाणि sharpened tridents in hand, मदोत्कटः excited by drink, शोणितगद्धमत्तः smeared with blood red fragrant sandal paste, दानवदेवशत्रुः enemy of Danavas and Devatas, सः he, पुष्पवर्षैः showering rain of flowers, अवकीर्यमाणः parasol covered his head, विनिर्ययौ sallied forth.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
पदातयश्चबहवोमहानादामहाबलाः । अन्वयूराक्षसाभीमाभीमाक्षाश्शस्त्रपाणयः ।।6.65.37।।
output: Rakshasas of loud voice, great prowess, and fearful with frightening eyes, lifted the many weapons in hand and followed on foot.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
रक्ताक्षास्सुमहाकायानीलाञ्चनचयोपमाः । शूलानुद्यम्यखडगांश्चनिशितांश्चपरश्वधान् ।।6.65.38।। बहुव्यामांश्चपरिघान्गदाश्चमुसलानि च । तालस्कन्धांश्चविपुलान्क्षेपणीयान्दुरासदान् ।।6.65.39।।
output: रक्ताक्षाः of blood red eyes, सुमहाकायाः of huge body size, नीलाञ्चनचयोपमाः dark blue coloured perplexed, शूलान् tridents, खडगांश्च swords, निशितान् sharpened, परश्वधान् whetted axes, बहुव्यामांश्च many kinds, परिघान् iron bars, गदाश्च maces also, मुसलानि च clubs, क्षेपणीयान् mallets, दुरासदान् evil minded, विपुलान् vast, तालस्कन्धांश्च palmyra trees, उद्यम्य set out

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
रक्ताक्षास्सुमहाकायानीलाञ्चनचयोपमाः । शूलानुद्यम्यखडगांश्चनिशितांश्चपरश्वधान् ।।6.65.38।। बहुव्यामांश्चपरिघान्गदाश्चमुसलानि च । तालस्कन्धांश्चविपुलान्क्षेपणीयान्दुरासदान् ।।6.65.39।।
output: Rakshasas with blood red eyes, of huge body size, dark blue in colour, holding tridents, sharpened whetted axes and weapons of many kinds, iron bars and maces, clubs, mallets and palmyra trees, the evil minded vast army set out.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अथान्यद्वपुरादायदारुणंरोमहर्षणम् । निष्पपातमहातेजाःकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः ।।6.65.40।। धनुःशतपरीणाहः स षट्छत्रसमुच्छ्रितः । रौद्रःशकटचक्राक्षोमहापर्वतसन्निभः ।।6.65.41।।
output: अथ and then, महातेजाः extremely energetic, महाबलः endowed with mighty strength, सःकुम्भकर्णः that Kumbhakarna, दारुणम् fearful appearance, रोमहर्षणम् horripilating, अन्यत् वपुः another form, आदाय taking hold, धनुःशतपरीणाहः hundred bows in breadth, षट्छत्रसमुच्छ्रितः six hundred bows in length, शकटचक्राक्षः wheels of chariot, महापर्वतसन्निभः like a huge mountain, रौद्रः enraged, निष्पपात set out .

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अथान्यद्वपुरादायदारुणंरोमहर्षणम् । निष्पपातमहातेजाःकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः ।।6.65.40।। धनुःशतपरीणाहः स षट्छत्रसमुच्छ्रितः । रौद्रःशकटचक्राक्षोमहापर्वतसन्निभः ।।6.65.41।।
output: अथ and then, महातेजाः extremely energetic, महाबलः endowed with mighty strength, सःकुम्भकर्णः that Kumbhakarna, दारुणम् fearful appearance, रोमहर्षणम् horripilating, अन्यत् वपुः another form, आदाय taking hold, धनुःशतपरीणाहः hundred bows in breadth, षट्छत्रसमुच्छ्रितः six hundred bows in length, शकटचक्राक्षः wheels of chariot, महापर्वतसन्निभः like a huge mountain, रौद्रः enraged, निष्पपात set out .

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
सन्निपत्य च रक्षांसिदग्धशैलोपमामहान् । कुम्भकर्णोमहावक्त्रःप्रहसन्निदमब्रवीत् ।।6.65.42।।
output: Thus spoke, Kumbhakarna who resembled a charred mountain, with wide mouth, reaching near the Rakshasas, laughing.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
अद्यवानरमुख्यानांतानियूथानिभागश । निर्दहिष्यामिसङ्ख्रुद्धश्शलाभानिवपावकः ।।6.65.43।।
output: Thereafter, furious Kumbhakarna said "Now I will consume all the battalions of Vanaras just as moths are consumed by fire."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
नापराध्यन्तिमेकामंवानरा: वनचारिणः । जातिरस्मद्विधानांसापुरोद्यानविभूषणम् ।।6.65.44।।
output: "These forest rangers have never desired to do any harm to me. This clan serve as ornaments of our gardens."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
पुररोधस्यमूलंतुराघवस्सहलक्ष्मणः । हतेतस्मिन् हतंसर्वंतंवधिष्यामिसंयुगे ।।6.65.45।।
output: सहलक्ष्मणः accompanied by Lakshmana, राघवः Raghava, पुररोधस्य be seized, मूलम् root cause, तस्मिन् their, हते killed, सर्वम् all, हतम् killed, संयुगे in combat, तम् them, वधिष्यामि destroy.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
एवंतस्यब्रुवाणस्यकुम्भकर्णस्यराक्षसाः । नादंचक्रुर्महाघोरंकम्पयन्तइवार्णवम् ।।6.65.46।।
output: When Kumbhakarna had spoken that way the Rakshasas made noise that was like the sound of an agitated ocean.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
तस्यनिष्पततस्तूर्णंकुम्भकर्णस्यधीमतः । बभूवुर्घोररूपाणिनिमित्तानिसमन्ततः ।।6.65.47।।
output: As wise Kumbhakarna was proceeding swiftly , dreadful portents appeared.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
उल्काशनियुतामेघाबभूवुर्गर्धभारुणाः । ससागरवनाचैववसुधासमकम्पत ।।6.65.48।।
output: उल्काशनियुताः thunder and lightning, गर्धभारुणाः donkey coloured, मेघाः clouds, बभूवुः appeared, ससागरवना ocean and forests, वसुधा च earth, समकम्पत was shaken.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
घोररूपाश्शिवानेदुस्सज्वालकबलैर्मुखैः । मण्डलान्यपसव्यानिबबन्धुश्चविहङ्गमाः ।।6.65.49।।
output: She jackals were seen with flaming morsels throwing from their mouths. Birds wheeled in a circular way and settled.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
निष्पपात च गृध्रोमालेवाऽस्यपथिगच्छतः । प्रास्फुरन्नयनंचास्यसव्योबाहुश्चकम्पत ।।6.65.50।।
output: पथि on the way, गच्छतः marching, अस्य his, शूले pike, गृध्रः eagle, निष्पपाप alighted, अस्य his, नयनम् eyes, प्रास्फुरत् twitched, सव्यः left, बाहुश्च shoulder, कम्पते throbbed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
निष्पपाततदाचोल्काज्वलन्तीभीमनिश्श्वना । आदित्योनिष्प्रभश्चासीन्नप्रवाति च ऽनिलः ।।6.65.51।।
output: तदा then, ज्वलन्ती burning meteor, भीमterrible sound, उल्का from the sky, निष्पपात fallen, आदित्यःच sun too, निष्प्रभः without glow, आसीत् dropped, अनिलः wind, सुखः not delightful, न प्रवाति च not blown.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अचिन्तयन्महोत्पातानुदितान्रोमहर्षणान् । निर्ययौकुम्भकर्णस्तुकृतान्तबलचोदितः ।।6.65.52।।
output: Kumbhakarna went unmindful of the portents which made hair stand on end propelled by the force of destiny.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
न लङ्घयित्वाप्राकारंपद्भ्यांपर्वतसन्निभः । ददर्शाभ्रघनप्रख्यंवानरानीकमद्भुतम् ।।6.65.53।।
output: He who resembled a mountain in form, leapt the boundary wall on foot like a cloud and witnessed the amazing Vanara troops.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तेदृष्टवाराक्षसश्रेष्ठंवानराःपर्वतोपमम् । वायुनुन्नाइवघनाययुस्सर्वादिशस्तदा ।।6.65.54।।
output: तेवानराः those Vanaras, पर्वतोपमम् like a mountain, राक्षसश्रेष्ठम् foremost of Rakshasas, दृष्टवा seeing, तदा then, वायुनुन्नाः swept by wind, घनाःइव like clouds, सर्वाः all, दिशः directions, ययुः dispersed.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
तद्वानरानीकमतिप्रचण्डंदिशोद्रवद्भिन्नमवाभ्रजालम् । स कुम्भकर्णस्समवेक्ष्यहर्षान्ननादभूयोघनवद्घनाभः ।।6.65.55।।
output: Heavy cloud like Kumbhakarna, a notorious one, perceiving the Vanara troops scattered like clouds in all directions emitted roar, laughing aloud.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
तेतस्यघोरंनिनदंनिशम्ययथानिनादंदिविवारिदस्य । पेतुर्धरण्यांबहवःप्लवङ्गानिकृत्तमूलाइवशालवृक्षाः ।।6.65.56।।
output: Hearing the dreadful roar of Kumbhakarna, that resembled the rumbling of clouds, many Vanaras fell on the ground like severed Sala trees.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 65:
विपुलपरिघवान् स कुम्भकर्णोरिपुनिधनायविनिस्पृतोत्मा । कपिषणभयमाददत्सुभीमंप्रभुरिवदण्डवान्युगान्ते ।।6.65.57।।
output: Armed with a huge iron bar, Kumbhakarna stood for destroying the enemies like the great time spirit, deadly God of Death waits at the end of the universe along with Kinkaras, like a king. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेपञ्चाषष्टितमस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the sixty fifth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic, the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स लङ्घयित्वाप्राकारंगिरिकूटोपमोमहान् । निर्ययौनगरात्तूर्णंकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः ।।6.66.1।।
output: Angada restores courage and confidence of Vanaras who feared Kumbhakarna and were fleeing from the battlefield. Destruction of some Vanaras at the hand s of Kumbhakarna.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ननाद च महानादंसमुद्रमभिनादयन् । विजयन्निवनिर्घातन्विधमन्निवपर्वतान् ।।6.66.2।।
output: निर्घातान् bringing out loud noise,विजयत्रि as if proclaiming victory, पर्वतान् mountains, विधमन् इव like breaking, महानादम् great sound, समुद्रम् ocean, अभिनादयन् reverberate, नादयन roared.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तमवध्यंमघवतायमेनवरुणेनवा । प्रेक्ष्यभीमाक्षमायान्तंवानराविप्रदुद्रुवुः ।।6.66.3।।
output: मघवता by Indra, यमेनby Yama, वरुणेनवा or even Varuna, अवध्यम् not be killed, भीमाक्षम् with frightening eyes, तम् him, प्रेक्ष्य observing, वानराः the Vanaras, विप्रदुद्रुवुः ran in fear.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 66:
तांस्तुविप्रद्रुतान् दृष्टवाराजपुत्रोऽङ्गदोऽब्रवीत् । नलंनीलंगवाक्षं च कुमुदं च महाबलम् ।।6.66.4।।
output: Seeing the Vanaras running in fear, Angada spoke to Nala, Nila, Gavaksha, Mahabala and Kumuda.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
आत्मानमत्रविस्मृत्यवीर्याण्यभिजनानि च । क्वगच्छतभयत्रस्ताःप्राकृताहरयोयथा ।।6.66.5।।
output: आत्मानम् yourself, अत्र there, वीर्याणि warriors, अभिजनानि च not knowing, विस्मृत्य forgetting, प्राकृताः by nature, हरयःयथा like the Vanaras, भयत्रस्ताः fearing, क्व where, गच्छत are you going.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
साधुसौम्या निवर्तध्वंकिप्राणान्परिरक्षथ । नालंयुद्धायवैरक्षोमहतीयंबिभीषका ।।6.66.6।।
output: सौम्याः good, साधु modest, निवर्तध्वम् return, प्राणान् life, किम् why, परिरक्षथ protecting, रक्षः Rakshasa, युद्धाय in war, नालम् not capable facing, इयम् this, महती great, बिभीषिका who can create fear.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
महतीमुथतितामेनांराक्षसानांबिभीषिकाम् । विक्रमाद्विधमिष्यामोनिवर्तध्वंप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.66.7।।
output: प्लवङ्गमाः Vanaras, राक्षसानाम् Rakshasas, उथतिताम् dispel, महतीम् huge, एनांबिभीषिकाम् this nightmare, विक्रमात् with our power, विधमिष्यामः kill them, निवर्तध्वम् come back.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कृच्छ्रेणतुसमाश्वस्यसङ्गम्य च ततस्ततः । वृक्षाद्रिहस्ताहरयस्सम्प्रतस्थूरणाजिरम् ।।6.66.8।।
output: Overcoming fear, the Vanaras getting together from here and there holding trees by hand, proceeded to the battlefield.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तेनिवृत्यतुसङ्कृद्धाःकुम्भकर्णंवनौकसः । निर्जघ्नुःपरमक्रुद्धास्समदाइवकुञ्जराः ।।6.66.9।।
output: Those forest rangers who were extremely enraged turned back to hit, determined like the elephants in rut went to vanquish Kumbhakarna.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
प्रांशुभिर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्चशिलाभिश्चमहाबलः । पादपैःपुष्पिताग्रैश्चहन्यमानो न कम्पते ।।6.66.10।।
output: शुभिः lofty, गिरिशृङ्गैश्च mountain peaks, शिलाभिश्च rocks also, पुष्टिताग्रैः trees with blossoms on top tops, पादपैः trees, हन्यमानः though hit, महाबलः Kumbhakarna, न कम्पते not shaken.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 66:
तस्यगात्रेषुपतिताभिद्यन्तेशतशश्शिलाः । पादपाःपुष्पिताग्राश्चभग्नाःपेतुर्महीतले ।।6.66.11।।
output: Fallen on his limbs many rocks got broken, even the treetops with blossoms were broken and fell on the ground.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सोऽपिसैन्यानिसङ्क्रुद्धोवानराणांमहौजसाम् । ममन्थपरमायत्तोवनान्यग्निरिवोत्थितः ।।6.66.12।।
output: Enraged Kumbhakarna began to destroy Vanaras endowed with extraordinary vigour, just as great forest fire burns the forest.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 66:
लोहितार्द्रास्तुबहवश्शेरतेवानरर्षभाः । निरस्तांपतिताभूमौताम्रपुष्पाइवद्रुमाः ।।6.66.13।।
output: Many bulls among the Vanaras lay on the ground like trees with red flowers on top tossed and fallen on the ground.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
लङ्घयन्तःप्रधावन्तोवानरानावलोकयन् । केचित्समुद्रेपतिताःकेचिद्गगनमास्थिताः ।।6.66.14।।
output: The Vanaras leapt without looking back. Indeed, some dropped into the ocean, and some flew into space.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 66:
वध्यमानास्तुतेवीराराक्षसेन च लीलया । सागरंयेनतेतीर्णाःपथातेनदुद्रुवुः ।।6.66.15।।
output: Struck by Rakshasa, the Vanaras ran in the same path crossing the ocean (by which they came).

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 66:
तेस्थलानितदानिम्नंविवर्णमानाभयात् । ऋक्षावृक्षान् समारूढाःकेचित्पर्वतमाश्रिताः ।।6.66.16।।
output: Out of fear the vanaras rushed to plains with pale countenance, some climbed up mountains and bears climbed up trees.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ममज्जुरर्णवेकेचिद्गुहाःकेचित्समाश्रिताः । निपेतुःकेचिदपरेकेचिन्नैवावतस्थिरे ।।6.66.17।। केचिद्भूमौनिपतिताःकेचित्सुप्तामृताइव ।
output: Some drowned in the ocean, some entered into the caves, some others not knowing what to do sat down and others fell on the ground and some slept as if dead.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तान्समीक्ष्याङ्गदोभग्नान्वानरानिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.66.18।। अवतिष्ठतयुध्यामोनिवर्तध्वंप्लवङ्गमाः ।
output: Seeing the monkeys routed, Angada spoke, 'Stay, return back. We will fight'

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
भग्नानांवो न पश्यामिपरिगम्यमहीमिमाम् ।।6.66.19।। स्थानंसर्वेनिवर्तध्वंकिंप्राणान् परिरक्षथ ।
output: इमाम् this, महीम् globe, परिक्रम्य go round, भग्नानाम् routed, वः or, स्थानम् place, न पश्यामि not see, सर्वे all, निवर्तध्वम् return, प्राणान् life, किम् why, परिरक्षथ refuge.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 66:
निरायुधानांद्रवतामसङ्गगतिपौरुषाः ।।6.66.20।। दाराह्युपहसिष्यन्ति स वैघातस्तुजीवताम् ।
output: "Monkeys! Your valour can't be challenged. If you run away for life abandoning weapons even your wives will ridicule you. That is more than death."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 66:
कुलेषुजातास्सर्वेस्मविस्तीर्णेषुमहत्सु च ।।6.66.21।। क्वगच्छतभयत्रस्ताःहरयःप्राकृतायथा । अनार्याःखलुयद्भीतास्त्यक्त्वावीर्यंप्रधावत ।।6.66.22।।
output: "You are born in noble families, and are widely spread. As such why are you running away like ordinary monkeys as if terrified giving up your valour. It is not worthy of you."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कुलेषुजातास्सर्वेस्मविस्तीर्णेषुमहत्सु च ।।6.66.21।। क्वगच्छतभयत्रस्ताःहरयःप्राकृतायथा । अनार्याःखलुयद्भीतास्त्यक्त्वावीर्यंप्रधावत ।।6.66.22।।
output: "You are born in noble families, and are widely spread. As such why are you running away like ordinary monkeys as if terrified giving up your valour. It is not worthy of you."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
विकत्थनानिवोयानि तदावैजनसंसदि । तानिवःक्वनुयातानिसोदग्राणिम हितानि च ।।6.66.23।।
output: "Earlier in the assembly of people you made vigorous statements and acclaimed yourselves highly with selfpraise. Where has it gone?"

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 66:
भीरुप्रवादाश्श्रूयन्तेयस्तुजीवतिधिक्कृतः । मार्गस्सत्पुरुषैर्जष्टःसेव्यतांत्यज्यतांभयम् ।।6.66.24।।
output: "He who is defeated lives, but people will say he is timid. Resorting to the path of good people and serving them gives up fear."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
शयामहेऽनिहताःपृथिव्यामल्पजीविताः । दुष्प्रापंब्रह्मलोकंवाप्राप्नुयामोयुधिसूदिता ।।6.66.25।।
output: अल्पजीविताः life span is reduced, निहताः having been killed, पृथिव्याम् in the world, शयामहेवाfall, युधिसूदिता killed in war, दुष्प्रापम् difficult to attain, ब्रह्मलोकम् world of Brahma, प्राप्नुयामः च will attain.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सम्प्राप्नुयामःकीर्तिंवानिहत्वाशत्रुमाहवे । जीवितंवीरलोकस्यमोक्ष्यामोवसुवानराः ।।6.66.26।।
output: "By killing the enemy, we will attain fame. Or else we will attain the world of Brahma, liberated."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
न कुम्भकर्णःकाकुत्स्थंदृष्टवाजीवन् गमिष्यति । दीप्यमानमिवासाद्यपतङ्गोज्वलनंयथा ।।6.66.27।।
output: "Just as flies reaching the blazing fire can't escape, so also Kumbhakarna can't escape with life after facing Kakuthsa."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 66:
लायनेनचोद्धिष्टाःप्राणान् रक्षामहेवयम् । एकेनबहवोभग्नायशोनाशंगमिष्यति ।।6.66.28।।
output: "Even though we are distinguished, if we preserve our life by running away for life, destroyed by one, our glory will come to an end."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
एवंब्रुवाणंतंशूरमङ्गदंकनकाङ्गदम् । द्रवमाणास्ततोवाक्यमूचुःशूरुविगर्हितम् ।।6.66.29।।
output: द्रवमाणाः fleeing away, एवम् in that manner, ब्रुवाणम् speaking, कनकाङ्गदम् adorned with gold armlets, शूरम् to the heroes, तम् that, अङ्गदम् Angada, ततः thereafter, शूरुविगर्हितम् condemned by hero, वाक्यम् words, ऊचुः said.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कृतंनःकदनंघोरंकुम्भकर्णेनरक्षसा । न स्थानकालोगच्छामोदयितंजीवितंहिनः ।।6.66.30।।
output: "Kumbhakarna, the Rakshasa has done havoc to us. This is not the moment to stay. Our life is dear to us."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
एतावदुक्त्वावचनंसर्वेतेभेजिरेदिशः । भीमंभीमाक्षमायान्तंदृष्टवावानरयूथपाः ।।6.66.31।।
output: All the Vanara troops having replied that way, seeing Kumbhakarna of frightful eyes coming towards them, scattered in all directions.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
द्रवमाणस्तुतेवीराअङ्गदेनवलीमुखाः । सान्त्वैश्चैहनुमानैश्चततस्सर्वेनिवर्तिताः ।।6.66.32।।
output: Though the heroic monkeys were running away, Angada by his good words and examples turned them to return from wherever they were.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 66:
प्रहर्षमुपनीताश्चवालिपुत्रेणधीमता । आज्ञाप्रतीक्षास्तस्थुश्चसर्वेवानरयूथपाः ।।6.66.33।।
output: All the Vanara troops having heard Angada, son of Vali happily restored awaiting his command.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 66:
ऋषभशरभमैन्दधूम्रनीलाःकुमुदसुषेणगवाक्षरम्भताराः । द्विविदपनसवायुपुत्रमुख्यास्त्वरिततराभिमुखंरणं ।।6.66.34।।
output: Rshaba, Sarabha, Mainda and Nila, Kumuda, Susena, Rambha, and Tara headed by Dwiviida, Panasa and Hanuman marched ahead swiftly to the battlefield. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेषष्टितमस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the sixty sixth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic, the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तेनिवृत्तामहाकायाश्श्रुत्वाङ्गदवचस्तदा । नैष्ठिकींबुद्धिमास्थायसर्वेसङ्ग्रामकाङ्क्षिणः ।।6.67.1।।
output: Kumbhakarna's terrific encounter with Sri Rama. Kumbhakarna's death in the hands of Sri Rama.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
समुदीरितवीर्यास्तेसमारोपितविक्रमाः । पर्यवस्थापितावाक्यैरङ्गदेनवलीमुखाः ।।6.67.2।। प्रयाताश्चगताहर्षंमरणेकृतश्चयाः । चक्रुस्सुतुमुलंयुद्धंवानरास्त्यक्तजीविताः ।।6.67.3।।
output: The Vanara leaders, having been reminded of their valour in battle by Angada gladly returned with a resolve to stake their life and carried on the battle.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
समुदीरितवीर्यास्तेसमारोपितविक्रमाः । पर्यवस्थापितावाक्यैरङ्गदेनवलीमुखाः ।।6.67.2।। प्रयाताश्चगताहर्षंमरणेकृतश्चयाः । चक्रुस्सुतुमुलंयुद्धंवानरास्त्यक्तजीविताः ।।6.67.3।।
output: The Vanara leaders, having been reminded of their valour in battle by Angada gladly returned with a resolve to stake their life and carried on the battle.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
अथवृक्षान्महाकायास्सानूनिसुमहान्ति च । वानरास्तूर्णमुद्यम्यकुम्भकर्णमभिद्रुताः ।।6.67.4।।
output: Thereafter the Vanaras of huge body wielding huge trees and mountain peaks quickly rushed towards Kumbhakarna.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कुम्भकर्णस्सङ्कृद्धोगदामुद्यम्यवीर्यवान् । अर्थयन्समहाकायस्समन्ताद् व्यक्षिपद्रिपून् ।।6.67.5।।
output: Valiant Kumbhakarna, a gigantic one, highly enraged lifted mace and crescent shaped arrow struck the enemies on all sides.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
शतानिसप्तचाष्टौ च सहस्राणि च वानराः । प्रकीर्णाःशेरतेभूमौकुम्भकर्णेनपोधिताः ।।6.67.6।।
output: Kumbhakarna held seven or eight or even hundred, thousand vanaras and threw them on the ground like serpents thrown by Garuda.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
षोडशाष्टौ च दश च विंशत्रतिंशस्तथैव च । परिक्षिप्य च बाहुभ्यांखादन्विपरिधावति ।।6.67.7।। भक्ष्यन् भृशसङ्क्रुद्धोगरुडःपन्नगानिव ।
output: Kumbhakarna became extremely angry, and caught hold of sixteen, eight, ten vanaras in the same way ninetynine and thirty and many more Vanaras and devoured them and went about like Garuda after having eaten the serpents.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कृच्छ्रेणचसमाश्वस्ताःसङ्गम्यचततस्ततः ।।6.67.8।। वृक्षाद्रिहस्ताहरयस्तस्थुस्सङ्ग्राममूर्थनि ।
output: The Vanaras collected from here and there, having restored confidence in themselves with great difficulty, held trees and mountains and stood in the forefront of the battle.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
ततःपर्वतमुत्पाट्यद्विविदःप्लवगर्षभः ।।6.67.9।। दुद्रावगिरिशृङ्गाभंविलम्बइवतोयदः ।
output: Thereafter Dwivida, a bull among the Vanaras lifted a mountain and went towards Kumbhakarna who resembled a threatening cloud.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
तंसमुत्पत्यचिक्षेपकुम्भकर्णायवानरः ।।6.67.10।। तमप्राप्यमहाकायंतस्यसैन्येऽपतत्तधा ।
output: Vanara (Dwivida) going near Kumbhakarna struck him with the mountain. He missed the target and it fell on his army.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ममर्दाश्वान्गजांश्चापिरथांश्चापिनगोत्तमः ।।6.67.11।। तानिचान्यानिरक्षांसिएवंचान्यगदिरेःशिरः ।
output: The huge mountain peak crushed the horses, elephants and chariots and Rakshasa charioteers also.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तच्चैलवेगाभिहतंहताश्वंहतसारथि ।।6.67.12।। रक्षसांरुधिरक्लिन्नंबभूवायोधनंमहत् ।
output: रक्षसाम् Rakshasas, महत् great, अयोधनम् battlefield, तच्छैलवेगाभिहतम् by the speed of the mountain, हताश्वम् horses crushed, हतसारथि charioteers dead, रुधिरक्लिन्नम् blood flowed, बभूव remained wet.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
रथिनोवानरेन्द्राणांशरैःकालान्तकोपमैः ।।6.67.13।। शिरांसिनर्दतांजह्रुस्सहसाभीमनिस्स्वना ।
output: The Rakshasa charioteers severed the roaring Vanara leaders forcibly with their arrows emitting frightening sounds. They were like the Lord of Death at universal dissolution.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
वानराश्चमहात्मानस्समुत्पाट्यमहाद्रुमान् ।।6.67.14।। रथावश्वान्गजानुष्ट्रान्राक्षसानभ्यसूदयन् ।
output: महात्मानः great, वानराश्च Vanaras, महाद्रुमान् huge trees, समुत्पाट्य uprooting, रथान् chariots, अश्वान् horses, उष्ट्रान् camels, राक्षसान् Rakshasas, अभ्यसूदयन् began to destroy.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
हनुमान् शैलशृङ्गाणिशिलाश्चविविधान् द्रुमान् ।।6.67.15।। ववर्षकुम्भकर्णस्यशिरस्यम्बरमास्थितः ।
output: हनूमान् Hanuman, अम्बरम् sky, आस्थितः stationed, कुम्भकर्णस्य Kumbhakarna's, शिरसि on the head, शैलशृङ्गाणि mountain peaks, शिलाश्च rocks, विविधान् several, द्रुमान् kinds of trees, ववर्षrained.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
तानिपर्वतशृङ्गाणिशूलेन स बिभेद ह ।।6.67.16।। बभञ्जवृक्षवर्षं च कुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः ।
output: Mighty Kumbhakarna split off the rocks, mountain peaks and the trees breaking them.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततोहरीणांतदनीकमुग्रंदुद्रावशूलंनिशितंप्रगृह्य । तस्थौ स तस्यापततःपुरस्तान्महीधराग्रंहनुमान् प्रगृह्य ।।6.67.17।।
output: Thereafter Kumbhakarna holding a sharp pike rushed towards Hanuman who uprooted a mountain peak and obstructed him placing it before him.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स कुम्भकर्णंकुपितोजघानवेगेनशैलोत्तमभीमकायम् । स चक्षुभेतेनतदाभिभूतोमेदार्द्रगात्रोरुधिरावसिक्तः ।।6.67.18।।
output: Enraged Hanuman struck Kumbhakarna endowed with a rock like frightening body. Overpowered by that blow Kumbhakarna was upset and bespattered with fat and got bathed in blood.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स शूलमासाद्यतटित्प्रकाशंगिरिर्यथाप्रज्वलिताग्रशृङ्गम् । बाह्वन्तरेमारुतिमाजघानगुहोऽचलंक्रौञ्चमिवोग्रशक्त्या ।।6.67.19।।
output: Kumbhakarna ,who was like a mountain blazing like fire, pierced at Maruti's chest with his pike shining like lightning just as Guha struck at Krauncha mountain.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
शूलनिर्भिन्नमहाभुजान्तरःप्रविह्वलःशोणितमुद्वमन् मुखात् । ननादभीमंहनुमान् महाहवेयुगान्तमेघस्न्तितस्वनोपमम् ।।6.67.20।।
output: The great son of windgod, pierced with pike in the chest, ejected blood from his mouth, and roared in a frightening manner which was like thunder rumbling at the time of dissolution of the universe.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततोविनेदुःसहसाप्रहृष्टारक्षोगणास्तंव्यथितंसमीक्ष्य । प्लवङ्गमास्तुव्यथिताभयर्ताःप्रदुद्रुवुःसंयतिकुम्भकर्णात् ।।6.67.21।।
output: ततः then, रक्षोगणाः Rakshasa army, व्यथितम् agonized तम् his, समीक्ष्य perceiving, प्रहृष्टाः happy, सहसा collected, विनेदुः rejoiced, प्लवङ्गमास्तु for Vanaras, व्यथिताः. frightened, भयार्ताः in fear, संयति , कुम्भकर्णात् Kumbhakarna's, प्रदुद्रुवुः fled.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततस्तुनीलोबलवान् पर्यवस्थापयन्बलम् । प्रविचिक्षेपशैलाग्रंकुम्भकर्णायधीमते ।।6.67.22।।
output: ततः thereafter, बलवान् endowed with strength, नीलः Neela, बलम् army, पर्यवस्थापयन् restoring the army, धीमते wise one, कुम्भकर्णाय Kumbhakarna, शैलाग्रम् with peak of a mountain, प्रविचिक्षेप flung.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
तदापतन्तंसम्प्रेक्ष्यमुष्टिनाभिजघान ह । मुष्टिप्रहाराभिहतंतच्छैलाग्रंव्यशीर्यत ।।6.67.23।। सविस्फुलिंगंसज्वालनिपपातमहेतले ।
output: (Kumbhakarna) observing the mountain peak coming towards him pierced it with his fist. Struck by the fist, the peak broke and sparks of fire came out shining brightly and fell on the ground.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ऋषभश्शरभोनीलोगवाक्षोगन्धमादनः ।।6.67.24।। पञ्चवानरशार्दूलाःकुम्बुकर्णमुपाद्रवन् ।
output: ऋषभः Rshaba, शरभः Sarabha, नीलः Neela, गवाक्षः Gavaksha, गन्धमादनः Gandhamadana, पञ्च five, वानरशार्धूलाः tigers among Vanaras, कुम्बकर्णम् Kumbhakarna, उपाद्रवन् attacked.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
शैलैर्ववृक्षैस्तलैःपादैर्मुष्टिभिश्चमहाबलाः ।।6.67.25।। कुम्भकर्णंमहाकायंसर्वतोऽभिप्रदुद्रुवुः ।
output: महाबलाः Vanaras of exceptional strength, शैलैः rock, वृक्षैः trees, तलैः palms, पादैः feet, मुष्टिभिः च and fist also, महाकायम् of huge body, कुम्बकर्णम् Kumbhakarna, सर्वतः all over, अभिप्रदुद्रुवुः attacked severely.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
स्पर्शानिवप्रहारांस्तान्वेद्वयानो न विव्यथे ।।6.67.26।। ऋषभंतुमहावेगंबाहुभ्यांपरिषस्वजे ।
output: Their attacks were like soft touches to Kumbhakarna, and no pain was experienced by him, and he encircled Rshaba by the shoulders with great impetuosity.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
कुम्भकर्णभुजाभ्यांतुपीडितोवानरर्षभः ।।6.67.27।। निपपातर्षभोभीमःप्रमुखाद्वान्तशोणितः ।
output: Rshaba, the bull among Vanaras, of frightful appearance pressed by Kumbhakarna's shoulders, started bleeding from his teeth and fell down.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
मुष्टिनाशरभंहत्वाजानुनानीलमाहवे ।।6.67.28।। आजघानगवाक्षंतुलेनेन्द्ररिपुस्तदा । पादेनाभ्यहनत्कृद्धस्तरसागन्धमादनम् ।।6.67.29।।
output: Angry Kumbhakarna (enemy of Indra) hit Sarabha with his fist, Neela with his knees hurt Gavaksha and slapped him with his palms. Gandhamadana was kicked with force.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
मुष्टिनाशरभंहत्वाजानुनानीलमाहवे ।।6.67.28।। आजघानगवाक्षंतुलेनेन्द्ररिपुस्तदा । पादेनाभ्यहनत्कृद्धस्तरसागन्धमादनम् ।।6.67.29।।
output: Angry Kumbhakarna (enemy of Indra) hit Sarabha with his fist, Neela with his knees hurt Gavaksha and slapped him with his palms. Gandhamadana was kicked with force.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
दत्तप्रहारव्यथितामुमुहुश्शोणितोक्षिताः । निपेतुस्तेतुमेदिन्यांनिकृत्ताइवकिंशुकाः ।।6.67.30।।
output: Hurt by the blows of Kumbhakarna, their eyes bathed in blood, the Vanaras fainted and fell on the ground like cut down Kimsuka trees.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तेषुवानरमुख्येषुपातितेषुमहात्मसु । वानराणांसहस्राणिकुम्बकर्णंप्रदद्रुवुः ।।6.67.31।।
output: महात्मसु great leaders, तेषु they being, वानरमुख्येषु important among Vanaras, पातितेषु fallen, वानराणाम् Vanaras, सहस्राणि thousands, कुम्भकर्णम् Kumbhakarna, प्रदुद्रुवुः went towards.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
तंशैलमिवशैलाभाःसर्वेतुप्लवगर्षभाः । समारुह्यसमुत्पत्यददंशुश्चमहाबलाः ।।6.67.32।।
output: The bulls among Vanaras themselves looking like mountains endowed with great strength climbed up Kumbhakarna and bit him.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
तंनखैर्धशनैश्चापिमुष्टिभिर्बाहुभिस्तथा । कुम्भकर्णंमहाबाहहुंतेजघ्नुःप्लवगर्षभाः ।।6.67.33।।
output: The bulls among Vanaras hurt Kumbhakarna, endowed with strong shoulders, by scratching with nails, biting with teeth and hitting him with arms and fists.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
स वानरसहस्त्रैरजितः पर्वतोपमैः । रराजराक्षसव्याघ्रोगिरिरात्मरुहैरिव ।।6.67.34।।
output: The tiger among Rakshasas covered with thousands of Rakshasas was resembling a mountain with trees grown on itself.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
बाहुभ्यांवानरान्सर्वान्प्रगृह्य स महाबलः । भक्ष्यामाससङ्क्रुद्धोगरुडःपन्नगानिव ।।6.67.35।।
output: महाबलः mighty strong, सः he, सर्वान् all, वानरान् Vanaras, बाहुभ्याम् shoulders, प्रगृह्य holding, सङ्क्रुद्धः highly enraged, गरुडः Garuda, पन्नगानिव serpents like, भक्ष्यामास started devouring.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
प्रक्षिप्ताःकुम्बकर्णेनवक्त्रेपातालसन्निभे । नासापुटाभ्यांनिर्जग्मुःकर्णाभ्यांचैववानराः ।।6.67.36।।
output: कुम्बकर्णेन Kumbhakarna, पातालसन्निभे the nethermost world, वक्त्रे mouth, प्रक्षिप्ताः thrust into, वानराः Vanaras, नासापुटाभ्याम् through nostrils, कर्णाभ्यांचैव and also through ears, निर्जग्मुः came out.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
भक्ष्यन्भृशसङ्क्रुद्धो हरीन् पर्वतसन्निभः । बभञ्जवानरान् सर्वान् सङ्क्रुद्धोराक्षसोत्तमः ।।6.67.37।।
output: The foremost of the Rakshasas, who resembled a mountain became enraged and mutilated the Vanaras.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
मांसशोणितसंक्लेदाकुर्वन् भूमिं स राक्षसः । चचारहरिनैन्येषुकालानगिरिवमूर्छितः ।।6.67.38।।
output: That terrible Rakshasa swooning and wetting the ground with flesh and blood ranged through the army of Vanaras like fire at the time of dissolution of the universe.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
वज्रहस्तोयथाशक्रःपाशहस्तइवान्तकः । शूलहस्तोबभौयुद्धेकुम्बकर्णोमहाबलः ।।6.67.39।।
output: शूलहस्तः holding pike in hand, महाबलः mighty, कुम्बकर्णः Kumbhakarna, युद्धे in battlefield, वज्रहस्तः thunderbolt in hand, शक्रःयथा like Indra, पाशहस्तः like noose in hand, अन्तकःइव like Lord of death, बभौ shone.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
यथाशुष्काण्यरण्यानिग्रीष्मेदहतिपावकः । तथावानरसैन्यानिकुम्बकर्णोविनिर्दहत् ।।6.67.40।।
output: Just as fire god consumes dried forest in summer, Kumbhakarna was consuming the Vanara army.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततस्तेवध्यमानास्तुहतयूथाविनायकाः । वानराभयसंविग्नाविनेदुर्विस्वरंभृशैः ।।6.67.41।।
output: Then with the army killed, the Vanaras moved without any leader making unnatural sounds out of fear and anger.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अनेकशोवध्यमानाःकुम्भकर्णेनवानराः । राघवंशरणंजग्मुर्व्यथिताःभिन्नचेतसः ।।6.67.42।।
output: कुम्भकर्णेन Kumbhakarna, अनेकशः in many ways, वध्यमानाः destroying, वानराः Vanaras, व्यथिताः worried, भिन्नचेतसः heartbroken, राघवम् Raghava, शरणंजग्मुः sought refuge.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
प्रभग्नान् वानरान् दृष्टवावज्रहस्तात्मजात्मजः । अभ्यधावतवेगेनकुम्भकर्णंमहाहवे ।।6.67.43।।
output: The son of Vali who sprung from Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt seeing the Vanaras routed, rushed towards Kumbhakarna to assault.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
शैलशृङ्गंमहद्गृह्यविनदंश्चमुहुर्मुहुः । त्रासयन्राक्षसान्सर्वान् कुम्भकर्णपदानुगान् ।।6.67.44।। चिक्षेपशैलशिखरंकुम्भकर्णस्यमूर्धनि ।
output: सः he, महत् huge, शैलशृङ्गम् peak of mountain, गृह्य taking, मुहुर्मुहुः again and again, विनदन् roaring aloud, कुम्भकर्णपदानुगान् following Kumbhakarna, सर्वान् all, राक्षसान् Rakshasas, त्रासयन् frightening शैलशिखरम् mountain top, कुम्भकर्णस्य Kumbhakarna's, मूर्धनि forehead, चिक्षेप crushed.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स तेनाभिहतोमूर्ध्निशैलेनेन्द्ररिपुस्तदा ।।6.67.45।। कुम्भकर्णःप्रजज्वालक्रोधेनमहतातदा । सोऽभ्यधावतवेगेनवालिपुत्रममर्षणम् ।।6.67.46।।
output: Hit on the forehead by Angada, Kumbhakarna, burning with fury rushed. The intolerant Rakshasa then rushed to Vali's son with force.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स तेनाभिहतोमूर्ध्निशैलेनेन्द्ररिपुस्तदा ।।6.67.45।। कुम्भकर्णःप्रजज्वालक्रोधेनमहतातदा । सोऽभ्यधावतवेगेनवालिपुत्रममर्षणम् ।।6.67.46।।
output: Hit on the forehead by Angada, Kumbhakarna, burning with fury rushed. The intolerant Rakshasa then rushed to Vali's son with force.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
कुम्भकर्णोमहानादस्त्रासयन् सर्ववानरान् । शूलंससर्जवैरोषादङ्गदेतुमहाबलः ।।6.67.47।।
output: Mighty Kumbhakarna agitated, making loud noise and frightening all the Vanaras hurled his pike on Angada.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
त मापतन्तंबुद्ध्वातुयुद्धमार्गविशारदः । लाघवान्मोचयामाबलवान् वानरर्षभः ।।6.67.48।।
output: युद्धमार्गविशारदः knowledgeable in warfare, बलवान् endowed with prowess, वानरर्षभः bull among Vanaras, आपतन्तम् stopped, तम् that, बुद्ध्वा approaching, लाघवात् agility, मोचयामास escaped.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
उत्पत्यचैनंतरसातलेनोरस्यताडयत् । स तेनाभिहतःकोपात्प्रमुमोहाचलोपमः ।।6.67.49।।
output: उत्पत्य jumping up, एनम् in that manner, तरसा slapped, तलेन with palm, उरसि on the chest, अताडयत् struck, तेन by that, कोपात् in anger, अभिहतः struck, अचलोपमः like mountain, सः he, प्रमुमोह unconscious.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
स लब्दसंज्ञोबलवान्मुष्टिमावर्त्यराक्षसः । अपहास्तेनचिक्षेपविसंज्ञः स पपात ह ।।6.67.50।।
output: The mighty Rakshasa regained his consciousness and, doubling his fist hit Angada with the back of his hand and Angada fell, lost senses.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तस्मिन् प्लवगशार्दूलेविसंज्ञेपतितेभुवि । तच्छूलंसमुपादायसुग्रीवमभिदुद्रुवे ।।6.67.51।।
output: प्लवगशार्दूले tiger among monkeys, तस्मिन् his, विसंज्ञे unconscious, भुवि on ground, पतिते fallen, तच्छूलम् that pike, समुपादाय taking out, सुग्रीवम् to Sugriva, समभिदुद्रुवे rushed towards.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
तमापतन्तंसम्प्रेक्ष्यकुम्भकर्णंमहाबलम् । उत्पपाततदावीरस्सुग्रीवोवानराधिपः ।।6.67.52।।
output: Valiant Sugriva, seeing the mighty Kumbhakarna coming towards him jumped (in excitement).

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स पर्वताग्रमुत्क्षिप्यसमाविध्यमहाबलः । अभिदुद्राववेगेनकुम्भकर्णंमहाबलम् ।।6.67.53।।
output: महाबलः of great prowess, सः he (Sugriva), पर्वताग्रम् mountain peak, उत्क्षिप्य lifting, समाविध्य whirling round, महाबलम् great strength, कुम्भकर्णम् Kumbhakarna, वेगेन swiftly, अभिदुद्राव darted towards.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तमापतन्तंसम्प्रेक्ष्यकुम्भकर्णःप्लवङ्गमम् । तस्थौविवृतसर्वाङ्गोवानरेन्द्रस्यसम्मुखः ।।6.67.54।।
output: कुम्भकर्णः Kumbhakarna, आपतन्तम् approaching, तम् him, प्लवङ्गमम् monkey, सम्प्रेक्ष्य looking, विवृतसर्वाङ्गः all limbs braced, वानरेन्द्रस्य Vanara Lord's, सम्मुखः forefront.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कपिशोणितदिग्धाङ्गंभक्ष्यन्तंप्लवङ्गमान् । कुम्भकर्णंस्थितंदृष्टवासुग्रीवोवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।।6.67.55।।
output: कपिशोणितदिग्धाङ्गम् smeared with the blood of Vanaras, प्लवङ्गमान् monkeys, भक्ष्यन्तम् eating, स्थितम् stood, कुम्भकर्णम् Kumbhakarna, दृष्टवा seeing, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कपिशोणितदिग्धाङ्गंभक्ष्यन्तंप्लवङ्गमान् । कुम्भकर्णंस्थितंदृष्टवासुग्रीवोवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।।6.67.55।।
output: कपिशोणितदिग्धाङ्गम् smeared with the blood of Vanaras, प्लवङ्गमान् monkeys, भक्ष्यन्तम् eating, स्थितम् stood, कुम्भकर्णम् Kumbhakarna, दृष्टवा seeing, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
त्वजतद्वानरानीकंप्राकृतैःकिंकरिष्यसि । सहस्वैकंनिपातंमेपर्वतस्यास्यराक्षस ।।6.67.57।।
output: तत् that, वानरानीकम् Vanara troops, त्यज give up, प्राकृतैः by nature, किंकरिष्यसि What work, राक्षस Rakshasa, मे with me, अस्यपर्वतस्य your mountain's, एकम् निपातम् one mountain, सहस्व bear.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
तद्वाक्यंहरिराजस्यसत्त्वधैर्यसमन्वितम् । श्रुत्वाराक्षसशार्दूलःकुम्भकर्णोऽब्रवीद्वचः ।।6.67.58।।
output: Hearing the king of Vanara's words of courage and strength, the tiger among Rakshasas, Kumbhakarna spoke these words.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
प्रजापतेस्तुपौत्रस्त्वंतथैवरक्षरजस्सुतः । श्रुतपौरुषसम्पन्नःकस्माद्गर्जसिवानर ।।6.67.59।।
output: "O Vanara! You are the grandson of creator Brahma and son of Rksharaja, endowed with fortitude and so roaring like this."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
स कुम्भकर्णस्यवचोनिशम्यव्याविध्यशैलंसहसामुमोच । तेनाजघानोरसिकुम्भकर्णंशैलेनवज्राशनिसन्निभेन ।।6.67.60।।
output: On hearing Kumbhakarna's words, Sugriva forcibly discharged a mountain resembling a thunderbolt on the chest of Kumbhakarna.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तच्छैलशृङ्गंसहसाविकीर्णंभुजान्तरेतस्यतदाविशाले । ततोनिषेदुःसहसाप्लवङ्गारक्षोगणाश्चापिमुदाविनेदुः ।।6.67.61।।
output: तदा then, तस्य his, विशाले broad, भुजान्तरे between shoulders, तत् that, शैलशृङ्गम् mountain peak, सहसा forcefully, विभिन्नम् broke into pieces, ततः thereafter, प्लवङ्गाः monkey, सहसा forcibly, विषण्णाः desperate, रक्षोगणाश्चापि the troops of Rakshasas, मुदा joy, विनेदुः roared.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
स शैलशृङ्गाभिहतश्चुकोपननादरोषाच्चविवृत्यवक्त्रम् । व्याविध्यशूलं च तटित्प्रकाशंचिक्षेपहर्यृक्षिपतेर्वधाय ।।6.67.62।।
output: Struck with mountain peaks, the Rakshasa became furious, and his pride was hurt. He opened his mouth widely making loud noises, his pike glowing like lightning, turned the pike into circles and hurled at Sugriva to put an end to him.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तत्कुम्भकर्णस्यभुजप्रविद्धंशूलंशितंकाञ्चनदामजुष्टम् । क्षिप्रंसमुत्पत्यनिगृह्यदोर्भ्यांबभञ्जवेगेनसुतोऽनिलस्य ।।6.67.63।।
output: अनिलस्यसुतः son of windgod, क्षिप्रम् instantly, समुत्पत्य seizing, कुम्भकर्णस्य Kumbhakarna's, भुजप्रविद्धम् with his arms, शितम् shaft, काञ्चनदामजुष्टम् covered with chains of gold, तत् that, शूलम् pike, दोर्भ्याम् both hands, निगृह्य holding, वेगेन quickly, बभञ्ज broke.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कृतंभारसहस्रस्यशूलंकालायसंमहत् । बभञ्जजानुमारोप्यतदाहृष्टःप्लवङ्गमः ।।6.67.64।।
output: Then a rejoiced monkey, resting the thousand bharas iron pike on his knee broke it.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
शूलंभग्नंहनुमतादृष्टवावानरवाहिनी । हृष्टाननादबहुशस्सर्वतश्चापिदुद्रुवे ।।6.67.65।।
output: Seeing the pike broken by Hanuman, the army of Vanaras rejoiced and roared repeatedly all over and rushed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
बभूवथपरित्रस्तोराक्षसोविमुखोऽभवत् । सिंहनादं च तेचक्रुःप्रहृष्टावनगोचराः ।।6.67.66।। मारुतिंपूजयाञ्चक्रुर्दृष्टवाशूलंतथागतम् ।
output: अथ and then, राक्षसः Rakshasa, परित्रस्तः dismayed, विमुखः mellowed, अभवत् became, ते they, वनगोचराः forest rangers, प्रहृष्टाः rejoiced, सिंहनादम् roared like lions, चक्रुः went round, तथागतम् broken that way, शूलम् pike, दृष्टाम् seeing, मारुतिम् Hanuman, पूजयाञ्चक्रुः applauded.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
स तत्तथाभग्नमवेक्ष्यशूलंचुकोपरक्षोधिपतिर्महात्मा । उत्पाट्यलङ्कामलयात्सशृङ्गंजघानसुग्रीवमुपेत्यतेन ।।6.67.67।।
output: That great soul, the Lord of Rakshasas seeing the pike broken in that way, was highly enraged. Taking Malaya Mountain from Lanka, he struck Sugriva who was approaching him.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
स शैलशृङ्गाभिहतोविसंज्ञःपपातभूमौयुधिवानरेन्द्रः । तंप्रेक्ष्यभूमौपतितंविसंज्ञनेदुःप्रहृष्टास्त्वथयातुधानाः ।।6.67.68।।
output: Struck by the piece of mountain the Vanara king became unconscious and dropped on the battlefield. Seeing that the Rakshasas were happy and naturally roared with a feeling of triumph.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
मभ्युपेत्याद्भुतघोरवीर्यं स कुम्भकर्णोयुधिवानरेन्द्रम् । जहारसुग्रीवमभिप्रगृह्ययथानिलोमेघमतिप्रचण्डः ।।6.67.69।।
output: सः he, कुम्भकर्णः Kumbhakarna, युधि battle, अद्भुतघोरवीर्यम् wonderful and dreadful valour, वानरेन्द्रम् Vanara Lord, तंसुग्रीवम् that Sugriva, अभिप्रगृह्य taking up again, अतिप्रचण्डः highly tempestuous, अनिलः wind, मेघंयथा like cloud, जहार took him.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स तंमहामेघनिकाशरूपमुत्पाट्यगच्छन्युधिकुम्भकर्णः । रराजमेरुप्रतिमानरूपोमेरुर्यथाभ्युछ्रचितघोरशृङ्गः ।।6.67.70।।
output: युधि in the battlefield, महामेघनिकाशरूपम् form which resembled huge cloud, तम् him, उत्पाट्य lifting, गच्छन् went, मेरुप्रतिमानरूपः form of Meru mountain, कुम्भकर्णः Kumbhakarna, अभ्युछ्रचितघोरशृङ्गः distinguished by lofty peak, मेरुर्यथा like Meru, रराज seemed.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
ततस्तमादायजगामवीरस्संस्तूयमानोयुधिराक्षसेन्द्रैः । शृण्वन्निनादंत्रिदिवालयानांप्लवङ्गराजग्रहविस्मितानाम् ।।6.67.71।।
output: Thereafter the heroic Rakshasa king having held Sugriva in the battle went, duly praised (by Rakshasas), hearing the roaring sounds of gods in heaven wondering at Sugriva's capture.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततस्तमादायतदा स मेनेहरीन्द्रमिन्द्रोपममिन्द्रवीर्यः । अस्मिन् हतेसर्वमिदंहतंस्यात्सराघवंसैन्यमितीन्द्रशत्रुः ।।6.67.72।।
output: इन्द्रवीर्यः equal to Indra in heroism, इन्द्रशत्रुः Indra's enemy, सः he, ततः then, इन्द्रोपमम् like Indra, तम् him, हरीन्द्रम् Indra of monkeys, आदाय seizing, तदा then, अस्मिन् his, हते killed, सराघवम् having been killed, सर्वम् all, इदम् like this, सैन्यम् army, हतम् killed, स्यात् including, इति thus, मेने thought.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
विद्रुतांवाहिनींदृष्टवावानराणामितस्ततः । कुम्भकर्णेनसुग्रीवंगृहीतंचापिवानरम् ।।6.67.73।। हनुमांश्चिन्तयामासमतिमान् मारुतात्मजः ।
output: Seeing the army running away here and there and Sugriva being captured by Kumbhakarna, wise Hanuman, the son of Maruti started thinking.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
एवंगृहीतेसुग्रीवेकिंकर्तव्यंमयाभवेत् ।।6.67.74।। यद्वैन्यायंमयाकर्तुंतत्करिष्यामिसर्वधा । भूत्वापर्वतसङ्काशोनाशयिष्यामिराक्षसम् ।।6.67.75।।
output: सुग्रीवे Sugriva, एवम् in this way, गृहीते captured, मया my, किम् what, कर्तव्यम् duty, भवेत् will be, मया my, यत् that which, कर्तुम् will do, न्याय्यम् justice, तत् that, सर्वधा thought, करिष्यामि will do, पर्वतसङ्काशः one who is like a mountain, भूत्वा to be done, राक्षसम् Rakshasa, नाशयिष्यामि will destroy.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
एवंगृहीतेसुग्रीवेकिंकर्तव्यंमयाभवेत् ।।6.67.74।। यद्वैन्यायंमयाकर्तुंतत्करिष्यामिसर्वधा । भूत्वापर्वतसङ्काशोनाशयिष्यामिराक्षसम् ।।6.67.75।।
output: 'Sugriva has been caught. What is my duty now? I will do what is just. I will destroy that Rakshasa who is in the form of a mountain', thought Maruti.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
मयाहतेसंयतिकुम्भकर्णेमहाबलेमुष्टिविशीर्णदेहे । विमोचितेवानरपार्थिवे च भवन्तुहृष्टाःप्लवगास्समस्ताः ।।6.67.76।।
output: महाबले mighty, कुम्भकर्णे Kumbhakarna, मुष्टिविशीर्णदेहे shattered hit by fist, संयति in duel, मया by me, हते killed, वानरपार्थिवे Vanara king विमोचिते delivered, समस्ताः all, प्लवगाः monkeys, हृष्टाः rejoice, भवन्तु will be.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अथवास्वयमप्येषमोक्षंप्राप्स्यतिपार्थिव । गृहीतोऽयंयदिभवेत्रिदशैस्सासुरोरगैः ।।6.67.77।।
output: अथवा or else, अयम् एषः he alone, पार्थिव remain, सासुरोरगैः Nagas, gods and demons त्रिदशैः all the three, गृहीतः captured, भवेद्यदि by himself, स्वयम् himself, मोक्षम् liberate, प्राप्स्यति will attain.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
मन्ये न तावदात्मानंबुध्यतेवानराधिपः । शैलप्रहाराभिहतःकुम्भकर्णेनसंयुगे ।।6.67.78।।
output: "I think that Sugriva, hit by Kumbhakarna with a mountain, has lost senses and is not able to know."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
अयंमुहूर्तात्सुग्रीवोलब्दसंज्ञोमहाहवे । आत्मनोवानराणां च यत्पथ्यंतत्करिष्यति ।।6.67.79।।
output: Sugriva will soon regain consciousness and do what is good for Vanaras.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
मयातुमोक्षितस्यास्यसुग्रीवस्यमहात्मनः । अप्रीतिश्चभवेत्कष्टाकीर्तिनाशश्चशाश्वतः ।।6.67.80।।
output: "If Sugriva is released by me, he will not be happy forever. His fame will be lost."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
तस्मान्मुहूर्तंकाङ्क्षिष्येविक्रमंपार्थिवस्यतु । भिन्नं च वानरानीकंतावदाश्वासयाम्यहम् ।।6.67.81।।
output: "Therefore, I will see the exhibition of his prowess for a while. Thereafter I shall reinforce the scattered army of Vanaras."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
इत्येवंचिन्तयित्वातुहनुमान्मारुतात्मजः । भूयःसंस्तम्भयामासवानराणांमहाचमूम् ।।6.67.82।।
output: मारुतात्मज son of Maruti, हनुमान् Hanuman, इत्येवम् in this way, चिन्तयित्वा thinking, अथ then, भूयः said, वानराणाम् to Vanaras, महाचमूम् huge army, संस्तम्भयामास brought determination.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स कुम्भकर्णोऽथविवेशलङ्कांस्पुरन्तमादायमहाकपिंतम् । विमानचर्यागृहगोपुरस्थैःपुष्पाग्य्रवर्षैरवकीर्यमाणः ।।6.67.83 ।
output: अत then, सःकुम्भकर्णः Kumbhakarna, स्फुरन्तम् shaking, तम् his, महाकपिम् great Vanara, आदाय taking, विमानचर्यागृहगोपुरस्थैः through the roads of lofty mansions, पुष्पाग्य्रवर्षैः showered with flowers, अवकीर्यमाणः hailed by Rakshasas, लङ्काम् Lanka, विवेश entered.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
लाजगन्धोदवर्षैस्तुसिच्यमानश्सनैश्शनैः । राजवीथ्यास्तुशीतत्वात्संज्ञांप्रापमहाबलः ।।6.67.84।।
output: Exceptionally strong Sugriva with parched grain and fragrant water showered on him in the royal path, being cool, regained consciousness.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततस्ससंज्ञामुपलभ्यकृच्छ्राद्बलीयसस्तस्यभुजान्तरस्थः । अवेक्षमाणःपुरसाजमार्गंविचिन्तयामासमुहुर्महात्मा ।।6.67.85।।
output: बलीयसः being strong, तस्य his, भुजान्तरस्थः from the arms, महात्मा great, सः he, कृच्छ्रात् painfully, संज्ञाम् senses, उपलभ्य having gained, पुरराजमार्गम् royal path of the city, अवेक्षमाणः started looking, मुहुः bewildered, विचिन्तयामास started pondering.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
एवंगृहीतेनकथंनुनामशक्यंमयासम्प्रतिकर्तुमद्य । तथाकरिष्यामियथाहरीणांभविष्यतीष्टं च हितं च कार्यम् ।।6.67.86।।
output: 'Caught in this way, how can I do (take action)? I will do what is possible, pleasing, and good to Vanaras now.'

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततःकराग्रैःसहसासमेत्यराजाहरीणाममरेन्द्रशत्रुम् । खरैश्चकर्णौदशनैश्चनासांददंशपार्श्वेषु च कुम्भकर्णम् ।।6.67.87।।
output: There after the king of Vanaras decided to act and tore off the ears of the enemy ruler of gods (Kumbhakarna) with his sharp nails, bit off the nose with his teeth, and sides of Kumbhakarna.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स कुम्भकर्णोहृतकर्णनासोविदारितस्तेनरदैर्नखैश्च । रोषाभिभूतःक्षतजार्द्रगात्रःसुग्रीवमाविध्यपिपेषभूमौ ।।6.67.88।।
output: Deprived of ears and nose by Sugriva, splitting with nails and teeth, Kumbhakarna was highly furious and pinning down Sugriva pounded him against the ground, limbs bespattered.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
स भूतलेभीमबलाभिपिष्टस्सुरारिभिस्स्सैरभिहन्यमानः । जगामखंवेगवदभ्युपेत्यपुनश्चरामेणसमाजगाम ।।6.67.89।।
output: Dropped on the ground by Kumbhakarna of dreadful strength, pressed against the ground surface, Sugriva bounced to the sky to get reunited with Rama.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कर्णनासाविहीनस्तुकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः । रराजशोणितैःसिक्तोगिरिःप्रस्रवणैरिव ।।6.67.90।।
output: कर्णनासाविहीनः devoid of nose and ears, महाबलः great hero, कुम्भकर्णः Kumbhakarna, शोणितैः with blood, सिक्तः drenched, प्रस्रवणैः like springs, गिरिःइव like mountain, रराज shone.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
शोणितार्द्रोमहाकायोराक्षसोभीमविक्रमः । युद्धायाभिमुखोभीमोमनश्चक्रेनिशाचरः ।।6.67.91।। नीलाञ्जनचयप्रख्यःसस्नध्यइवतोयदः । अमर्षाच्छोणितोद्गारीशुशुभेरावणानुजीः ।।6.67.92।।
output: शोणितार्द्रः drenched in blood, महाकायः of gigantic body, भीमविक्रमः of terrible valour, अमर्षात् intolerant, नीलाञ्जनचयप्रख्यः dark in colour like mountain of collyrium, तोयदःइव like cloud, शुशुभे evening, भीमः terrible appearance, निशाचरः night ranger, अभिमुखः towards, भूत्वा battlefield, युद्धाय to fight, मनः in mind, चक्रे went.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
शोणितार्द्रोमहाकायोराक्षसोभीमविक्रमः । युद्धायाभिमुखोभीमोमनश्चक्रेनिशाचरः ।।6.67.91।। नीलाञ्जनचयप्रख्यःसस्नध्यइवतोयदः । अमर्षाच्छोणितोद्गारीशुशुभेरावणानुजीः ।।6.67.92।।
output: Kumbhakarna of terrific valour and gigantic body, drenched in blood, dark in colour like a mountain of collyrium, resembling evening cloud, the night ranger went towards the battlefield.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
गतेतुतस्मिन् सुरराजशत्रुःक्रोधात्प्रदुद्रावरणायभूयः । अनायुधोऽस्मीतिविचिन्त्यरौद्रोघोरंतदामुद्गरमाससाद ।।6.67.93।।
output: Himself (Sugriva) gone, the enemy of the Lord of gods rushed again retreating, "I am ferocious, without weapon." Then seizing an iron mallet, Sugriva went reflecting.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
ततस्सपुर्यास्ससहसामहात्मानिष्क्रम्यतद्वानरसैन्यमुग्रम् । बभक्षरक्षोयुधिकुम्भकर्णःप्रजायुगान्तानगिरिवप्रवृद्धः ।।6.67.94।।
output: The great Kumbhakarna then departing instantly entered into Vanara army consumed them as fire at dissolution consumed people.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
बुभुक्षितःशोणइतमांसगृध्नुःप्रविव्यतद्वानरसैन्यमुग्रम् । चखादरक्षांसिहरीन् पिशाचान् ऋक्षांश्चमोहाद्युधिकुम्भकर्णः । यथैवमृत्युर्हरतेयुगान्ते स भक्ष्यामासहरींश्चमुख्यान् ।।6.67.95।।
output: बुभुक्षितः consumed, शोणितमांसगृध्नुः blood and flesh, कुम्भकर्णः Kumbhakarna, उग्रम् ferocious, तत् that, वानरसैन्यम् Vanara army, प्रविश्य entering, युधि battle, मोहात् delusion, रक्षांसि Rakshasas also, हरीन् Vanaras, पिशाचान् demons, ऋक्षान् च Bears, चखाद entering, युगान्ते at the end of universe, मृत्युः death, यथैव like the same way, हरते seizing, मुख्यान् principal, हरीन् Vanaras, भक्ष्यामास started consuming.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
एकंद्वौत्रीन् बहून् क्रुद्धोवानरान्सहराक्षसैः । समादायैकहस्तेनप्रचिक्षेपत्वरन्मुखे ।।6.67.96।।
output: Taking one, two, three, and many Vanaras along with Rakshasas hastily with one hand he was gulping them.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सम्प्रस्रवंस्तदामेदश्शोणिते च महाबलः । वध्यमानोनगेन्द्राग्रैर्भक्ष्यामासवानरान् ।।6.67.97।।
output: तदा then, महाबलः mighty, नगेन्द्राग्रैः peaks of mountains, वध्यमानः while being struck, मेदःशोणिते brain and blood, सम्प्रस्रवन् oozing out, वानरान् Vanaras, भक्ष्यामास feasting.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
तेभक्ष्यमाणाहरयोरामंजुग्मुस्तदागतिम् । कुम्भकर्णोभृशंक्रुद्धःकपीन् खादन् प्रधावति ।।6.67.98।।
output: Being devoured by Kumbhakarna, the Vanaras went for refuge to Rama. Enraged Kumbhakarna followed the Vanaras behind.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
शतानिसप्तचाष्टौ च विंशत्रतिंशत्तथैव च । सम्परिष्वज्यबाहुभ्यांखादवनिपरिधावति ।।6.67.99।।
output: Stretching his arms on all sides picking hundred, seven hundred, eight hundred and two hundred and three hundred, he ran devouring the vanaras.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
मेदोवसाशोणितदिग्धगात्रःकरायवसक्तग्रथितान्त्रमालः । ववर्षशूलानिसतीक्षणदंष्ट्रःकालोयुगान्तस्थइववृद्धः ।।6.67.100।।
output: His limbs smeared with fat and blood, with wreaths of entrails hanging on his ears, with sharp teeth, grown in his body to huge size, rained darts like the spirit of death at the end of the world.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तस्मिन् कालेसुमित्रायाःपुत्रःपरबलार्दनः । चकारलक्ष्मणःक्रुद्धोयुद्धंपरपुरञ्जयः ।।6.67.101।।
