output: तस्मिन् at that, काले time, सुमित्रायाः Sumitra's, पुत्रः son, परबलार्दनः winner of enemy forces, परपुरञ्जयः conqueror of forts, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, क्रुद्धः enraged, युद्धम् fight, चकार went.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
स कुम्भकर्णस्यशरान् शरीरेसप्तवीर्यवान् । निचखादाददेचान्यावनिससर्ज च लक्ष्मणः ।।6.67.102।।
output: Valiant Lakshmana pierced seven arrows on Kumbhakarna's body and discharged many arrows on him.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
पीड्यमानस्तदस्त्रंतुविशेषंतत्सराक्षसः । ततश्चुकोपबलवान्सुमित्रानन्दवर्दनः ।।6.67.103।।
output: सःराक्षसः that Rakshasa, पीड्यमानः having been tormented, तत् his, तदस्त्रम् dart, विशेषम् put an end ततः there upon, बलवान् mighty, सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः enhancer of Sumitra's joy, चुकोप flew into rage.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अथास्यकवचंशुभ्रंजाम्भूनदमयंशुभम् । प्रच्छादयामासशरैस्सन्ध्याभ्रमिवमारुतः ।।6.67.104।।
output: अत then, मारुतः wind, सन्ध्याभ्रमिव evening cloud covers, अस्य his, शुभ्रम् glittering, जाम्भूनदमयम् golden, शुभम् charming, कवचम् shield, शरैः with arrows, प्रच्छादयामास covered.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
नीलाञ्जनचयप्रख्यश्शरैःकाञ्चनभूषणैः । अपीड्यमानश्शुशुभेमेघैस्सूर्यइवांशुमान् ।।6.67.105।।
output: Adorned with golden ornaments (Kumbhakarna), covered with darts without being tormented he looked like a dark mountain shining like sun rays covered by clouds.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
ततस्सराक्षसोभीमस्सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनम् । सावज्ञमेवप्रोवाचवाक्यंमेघौघनिस्स्वनः ।।6.67.106।।
output: Thereupon the Rakshasa sounding like the rumblings of clouds disdainfully spoke these words to Lakshmana, the son of Sumitra.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अन्तकस्याप्यकष्टेन युधि जेतारमाहवे । युध्यतामामभीतेनख्यापितावीरतात्वया ।।6.67.107।।
output: युधि in battle, अकष्टेन without difficulty, अन्तकस्यापि even the Lord of Death, जेतारम् conquered, माम् to me, आहवे challenging, युध्ता in battle, अभीतेन without fear, त्वया by you, वीरता valiance, ख्यापिता exhibited.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
प्रगृहीतायुधस्येहमृत्योरिवमहामृधे । तिष्ठन्नप्रग्रतःपूज्यःकिमुयुद्धप्रदायकः ।।6.67.108।।
output: "He who is ready to face me, a rival of Lord of Death in conflict, with weapons in hand in great battle is worthy of honour to me."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
ऐरावतंबलेनसमारूढोवृतःसर्वामरैःप्रभुः । नैवशक्रोऽपिसमरेस्थितपूर्वःकदाचन ।।6.67.109।।
output: "Indra mounted on the elephant, Airavata surrounded by all Devatas, indeed never stood before me in conflict."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अद्यत्वयाहम्सौमित्रेबालेनापि , नापिपराक्रमैः । तोषितोगन्तुमिच्छामित्यामनुज्ञाप्यराघवम् ।।6.67.110।।
output: सौमित्रे Saumitri, अद्य now, अहम् I, त्वया you, बलेनापिएवेनथोउगः even though young, पराक्रमैः in valour, तोषितः gratified, त्वाम् your, अनुज्ञाप्य taking leave of you, राघवम् Raghava, गन्तुम् to go, इच्छामि wish.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यत्तुवीर्यबलोत्साहैस्तोषितोऽहंरणेत्वया । राममेवैकमिच्छामिहन्तुंयस्मिन् हतेहतम् ।।6.67.111।।
output: "I am gratified by your valour, strength and enthusiasm which has been exhibited by you in the battle. However, I wish to kill Rama alone."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
रामेमयात्रनिहतेयेऽन्येस्थास्यन्तिसंयुगे । तानहंयोधयिष्यामिस्वबलेनप्रमाथिना ।।6.67.112।।
output: अत्र there, मया by me, रामे Rama, निहते put an end, संयुगे in conflict, अन्ये others, ये whoever, स्थास्यन्ति remains, तान् them, प्रमाथिना striking down, स्वबलेन with my army, अहम् I, योधयिष्यामि to fight.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
इत्युक्तवाक्यंतद्रक्षःप्रोवाचस्तुतिसंहितम् । मृधेघोरतरंवाक्यंसौमित्रिःप्रहसन्निव ।।6.67.113।।
output: When that Rakshasa made such boastful and dreadful statements in the battlefield, laughing heartily, Saumitri replied as follows.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यस्त्वंशक्रादिभिर्वरैरसह्यःप्राप्यपौरुषम् । तत्सत्यंनान्यथावीरदृष्टस्तेऽद्यपराक्रमः ।।6.67.114।। एषदाशरथीरामस्तिष्ठत्यद्रिरिवाचलः ।
output: "O Hero! that heroism you have acquired is irresistible even by Indra is true. Now your prowess has been witnessed. Rama stands here, immovable like a mountain."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
इतिश्रुत्वाह्यनादृत्यलक्ष्मणं स निशाचरः ।।6.67.115।। अतिक्रम्य च सौमित्रिंकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः । राममेवाभिदुद्रावकम्पयन्निवमेदिनीम् ।।6.67.116।।
output: निशाचरः night ranger, महाबलः of mighty strength, सःकुम्भकर्णः he, Kumbhakarna, इति thus, श्रुत्वा hearing, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana, अनादृत्य disregarding, सौमित्रिम् Lakshmana, अतिक्रम्य च overlooking, मेदिनम् earth, कम्पयन्निव to shake, राममेव Rama alone, अभिदुद्राव rushed towards.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
इतिश्रुत्वाह्यनादृत्यलक्ष्मणं स निशाचरः ।।6.67.115।। अतिक्रम्य च सौमित्रिंकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः । राममेवाभिदुद्रावकम्पयन्निवमेदिनीम् ।।6.67.116।।
output: निशाचरः night ranger, महाबलः of mighty strength, सःकुम्भकर्णः he, Kumbhakarna, इति thus, श्रुत्वा hearing, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana, अनादृत्य disregarding, सौमित्रिम् Lakshmana, अतिक्रम्य च overlooking, मेदिनम् earth, कम्पयन्निव to shake, राममेव Rama alone, अभिदुद्राव rushed towards.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अथदाशरथींरामोरौद्रमस्त्रंप्रयोजयन् । कुम्भकर्णस्यहृदयेससर्जनिशितान् शरान् ।।6.67.117।।
output: Sri Rama, son of Dasaratha, now released a sharp arrow presided over by Rudra and fixed into the chest of Kumbhakarna.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तस्यरामेणविद्धस्यसहसाभिप्रधावतः । अङ्गालमिश्राःक्रुद्धस्यमुखान्निश्चेरुरर्चिषः ।।6.67.118।।
output: As Rama hit in anger, at once fire mixed with flames shot forth from Kumbhakarna's mouth.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
रामास्त्रविद्धोघोरंवैनदन्राक्षसपुङ्गवः । अभ्यधावतसङ्कृद्धोहरीन् निद्रावयन् रणे ।।6.67.119।।
output: Pierced by Rama's missiles, the foremost of the Rakshasas, Kumbhakarna was very angry and rushed towards him dispersing all the vanaras in the battle.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तस्योरसिनिमग्नास्तेशराबर्हिणवाससः । हस्ताच्छास्यपरिभ्रष्टागदाचोर्व्यांपपात ह ।।6.67.120।।
output: बर्हिणवाससः adorned by peacock's plumes, तेशराः those arrows, तस्य his, उरसि breast, निमग्नाः lost senses, अस्य his, हस्तात् from hand, परिभ्रष्टा slipped, गदा mace, उर्व्याम् naturally, पपात ह fallen.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
आयुधानि च सर्वाणिविप्राकीर्यन्तभूतले । स निरायुधमात्मानंयदामेनेमहाबलः ।।6.67.121।। मुष्टिभ्यां च चरणाभ्यां च चकारकदनंमहत् ।
output: All his weapons scattered on the ground, the mighty Kumbhakarna deprived of weapons thought for himself and created havoc with his feet and fists.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स बाणैरतिविद्धाङ्गःक्षतजेनसमुक्षितः ।।6.67.122।। रुधिरंपरिसुस्रावगिरिःप्रस्रवणंयथा ।
output: Pierced by arrows excessively all over his limbs, bathing in blood flowing from the injury was like a mountain with a spring.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स तीव्रेण च कोपेनरुधिरेण च मूर्छितः ।।6.67.123।। वानरान्राक्षसानृक्षान्खादन्विपरिधावति ।
output: Kumbhakarna in violent anger, blood flowing from the injury, went about devouring Vanaras, Rakshasas and bears.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अथशृङ्गंसमाविध्यभीमंभीमपराक्रमः । चिक्षेपराममुद्धिश्यबलवानन्तकोपमः ।।6.67.124।।
output: Thereupon, Kumbhakarna endowed with terrific valour like God of Death hurled towards Rama a mountain peak whirling it round which split.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अप्राप्तमन्तरारामःसप्तभिस्तमजिह्मगैः । चिच्छेदगिरिशृङ्गंतंपुनःसन्धायकार्मुकम् ।।6.67.125।।
output: Rama once again taking the bow, split the peak of the mountain with seven unfailing arrows on its way even before it reached the target.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततस्तुरामोधर्मात्मातस्यशृङ्गंमहत्तदा ।।6.67.126।। शरैःकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गैश्चिच्छेदपुरुषर्षभः ।
output: The righteous Rama, a bull among men, taking his arrows adorned with gold split the peak of the mountain.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
तन्मेरुशिखराकारंद्योतमानमिवश्रिया ।।6.67.127।। द्वेशतेवानराणां च पतमानमपातयत् ।
output: While falling down, Kumbhakarna was like Mount Meru, shining by his splendour was falling down and knocking down two hundred monkeys.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तस्मिन् काले स धर्मात्मालक्ष्मणोराममब्रवीत् ।।6.67.128।। कुम्भकर्णवधेयुक्तोयोगान् परिमृशन्बहून् ।
output: At that time, righteous Lakshmana who was attentively deliberating on many plans to kill Kumbhakarna, said to Rama.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
नैवायंवानरान्राजन्नविजानातिराक्षसान् ।।6.67.129।। मत्तश्शोणितगन्धे न स्वान् परांश्चैवखादति ।
output: राजन् king, अयम् this, वानरान् Vanaras, नैवविजानाति not knowing, राक्षसान् Rakshasas, न nor, शोणितगन्धेन smell of blood, मत्तः intoxicated, स्वान् his people, परांश्चव foes, खादते devouring.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
साध्वेनमधिरोहस्तुसर्वतोवानरर्षभाः ।।6.67.130।। यूथपाश्चयथामुख्यास्तिष्ठन्त्वस ।
output: Let the bulls among Vanaras climb upon him and the foremost of Vanaras and the troops stand all over.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अप्ययंदुर्मतिःकालेगुरुभारप्रपीडितः ।।6.67.131।। प्रपतन्राक्षसोभूमौनान्यान्हन्यात्ल्पवङ्गमान् ।
output: Distressed by heavy weight unable to get up evil minded Rakshasa fallen on the ground will not destroy monkeys.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तस्यतद्वचनंश्रुत्वाराजपुत्रस्यधीमतः ।।6.67.132।। तेसमारुरुहुर्हृष्टाःकुम्भकर्णंप्लवङ्गमाः ।
output: Having heard the words of the wise Prince, the monkeys collected climbed on Kumbhakarna happily.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
कुम्भकर्णस्तुसङ्कृद्धस्समारूढःप्लवङ्गमैः ।।6.67.133।। व्यधूनयत्तान्वेगेनदुष्टहस्तीवहस्तिपान् ।
output: Enraged Kumbhakarna shook off the monkeys climbed on his body like a harsh elephant shakes off its rider.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
तान् न्दृष्टवानिर्धुतान्रामोदुष्टोऽयमितिराक्षसः ।।6.67.134।। समुत्पपातवेगेनधनुरुत्तममाददे ।
output: Seeing the Vanaras shaken, Rama went towards the Rakshasa instantly and took out his best bow.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
क्रोधरक्तेक्षणोवीरोनिर्दहन्निवचक्षुषा ।।6.67.135।। राघवोराक्षसंरोषाभिदुद्राववेगितः । यूथपान्हर्षयन्सर्वान्कुम्भकर्णभयार्दितान् ।।6.67.136।।
output: Raghava's eyes turned red with anger, went quickly in anger as monkeys and troop leaders oppressed by Kumbhakarna were rejoiced.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
क्रोधरक्तेक्षणोवीरोनिर्दहन्निवचक्षुषा ।।6.67.135।। राघवोराक्षसंरोषाभिदुद्राववेगितः । यूथपान्हर्षयन्सर्वान्कुम्भकर्णभयार्दितान् ।।6.67.136।।
output: Raghava's eyes turned red with anger, went quickly in anger as monkeys and troop leaders oppressed by Kumbhakarna were rejoiced.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स चापमादायभुजङ्गकल्पंधृढज्यमुग्रंतपनीयचित्रम् । हरीन् समाश्वास्यसमुत्पपातरामोनिबद्धोत्तमतूणबाणः ।।6.67.137।।
output: सःरामः that Rama, भुजङ्गकल्पम् resembled a great serpent, धृढज्यम् formidable, उग्रम् frightening, तपनीय shining with polished gold चित्रम् beautiful, चापम् bow, आदाय taking, हरीन् , monkey, समाश्वास्य restoring confidence, निबद्धोत्तमतूणबाणः with quiver full of excellent arrows fastened, समुत्पपात went forward.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स वानरगणैस्तैस्तुवृतःपरमदुर्जयः । लक्ष्मणानुचरोरामस्सम्प्रतस्थेमहाबलः ।।6.67.138।।
output: परमदुर्जयः extremely difficult to win over, लक्ष्मणानुचरः followed by Lakshmana, रामः Rama, महाबलः mighty, तु also, तैः both, वानरगणैः Vanara troops, वृतः surrounded by, सम्प्रतस्थे went with full conviction.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
स ददर्शमहात्मानंकिरीटिनमरिन्दमम् । शोणितावृतरक्ताक्षंकुम्भकर्णंमहाबलम् ।।6.67.139।।
output: Great Rama, endowed with extraordinary might, saw Kumbhakarna, the tamer of enemies covered with blood and having red eyes.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
सर्वान् समभिधावन्तंयथारुष्टंदिशागजम् । मार्गमाणंहरीन्कक्रुद्धंराक्षसैःपरिवारितम् ।।6.67.140।।
output: Surrounded by Rakshasas, he was searching for Vanaras, like an elephant, guarding a quarter, searches.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
व्निध्यमन्दरसङ्काशंकाञ्चनाङ्गदभूषणम् । स्रवन्तंरुधिरंवक्त्राद्वर्षामेघमिवोथतितम् ।।6.67.141।।
output: (Kumbhakarna) Adorned with gold armlets, blood flowing from his mouth was like a rain cloud showering from Vindhya or Mandara mountain.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
जिह्वयापरिलिह्यन्तंसृक्किणीशोणितेक्षणम् । मृद्नन्तंवानरानीकंकालान्तकयमोपमम् ।। 6.67.142।।
output: With blood red eyes, licking the corner of his mouth with his tongue, crushing Vanara army, he looked like God of Death at dissolution.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तंदृष्टवाराक्षसश्रेष्ठंप्रदीप्तानलवर्चसम् । विस्फारयामासतदाकार्मुकंपुरुषर्षभः ।।6.67.143।।
output: पुरुषर्षभः bull among men, प्रदीप्तानलतेजसम् shining like fire, तम् him, राक्षसश्रेष्ठम् foremost of Rakshasas, दृष्टवा seeing, तदा then, कार्मुकम् bow. विस्फारयामास stretched.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स तस्यचापनिर्घोषात्कुपितोराक्षसर्षभः । अमृष्यमाणस्तंघोषमभिदुद्रावराघवम् ।।6.67.144।।
output: तस्य his, चापनिर्घोषात् twang of bow, कुपितः enraged, सः he, राक्षसर्षभः bull among Rakshasas, तंघोषम् that loud sound, अमृष्यमाणदु unable to bear, राघवम् Raghava, अभिदुद्राव rushed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततस्तुवातोद्धतमेघकल्पंभुजङ्गराजोत्तमभोगबाहुम् । तमापतन्तंधरणीराभमुवाचरामोकुम्भकर्णम् ।।6.67.145।।
output: ततः thereafter, रामः Rama, वातोद्धतमेघकल्पम् like a cloud chased by wind, भजङ्गराजोत्तमभोगबाहुम् one whose hands were like Vasuki's body, धरणीधराभम् mountain like, युधि battlefield, आपतन्तम् coming to attack, कुम्भकर्णम् Kumbhakarna, उवाच spoke.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
आगच्छरक्षोधिपमाविषादमवस्थितोऽहंप्रगृहीतचापः । अवेहिमांराक्षसवंशनाशनंयस्त्वंमुहूर्ताद्भविता ।।6.67.146।।
output: "O king of Rakshasas! Come. Do not be despondent. I stand with my bow. In a moment I will destroy you. Look, the Rakshasa clan will be put to an end."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
रामोऽयमितिविज्ञायजहासविकृतस्वनम् । अभ्यधावतसङ्ककृद्धोहरीवनिद्रावयन्रणे ।।6.67.147।।
output: Knowing that this is Rama, Kumbhakarna laughed in an unnatural manner making a sound and ran after scattering the monkeys in great rage.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
पातयन्निवसर्वेषांहृदयनिवनौकसाम् । प्रहस्यविकृतंभीमंसमेघस्न्तितोपमम् ।।6.67.148।। कुम्भकर्णोमहातेजाराघवंवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
output: Highly energetic Kumbhakarna laughing in hideous ways making sounds like rumblings of clouds breaking the hearts of forest rangers spoke these words.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
नाहंविराधोविज्ञेयो न कबन्दःखरो न च । न वाली न च मारीचःकुम्भकर्णःसमागतः ।।6.67.149।।
output: अहम् I am, विराधः Viradha, न विज्ञेयः not Vijeya, कबन्दः Kabhanda, न not, खरः Khara, नच not also, वाली Vali, न not, मारीचः च Maricha also, न not, कुम्भकर्णः Kumbhakarna, समागतः have come.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
पश्यमेमुद्गरंभीमंसर्वकालायसंमहत् । अनेननिर्जितादेवादानवाश्चपुरामया ।।6.67.150।।
output: "See my terrible club made of wrought iron. By this I have won earlier Devatas and Danavas."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
विकर्णवासइतिमांनावज्ञातुंत्वमर्हसि । स्वल्पाऽपिहि न मेपीडार्णनासाविनाशनात् ।।6.67.151।।
output: "Do not think I have been deprived of ears and nose and look with contempt. I do not have little pain."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
दर्शयेक्ष्वाकुशार्दूलवीर्यंगात्रेषुमेलघु । ततस्त्वांभक्षयिष्यामिदृष्टपौरुषविक्रमम् ।।6.67.152।।
output: "O Tiger of the Ikshvaku clan! Exhibit your manliness, prowess, and valour on me. I will eat you up later."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स कुम्भकर्णस्यवचोनिशम्यरामस्सुपुङ्खान् विससर्जन् । तैराहतोवज्रसमवेगैर्नचुक्षुभे न व्यथतेसुरारिः ।।6.67.153।।
output: सःरामः that Rama, कुम्भकर्णस्य Kumbhakarna's, वचः words, निशम्य bewildered, सपुङ्खान् plumed arrows, बाणान् arrows, विससर्ज discharged, वज्रसमवेगैः at the speed of thunderbolt, तैः those, आहतः having been struck, सुरारिः enemy of Devatas, न चुक्षुभे न व्यथते not shaken or agonized.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यैस्सायकैस्सालवरानिकृत्तावालीहतोवानरपुङ्गवश्च । तेकुम्भकर्णस्यतदाशरीरंवज्रोपमं न व्यधयांप्रचक्रुः ।।6.67.154।।
output: यैः by that, सायकैः arrows, सालवराः Sala trees, निकृत्ताः cut down, वानरपुङ्गवः Vanara leaders, वाली च Vali also, हतः struck, ते that, तदा then, वज्रोपमम् like thunderbolt, कुम्भकर्णस्यशरीरम् Kumbhakarna's body, न व्यधयांप्रचक्रुः not able to affect him.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स वारिधाराइवसायकास्तान् पिबन् शरीरेणमहेन्द्रशत्रुः । जघानरामस्यशरप्रवेगंव्याविध्यतंमुग्रवेगम् ।।6.67.155।।
output: The enemy of Lord Indra drank the arrows through his body and hurled his club at great speed whirling it round and round arrested the arrows of Rama.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततस्तुरक्षःक्षतजावलिप्तंवित्रासनंदेवमहचमूनाम् । व्याविध्यतंमुद्गरमुग्रवेगंनिद्रावयामासचमूंम् ।।6.67.156।।
output: ततः then, रक्षः Rakshasa, क्षतजावलिप्तम् covered with cuts and wounds, देवमहाचमूनाम् frightening even to the mighty celestials, वित्रासनम् covered with blood, उग्रवेगम् at high speed, तंमुद्गरम् that club, व्याविध्य scattered, हरीणाम् monkeys, चमूम् , विद्रावयामास with the club.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
वायव्यमादायततोमहास्त्रंरामःप्रचिक्षेपनिशाचराय । समुद्गरंतेनजघानबाहुं स कृत्तबाहुस्तुमुलंनाद ।।6.67.157।।
output: Thereupon taking up the weapon of Wind God, Rama discharged on the night ranger and severed his right arm with the mace. His arm torn off, Kumbhakarna made uproarious noise.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स तस्यबाहुर्गिरिशृङ्गकल्पःसमुद्गरोराघवबाणकृत्तः । पपाततस्मिन् हरिराजसैन्येजघानतांवानरवाहिनीं ।।6.17.158।।
output: Kumbhakarna's arm severed by Rama's arrow was like a mountain peak. It fell on Vanara army too and killed the monkey king's army.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तेवानराभग्नहतावशेषाःपर्यन्तमाश्रित्यतदाविषण्णाः । प्रपीडिताङ्गाददृशुस्सुघोरंनरेन्द्ररक्षोधिपन्निपातम् ।।6.67.159।।
output: तदा then, भग्नहतावशेषाः Vanaras who escaped from getting killed and mutilated, तेवानराः those Vanaras, प्रपीडिताङ्गाः feeling desperate, विषण्णाः terrible, पर्यन्तम् close, आश्रित्य going, सुघोरम् dreadful, नरेन्द्ररक्षोधिपसन्निपातम् between Kumbhakarna and Rama, ददृशुः witnessed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स कुम्भकर्णोऽस्त्रनिकृत्तबाहुर्महासिकृत्ताग्रइवाचलेन्द्रः । उत्पाटयामासकरेणवृक्षंततोऽभिदुद्रावरणेनरेन्द्रम् ।।6.67.160।।
output: अस्त्रनिकृत्तबाहुः arm cut off by arrow, महासिना like peak cut off, कृत्ताग्रः deprived of limb, अचलेन्द्रःइव like a mountain, सः he कुम्भकर्णः Kumbhakarna, करेण Palmyra, वृक्षम् tree, उत्पाटयमास seized, ततः thereafter, रणे battle, नरेन्द्रम् king, अभिदुद्राव went towards.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स तस्यबाहुंसहतालवृक्षंसमुद्यतंपन्नगभोगकल्पम् । इन्द्रास्त्रयुक्तेनजघानरामोबाणेनजाम्भूनदचित्रितेन ।।6.67.161।।
output: सःरामः that Rama, इन्द्रास्त्रयुक्तेन yoking bow charged with Indra's mantra, जाम्भूनदचित्रितेन decked with gold, बाणेन arrow, तस्य of his, पन्नगभोगकल्पम् like coils of serpent, समुद्यतम् held, सतालवृक्षम् the Palmyra tree, बाहुम् arms, जघान severed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स कुम्भकर्णस्यभुजोनिकृत्तःपपातभूमौगिरिसन्निकाशः । विवेष्टमानोनिजाघनवृक्षान् शैलान्शिलावानरराक्षसांश्च ।।6.67.162।।
output: कुम्भकर्णस्य Kumbhakarna's, गिरिसन्निकाशः resembled a mountain, सःभुजः that arm, निकृत्तः severed, भूमौ on ground, पपात fell, विवेष्टमानाः turning round and round, वृक्षान् trees, शैलान् mountains, शिलावानरराक्षसांश्च mountains, Vanaras and Rakshasas, निजघान crushed.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
तंछिन्नबाहुंसमवेक्ष्यरामःसमापतन्तंसहसानदन्तम् । द्वावर्धचन्द्रौनिशितौप्रगृह्यचिच्छेदपादौयुधिराक्षसस्य ।।6.67.163।।
output: Perceiving Kumbhakarna with broken arms rushing towards him, Rama at once took a sharp moon shaped arrow and split his feet.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तौतस्यपादौप्रदिशोदिशश्चगिरेर्गुहाश्चैवमहार्णवं च । लङ्कां च सेनांकपिराक्षसानांविनादयन्तौविनिपेततुश्च ।।6.67.164।।
output: तस्य his, तौ both, पादौ feet, प्रदिशः quarters, दिशश्च directions, गिरेः mountains, गुहाश्चैव even caves of Trikuta too, महार्णवंच great ocean also, लङ्कां च Lanka also, कपिराक्षसानाम् even the Vanaras and Rakshasas, सेनाम् army, विनादयन्तौ resounded, विनिपेततुश्च filled all over.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
निकृत्तबाहुद्विनिकृत्तपादोविदार्यवक्त्रंबडबामुखाभम् । दुद्रावरामंसहसाभिगर्जन् राहुर्यथाचन्द्रमिवान्तऽरिक्षे ।।6.67.165।।
output: Arms broken, feet cut off, dilating his mouth like fire, shouting aloud like Rahu entering moon in the sky he rushed to Rama speedily.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अपूरयत्तस्यमुखंशिताग्रैरामश्शरैर्हेमपिनद्धपुङ्खैः । स पूर्णवक्त्रो न शशाकवक्तुंचुकूजकृच्छ्रेणमुमूर्छचापि ।।6.67.166।।
output: रामः Rama, शिताग्रैः sharp pointed, हेमपिनद्धपुङ्खैः gold encrusted, शरैः shafts, तस्य his, मुखम् mouth, अपूरयत् filled, सः he, पूर्णवक्त्रः mouth fully, वक्तुम् mouth, न शशाक not able to speak, कृच्छ्रेण moaned, चुकूज shouted, मुमूर्छचापि fainted.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अथाददेसूर्यमरीचिकल्पं स ब्रह्मदण्डान्तककाकलकल्पम् । अरिष्टमैन्द्रंनिशितंसुपुङ्खंरामश्शरंमारुततुल्यवेगम् ।।6.67.167।।
output: अथ and then, सःरामः that Rama, सूर्यमरीचिकल्पम् effulgent as sunbeam with feathers, ब्रह्मदण्डान्तककालकल्पम् rod of Brahma and the Time spirit, अरिष्टम् destructive, निशितम् sharp, सुपुङ्खम् fatal to the enemies, मारुततुल्यवेगम् fast as the wind, ऐन्द्रंशरम् Indra's arrow charged with mantra, आददे took.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
तंवज्रजाम्भूनदचारुपुङ्खंप्रदीप्तसूर्यज्वलनप्रकाशम् । महेन्द्रवज्राशनितुल्यवेगंरामःप्रचिक्षेपनिशाचराय ।।6.67.168।।
output: Rama crushed the night ranger to pieces with his arrow encrusted with diamonds and gold, glowing like the Sun 's rays and fire which resembled Indra's thunderbolt, in speed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स सायकोराघवबाहुचोदितोदिशस्स्वभासादशसम्प्रकाशयन् । विधूमवैश्वानरभीमदर्शनोजगामशक्राशनिवीर्यविक्रमः ।।6.67.169।।
output: राघवबाहुचोदितः discharged from Rama's arm, विधूमवैश्वानरभीमदर्शनः terrific just as Vritasura's head was cut off by Indra, the Lord of gods, शक्राशनिवीर्यविक्रमः which was like Indra's thunderbolt, सःसायकः like burning fire, स्वभासा by its brilliance, दश ten, दिशः directions, प्रकाशयन् shining, जगाम went.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स तन्महापर्वतकूटसन्निभंविवृत्तदंष्ट्रंचलचारुकुण्डलम् । चकर्तरक्षोधिपतेश्शिरस्तदायथैववृत्रस्यपुरापुरन्दरः ।।6.67.170।।
output: सः that, महापर्वतकूटसन्निभम् lofty peak of a mountain, विवृत्तदंष्ट्रम् distinguished by large pointed teeth, चलचारुकुण्डलम् shaking ear rings, रक्षोधिपतेः Rakshasa king, शिरः head, तदा then, पुरा earlier, पुरन्दरः Indra, वृत्रस्य Vritasya, यतैव like that, चकर्त severed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कुम्भकर्णशिरोभातिकुण्डलालङ्कृतंमहत् । आदित्येऽभ्युदितेरात्रौमध्यस्थइवचन्द्रमाः ।।6.67.171।।
output: कुण्डलालङ्कृतम् adorned with earrings, महत् huge, कुम्भकर्णशिरः head of Kumbhakarna, रात्रौ night, आदित्ये by Aditi, उदिते risen, मध्यस्थः in the middle, चन्द्रमाःइव like the moon, भाति shone.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 67:
तद्रामबाणाभिहतंपपातरक्षःशिरःपर्वतसन्निकाशम् । बभञ्जचर्यागृहगोपुराणिप्राकारमुच्चंतमपातयच्च ।।6.67.172।।
output: Killed by Rama's arrow, that head of the Rakshasa, which was like a mountain had demolished the walls and houses and peaks of buildings.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तच्चातिकायंहिमहत्प्रकाशंरक्षस्तदातोयनिधौपपात । ग्राहान्परान् मीनवरान्भुजङ्गान् ममर्दभूमिच तदाविवेश ।।6.67.173।।
output: The shining huge body of Rakshasa fell into the ocean crushing the other beings in the ocean like alligators, fishes and serpents that entered into the earth.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तस्मिन्हतेब्राह्मणदेवशत्रौमहाबलेसंयतिकुम्भकर्णे । चचालभूर्भूमिधराश्चसर्वेहर्षाच्चदेवास्तुमुलंविनेदुः ।।6.67.174।।
output: ब्राह्मणदेवशत्रौ the enemy of Brahmans and Devatas, महाबले mighty, तस्मिन् his, कुम्भकर्णे Kumbhakarna, संयति having died, हते killed, भूः earth, चचाल mountains, सर्वे all, भूमिधराश्च god of earth, देवाः च Devatas, हर्षात् rejoiced, तुमुलम् highly, विनेदुः uproar.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततस्तुदेवर्षिमहर्षिपन्नगाःसुराश्चभूतानिसुपर्णगुह्यकाः । सयक्षगन्धर्वगणानभोगताःप्रहर्षितारामपराक्रमेण ।।6.67.175।।
output: ततः thereafter, देवर्षिमहर्षिपन्नगाः celestial sages and sages, as well as serpents, सुराश्च Devatas, भूतानि all beings, सुपर्णगुह्यकाः eagles and Guhyakas, सयक्षगन्धर्वगणाः Yaksha, Gandharvas, नभोगताः highly rejoiced, रामपराक्रमेण by Rama's valour, सन्तोषिताः rejoiced very much.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततस्तुतेतस्यवधेनभूरिणामनस्विनोनैरृतराजबान्धवाः । विनेदुरुच्चैर्व्यथितारघूत्तमंहरिंसमीक्ष्यैवयथासुरार्धिताः ।।6.67.176।।
output: Thereupon, the courageous kinsfolk of Ravana, resolute in mind, pained by the death of Kumbhakarna, feared the foremost of Raghus, just as elephants feared seeing the Lord of Devatas, and emitted loud cries.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स देवलोकस्यतमोनिहत्यसूर्योयथाराहुमुखाद्विमुक्तः । तथाव्यभासीद्धरिसैन्यमध्येनिहत्यरामोयुधिकुम्भकर्णम् ।।6.67.177।।
output: Having killed Kumbhakarna, in the combat, Rama shone brilliantly just as Sun liberated from Rahu's mouth, after dispersing the darkness of the abode of Devatas.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
प्रहर्षमीयुर्भवश्चवानराःप्रबुद्धपद्मप्रतिमैरिवाननैः । अपूजयन् राघवमिष्टभागिनंहतेरिसौभीमबलेदुरासदम् ।।6.67.178।।
output: Many Vanaras, with their faces resembling full blown lotuses joyfully laughed and worshipped Rama for getting rid of an enemy of terrific strength.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 68:
कुम्भकर्णंहतंदृष्टवाराघवेणमहात्मना । राक्षसाराक्षसेन्द्रायरावणायन्यवेदयन् ।।6.68.1।।
output: Seeing Kumbhakarna slain by the glorious Raghava, the Rakshasas informed Ravana, the king of Rakshasas.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 68:
राजन् स कालसङ्काशस्संयुक्तःकालकर्मणा । विद्राव्यवानरींसेनांभक्षयित्वा च वानरान् ।।6.68.2।।
output: "O King! Kumbhakarna, who was equal to the God of Death, devoured and won over the Vanaras, scattered the army, has joined death as a consequence of time (fate)."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 68:
प्रतपित्वा मुहूर्तंतुप्रशान्तोरामतेजसा । कायेनार्थप्रविष्टेनसमुद्रंभीमदर्शनम् ।।6.68.3।। निकृत्तकण्ठोरुभुजोविक्षरन्रुधिरंबहु । रुद्ध्वाद्वारंशरीरेणलङ्कायाःपर्वतोपमः ।।6.68.4।। कुम्भकर्णस्तवभ्राताकाकुत्स्थशरपीडितः । लगण्डभूतोविकृतोदावदग्धइवद्रुमः ।।6.68.5।।
output: "Your brother Kumbhakarna showed his might for a short time. But by virtue of Rama's energy and arrows, his mountainlike body was reduced to a trunk of dreadful appearance. Bleeding excessively, he was like a mass submerged in an ocean of blood. like a tree caught in forest fire he was blocking the gate of Lanka in ugly form with a head, nose and ears chopped off."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
प्रतपित्वा मुहूर्तंतुप्रशान्तोरामतेजसा । कायेनार्थप्रविष्टेनसमुद्रंभीमदर्शनम् ।।6.68.3।। निकृत्तकण्ठोरुभुजोविक्षरन्रुधिरंबहु । रुद्ध्वाद्वारंशरीरेणलङ्कायाःपर्वतोपमः ।।6.68.4।। कुम्भकर्णस्तवभ्राताकाकुत्स्थशरपीडितः । लगण्डभूतोविकृतोदावदग्धइवद्रुमः ।।6.68.5।।
output: "Your brother Kumbhakarna showed his might for a short time. But by virtue of Rama's energy and arrows, his mountainlike body was reduced to a trunk of dreadful appearance. Bleeding excessively, he was like a mass submerged in an ocean of blood. like a tree caught in forest fire he was blocking the gate of Lanka in ugly form with a head, nose and ears chopped off."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
प्रतपित्वा मुहूर्तंतुप्रशान्तोरामतेजसा । कायेनार्थप्रविष्टेनसमुद्रंभीमदर्शनम् ।।6.68.3।। निकृत्तकण्ठोरुभुजोविक्षरन्रुधिरंबहु । रुद्ध्वाद्वारंशरीरेणलङ्कायाःपर्वतोपमः ।।6.68.4।। कुम्भकर्णस्तवभ्राताकाकुत्स्थशरपीडितः । लगण्डभूतोविकृतोदावदग्धइवद्रुमः ।।6.68.5।।
output: तव your, भ्राता brother, कुम्भकर्णः Kumbhakarna, मुहूर्तम् for a short time, प्रतपित्वा showed his might, रामतेजसा by Rama's energy, प्रशान्तः became, पर्वतोपमः mountain like, काकुत्स्थशरपीडितः pained by Kakutstha's arrows, अर्थप्रविष्टेन half of the trunk of his body, कायेन body, भीमदर्शनम् of dreadful appearance, समुद्रम् ocean, निकृत्तकण्ठोरुभुजः headless and limbless ugly form, बहुरुदिरं excessive blood, विक्षरन् appearing as if, शरीरेण from the body, लङ्कायाः Lanka, द्वारम् gate, रुद्ध्वा blocking, दावदग्धः forest fire, द्रुमःइव like tree, विकृतः ugly form, लगण्डभूताः head with nose and ears chopped off.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 68:
तंश्रुत्वाविनिहतंसङ्ख्येकुम्भकर्णंमहाबलम् । रावणश्शोकसन्तप्तोमुमोह च पपात च ।।6.68.6।।
output: Hearing that Kumbhakarna of great strength was slain, Ravana immersed in grief became deluded and fell.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 68:
पितृव्यंनिहतंश्रुत्वादेवान्तकनरान्तकौ । त्रिशिराश्चातिकायश्चरुरुदुश्शोकपीडिताः ।।6.68.7।।
output: Hearing about uncle's destruction, the sons of Ravana, Devanthaka, Naranthaka, Trisira and Atikaya, roared aloud afflicted by grief.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 68:
भ्रातरंनिहतंश्रुत्वारामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । महोदरमहापार्श्वौशोकाक्रान्तौबभूवतुः ।।6.68.8।।
output: Ravana's brothers, Mahodara and Mahaparsva were overtaken by sorrow on hearing about the unwearied action of Rama and slaying of Kumbhakarna.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 68:
ततःकृच्छ्रात्समासाद्यसंज्ञांराक्षसपुङ्गवः । कुम्भकर्णवधाद्दीनोविललापकुलेन्द्रियः ।।6.68.9।।
output: Thereafter the foremost of the Rakshasas regained consciousness with great difficulty and awakened to the situation of Kumbhakarna's destruction, wailed disturbed in mind.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 68:
हावीर रिपुदर्पघ्न कुम्भकर्ण महाबल । त्वंमांविहायवैदैवाद्यातोऽसियमसादनम् ।।6.68.10।।
output: "Ha! Hero! Kumbhakarna! You, who crushed the pride of the enemy, endowed with great prowess have deserted me and gone to the abode of death, actually by divine will."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ममशल्यमनुद्धृत्यबान्धवानांमहाबल । शत्रुसैन्यंप्रताप्यैकस्त्वंमांसन्त्यज्यगच्छसि ।।6.68.11।।
output: "O Kumbhakarna of extraordinary might! You have tormented the enemy army singlehanded with valour. You are going alone leaving me and the kinsfolk."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 68:
इदानींखल्वहंनास्मियस्यमेदक्षिणोभुजः । पतितोयंसमाश्रित्य न बिभेमिसुरासुरान् ।।6.68.12।।
output: "I who depended on you like my right arm did not fear Devatas or Danavas and I am destroyed now."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
कथमेवंविधोवीरोदेवदानवदर्पहा । कालाग्निरुद्राप्रतिमोरणेराघवेणवैहतः ।।6.68.13।।
output: देवदानवदर्पहा one who crushed the pride of Devas and Danavas, कालाग्निरुद्राप्रतिमः equal to time spirit and death at the time of destruction, एवंविधः being so, वीरः hero, रणे in battle, राघवेण by Raghava, कथम् how, हतःवै did you die?

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यस्यतेवज्रनिष्पेषो न कुर्वाद्व्यसनंसदा । स कथंरामबाणार्तंप्रसुप्तोऽसिमहीतले ।।6.68.14।।
output: "You are never affected by the strike of thunderbolt. How are you sleeping on the ground hit by Rama's arrows?"

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
एतेदेवगणास्सार्थमृषिभिर्गगनेस्थिताः । निहतंत्वांरणेदृष्टवानिनदन्तिप्रहर्षिताः ।।6.68.15।।
output: "These Devatas and all sages are standing in the sky, seeing the battle and laughing aloud seeing your destruction."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ध्रुवमद्यैवसंहृष्टालब्धलक्षाःप्लवङ्गमाः । आरोक्ष्यन्तीहदुर्गाणिलङ्काद्वाराणिसर्वशः ।।6.68.16।।
output: "Having found an opportunity, all the Vanaras, highly rejoiced, on this very day, will surely climb over the gates of forts of Lanka determined."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
राज्येननास्तिमेकार्यंकिंकरिष्यामिसीतया । कुम्भकर्णविहीनस्यजीवितेनास्तिमेमतिः ।।6.68.17।।
output: "I have no purpose with the kingdom. What will I do with Sita? I have lost my life and mind with Kumbhakarna's death."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
यद्यहंभ्रातृहन्तारं न हन्मियुधिराघवम् । ननुमेमरणंश्रेयो न चेदंव्यर्थजीवितम् ।।6.68.18।।
output: अहम् I am, भ्रातृहन्तारम् who killed my brother, राघवम् Raghavan, युधि in battle, न हन्मियदि if I do not kill, मे my, मरणम् death, श्रेयःननु better for me, इदम् thus, व्यर्थजीवितम् waste of life, न not worth.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अद्यैवतंगमिष्यामिदेशंयत्रानुजोमम । न हिभ्रातृ़न् समुत्सृज्यक्षणंजीवितमुत्सहे ।।6.68.19।।
output: "This very day, this very minute I shall reach the region where my brother died, I have no interest in life."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 68:
देवाहिमांहसिष्यन्तिदृष्टवापूर्वापकारिणम् । कथमिन्द्रंजयिष्यामिकुम्भकर्ण हतेत्वयि ।।6.68.20।।
output: "Devatas who were harmed by me earlier will laugh at me now that Kumbhakarna is slain. How will I win Indra?"

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तदिदंमामनुप्राप्तंविभीषणवचश्शुभम् । यदज्ञानान्मयातस्य न गृहीतंमहात्मनः ।।6.68.21।।
output: अज्ञानात् this calamity, महात्मनः great soul, तस्य his, यत् that which, मया by me, न गृहीतम् not taken, तत् that, इदम् such, शुभम् auspicious, विभीषणवचः Vibheeshana's words of advice, माम् me, अनुप्राप्तम् not accepted.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
विभीषणवचोयावत्कुम्भकर्णप्रहस्तयोः । विनाशोऽयंसमुत्पन्नोमांव्रीडयतिदारुणः ।।6.68.22।।
output: "Thus, loss of both Kumbhakarna and Prahastha is dreadful. It is because of not following the words of advice of Vibheeshana totally. It hurts me."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तस्यायंकर्मणःप्राप्तोविपाकोममशोकदः । यन्मयाधार्मिकश्शमान् स निरस्तोविभीषणः ।।6.68.23।।
output: "Righteous and prosperous Vibheeshana has been expelled by me earlier. By that action, I have obtained this grief."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
एवंविलपमानस्यरावणस्यदुरात्मनः । श्रुत्वाशोकाभितप्तस्यत्रिशिरावाक्यमब्रवीत् ।।6.69.1।।
output: Hearing the lamentations of the evilminded Ravana, Trisira spoke to him.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
एवमेवमहावीर्योहतोनस्तातमध्यमः । न तुसत्पुरुषाराजन्विलपन्तियथाभवान् ।।6.69.2।।
output: "There is no doubt that Kumbhakarna, who is your middle father and uncle, was also endowed with great prowess. He has been killed. O King! Good men like you do not wail."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
नूनंत्रिभुवनस्यापिपर्याप्तस्त्वमसिप्रभो । स कस्मात्प्राकृतइवशोचस्यात्मानमीदृशम् ।।6.69.3।।
output: "O King! You are a conqueror of the three worlds. Why do you wail like a common man?"

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ब्रह्मदत्ताऽस्तितेशक्तिःकवचस्सायकोधनुः । सहस्रखरसंयुक्तोरथोमेघस्वनोमहान् ।।6.69.4।।
output: "You are bestowed by Brahma with a javelin, a shield and an arrow and a chariot yoked by a thousand donkeys making rumbling sounds like a cloud."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
त्वयाऽसकृद्विशस्त्रेणविशस्तादेवदानवाः । स सर्वायुधसम्पन्नोराघवंशास्तुमर्हसि ।।6.69.5।।
output: "Devas and Danavas have been won over by you, deprived of weapons also. Now endowed with all weapons you will be able to win Raghava."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
कामंतिष्ठमहाराजनिर्गमिष्याम्यहंरणम् । उद्धरिष्यामितेशत्रूंन्गरुडःपन्नगानिव ।।6.69.6।।
output: "O King! Stay on. I will move forth to the battlefield and uproot your enemy like Garuda uprooted serpents."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
शम्बरोदेवराजेननरकोविष्णुवायथा । तथाऽद्यशयितारामोमयायुधिनिपातितः ।।6.69.7।।
output: शम्बरः Sambara, देवराजेन Lord of Devas, नरकः Naraka, विष्णुना like Vishnu, यथा that way, तथा in the same manner, मया by me, अद्य struck, युधि in combat, निपातितः destroyed, रामः Rama, शयिता throw down.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
श्रुत्वात्रिशिरसोवाक्यंरावणोराक्षसाधिपः । पुनर्जातमिवात्मानंमन्यतेकालचोदितः ।।6.69.8।।
output: राक्षसाधिपः King of Rakshasas, रावणः Ravana, त्रिशिरसः Trisira's, वाक्यम् words, श्रुत्वा hearing, कालचोदितः impelled by destiny, आत्मानम् himself, पुनः again, जातम् इव as if born again, मन्यते thought.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
श्रुत्वात्रिशिरसोवाक्यंदेवान्तकनरान्तकौ । अतिकायश्चतेजस्वीबभूवुर्युद्धहर्षिताः ।।6.69.9।।
output: त्रिशिरसः Trisira, वाक्यम् words, श्रुत्वा hearing, देवान्तकनरान्तकौ Devanthaka and Naranthaka both, तेजस्वी glorious, अतिकायश्च Atikaya, युद्धहर्षिताः enthusiastic to fight war, बभूवुः became.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततोऽहमहमित्येवगर्जन्तोनैरृतर्षभाः । रावणस्यसुतावीराश्शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमाः ।।6.69.10।।
output: Then Ravana's sons, the heroes, and bulls among ogres, equal to Indra in valour, roared saying, "I will start", "I will lead."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
अन्तरिक्षगतास्सर्वेसर्वेमायाविशारदाः । सर्वेत्रिदशदर्पघ्नास्सर्वे च रणदुर्जयाः ।।6.69.11।।
output: All (sons of Ravana) are capable of coursing through the sky, experts in conjuring tricks, capable of crushing the pride of Devatas and all, are fierce in fighting.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
सर्वेसुबलसम्पन्नास्सर्वेविस्तीर्णकीर्तयः । सर्वेसमरमासाद्य न श्रूयन्तेस्मपराजिताः ।।6.69.12।। देवैरपिसगन्धर्वैस्सकिन्नरमहोरगैः ।
output: All sons of Ravana possessed stupendous strength, all were very famous, and never got defeated in war be it Gandharvas, Kinnaras or even gods will get vanquished by them.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सर्वेस्त्रविदुषोवीरास्सर्वेयुद्धविशारदाः ।।6.69.13।। सर्वेप्रसवरविज्ञानास्सर्वेलब्धवरास्तथा ।
output: सर्वall, अस्त्रविदुषः experts in the use of weapons, वीराः heroes, सर्वेall, युद्धविशारदाः skilled in warfare, सर्वall, प्रवरविज्ञानाः knowledgeable in scriptures, तथा so also, सर्वे all, लब्धवराः received boons.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
सतैस्तथाभास्करतुल्यवर्चसैःपुस्त्रैर्वृतश्शत्रुबलप्रमार्दनैः । रराजराजामघवान्यथामरै ।र्वृतोमहादानवदर्पनाशनैः ।।6.69.14।।
output: Surrounded by his sons, who matched Sun in brilliance and capable of crushing the pride of foes, great in destroying immortals, Ravana shone like Lord gods.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स पुत्रान् सम्परिष्वज्यभूषयित्वा च भूषणैः । आशीर्भिश्चप्रशस्ताभिःप्रेषयामाससम्युगे ।।6.69.15।।
output: Ravana embraced his sons, decked them with ornaments and jewels and enriched them and offered benediction and sent to encounter.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
युद्धोन्मत्तं च मत्तं च भ्रातरौचापिरावणः । रक्षणार्थंकुमाराणांप्रेषयामाससंयुगे ।।6.69.16।।
output: Ravana sent his two brothers Yuddhonmatta and Matta for the protection of his sons for defence in combat.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तेऽभिवाद्यमहात्मानंरावणंरिपुरावणम् । कृत्वाप्रदक्षिणंचैवमहाकायाःप्रतस्थिरे ।।6.69.17।।
output: Those heroes greeting gigantic Ravana, went around him clockwise (as per tradition) and departed.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
सर्वौषधीभिर्गन्धैश्चसमालभ्यमहाबलाः । निर्जग्मुर्नैरृतश्रेष्ठाषडेतेयुद्धकाङ्क्षिणः ।।6.69.18।।
output: The six leaders endowed with great strength, anointing themselves with fragrance, which can ward off injury went to fight.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
त्रिशिराश्चातिकायश्चदेवान्तकनरान्तकौ । महोदरमहापार्श्वौनिर्जग्मुःकालचोदिताः ।।6.69.19।।
output: Trisira, also Atikaya, Devanthaka, Naranthaka, Mahodara and Mahaparsva impelled by destiny went.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततस्सुदर्शनंनागंनीलजीमूतसन्निभम् । ऐरावतकुलेजातमारुरोहमहोदरः ।।6.69.20।।
output: Thereafter Mahodara mounted on an elephant born of Airavata (Indra 's elephant) family, by name Sudarsana went.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सर्वायुधसमायुक्तंतूणीभिश्चस्वलङ्कृतम् । रराजगजमास्थायसवितेवास्तमूर्धनि ।।6.69.21।।
output: सर्वायुधसमायुक्तः ready with all kinds of weapons, तूणीभिश्चा quivers also, स्वलङ्कृतः decked, गजम् elephant, आस्थाय mounted, अस्तमूर्धनि on the western region, सवितेव like Sun, रराज shone.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
हयोत्तमसमायुक्तंसर्वायुधसमाकुलम् । आरुरोहरथश्रेष्ठंत्रिशिरारावणात्मजः ।।6.69.22।।
output: Ravana's brother, Trisira went mounted on a chariot yoked to the best of horses with all kinds of weapons.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
त्रिशिरारथमास्थायविरराजधनुर्धरः । सविद्युदुल्कश्शैलाग्रेस्सेन्द्रइवाम्बुदः ।।6.69.23।।
output: Wielding a bow and sitting like a leader in the chariot Trisira shone as if attended by lightning, meteors, light, and rainbows.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
त्रिभिःकिरीटैश्शुशुभेत्रिशिरास्सरथोत्तमे । हिमवानिशैलेन्द्रस्त्रिभिःकाञ्चनपर्वतैः ।।6.69.24।।
output: Trisira seated in the best of chariots, with his three heads adorned with crowns shone like the golden mountain, Himalayas with its three peaks.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अतिकायोऽपितितेजस्वीराक्षसेन्द्रसुतस्तदा । आरुरोहरथश्रेष्ठंश्रेष्ठस्सर्वधनुष्मताम् ।।6.69.25।।
output: तदा then, अतितेजस्वी very bright, राक्षसेन्द्रसुतः Lord of Rakshasas's son, सर्वधनुष्मताम् all archers, श्रेष्ठः best of, अतिकायः Atikaya, रथश्रेष्ठम् best of chariots, आरुरोह mounted.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
सुचक्राक्षंसुसंयुक्तंस्वनुकर्षंसुकूबरम् । तूणीबाणासनैर्दीप्तंप्रासासिपरिघाकुलम् ।।6.69.26।।
output: The chariot (of Atikaya) had excellent wheels, well fitted with strong axles, stout poles, equipped with quivers and bows, with best of spears, bars, and swords.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सकाञ्चनविचित्रेणमकुटेनविराजता । भूषणैश्चबभौमेरुःप्रभाभिरिवभासयन् ।।6.69.27।।
output: सः he, काञ्चनविचित्रेण wonderful gold, विराजता shining, मकुटेन coronet, भूषणैश्च encrusted, प्रभाभिः sparkling, भासयन् splendid, मेरुःइव like Meru, बभौ seemed.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
स रराजरथेतस्मिन् राजसूनुर्महाबलः । वृतोनैरृतशार्दूलैर्वज्रपाणिरिवामरैः ।।6.69.28।।
output: The tiger among ogres (Atikaya) surrounded by the great army of ogres, the prince was shining in the chariot like Indra, the king of gods and wielder of thunderbolt.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
हयमुच्चैश्श्रवःप्रख्यंश्वेतंकनकभूषणम् । मनोजवंमहाकायमारुरोहनरान्तकः ।।6.69.29।।
output: Naranthaka, mounted on Uchaisrava, the white horse, decked in gold, was swift as thought in speed.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
गृहीत्वाप्रासमुल्काभंविरराजनरान्तकः । शक्तिमादायतेजस्वीगुहशशिखिगतोयथा ।।6.69.30।।
output: Naranthaka seizing a barbed missile like a burning spear, looked like son of Lord Siva wielding javelin in hand.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
देवान्ककस्समादायपरिघंवज्रभूषणम् । परिगृह्यगिरिंदोर्भ्यांवपुर्विष्णोर्विडम्बयन् ।।6.69.31।।
output: Devanthaka, holding a bar encrusted with diamonds in both hands, seemed like Vishnu in disguise with a mountain (to churn the milky ocean).

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
महापार्श्वोमहाकायोगदामादायवीर्यवान् । विरराजगदापाणिःकुबेरइवसंयुगे ।।6.69.32।।
output: Mahaparsva holding an ace in hand in the war shone like Kubera.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तेप्रतस्थुर्महात्मानोऽमरावत्यास्सुराइव । तान् गजैश्चतुरङ्गैश्चरथैश्चाम्बुन्दिस्स्वनैः ।।6.69.33।। अनूत्पेतुर्महात्मानोराक्षसाःप्रवरायुधाः ।
output: Those great souls followed by elephants, horses, Rakshasas with superb weapons sounding like the rumbling of rainy clouds went like gods of Amaravati.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
तेविरेजुर्महात्मानःकुमारास्सूर्यवर्चसः ।।6.69.34।। किरीटिनश्रशियाजुष्टाग्रहादीप्ताइवाम्बरे ।
output: The great princes were wearing crowns resplendent like the Sun and glowing like planets in the sky.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
प्रगृहीताबभौतेषांशस्त्राणामावळिस्सिता ।।6.69.35।। शारदाभ्रप्रतीकाशाहंसावळिरिवाम्बरे ।
output: The princes, grasping the white weapons shone like flocks of white cranes in the dark autumnal clouds in the sky.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
मरणंवापिनिश्चित्यशत्रूणांवापराजयम् ।।6.69.36।। इतिकृत्वामतिंवीरानिर्जग्मुस्संयुगार्थिनः ।
output: Those heroes determined to defeat the enemy even if it meant death and went thinking for the combat.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
जगर्जुश्चप्रणेदुश्चचिक्षिपुश्चापिसायकान् ।।6.69.37।। जगृहुश्चमहात्मानोनिर्वातायुद्धदुर्मदाः ।
output: The great Rakshasas who were fierce in combat went roaring shouting loudly and discharging arrows.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
क्ष्वेळिडितास्फोटिनिनदैश्चचाल च वसुन्दरा ।।6.69.38।। रक्षसांसिंहनादैश्चसंस्फोटेवतदाम्बरम् ।
output: By the sound of their clapping of arms and their lion roar it was as though the sky was breaking and the earth was shaking.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अभिनिष्क्रम्यमुदिताराक्षसेन्द्रामहाबलाः ।।6.69.39।। ददृशुर्वानरानीकंसमुद्यतशिलानगम् ।
output: महाबलाः possessed of extraordinary might, ते they, राक्षसेन्ध्राः Rakshasa army, अभिनिष्क्रम्य departing from there, समुद्यतशिलानगम् ready with many rocks, वानरानीकम् Vanara army, ददृशुः witnessed.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
हरयोपिमहात्मानोददृशुर्नेरृतम् ।।6.69.40।। हस्त्यश्वरथसम्बाधंकिङ्किणीशतनादितम् । नीलजीमूतसङ्काशंसमुद्यतमहायुधम् ।।6.69.41।। दीप्तानलरविप्रख्यैस्सर्वतोनैरृतैर्वृतम् ।
output: The huge monkeys also saw groups of elephants, horses and chariots and heard hundreds of bells of the chariots and Rakshasas all over like groups of dark clouds with huge weapons glowing like fire and Sun surrounded by Rakshasa army.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
हरयोपिमहात्मानोददृशुर्नेरृतम् ।।6.69.40।। हस्त्यश्वरथसम्बाधंकिङ्किणीशतनादितम् । नीलजीमूतसङ्काशंसमुद्यतमहायुधम् ।।6.69.41।। दीप्तानलरविप्रख्यैस्सर्वतोनैरृतैर्वृतम् ।
output: महात्मानः huge gigantic, हरयोऽपि Vanaras also, हस्त्यश्वरथसम्भाधम् groups of elephants, horses and chariots, किङ्किणीशतनादितम् sounds of hundreds of bells of the chariots, नीलजीमूतसङ्काशम् like group of dark clouds, समुद्यतमहायुधम् with huge weapons, सर्वतः all, दीप्तानलरविप्रख्यैः glowing like fire and Sun, नैरृतैः Rakshasas, वृतम् surrounded, राक्षसम् Rakshasas, बलम् army, ददृशुः saw.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
तद्दृष्टवाबलमायान्तंलब्धलक्षाःप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.69.42।। समुद्यतमहाशैलास्सम्प्रणेदुर्महाबला । अमृष्यमाणारक्षांसिप्रतिनर्दन्तवानराः ।।6.69.43।।
output: Seeing the Rakshasa army approaching, the monkeys found an opportunity to attack them and collected huge mountains, deadly strong trees in great joy unable to tolerate roared in return.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
तद्दृष्टवाबलमायान्तंलब्धलक्षाःप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.69.42।। समुद्यतमहाशैलास्सम्प्रणेदुर्महाबला । अमृष्यमाणारक्षांसिप्रतिनर्दन्तवानराः ।।6.69.43।।
output: Seeing the Rakshasa army approaching, the monkeys found an opportunity to attack them and collected huge mountains, deadly strong trees in great joy unable to tolerate roared in return.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
ततस्समुद्घुष्टरवंनिशम्य।रक्षोगणावानरयूथपानाम् । अमृष्यमाणाःपरहर्षमुग्रं।महाबलाःभीमतरंविनेदुः ।।6.69.44।।
output: There upon the Vanara leaders, endowed with extraordinary prowess, beholding the joy of Rakshasa troops, unable to bear roared dreadfully.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तेराक्षसबलंघोरंप्रविश्यहरियूथपाः । विचेरुरुद्यतैश्शैलैर्नगाश्शिखरिणोयथा ।।6.69.45।।
output: Those monkey leaders entering dreadful Rakshasa army uplifted rocks and mountains with trees and shone.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
केचिदाकाशमाविश्यकेचिदुर्व्यांप्लवङ्गमाः । रक्षस्सैन्येषुसङ्कृद्धाःश्चेरुर्द्रुमशिलायुधाः ।।6.69.46।।
output: केचित् some, प्लवङ्गमाः monkeys, आकाशम् sky, आविश्य springing, केचित् some, उर्व्याम् staying on earth, सङ्कृद्धाः highly enraged, द्रुमशिलायुधाः trees and rocks as weapons, रक्षस्सैन्येषु Rakshasa army, चेरुः ranged.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
द्रुमांश्चविपुलस्कन्थान् गृह्यवानरपुङ्गवाः । तद्युद्धमभवद्घोरंरक्षोवानरसङ्कुलम् ।।6.69.47।।
output: Vanara leaders seizing huge branches of trees fought a frightening war with Rakshasas.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तेपादपशिलाश्शैलैश्चक्रुर्वृष्टिमनूपमाम् । बाणौघैर्वार्यमाणाश्चहरयोभीमविक्रमाः ।।6.69.48।।
output: बाणौघैः arrows, वार्यमाणाः heroic, भीमविक्रमाः of dreadful valour, ते those, हरयः monkeys, पादपशिलाश्शैलैः trees, rocks and mountains, अनूपमाम् unparalleled, वृष्टिम् rain, चक्रुः showered.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सिंहनादान्विनेदुश्चरणेराक्षसवानराः । शिलाभिश्चूर्णयामासुर्यातुधानान् प्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.69.49।।
output: रणे in the battlefield, राक्षसवानराः Rakshasas and Vanaras, सिंहनादान् roaring like lions, विनेदुः enthusiastic, प्लवंवङ्गमाः Vanaras, यातुधानान् pounded, शिलाभिः rocks, चूर्णयामासुः crushed.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
नर्जघ्नुस्संयुगेक्रुद्धाःकवचाभरणावृतान् । केचिद्रथगतावनीरान्गजवाजिगतानपि ।।6.69.50।।
output: In the combat, the enraged Vanaras killed Rakshasas decked with shields and ornaments. Some killed the ones mounted on chariots, elephants, and horses.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
निर्जघ्नुस्सहसाऽप्लुत्ययातुधानान् प्लवङ्गमाः । शैलशृङ्गाचिताङ्गाश्चमुष्टिभिर्वान्तलोचनाः ।।6.69.51।। चेरुःपेतुश्चनेदुश्चतत्रराक्षसपुङ्गवाः ।
output: The Rakshasa leaders, hit by the blows of Vanaras, fell down on the mountain peaks, trembling with their eyes protruded by the blows of fists.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
राक्षसाश्चशरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्बिदुःकपिकुञ्जरान् ।।6.69.52।। शूलमुद्गरखडगैश्चजघ्नुःप्रासैश्चशक्तिभिः ।
output: The Rakshasas also pierced with arrows the foremost of the monkeys and struck with tridents swords and lances.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
अन्योन्यंपातयामासुःपरस्परजयैषिणः ।।6.69.53।। रिपुशोणितदिग्धाङ्गास्तत्रवानरराक्षसाः
output: Their limbs stained with the blood of foes, both Vanaras and Rakshasas eager to conquer one another started striking one another.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततश्शैलैश्चखडगैश्चविसृष्टैर्हरिराक्षसैः ।।6.69.54।। मुहूर्तेनावृताभूमिरभवच्छोणिताप्लुता ।
output: Then in a short while the battlefield was covered with blood and rocks and swords used by the monkeys and Rakshasas.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
विकीर्णैःपर्वताकारैरक्षोभिररिमर्दनैः ।।6.69.55।। आसीद्वसुमतीपूर्णातदायुद्धमदान्वितैः ।
output: तदा then, वसुमती earth, विकीर्णैः filled, पर्वताकारैः of mountain like, अभिमर्दितैः crushed, युद्धमदान्वितैः drunk pride of warfare, रक्षोभिः Rakshasas also, पूर्णा fully, आसीत् lying scattered.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
आक्षिप्ताःक्षिप्यमाणाश्चभग्नशूलाश्चवानरैः ।।6.69.56।। पुनरङ्गैस्तदाचक्रुरासन्नायुद्धमद्भुतम् ।
output: Vanaras, were lifting and dropping the scattered Rakshasas, breaking the tridents and a wonderful war went on using their limbs.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
वानरान्वानरैरेवजघ्नुस्तेनैरृतर्षभाः ।।6.69.57।। राक्षसान्राक्षसैरेवजघ्नुस्तेवानराअपि ।
output: The bull among Rakshasas struck at Vanaras with other Vanaras and the monkeys struck Rakshasas with other Rakshasas.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
आक्षिप्य च शिलास्तेषांनिजघ्नाराक्षसाहरीन् ।।6.69.58।। तेषांचाछचिद्यशस्त्राणिजघ्नूरक्षांसिवानराः ।
output: हरीन् monkeys, तेराक्षसाः those Rakshasas, शिलाः rocks, सेषाम् left over, आक्षिप्य taking, जघ्नुः struck, वानराः च Vanaras also, तेषाम् while they, शस्त्राणि weapons, आछचिद्य tearing, रक्षांसि Rakshasas, निजघ्नुः struck.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
निजघ्नुश्शैलशूलार्स्सैर्भिभिदुश्चपरस्परम् ।।6.69.59।। सिंहनादान्विनेदुश्चरणेराक्षसावानराः ।
output: In the battlefield both Vanaras and Rakshasas struck at one another with their head, rocks and swords and emitted lion roar.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
छिन्नवर्णतनुत्राणाराक्षसावानरैर्हताः ।।6.69.60।। रुधिरंप्रसृतास्तत्ररससारमिवद्रुमाः ।
output: The Rakshasas killed by Vanaras, their shields and weapons broken, blood flowed from their limbs just as sap exudes from broken trees.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
रथेन च रथंचापिवारणेनैववारणम् ।।6.69.61।। हयेन च हयंकेचिन्निजघ्नुर्वानरारणे ।
output: In the battlefield a chariot with another chariot, an elephant with another elephant, a horse with another horse struck one another.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
क्षुरप्रैरर्धचन्द्रैश्चभल्लैश्चनिशितैश्शरैः ।।6.69.62।। राक्षसावानरेन्द्राणांबिभिदुःपादपान् शिलाः ।
output: राक्षसाः Rakshasa, क्षुरप्रैः horse shoe shaped, अर्धचन्द्रेःच halfmoon shaped, भल्लैश्च spear shaped heads, निशितैः sharp, शरैः arrows, वानरेन्द्राणाम् Vanara leaders, पादपान् trees, शिलाः rocks, बिभिदुः shattered.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
विकीर्णैपर्वताग्रैश्चद्रुमैछशिनैश्चसंयुगे ।।6.69.63।। हतैश्चकपिरक्षोभिर्दुर्गमावसुधाऽभवत् ।
output: The battlefield, covered with broken trees and mountains, fallen vanaras and rakshasas, seemed difficult to tread on ground.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तेवानरागर्वितहृष्टचेष्टास्सङ्ग्राममासाद्यभयंविम । युद्धंस्मसर्वेसहराक्षसैस्सैयुधाश्चक्रुरदीनसत्त्वाः ।।6.69.64।।
output: तेवानराः those Vanaras, सङ्ग्रामम् war field, आसाद्य reaching, गर्वितहृष्टचेष्टाः rejoicing full of pride, भयम् feared, विमुच्य leaving behind, सर्वे all, अदीनसत्त्वाः not depressed at all, नानायुधैः several kinds, राक्षसैस्सह with Rakshasas, युद्धम् war, चक्रुःस्म carried out.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तस्मिन्प्रवृत्तेतुमुलेविमर्देप्रहृष्यमाणेषुवलीमुखेषु । निपात्यमानेषु च राक्षसेषुमहर्षयोदेवगणाश्चनेदुः ।।6.69.65।।
output: As the conflict progressed and tumultuous fighting was on, Vanaras were feeling exultant and seeing Rakshasas struck down the ascetics and Devatas made loud noises in joy.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततोहयंमारुततुल्यवेगमारुह्यशक्तिंनिशितांप्रगृह्य । नरान्तकोवानरराजसैन्यंमहार्णवंमीनइवाविवेश ।।6.69.66।।
output: Then Naranthaka, mounted on horseback went at wind speed taking hold of javelin and entered Vanara army just as fish entered the ocean.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
स वानरान् सप्तशतानिवीरःप्रासेनदीप्तेनन्वििर्बिभेद । एकःक्षणेनेन्द्ररिपुर्महात्माजघानसैन्यंहरिपुङ्गवानाम् ।।6.69.67।।
output: Great hero (Naranthaka) single handed persistently destroyed seven hundred Vanaras with his glowing spear. In that way the enemy of Indra shattered Vanara army and monkey leaders.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
ददृशुश्चमहात्मानंहयपृष्ठेप्रतिष्ठितम् । चरन्तंहरिसैन्येषुविद्याधरमहर्षयः ।।6.69.68।।
output: Vidhyadhara, the great sage, witnessed Naranthaka moving seated on the horseback firmly.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स तस्यददृशेमार्गोमांसशोणितकर्दमः । पतितैःपर्वताकारैर्वानरैरभिसंवृतः ।।6.69.69।।
output: On the way he saw flesh and blood fallen like a heap of a mountain covered fully with Vanaras.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
यावद्विक्रमितुंबुधदिंचक्रुःप्लवगपुङ्गवाः । तावदेतानतिक्रम्यनिर्बिभेदनरान्तकः ।।6.69.70।।
output: Naranthaka went past the Vanara leaders all over even before they attempted, he destroyed them.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
ददाहहरिसैन्यानिवनानीवविभावसुः । यावदुत्पाटयामासुर्वृक्षान्शैलान्वनौकसः ।।6.69.71।। तावत्प्रासहताःपेतुर्वज्रकृत्ताइवाचलाः ।
output: Uplifting his lance in the battle, Naranthaka consumed the Vanara troops as fire would burn up forests even before the Vanaras uprooted trees and rocks. many Vanaras fell like mountains hit by a thunderbolt.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ज्वलन्तम्प्रासमुद्यम्यसङ्ग्रामान्तेनरान्तकः ।।6.69.72।। दिक्षुसर्वासुबलवान् विचचारनरान्तकः । प्रमृद्नन्सर्वतोयुद्धेप्रावृटकालेयथानिलः ।।6.69.73।।
output: Mighty Naranthaka, the destroyer of humans, ranged over all sides in all directions in the battlefield, like the wind in the rainy season, taking a burning spear and crushing everything.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ज्वलन्तम्प्रासमुद्यम्यसङ्ग्रामान्तेनरान्तकः ।।6.69.72।। दिक्षुसर्वासुबलवान् विचचारनरान्तकः । प्रमृद्नन्सर्वतोयुद्धेप्रावृटकालेयथानिलः ।।6.69.73।।
output: नरान्तकः Naranthaka, बलवान् mighty, नरान्तकः capable of killing humans, सङ्ग्रामान्ते in the battle, ज्वलन्तम् burning, प्रासम् spear, उद्यम्य taking up, युद्धे in battle, अनिलः wind, प्रावृटकालेइव like in the rainy season, सर्वतः everything, प्रमृद्नन् crushing, सर्वासु all sides, दिक्षु directions, विचचार ranged about.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
न शेकुर्भाषितुंवीरा न स्थातुंस्पन्दितुंभयात् । उत्पतन्तंस्थितंयान्तंसर्वान्विव्याधवीर्यवान् ।।6.69.74।।
output: The gallant monkeys got terrified and could not flee, nor stand, nor move. The audacious Naranthaka marching ahead pierced the Vanaras either marching or jumping or stationary.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
एकेनानन्तकल्पेनप्रासेनादित्यतेजसा । भग्नानिहरिसैन्यानिनिपेतुर्धरणीतले ।।6.69.75।।
output: With lance that looked like death and the spear glowing like the Sun, Naranthaka routed the Vanaras, who fell down.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
वज्रनिष्पेषदृशंप्रासस्याभिनिपातनम् । न शेकुर्वानरास्सोढुंतेविनेदुर्महास्वनम् ।।6.69.76।।
output: ते those, वानराः Vanaras, वज्रनिष्पेषसदृशम् like the strike of thunderbolt, प्रासस्य spear's, अभिनिपातनम् very severe, सोढुम् impact, न शेकुः not bear, महास्वनम् very loud voice, विनेदुः cried.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
पततांहरिवीराणांरूपाणिप्रचकाशिरे । वज्रभिन्नाग्रकूटानांशैलानांपततामिव ।।6.69.77।।
output: The forms of the monkey heroes fallen down unconscious shone like mountain peaks struck by the thunderbolt and fallen.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
येतुपूर्वंमहात्मानःकुम्भकर्णेनपातिताः । तेस्वस्थावानरश्रेष्ठास्सुग्रीवमुपतस्थिरे ।।6.69.78।।
output: The Vanaras who were struck by Kumbhakarna and fallen unconscious, came and stood before Sugriva.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
विप्रेक्षमाणस्सुग्रीवोददर्शहरिवाहिनीम् । नरान्तकभयत्रस्तांविद्रवन्तीमितस्ततः ।।6.69.79।।
output: Sugriva looked around all over the monkey troops running here and there out of fear of Naranthaka.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
विद्रुतांवाहिनींदृष्टवा स ददर्शनरान्तकम् । गृहीतप्रासमायान्तंहयपृष्ठेप्रतिष्ठितम् ।।6.69.80।।
output: सः he, Sugriva, विद्रुताम् running, वाहिनीम् troops, दृष्टवा seeing, गृहीतप्रासम् taking hold of spear, हयपृष्ठेप्रतिष्ठितम् seated on horseback, आयान्तम् advancing, नरान्तकम् Naranthaka, ददर्श saw.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
अथोवाचमहातेजास्सुग्रीवोवानराधिपः । कुमारमङ्गदंवीरंशक्रतुल्यपराक्रमम् ।।6.69.81।।
output: Sugriva, the Lord of Vanaras seeing (Naranthaka advancing) spoke to his son Angada who resembled Indra in valour.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
गच्छत्वंराक्षसंवीरोयोऽसौतुरगमास्थितः । क्षोभयन्तहरिबलंक्षिप्रंप्राणैर्वियोजय ।।6.69.82।।
output: "Oh! March ahead and immediately release the life of the Rakshasa seated on horseback terrifying the Vanara army."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स भर्तुर्वचनंश्रुत्वानिष्पपाताङ्गदतः । अनीकान्मेघसङ्काशादंशुमानिववीर्यवान् ।।6.69.83।।
output: On hearing the king's words, Angada went just as the sun rays comes out of a cluster of clouds.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
शैलसङ्घातसङ्काशोहरीणामुत्तमोऽङ्गदः । रराजाङ्गदसन्नद्धस्सधातुरिवपर्वतः ।।6.69.84।।
output: Angada, the best of the Vanaras, adorned with arm lets resembled masses of rocks and shone like a mountain with metal streaks.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
निरायुधोमहातेजाःकेवलंनखदंष्ट्रवान् । नरान्तकमभिक्रम्यवालिपुत्रोऽब्रवीद्वचः ।।6.69.85।।
output: Brilliant Angada, unarmed only with nails and teeth (to fight) advanced towards Naranthaka and spoke these words.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तिष्ठकिंप्राकृतैरेभिर्हरिभिस्त्वंकरिष्यसि । अस्मिन्वज्रसमस्पर्शंप्रासंक्षिपममोरसि ।।6.69.86।।
output: "Stop! What can you do with these common monkeys? Throw your spear at me, which equals thunderbolt."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अङ्गदस्यवचश्श्रुत्वाप्रचुक्रोधनरान्तकः । सन्दश्यदशनैरोष्ठंन्वििश्श्वस्यभुजङ्गवत् ।।6.69.87।। अभिगम्याङ्गदंक्रुद्धोवालिपुत्रंनरान्तकः । प्रासंसमाविध्यतदाङ्गदायसमुज्ज्वलन्तंसहसोत्ससर्ज । स वालिपुत्रोरसिवज्रकल्पेबभूवभग्नोन्यपतच्चभूमौ ।।6.69.88।।
output: नरान्तकः Naranthaka, अङ्गदस्य Angada's, वचः words, श्रुत्वा hearing, प्रचुक्रोध flew in rage, सः he नरान्तकः Naranthaka, क्रुद्धः enraged, दशनैः ten, ओष्ठम् lips, सन्दश्य biting, भुजङ्गवत् like a serpent, न्वििश्श्वस्य च hissing, वालिपुत्रम् Vali's son, अङ्गदम् Angada, अभिगम्य going forward, समुज्ज्वलन्तम् glowing like fire, प्रासम् spear, समाविध्य hurled, तदा then, अङ्गदाय Angada, सहसा violently, उत्ससर्ज chest, सः he, वज्रकल्पे struck, वालिपुत्रोरसि chest of Vali's son, भग्नःबभूव shattered, भूमौ on ground, न्यपतच्च went round and fell.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अङ्गदस्यवचश्श्रुत्वाप्रचुक्रोधनरान्तकः । सन्दश्यदशनैरोष्ठंन्वििश्श्वस्यभुजङ्गवत् ।।6.69.87।। अभिगम्याङ्गदंक्रुद्धोवालिपुत्रंनरान्तकः । प्रासंसमाविध्यतदाङ्गदायसमुज्ज्वलन्तंसहसोत्ससर्ज । स वालिपुत्रोरसिवज्रकल्पेबभूवभग्नोन्यपतच्चभूमौ ।।6.69.88।।
output: Hearing Angada's words Naranthaka flew into a rage. Biting his lips with teeth, hissing like a serpent Naranthaka stood before Angada. He hurled his spear glowing like fire on Angada's chest violently. It struck Angada and shattered, went round, and fell.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
तंप्रासमालोक्यतदाविभग्नंसुपर्णकृत्तोरगभोगकल्पम् । तलंसमुद्यम्य स वालिपुत्रस्तुरङ्गमतस्यजघानमूर्ध्नि ।।6.69.89।।
output: Then Vali's son beholding the broken and shattered spear fallen like the coils of serpent, raised his palm and struck at the head of Naranthaka's horse.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
निमग्नतालुस्फ्सुटिताक्षितारोनिष्क्रान्तजिह्वोऽचलसन्निकाशः । स तस्यवाजीनिपपातभूमौतलप्रहारेणविशीर्णमूर्धा ।।6.69.90।।
output: तस्य his, अचलसन्नकाशः closely resembling mountain, सःवाजी that Angada, तलप्रहारेण by the stroke of the palm, विशीर्णमूर्धा head broken, निमग्नतालुः cheeks drawn in, स्फुटिताक्षितारः eyeballs broken, निष्क्रान्तजिह्वः tongue ejected, भूमौ on ground, निपपात fell.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
नरान्तकःक्रोधवशंजगामहतंतुरङ्गंपतितंनिरीक्ष्य । स मुष्टिमुद्यम्यमहाप्रभावोजघानशीर्षेयुधि वालिपुत्रम् ।।6.69.91।।
output: Observing the horse fallen, Naranthaka, endowed with great power, overcome by anger raised his fist and struck at the head of Vali's son.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
अथाङ्गदोमुष्टिविशीर्णमूर्धासुस्रावतीव्रंरुधिरंभृशोष्णम् । मुहुर्विजज्वालमुमोहचापिसंज्ञांसमासाद्यविसिष्मिये च ।।6.69.92।।
output: Angada's head smashed by the blow of the fist of Naranthaka, hot blood flowed rapidly for a while. Recovering from delusion, gaining consciousness he wondered at the strength of Naranthaka.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
अथाङ्गदोमृत्युसमानवेगंसंवर्त्यमुष्टिंगिरिशृङ्गकल्पम् । निपातयामासतदामहात्मानरान्तकस्योरसिवालिपुत्रः ।।6.69.93।।
output: Angada clenching his fist, whose vehemence was equal to vehemence of death coming down from the top of the mountain peak, brought down Naranthaka.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
स मुष्टिनिष्पिष्टविभिन्नवक्षाज्वालावमन्शोणितदिग्धगात्रः । नरान्तकोभूमितलेपपातयथाऽचलोवज्रनिपातभग्नः ।।6.69.94।।
output: Naranthaka's chest having been split by a blow on his chest, vomiting flaming blood from his throat was as if shattered by the stroke of lightning fell down like a mountain.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 69:
अथान्तरिक्षेत्रिदशोत्तमानांवनौकसांचैवमहाप्रणादः । बभूवतस्मिन्निहतेऽग्य्रवीर्येनरान्तकेवालिसुतेनसंख्ये ।।6.69.95।।
output: Naranthaka, the foremost of the heroes, having been killed in combat, the Devatas and gods of the three worlds experienced great joy.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
नरान्तकंहतंदृष्टवाचुक्रुशुर्नैरृतर्षभाः । देवान्तकस्त्रिमूर्धा च पौलस्त्यश्चमहोदरः ।।6.70.1।।
output: नरान्तकम् Naranthaka, हतम् killed, दृष्टवा seeing, नैरृतर्षभाः bull among Rakshasas, देवान्तकः Devanthaka, त्रिमूर्धा च Trisira, पौलस्त्यः of Paulastya, महोदरः च and Mahodara, चुक्रुशुः cried aloud.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
आरूढोमेघसङ्काशंवारणेन्द्रंमहोदरः । वालिपुत्रंमहावीर्यमभिदुद्राववीर्यवान् ।।6.70.2।।
output: महोदरः Mahodara, मेघसङ्काशम् resembling cloud, वारणेन्द्रम् best of elephants, आरूढः mounted, वीर्यवान् courageous, महावीर्यम् brave, वालिपुत्रम् Vali's son, अभिदुद्राव chased.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
भ्रारातृव्यसनसन्तप्तस्तदादेवान्तकोबली । आदायपरिघंदीप्तमङ्गदंसमभिद्रवत् ।।6.70.3।।
output: तदा then, भ्रातृव्यसनसन्तप्तः immersed in the grief of brother, बली powerful, देवान्तकः Devanthaka, दीप्तम् glowing, परिघम् iron bar, आदाय taking hold of, अङ्गदम् at Angada, समभिद्रवत् rushed forward.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 70:
रथमादित्यसङ्काशंयुक्तंपरमवाजिभिः । आस्थायत्रिशिरावीरोवालिपुत्रमथाभ्ययात् ।।6.70.4।।
output: Then Trisira, seated on the chariot, effulgent as the Sun, yoked to the best horse marched towards Angada.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 70:
स त्रिभिर्देवदर्पघ्नेर्नेरृतीन्द्रेरभिद्रुतः । वृक्षमुत्पाटयामासमहाविटपमङ्गदः ।।6.70.5।।
output: Angada observed that all the three chiefs of Rakshasas, who were capable of crushing the pride of gods marching towards him and uprooted a huge tree.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
देवान्तकायतंवीरच्शिक्षेपसहसाङ्गदः । महावृक्षंमहाशाखंशक्रोदीप्तमिवाशनिम् ।।6.70.6।।
output: वीरः hero, अङ्गदः Angada, महाशाखम् huge branches, तम् those, महावृक्षम् huge tree, शक्रः branches, दीप्तम् flaming, अशनम् इव flaming thunderbolt, सहसा with force, देवान्तकाय Devanthaka, चिक्षेप hurled.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 70:
त्रिशिरास्तंप्रचिच्छेदशरैराशीविषोपमैः । स वृक्षंकृत्तमालोक्यउत्पपाततदाङ्गदः ।।6.70.7।।
output: Trisira split the trees with the arrows which were like venomous serpents. Observing Angada's action he flew up.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 70:
स ववर्षततोवृक्षान् शैलाश्चकपिकुञ्जरः । तान् प्रचिच्छेदसङ्कृद्धस्त्रिशिरानिशितैश्शरैः ।।6.70.8।।
output: Then the leader of the monkeys, rained trees and rocks. Angry Trisira attacked all of them with sharp arrows.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
परिघाग्रेणतान् वृक्षान्बभञ्ज च महोदरः । त्रिशिराश्चाङ्गदंवीरमभिदुद्रावसायकैः ।।6.70.9।।
output: Mahodara shattered those trees with the iron clubs. Trisira attacked brave Angada with arrows.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
गजेनसमभिद्रुत्यवालिपुत्रंमहोदरः । जघानोरसिसङ्कृद्धस्तोमरैर्वज्रसन्निभैः ।।6.70.10।।
output: महोदरः Mahodara, गजेन with elephant, वालिपुत्रम् Vali's son, समभिद्रुत्य chased towards, सङ्कृद्धः in anger, वज्रसन्निभैः which were like lightning, तोमरैः iron clubs, उरसि chest, जघान attacked.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
देवान्तकश्चसङ्कृद्धःपरिघेणतदाङ्गदम् । उपगम्याभिहत्याशुव्यपचक्रामवेगवान् ।।6.70.11।।
output: तदा then, वेगवान् quickly, देवान्तकः च Devanthaka also, सङ्कृद्धः very furious, अङ्गदम् Angada, उपगम्य came over, आशु directly, परिघेण by the iron club, अभिहत्य attacked, व्यपचक्राम retreated.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सत्रिभिर्नैरृतश्रेष्ठैर्युगतपत्समभिद्रुतः । न विव्यथेमहातेजावालिपुत्रःप्रतापवान् ।।6.70.12।।
output: Eminent and highly energetic son of Vali did not feel perturbed when three of the foremost Rakshasas attacked him together.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स वेगवान्महावेगंकृत्वापरमदुर्जयः । तलेनभृशमुत्पत्यजघानास्यमहागजम् ।।6.70.13।।
output: Angada, who was endowed with high speed, and exceedingly difficult to encounter, jumped up the huge elephant of Mahodara attacked him.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 70:
तस्यतेनप्रहारेणनागराजस्यसंयुगे । पेततुर्लोचनेतस्यविननाद स वारणः ।।6.70.14।।
output: By that blow of Angada, that king of elephant's eyes dropped, and it cried.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
विषाणंचास्यसःनिष्कृष्यवालिपुत्रोमहाबलः । देवान्तकमभिप्लुत्यताडयामाससंयुगे ।।6.70.15।।
output: महाबलः mighty, वालिपुत्रः Vali's son, संयुगे in battle, अस्य his, विषाणम् tusk, निष्कृष्य removed, देवान्तकम् Devanthaka, अभिद्रुत्य jumping over, ताडयामास hit him.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स विह्वलस्तुतेजस्वीवातोद्धूतइवद्रुमः । लक्षारससवर्णं च सुस्रावरुधिरंमहत् ।।6.70.16।।
output: तेजस्वी astonishing, सः he, वातोद्धूतः thrown by the wind, द्रुमःइव like a tree, विह्वलः shaken, लाक्षारससवर्णम् colour of lacquer, महत् huge amount, रुधिरम् blood, सुस्राव shed.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अथाश्वस्यमहातेजाःकृच्छ्राद्देवान्तकोबली । आविध्यपरिघंवेगादाजघानतदाङ्गदम् ।।6.70.17।।
output: Thereafter the terribly strong Devanthaka taking iron spike quickly pierced Angada.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 70:
परिघाभिहतश्चापिवानरेन्द्रात्मजस्तदा । जानुभ्यांपतितोबूमौपुनरेवोत्पपात ह ।।6.70.18।।
output: Then, hurt by the club the son of Vanara king fell down on his knees once again and got up.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तमुत्पतन्तंत्रिशिरास्त्रिभिर्बाणैरजिह्मगैः । घोरैर्हरिपतेःपुत्रेंललाटेऽभिजघान ह ।।6.70.19।।
output: त्रिशिराः Trisira, उत्पतन्तम् who got up, पुत्रम् son, तम् him, घोरैः terrible, अजह्मगैः straight going three, बाणैः arrows, ललाटे on forehead, अभिजघान ह again hit.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततोऽङ्गदंपरिक्षिप्तंत्रिभिर्नैरृतपुङ्गवैः । हनूमानपिविज्ञायनीलश्चापिप्रतस्थतुः ।।6.70.20।।
output: Then finding Angada surrounded by the three Rakshasa leaders, Hanuman as well as Neela set out.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तश्चिक्षेपशैलाग्रंनीलस्त्रिशिरसेतदा । तद्रावणसुतोधीमाबनिभेदनिशितैश्शरैः ।।6.70.21।।
output: Thereafter Neela hit Trisira with the peak of the mountain and Ravana's son broke the mountain into pieces with arrows.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तद्बाणशतनिर्भिन्नंविदारितशिलातलम् । सविस्फुलिंगंसज्वालंनिपपातगिरेशशिरः ।।6.70.22।।
output: Hit by hundreds of arrows, the mountain peak broke into pieces of stones like sparks and flames fell from it.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 70:
ततोजृम्भितमालोक्यहर्षाद्वेवान्तकस्तदा । परिघेणाभिदुद्रावमारुतात्मजमाहवे ।।6.70.23।।
output: Mighty Devanthaka, observing (Trisira's action), was happy on the battlefield, and went with his club to assault Hanuman.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तमापतन्तमुत्प्लुत्यहनुमान्मारुतात्मजः । आजघानतदामूर्ध्निवज्रकल्पेनमुष्टिना ।।6.70.24।।
output: Then the son of wind god, Hanuman observing Devanthaka coming towards him, got up and hit him on the forehead with his thunderbolt like fist.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
शिरसिप्रहरवनीरस्तदावायुसुतोबली । नादेनाकम्पयच्चैवराक्षसान् स महाकपिः ।।6.70.25।।
output: तदा then, वीरः heroic, बली strong, वायुसुतः son of wind god, शिरसि on head, प्रहरत् blow, सः he, महाकपिः great monkey, नादेन sound, राक्षसान् Rakshasas, अकम्पयच्चैव trembled.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
मुष्टिनिष्पिष्टविभिन्नमूर्धानिर्वान्तदन्ताक्षिविलम्बिजिव्वाः । देवान्तकोराक्षसराजसूनुर्गतासुरुत्व्यांसहसापपात ।।6.70.26।।
output: मुष्टिनिष्पिष्टविभिन्नमूर्धा skull shattered by the blow, निर्वान्तदन्ताक्षिविलम्बिजिव्वाः teeth, eyes and tongue forced out, राक्षसराजसूनुः son of king of Rakshasas, सः he, देवान्तकः Devanthaka, गतासुः dead, सहसा instantly, उर्व्याम् on ground, पपात fell.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तस्मिन्हतेराक्षसयोधमुख्येमहाबलेसंयतिदेवशत्रौ । क्रुद्धस्त्रिमूर्धानिशिताग्रमुग्रंववर्षनीलोरसिबाणवर्षम् ।।6.70.27।।
output: Devanthaka, the foremost of Rakshasa warriors, an enemy of gods, endowed with great strength, having been killed in the conflict, Trisira became angry and rained arrows on Neela's chest.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
महोदरस्तुसङ्कृद्धःकुञ्जरंपर्वतोपमम् । भूयस्समधिरुह्याशुमन्दरंरमशिमानिव ।।6.70.28।। ततोबाणमयंवर्षंनीलस्योरस्यपातयत् । गिरौवर्षंतडिच्चक्रचापवानिवतोयदः ।।6.70.29।।
output: सः he, महोदरस्तु at Mahodara, सङ्कृद्धः enraged, रमशिमान् Sun god, मन्दरम् इव springing on Mandara, पर्वतोपमम् over the mountain, कुञ्जरम् elephant, भूयः becoming, समधिरुह्य mounted, आशु quickly, ततः then, नीलस्य Neela's, उपरि chest, तोयदः water, तडिच्चक्रचापवानि rainy cloud with lightning and rainbow, वर्षम् wetted, गिरौइव on the mountain like, बाणमयम् covered with arrows, वर्षम् rain, अपातयत् showered.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
महोदरस्तुसङ्कृद्धःकुञ्जरंपर्वतोपमम् । भूयस्समधिरुह्याशुमन्दरंरमशिमानिव ।।6.70.28।। ततोबाणमयंवर्षंनीलस्योरस्यपातयत् । गिरौवर्षंतडिच्चक्रचापवानिवतोयदः ।।6.70.29।।
output: सः he, महोदरस्तु at Mahodara, सङ्कृद्धः enraged, रमशिमान् Sun god, मन्दरम् इव springing on Mandara, पर्वतोपमम् over the mountain, कुञ्जरम् elephant, भूयः becoming, समधिरुह्य mounted, आशु quickly, ततः then, नीलस्य Neela's, उपरि chest, तोयदः water, तडिच्चक्रचापवानि rainy cloud with lightning and rainbow, वर्षम् wetted, गिरौइव on the mountain like, बाणमयम् covered with arrows, वर्षम् rain, अपातयत् showered.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 70:
ततश्शरौघेरभिवर्ष्यमाणोविभिन्नगात्रःकपिसैन्यपालः । नीलोबभूवाथविसृष्टगात्रोविष्टम्भितस्तेनमहाबलेन ।।6.70.30।।
output: Neela's body wetted by arrows all over, the limbs pierced with arrows, the monkey leader remained powerless and could not move in spite of being extraordinarily strong.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 70:
ततस्तुनीलःप्रतिलभ्यसंज्ञांशैलंसमुत्पाट्यसवृक्षषंण्डम् । ततस्समुत्पत्यभृशोग्रवेशोमहादरंतेनजघानमूर्ध्नि ।।6.70.31।।
output: Thereafter Neela also regained his senses and uprooting a mountain filled with trees went over Mahodara at high speed and attacked him on the forehead.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तत: स्सशैलेद्रनिपातभग्नोमहोदरस्तेनमहाद्विपेन । विपोथितोभूमितलेगतासुःपपातवज्राभिहतोयथाद्रिः ।।6.70.32।।
output: Then smashed by the impact of the mountain, along with his elephant Mahodara's body fell to the ground. Released from life, he fell like a mountain struck with lightning.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
पितृव्यंनिहतंदृष्टवात्रिशिराश्चापमाददे । हनूमन्तं च सङ्कृद्धोविव्याथनिशितैश्शरैः ।।6.70.33।।
output: त्रिशिराः Trisira, पितृव्यम् uncle, निहतम् killed, दृष्टवा seeing, सङ्कृद्धः very angry, चापम् bow, आददे seized, हनूमन्तम् Hanuman, निशितैः sharp, शरैः arrow, विव्याथ pierced.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स वायुसुनूःकुपितश्चिक्षेपशिखरंगिरेः । त्रिशिरास्तच्छरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्बिभेदबहुधाबली ।।6.70.34।।
output: सः he, वायुसूनुः son of wind god, कुपितः in anger, गिरेः mountain, शिखरम् top, चिक्षेप hurled, बली mighty, त्रिशिराः Trisira, तीक्ष्णैः sharp, शरैः arrow, बहूधा several pieces, बिभेद split into.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तद्व्यर्थंशिखरंदृष्टवाद्रुमवर्षंमहाकपिः । विससर्जरणेतस्मिन्रावणस्यसुतंप्रति ।।6.70.35।।
output: Then seeing that the top of the mountain hurled was ineffective in that battle over Ravana's son, Hanuman discharged rain of trees.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तमापतन्तमाकाशेद्रुमवर्षंप्रतापवान् । त्रिशिरानिशितैर्बाणैश्चिच्छेद च ननाद च ।।6.70.36।।
output: प्रतापवान् stupendous, त्रिशिराः Trisira, आ पतन्तम् tore, तम् them, द्रुमवर्षम् rain of trees, निशितैः whetted, बाणैः rain, आकाशे the sky, चिच्छेद shattered, ननादच roared.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
हनूमानुतोप्लुत्यहयंस्त्रीशिरसस्तदा । विददारनखैःक्रुद्धोनागेन्द्रंमृगराडिव ।।6.70.37।।
output: तदा then, हनुमान् तु Hanuman also, क्रुद्धः angry, उत्प्लुत्य jumping up, त्रिशिरसः at Trisira, हयम् horse, मृगराट् lion, नागेन्द्रम् इव like lordly elephant, नखैः nails, विददार tore.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 70:
अथशक्तिंसमादायकाळरात्रिमिवान्तकः । चिक्षेपानिलपुत्रायत्रिशिरारावणात्मजः ।।6.70.38।।
output: In the same manner, Trisira, the son of Ravana sprung up and seized a javelin, just as God of death in dark night and hurled at the son of wind god and shattered.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 70:
दिवःक्षिप्तामिवोल्कांतांशक्तिंक्षिप्तामसङ्गताम् । गृहीत्वाहरिशार्दूलोबभञ्ज च ननाद च ।।6.70.39।।
output: Hanuman, the best of monkeys, snapped the javelin flung by Trisira on him, which came down unobstructed like a meteor from heaven and the monkeys roared.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तांदृष्टवाघोरसङ्काशांशक्तिंभग्नांहनूमता । प्रहृष्टावानरगणाविनेदुर्जलदाइव ।।6.70.40।।
output: Seeing the dreadful form of shattered javelin, all Vanaras rejoiced and thundered like rain clouds.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तःखडगंसमुद्यम्यत्रिशिराराक्षसोत्तमः । निजघानतदाव्यूढेवायुपुत्रस्यवक्षसि ।।6.70.41।।
output: Trisira, the foremost of Rakshasas then lifted his sword, placed it on the chest of Hanuman and dug into it.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
खडगप्रहाराभिहतोहनुमान्मारुतात्मजः । आजघानतिशिरसंतलेनोरसिवीर्यवान् ।। 6.70.42।।
output: खडगप्रहाराभिहतः hit by sword, वीर्यवान् hero, मारुतात्मजः wind god's son, हनुमान् Hanuman, तलेन palm, तिशिरसम् Trisira, उरसि chest, आजघान attacked.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सतलाभिहतस्तेनस्रस्तहस्तायुधोभुवि । निपपातमहातेजास्त्रिशिरास्त्यक्तचेतनः ।।6.70.43।।
output: महातेजाः highly energetic, सःत्रिशिराः that Trisira, तेन by that, तलाभिहतः hit by palm, स्रस्तहस्तायुधः weapon dropped from hand, त्यक्तचेतनः senses lost, भुवि ground, निपपात fell.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 70:
स तस्यपततःखङ्गंतमाच्छिद्यमहाकपिः । ननादगिरिसङ्काशस्त्रासयन् सर्वनैरृता ।।6.70.44।।
output: Taking the sword from Trisira, as he was falling, the great Vanara who resembled a mountain roared, creating terror in all, surrounded there.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अमृष्यमाणस्तंघोषमुत्पपातनिशाचरः । उत्पत्य च हनूमन्तंताडयामासमुष्टिना ।।6.70.45।।
output: Unable to bear that roar, that Rakshasa got up jumping and struck Hanuman with his fist.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 70:
तेनमुष्टिप्रहोरेणसञ्चुकोपमहाकपिः । कुपितश्चनिजग्राहकिरीटेराक्षसर्षभम् ।।6.70.46।।
