output: "O Lord of Rakshasas, Vibheeshana! I wish to hear the words spoken by you. You may repeat that which you wanted to convey. I wish to hear."

output: "O great Lord! Hear me, which is yet to be submitted by me to you. You are afflicted without cause and pained at heart."

instruction:

output: "O king! Give up this false agony which has set in. It enhances the joy of the enemy. Give up this anxiety."

instruction:

output: "Delight of Raghus! You may listen to my words of advice. Let Saumithri march ahead to Nikumbhilam accompanied by the great army. On reaching, let Lakshmana who is capable of killing Indrajith discharge venomous serpents like deadly poisonous arrows from his bow in circular form and kill Rakshasas."

output: "Indrajith has reached Nikumbhilam accompanied by the army. If he completes the sacrifice and comes from there after completion of the sacrifice, know that we are all killed.

instruction:

output: "O mighty armed Rama! that enemy of yours, while you have not reached Nikumbhilam and not propitiated fire sacrifice, can cause your death. Such a boon was granted to him, the enemy of Indra by the Lord of all worlds."

instruction:

output: Rama, you are endowed with extraordinary prowess! Order now for the destruction of Indrajith as with his death Ravana and all his kinsfolk are killed, you may know.

instruction:

output: Hearing Vibheeshana, Rama said" the conjuring skills of Indrajith of truthful valour is known to me."

instruction:

output: He is skilled in the use of Brahma's weapon, intelligent in conjuring, endowed with mighty prowess, and can make even varuna and Devatas unconscious.

instruction:

instruction:

output: Knowing the wickedminded enemy of conjuring valour, Rama spoke as follows to Lakshmana, richly endowed with fame (of winning wars).

instruction:

output: "O Lakshmana! Surrounded by the entire army of Vanara king, with Hanuman as commander in chief of the army, protected by Jambavan, king of Bears, put an end to the son of Ravana who is well versed in tricks."

instruction:

output: "O Lakshmana! Surrounded by the entire army of Vanara king, with Hanuman as commander in chief of the army, protected by Jambavan, king of Bears, put an end to the son of Ravana who is well versed in tricks."

instruction:

output: "This great soul, night ranger (Vibheeshana) who knows his conjuring tricks well, will follow behind you with ministers."

instruction:

output: Now the arrows released from my bow will drop in Lanka, just as swans descend into lotus pond and pierce into Ravana's son.

output: Brilliant Lakshmana, having spoken that way in front of his brother, went speedily desirous of killing Ravana's son.

output: Lakshmana, a valourous prince having received blessings from his eldest brother, went quickly accompanied by Vibheeshana.

output: Mighty Bears and Vanaras of huge body, fighting in the battle caused great fear in Rakshasas.

instruction:

output: Seeing Lakshmana prepared for war, the Rakshasa army endowed with speed surrounded him.

instruction:

output: In the meantime, Hanuman, who resembled a mountain, a tamer of enemies, who is difficult to overpower, taking up huge trees fighting with Rakshasas created havoc like fire at the time of dissolution and went about.

instruction:

output: Between the skilful Rakshasas armed with sharp tridents, swords, javelins in hand, with spears in hand, bright iron bars glowing like fire, with iron axes, dreadful hammers, Bhindi palas and Hanuman, with thunderbolt like fists that descended like lightning, and slaps which descended like mountains, a huge skillful war took place.

output: Indrajith witnessed Hanuman, the foremost of Vanaras without weapons, fearlessly fighting.

instruction:

अस्मिंन्विनिहतेपापेराक्षसेरणमूर्थनि । रावणंवर्जयित्वातुशेषमस्यबलंहतम् ।।6.90.9।।
output: "If this wicked Rakshasa is struck down, except Ravana all his army is killed."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
प्रहस्तोनिहतोवीरोनिकुम्भश्चमहाबल. । कुम्भकर्णश्चकुम्भश्चधूम्राक्षश्चनिशाचरः ।।6.90.10।। जम्बुमालीमहामालीतीक्ष्णवेगोऽशनिप्रभः । सुप्तघ्नोयज्ञकोपश्चवज्रदंष्ट्रश्चराक्षसः ।।6.90.11।। सम्ह्रादीविकटोऽरिघ्नस्तपनोदमएव च । प्रघासःप्रघसश्चैवप्रजङ्घोजङ्घएव च ।।6.90.12।। अग्निकेतुश्चदुर्धर्षोरश्मिकेतुश्चवीर्यवान् । विद्युज्जिह्वाद्विजिह्वश्चसूर्यशत्रुश्चराक्षसः ।।6.90.13।। अकम्पनःसुपार्श्वश्चचक्रमाली च राक्षसः । कम्पनस्सत्त्ववन्तौतौदेवान्तकनरान्तकौ ।।6.90.14।।
output: प्रहस्तः Prahastha, निहतः killed, वीरः hero, निकुम्भश्च Nikumbha also, महाबलः of great prowess, कुम्भकर्णश्च Kumbhakarna also, कुम्भश्च Kumbha aslo, धूम्राक्षः Dhum raksha, निशाचरः night ranger, जम्बुमाली Jambumali, महामाली Mahamali, तीक्ष्णवेगः Teekshnavega, अशनिभ्रः Asanibhra, सुप्तघ्नः Suptagna, यज्ञकोपश्च Yagna kopa, वज्रदंष्ट्रः Vajradamshtra, राक्षसः Rakshasa, सम्ह्रादी Samhadri, अरिघ्नः Arigna, विकटः Vikata, तपनः Tapana, दमएव च Dama also, प्रघासः Praghasa, प्रघसIश्चैव Praghasa, प्रजङ्घ Prajangha:, जङञःएव च Jangha also, दुर्धर्षः Durdarsha, अग्निकेतुश्च Agniketha also, वीर्यवान् heroes, रश्मिकेतुश्च Rasmikethu, विद्युज्जिह्व Vidyajihva, द्विजिह्वः Dwijihwa, सूर्यशत्रुः Suryasatru, राक्षसश्च Rakshasas, अकम्पनः Akampana, सुपार्श्वश्च Suparswa, चक्रमाली Chakramali, राक्षसश्च Rakshasas, कम्पनः Kampana, सत्त्ववन्तौ energetic, देवान्तकनरान्तकौ Devanthaka and Naranthaka

output: "The heroic Prahastha, Nikumbha also and Kumbhakarna of mighty prowess, Kumbha also, night ranger Dum raksha, Jambumali, Mahamali, Teekshanavega, Asanibhra, Suptanga, Yagnakopa, Vajradamshtra, Rakshasas Simhadri, Arigna, Vikata, Tapana, Dama also, Praghaasa, Praghasa, Prajaghna, and Jaghan also, Durdarsha, Agniketha, heroes Rasmikethu, Vidyajihva, Dwijihwa, Suryasatru, and Rakshasas Akampana, Suparswa, Chakramali, and Rakshasas Kampana, and energetic Devanthaka and Naranthaka have been killed by you."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 90:
एतान्निहत्यातिबलान्बहून्राक्षससत्तमान् । बाहुभ्यांसागरंतीर्त्वालङ्घ्यतांगोष्पदं लघु ।6.90.15।।
output: "You have made short of many exceedingly mighty leaders of Rakshasas and swum the ocean. You cross this hoof mark of a cow without delay."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 90:
एतावदेवशेषंवोजेतव्यमिहवानराः । हतास्सर्वेसमागम्यराक्षसाबलदर्पिताः ।।6.90.16।।
output: "O Vanaras! Left over Rakshasas only to be conquered now. Rakshasas, who were proud of their might have been killed on meeting you."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अयुक्तंनिधनंकर्तुंपुत्रस्यजनितुर्मम । घृणामपास्यरामार्थेनिहन्यांभ्रातुरात्मजम् ।।6.90.17।।
output: जनितुः father, मम my, पुत्रस्य son like, निधनम् striking, कर्तुम् will do, अयुक्तम् not proper, रामार्धे for the sake of Rama, घृणाम् taking pity, अपास्य helpless, भ्रातुः brother, आत्मजम् my son, निहन्याम् take out life

instruction:

output: हन्तुकामस्य wish to kill, मे my, चक्षुः eyes, बाष्पम् tears, निरुध्यति clouding, महाबाहुः mightyarmed, एषः so, लक्ष्मणःएव Lakshmana, तमशमयिष्यति will kill him, वानराःVanara, सम्भूय collected, अस्य to him, समीपगान् coming near, भृत्यान् attendants, घ्नत destroy

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 90:
इतितेनातियशसाराक्षसेनाभिचोदिताः ।।6.90.19।। वानरेन्द्राजहृषिरेलाङ्गूलानि च विव्यधुः ।
output: Incited by the encouraging words of Vibheeshana (Rakshasa), Vanara chiefs rejoiced and went shaking their tails.

instruction:

output: ततः then, कपिशार्दूलाः tigers among monkeys, पुनःपुनः again and again, श्रवेड़न्तःश्च roaring, मेघान् clouds, दृष्टवा seen, बर्हिणःइव like peacocks, विविधान् several, नादान् sounds, मुमुचुः made

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
जाम्बवानपितैःसर्वैःसयूथ्यैरभिसम्वृतः ।।6.90.21।। तेऽश्मभिस्ताडयामासुर्नखैर्धन्स्सैश्चराक्षसान् ।
output: All the troops surrounded by Jambavan too, pierced the Rakshasas with their nails and teeth.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
निघ्नन्तमृक्षाधिपतिंराक्षसास्तेमहाबलाः ।।6.90.22।। परिवव्रुर्भयंत्यक्त्वातमनेकविधायुथाः ।
output: The Rakshasas who were endowed with mighty strength giving up fear, armed with different kinds of weapons surrounded Jambavan, the Lord of Bears.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
शरैःपरशुभिस्तीक्ष्णैःपट्टिशैर्यष्टितोमरैः ।।6.90.23।। जाम्बवन्तंमृधेजघ्नुर्निघ्नन्तंराक्षसींचमूम् ।
output: मृधे, राक्षसीम् Rakshasas, चमूम् army, निघ्नन्तम् destroying, जाम्बवन्तम् Jambavan, शरैः arrows, तीक्ष्णैः pointed, परशुभिः axes, पट्टिशैः iron bars, यष्टितोमरैः sharpedged spears, जघ्नुः assailed

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स सम्प्रहारस्तुमुलःसञ्जज्ञेकपिरक्षसाम् ।।6.90.24।। देवासुराणांक्रुद्धानांयथाभीमोमहास्वनः ।
output: Fearful and vehement battle took place between enraged Vanaras and Rakshasas making loud clamours like the battle (in the past) between Devas and asuras.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
हनुमानपिसङ्क्रुद्धःसानुमुत्पाट्यपर्वतात् ।।6.90.25।। स लक्ष्मणंस्वयंपृष्ठादवरोप्यमहामनाः । रक्षसांकदनंचक्रेसमासाद्यसहस्रशः ।।6.90.26।।
output: Great selfHanuman too became furious and dismounting Lakshmana from his back uprooted a sala tree from a mountain and went on exterminating thousands of Rakshasas.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:

output: महामनाः great self, सःहनुमानपि Hanuman too, सङ्क्रुद्धः very furious, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana, स्वयम् himself, पृष्ठात् back, अवरोप्य dismount, पर्वतात् from a mountain, सानुम्Sala tree, उत्पाट्य uprooted, समासाद्य thousands, सहस्रशः thousands, रक्षसाम् of Rakshasa, कदनम् exterminate, चक्रे went on

instruction:

instruction:

स रथंभूषयित्वाथरुचिरंहेमभूषितम् । प्रासासिशरसंयुक्तंयुक्तंपरमवाजिभिः ।।6.91.9।। अधिष्ठितंहयज्ञेनसूतेनाप्तोपदेशिना । आरुरोहमहातेजारावणिःसमतिञ्जियः ।।6.91.10।।
output: Ravana's son ascended a decorated chariot yoked to horses, directed by a charioteer who could tender good advice and a knower of the nature of horses. It was a beautiful chariot decked with darts and swords adorned with gold which Ravana's son of extraordinarily bright, who has won enemies, ascended.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स राक्षसगणैर्मुख्यैर्वृतोमन्दोदरीसुतः । निर्ययौनगरावदीरःकृतान्तबलचोदितः ।।6.91.11।।
output: वीरः heroic, सःमन्दोदरीसुतः that Mandodari's son, मुख्यैः chief, राक्षसगणैः of Rakshasa army, वृतःsurrounded, कृतान्तबलचोदितः impelled by the force of destiny, नगरात् from the city, निर्ययौ departed

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
सोऽभिनिष्क्रम्यनगरादिन्द्रजित्परवीरहा । अभ्ययाज्ञवनैरश्वैर्लक्ष्मणंसविभीषणम् ।।6.91.12।।
output: Heroic in the act of destruction of enemies, Indarjith having started from the city in his chariot drawn by swift horses assailed Vibheeshana and Lakshmana.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततोरथस्थमालोक्यसौमत्रीरावणात्मजम् । वानराश्चमहावीर्याराक्षसश्चविभीषणः ।।6.91.13।। विस्मयंपरमंजग्मुर्लाघवात्तस्यधीमतः ।
output: ततः then, रथस्थम् seated in the chariot, रावणात्मजम् Indrajith, आलोक्य seeing, सौमित्रिः Saumithri, महावीर्याः great hero, वानराश्च at Vanaras, विभीषणश्च Vibheeshana too, धीमतः wise, तस्य his, लाघवात् easily, परमम् highly, विस्मयम् wondered, जग्मुः experienced

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
रावणिश्चापिसङ्क्रुद्धोरणेवानरयूथपान् ।।6.91.14।। पातयामासबाणौघैःशतशोऽथसहस्रशः ।
output: Indrajith, highly enraged, struck Vanara leaders with a volley of hundreds and thousands of arrows.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
मण्डलीकृतधनूरावणिःसमतिञ्जयः ।।6.91.15।। हरीनभ्यहनत्कृद्धःपरंलाघवमास्थितः ।
output: Indrajith, a winner of combat, became highly furious and stretched his bow showing his skill easily struck at Vanaras.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
तेवध्यमानाहरयोनाराचैर्भीमविक्रमैः ।।6.91.16।। सौमित्रिंशरणंप्राप्ताःप्रजापतिमिवप्रजाः ।
output: (The Vanaras), though endowed with prowess and of terrific courage, struck by the Rakshasa, they sought refuge of Lakshmana, their Lord, just as people seek the refuge of their Lord, the creator.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततःसमरकोपेनज्वलितोरघुनन्दनः ।।6.91.17।। चिच्छेदकार्मुकंतस्यदर्शयन् पाणिलाघवम् ।
output: ततः there, रघुनन्दनः delight of Raghus, समरकोपेन angry in battle, ज्वलितः glowing, पाणिलाघवम् showing the skill of his hand s, दर्शनयन् showing, तस्य his, कार्मुकम् bow, चिच्छेद shattered

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
सोन्यऽत्कार्मुकम् मादायसज्जंचक्रेत्वरन्निव ।।6.91.18।। तदप्यस्यत्रिभिर्बाणैर्लक्ष्मणोनिरकृन्तत ।
output: Indrajith seizing another bow hastily targeted at Lakshmana and Lakshmana split them with three arrows.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अथैवंछिन्नधन्वानमाशीविषविषोपमैः ।।6.91.19।। विव्याधोरसिसौमित्रीरावणिंपञ्चभिःशरैः ।
output: Then Saumithri pierced with five arrows into the chest of Indrajith like a venomous serpent and split the bow.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तेतस्यकायंनिर्भिद्यमहाकार्मुकनिस्सृताः ।।6.91.20।। निपेतुर्धरणींबाणारक्ताइवमहोरगाः ।
output: महाकार्मुकनिःसृताः released from the great bow, तेthose, बाणाः arrows, तस्य his, कायम् body, निर्भिद्य entering, रक्ताः red, महोरगाः huge serpent, इव like, धरणीम् ground, निपेतुःdropped

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
भिन्नवर्मारुधिरंवमन्वक्त्रेणरावणिः ।।6.91.21।। जग्राहकार्मुकश्रेष्ठंदृढज्यंबलवत्तरम् ।
output: Bow split, ejecting blood from mouth, Indrajith took his strong best of bows which had a stout string.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
सःलक्ष्मणंसमुद्धिश्यपरंलाघवमाश्रितः ।।6.91.22।। ववर्षशरवर्षाणिवर्षाणीवपुरन्दरः ।
output: Indrajith, aiming at Lakshmana, let loose rain of arrows easily like rain.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
मुक्तमिन्द्रजितातत्तुशरवर्षमरिन्दमः ।।6.91.23।। अवारयदसम्भ्रान्तोलक्ष्मणःसुदुरासदम् ।
output: Lakshmana, the tamer of enemies, without reacting intercepted the shower of arrows released by Indrajith which was difficult to resist.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
संदर्शयामासतदारावणिंरघुनन्दनः ।।6.91.24।। असम्ब्रान्तोमहातेजेस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ।
output: Highly energetic Lakshmana, a delight of Raghus, unperturbed, demonstrated to Indrajith, which was a wonder indeed.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तस्तान् राक्षसान् सर्वांस्त्रिभिरेकैकमाहवे ।।6.91.25।। अविध्यत्परमक्रुद्धश्शीघ्रास्त्रंसम्प्रदर्शयन् । राक्षसेन्द्रसुतंचापिबाणौघैस्समताडयत् ।।6.91.26।।
output: Then extremely angry Lakshmana pierced all the Rakshasas quickly, each one with three arrows and struck them and even the son of Rakshasa king, exhibiting his skills.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तस्तान् राक्षसान् सर्वांस्त्रिभिरेकैकमाहवे ।।6.91.25।। अविध्यत्परमक्रुद्धश्शीघ्रास्त्रंसम्प्रदर्शयन् । राक्षसेन्द्रसुतंचापिबाणौघैस्समताडयत् ।।6.91.26।।
output: Then extremely angry Lakshmana pierced all the Rakshasas quickly, each one with three arrows and struck them and even the son of Rakshasa king, exhibiting his skills.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सोऽतिविद्धोबलवताशत्रुणाशत्रुघातिना । असक्तंप्रेषयामासलक्ष्मणायबहून् शरान् ।।6.91.27।।
output: शत्रुघातिना destroyer of hostile enemies, बलवता forcibly, शत्रुणा foes, अतिविद्धः grievously wounded, सः he, लक्ष्मणाय Lakshmana, बहून् many, शरान् arrows, असक्तम् continuously released, प्रेषयामास directed

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तानप्राप्तान् शितैर्भाणैश्चिच्छेदपरवीरहा । सारथेरस्य च रणेरथिवोरघुसत्तमः ।।6.91.28।। शिरोजहारधर्मात्माभल्लेनानतपर्वणा ।
output: Heroic enemy, the righteous Lakshmana, tore the head of the carwarrior as well as the charioteer in the battle with bhala (spear), even before Indrajith discharged pointed arrows at him.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
सूतास्तेहयास्तत्ररथमूहुरविक्लबाः ।।6.91.29।। मण्डलान्यभिधावन्तस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ।
output: There, though there was no charioteer, the horses went round in circles and as they went forward it was wonderful.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अमर्षवशमापन्नःसौमित्रिर्दृढविक्रमः ।।6.91.30।। प्रत्यविद्ध्यद्धयांस्तस्यशरैर्वित्रासयन् रणे ।
output: दृढविक्रमः untiring valour, सौमित्रिः Saumithri, रणे in battle, अमर्षवशम् overcome with fury, आपन्नः afflicted, तस्य his, हयान् horses, वित्रासयन् destroyed, शरैः with arrows, प्रत्यविध्यत् struck to scare them

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अमर्षमाणस्तत्कर्मरावणस्यसुतोबली ।।6.91.31।। विव्याथदशभिर्बाणैस्सौमित्रिंतममर्षणम् ।
output: रावणस्य Ravana's, सुतः son, बली strong, तत् that, कर्म action, अमृष्यमाणः not tolerating, अमर्षणम् angry, तंसौमित्रिम् that Saumithri, दशभिः ten, बाणैः arrows, विव्याथ struck.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
तेतस्यवज्रप्रतिमाःशरास्सर्पविषोपमाः ।।6.91.32।। विलयंजग्मुरागत्यकवचंकाञ्चनप्रभम् ।
output: His arrows, which resembled thunderbolts and were like venomous serpents, touching Lakshmana's shield shining like gold, broken, and fallen

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
अभ्येद्यकवचंमत्वालक्ष्मणंरावणात्मजः ।।6.91.33।। ललाटेलक्ष्मणंबाणैस्सुपुङ्खैस्त्रिभिरिन्द्रजित् । अविध्यत्परमक्रुद्धःशीघ्रमस्त्रंप्रदर्शयन् ।।6.91.34।।
output: रावणात्मजः Ravana's son, इन्द्रजित् Indrajith, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana, अभेद्यकवचम् not possible to break, मत्वा knowing, परमक्रुद्धःenraged, अस्त्रम् weapon, शीघ्रम् quickly, प्रदर्शयन् showing, लक्ष्मणम् Lakshmana, सुपुङ्खैः plumes, त्रिभिःमाणैःthree arrows with gems, ललाटे on the forehead, अविध्यत् struck

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
अभ्येद्यकवचंमत्वालक्ष्मणंरावणात्मजः ।।6.91.33।। ललाटेलक्ष्मणंबाणैस्सुपुङ्खैस्त्रिभिरिन्द्रजित् । अविध्यत्परमक्रुद्धःशीघ्रमस्त्रंप्रदर्शयन् ।।6.91.34।।
output: Ravana's son, knowing that it is not possible to break the shield of Lakshmana, quickly showed his weapon with three arrows with plumes and gems and struck him on the forehead.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तैःपृषत्कैर्ललाटस्थैश्शुशुभेरघुनन्दनः । रणाग्रेसमरश्लाघीत्रिशृङ्गइवपर्वतः ।।6.91.35।।
output: समरश्लाघी who loved to fight, रघुनन्दनः delight of Raghus, ललाटस्थैः on the forehead, तैः those, पृषत्कैः arrows, समरे in battle, त्रिशृङ्गःthree peaks, पर्वतःइव like mountain, शुशुभेcharming peaks.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
स तथाह्यर्दितोबाणैराक्षसेनतदामृधे । तमाशुप्रतिविव्याधलक्ष्मणःपञ्चभिःशरैः ।।6.91.36।। विकृष्वेन्द्रजितोयुद्धेवदनेशुभकुण्डले ।
output: Then in the battle, pierced by Rakshasa in that manner, Laksmana immediately stretched his bow and struck with five arrows on the face of Indrajith, who was adorned with auspicious earrings.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
लक्ष्मणेन्द्रजितौवीरौमहाबलशरासनौ ।।6.91.37।। अन्योन्यंजघ्नतुर्बाणैर्विशिखैर्मीविक्रमौ ।
output: Both heroes of extraordinary might and equipped with huge arms, endowed with terrific valour, Lakshmana and Indrajith struck one another with sharp arrows.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
ततःशोणितदिग्धाङ्गौलक्ष्मणेन्दजितावुभौ ।।6.91.38।। रणेतौराजतुर्वीरौपुष्पिताविवकिंशुकौ ।
output: Then smeared with blood the two, Lakshmana and Indrajit, shone like fully blossomed Kimsuka in battle.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तौपरस्परमभ्येत्यसर्वगात्रेषुधवनिनौ ।।6.91.39।। घोरैर्विव्यधतुर्भाणैःकृतभावावुभौजये ।
output: Both wishing for victory, set to tear each other, pierced dreadful arrows on one another all over the limbs, opposing.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
ततःसमरकोपेनसम्वृतोरावणात्मजः ।।6.91.40।। विभीषणंत्रिभिर्बाणैर्विव्याथवदनेशुभे ।
output: Then Ravana's son in his charming countenance, filled with wrath because of conflict, struck at Vibheeshana with three arrows.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अयोमुखैस्त्रिभिर्विद्ध्वाराक्षसेन्द्रंविभीषणम् ।।6.91.41।। एकैकेनाभिविव्याथतान्सर्वान् हरियूथपान् ।
output: Having struck Vibheeshana with three arrows, he struck again all the Vanara leaders with one arrow each.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तस्मैदृढतरंक्रुद्धोजघानगदयाहयान् ।।6.91.42।। विभीषणोमहातेजारावणेस्सदुरात्मनः ।
output: महातेजाः brilliant, सःविभीषणः that Vibheeshana, तस्मै his, दृढतरम् mace, क्रुद्धःangry, दुरात्मनःevil minded, रावणेः Indrajith, हयान् horses, गदयाelephants, जघान struck

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
पहताश्वादवाप्लुत्यरथान्निहतसारथे: ।।6.91.43।। रथशक्तिंमहातेजाःपितृव्यायमुमोच ह ।
output: निहितसारथिः charioteer destroyed, महातेजाः highly energetic, सः he, हतश्वात् horses killed, रथात् from the chariot, अवाप्लुत्य leaping down, अथ now, पितृव्याय uncle, रथ chariot, शक्तिम् javelin, मुमोच ह hurled

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तामापततनींसम्प्रेक्ष्यसुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः ।।6.91.44।। चिच्छेदनिशितैर्बाणैर्धशथापातयद्भुवि ।
output: सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः delight of Sumithra, enhancer of Sumithra's joy, आपतीन्तम् coming towards, ताम् those, सम्प्रेक्ष्य observing, निशितैः pointed, बाणैः arrows, चिच्छेद split it, दशधा to ten, भुवि ground, अपातयत् fallen

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
तस्मैदृढतनुःक्रुद्धोहताश्वायविभीषणः ।।6.91.45।। वज्रस्पर्शसमान् पञ्चससर्जोरसिसायकान् ।
output: Vibheeshana of strong body, pierced five arrows like thunderbolt in impact into the chest of Indrajith.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तेतस्यकायंभित्वातुरुक्मपुङ्खानिमित्तगाः ।।6.91.46।। बभूवुर्लोहितादिग्धारक्ताइवमहोरगाः ।
output: The arrows with red feathers of Vibheeshana having penetrated the body of Indrajith, piercing into the body they became red coloured seemed like a red serpent.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सःपितृव्यस्यसङ्क्रुद्धःइन्द्रजिच्छरमाददे ।।6.91.47।। उत्तमंरक्षसांमध्येयमदत्तंमहाबलम् ।
output: सःइन्द्रजित् that Indrajith, पितृव्यस्य uncle, सङ्क्रुद्धःangry, रक्षसाम् Rakshasas, मध्ये midst, यमदत्तम् given by Yama, महाबलम् might strong, उत्तमम् best, शरम् arrow, आददे seized

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तंसमीक्ष्यमहातेजामहेषुंतेनसंहितम् ।।6.91.48।। लक्ष्मणोऽप्याददेबाणमद्यभदीमपराक्रमः ।
output: महातेजाः extraordinarily brilliant, भीमपराक्रमः of terrific valour, लक्ष्मणोऽपि Lakshmana also, संहितम् yoked, महेषुम् mighty shaft, समीक्ष्य perceiving, अन्यत् another, बाणम् arrow, आददे took up

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
कुबेरेणस्वयंस्वप्नेयद्दत्तममितात्मना ।।6.91.49।। दुर्जयंदुर्विषह्यं च सेन्द्रैरपिसुरासुरैः ।
output: That arrow was gifted to Lakshmana in dream by Kubera, the god of wealth and even Suras or Asuras cannot resist it and is difficult to win.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तयोस्तुधनुषीश्रेष्ठेबाहुभिःपरिघोपमैः ।।6.91.50।। विकृष्यमाणेबलवत् क्रौञ्चविवचुकूजतुः ।
output: परिगोपमैः resembling iron bars, बाहुभिः arms, बलवत् with great strength, विकृष्यमाणे drawn, तयोः those two, श्रेष्ठेexcellent, धनुषी bows, क्रौञ्चविव like Krauncha, चुकूजतुः made noise

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
ताभ्यांतुधनुषिश्रेष्ठेसंसितौसायकोत्तमौ ।।6.91.51।। विकृष्यमाणेवीराभ्यांभृशंजज्वलतुःश्रिया ।
output: The two best bows of both the heroes together, being powerful, shone with splendour when drawn with bowstring.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तौभासयन्तावाकाशंधनुर्भ्यांविशिखौच्युतौ ।।6.91.52।। मुखेनमुखमाहत्यसन्निपेततुरोजसा ।
output: धनुर्ब्याम् from the bows, च्युतौ released, तौ those, विशिखौ arrows, आकाशम् sky, भासयन्तौ lighting, मुखेन heads collided, मुखम् hitting the head, आहत्य meeting, ओजसा glowing, सन्निपेततुः rubbed against each other

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
सन्निपातस्तयोश्चासीच्छरयोर्घोररूपयोः ।।6.91.53।। सधूमविस्फुलिङ्गश्चतज्जोऽनगिर्दारुणोऽभवत् ।
output: By the impact of the two arrows brought together, a formidable form of fire frightening with smoke and sparks was created.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
तौमहाग्रहसङ्काशावन्योन्यंसन्निपत्य च ।।6.91.54।। सङ्ग्रामेशतधायातौमेदिन्यांचैवपेततुः ।
output: In the battle both of them touching each other in conflict like the major planets flew into a hundred pieces and fell on earth.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
शरौप्रतिहतौदृष्टवातावुभौरणमूर्धनि ।।6.91.55।। व्रीडितौजातरोषौ च लक्ष्मणेन्द्रजितौतदा ।
output: Then both Lakshmana and Indrajith in the face of the battle seeing their arrows in nought with each other were abashed and got agitated.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
सुसंरर्ब्धस्तुसौमित्रिरस्त्रंवारुमाददे ।।6.91.56।। रौद्रंमहेन्द्रजिद्युद्धेऽप्यसृजद्युद्धनिष्ठितः ।
output: Enraged Saumithri, seizing the weapon of Varuna, skilled in warfare loosened on Indrajith (Mahendra's enemy), which was presided over by Rudra.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तेनतद्विहतंशस्त्रंवारुणंपरमाद्भुतम् ।।6.91.57।। ततःक्रुद्धोमहातेजाइन्द्रजित्समितिञ्जयः । आग्नेयंसन्दधेदीप्तं स लोकंसङ्क्षिपन्निव ।।6.91.58।।
output: Then the very wonderful weapon of Varuna was made ineffective by the highly energetic Indrajith's who used glowing fire missiles as if to destroy the whole world.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
तेनतद्विहतंशस्त्रंवारुणंपरमाद्भुतम् ।।6.91.57।। ततःक्रुद्धोमहातेजाइन्द्रजित्समितिञ्जयः । आग्नेयंसन्दधेदीप्तं स लोकंसङ्क्षिपन्निव ।।6.91.58।।
output: Then the very wonderful weapon of Varuna was made ineffective by the highly energetic Indrajith's who used glowing fire missiles as if to destroy the whole world.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सौरेणास्त्रणतवदीरोलक्ष्मणःपर्यवारयत् । अस्त्रंनिवारितंदृष्टवारावणिःक्रोथमूर्छितः ।।6.91.59।। आददेनिशितंबाणमासुरंशत्रुदारुणम् ।
output: Then Lakshmana used a Sun missile and repelled (Indrajith's fire missile). Seeing his missile obstructed, Indrajith deluded with anger used a sharp Asura missile capable of destroying the enemy.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
तस्माच्चापाद्विनिष्पेतुर्भास्वराःकूटमुद्गराः ।।6.91.60।। शूलानि च मुशुण्ड्यश्चगदाःखङ्गा: परश्वथा: ।
output: By the Sun missile, the Kutamudgaras, tridents, Bhusundas, swords and axes issued forth from Indrajith's bow.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
तद्दृष्टवालक्ष्मणःसङ्ख्येघोरमस्त्रंसुदारुणम् ।।6.91.61।। अवार्यंसर्वभूतानांसर्वशस्त्रविदारणम् । महेश्वरेणद्युतिमांस्तदस्त्रंप्रत्यवारयत् ।।6.91.62।।
output: Effulgent Lakshmana, seeing the terrible Asura missile and deliberating that it is capable of destroying all human beings and difficult to repel, used a Maheswara missile to divert.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
तद्दृष्टवालक्ष्मणःसङ्ख्येघोरमस्त्रंसुदारुणम् ।।6.91.61।। अवार्यंसर्वभूतानांसर्वशस्त्रविदारणम् । महेश्वरेणद्युतिमांस्तदस्त्रंप्रत्यवारयत् ।।6.91.62।।
output: Effulgent Lakshmana, seeing the terrible Asura missile and deliberating that it is capable of destroying all human beings and difficult to repel, used a Maheswara missile to divert.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तयोःसमुतुलंयुद्धंसम्बभूवारोमहर्षणम् । गगनस्थानिभूतानिलक्ष्मणंपर्यवारयन् ।।6.91.63।।
output: The war between both was wonderful and horripulating. Beings from the sky saw Lakshmana diverting the Asura missile.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
भैरवाभिरुतेभीमेयुद्धेवानरक्षसाम् । भूतैर्बहुभिराकाशंविस्मितैरावृतंबभौ ।।6.91.64।।
output: वानररक्षसाम् Vanaras and Rakshasas, भैरवाभिरुते frightful, भीमे fierce, युद्धे battle, विस्मितैः astonished, बहुभिः many, भूतैःbeings, आवृतम् surrounded, आकाशम् in the sky, बभौ charming

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ऋषयःपितरोदेवागन्धर्वगरुडोरगाः । शतक्रतुंपुरस्कृत्यररक्षुर्लक्ष्मणंरणे ।।6.91.65।।
output: ऋषयः Rsis, पितरः manes, देवाः Devatas, गन्धर्वगरुडोरगाः Gandharvas, Garuda, serpents शतक्रतुम् who had done hundred sacrifices, पुरस्कृत्य having performed, लक्ष्मणं Lakshmana, रण war, ररक्षुःprotected

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अथान्यंमार्गणश्रेष्ठंसन्दधेराघवानुजः । हुताशनसमस्पर्शंरावणात्मजदारणम् ।।6.91.66।।
output: And thereafter, Raghava's brother fitted another excellent arrow which had the impact of the touch of fire capable of tearing Indrajith.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
सुपत्रमनुवृत्ताङ्गंसुपर्वाणंसुसंस्थितम् । सुवर्णविकृतंवीरश्शरीरान्तकरंशरम् ।।6.91.67।। दुरावारंदुर्विषहंराक्षसानांभयावहम् । आशीविषविषप्रख्यंदेवसङ्घैःसमर्चितम् ।।6.91.68।।
output: The arrow with lovely feathers, consisting of beautiful parts, skilfully done, well jointed, decked with gold, was not only difficult to put off but also difficult to bear, was capable of destroying enemies, frightful, resembling venomous serpents, and worshipped by gods.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सुपत्रमनुवृत्ताङ्गंसुपर्वाणंसुसंस्थितम् । सुवर्णविकृतंवीरश्शरीरान्तकरंशरम् ।।6.91.67।। दुरावारंदुर्विषहंराक्षसानांभयावहम् । आशीविषविषप्रख्यंदेवसङ्घैःसमर्चितम् ।।6.91.68।।
output: The arrow with lovely feathers, consisting of beautiful parts, skilfully done, well jointed, decked with gold, was not only difficult to put off but also difficult to bear, was capable of destroying enemies, frightful, resembling venomous serpents, and worshipped by gods.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
येनशक्रोमहातेजादानवानजत्प्रभुः । पुरादेवासुरेयुद्धेवीर्यवान् हरिवाहनः ।।6.91.69।।
output: In the past at the war between Devas and Asuras, a mighty and energetic valiant Lord of Devas who had green horses conquered Danavas (with the same sword).

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
तदैन्द्रमस्त्रंसौमित्रिःसम्युगेष्वपराजितम् । शरश्रेष्ठंधनु: श्रेष्ठेविकर्षन्निदमिब्रवीत् ।।6.91.70।। लक्ष्मीवान् लक्ष्मणोवाक्यमर्थसाधकमात्मनः ।
output: Son of Saumithri, that prosperous Lakshmana, drawing Indra's missile, the foremost one, and also the best of arrows, which has never been defeated, spoke these words set to achieve the purpose.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
धर्मात्मासत्यसन्धश्चरामोदाशरथिर्यति ।।6.91.71।। पौरुषेचाप्रतिद्वन्द्वःशरैनंजसिरावणिम् ।
output: दाशरथिःDasharatha's son, रामःRama, धर्मात्मा righteous, सत्यसन्धश्च truthful, पौरुषे unrivalled in might, अप्रतिद्वन्द्वः न यदि if true to his promise, शर arrow, एम् this, रावणिम् Indrajith, जहि will kill

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
इत्युक्त्वाबाणमाकर्णंविकृष्यतमजिह्मगम् ।।6.91.72।। लक्ष्मणःसमरेवीरःससर्जेन्द्रजितंप्रति ।
output: Having spoken that way, Lakshmana, heroic in battle, bending the bow, stretching the arrow till the ear released on Indrajith.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ऐन्द्रास्त्रेणसमायुज्यलक्ष्मणःपरवीरहा ।।6.91.73।। ततशिरःसशिरस्त्राणंश्रीमज्ज्वलितकुण्डलम् । प्रमथ्येन्द्रजितःकायात्पातयामासभूतले ।।6.91.74।।
output: Prosperous Lakshmana, the destroyer of enemies, aiming at Indrajith's head shining with earrings belonging to the head severed from the body, it fell on ground.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ऐन्द्रास्त्रेणसमायुज्यलक्ष्मणःपरवीरहा ।।6.91.73।। ततशिरःसशिरस्त्राणंश्रीमज्ज्वलितकुण्डलम् । प्रमथ्येन्द्रजितःकायात्पातयामासभूतले ।।6.91.74।।
output: परवीरहा destroyer of enemies, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, ऐन्द्रास्त्रण Indra's missile, समायुज्य aiming, सशिरस्त्राणम् belonging to the head, श्रीमत् prosperous, ज्वलितकुण्डलम् shining earrings, तत् that, शिरः head, प्रमथ्य severed, इन्द्रजितः Indrajith, कायात् from body, भूतलेon earth, पातयामास fell

instruction:

तद्राक्षसतनूजस्यभिन्नस्कन्धंशिरोमहत् । तपनीयनिभंभूमौददृशेरुधिरोक्षितम् ।।6.91.75।।
output: भिन्नस्कन्धम् trunk broken, रुधिरोक्षितम् bathed in blood, राक्षसतनूजस्य Indrajith's, महत् huge, तत् शिरः head, तपनीयनिभम् shining like gold, भूमौ on the earth, ददृशे seen

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
हतः स निपपाताथधरण्यांरावणात्मजः । कवचीसशिरस्त्राणोविद्धस्थशरासनः ।।6.91.76।।
output: अत and then, कवची shield, सशिरस्त्राण helmet of the head, विद्धिस्थश रासनः protection on broken, सःरावणात्मजः that Indrajith, हतःkilled, धरण्याम् on the earth, निपपात ह thrown

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
चुक्रुशुस्तेततःसर्वेवानराःसविभीषणाः । हृष्यन्तोनिहतेतस्मिन् देवावृत्रवधेयथा ।।6.91.77।।
output: Then Vibheeshana and all the Vanaras rejoiced just as Devas, when Vrtasura was killed.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अथान्तरिक्षेभूतानामृषीणां च महात्मनाम् । जज्ञेऽथजयसन्नादोगन्धर्वाप्सरसामपि ।।6.91.78।।
output: Then shouts of victory aroused from the heavens from the created beings of heaven, Rsis also, Gandharvas and Apsaras.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
पतितंतमभिज्ञायराक्षसीसामहाचमूः । वध्यमानादिशोभेजेहरिभिर्जितकाशिभिः ।।6.91.79।।
output: Great army of Rakshasas even though desired to win seeing (Indrajith dead), Vanaras started attacking them. Unable to bear Rakshasas screamed.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
वानरैर्वध्यमानास्तेशस्त्रानुत्सृज्यराक्षसाः । लङ्कामभिमुखास्सस्रुर्भ्रष्टसंज्ञाःप्रधाविताः ।।6.91.80।।
output: तेराक्षसाः those Rakshasas, वानरैः Vanaras, वध्यमानाः being killed, शस्त्राणि weapons, उत्सृज्य leaving, भ्रष्टसंज्ञाःsenses lost, प्रधाविताः assaulted, लङ्काम् to Lanka, अभिमुखाःtowards, सस्रुः went running

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
दुद्रुवुर्भहुधाभीताराक्षसाश्शतशोदिशः । त्यक्त्वाप्रहरणान्सर्वेपट्टसासिपरश्वधान् ।।6.91.81।।
output: All Rakshasas feared and panic stricken fled in hundreds, in groups in all directions leaving their sharpedged spears, swords, and axes.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
केचिल्लङ्कांपरित्रस्ताःविष्टावानरार्दिताः । समुद्रेपतिताःकेचित्केचित्पर्वतमाश्रिताः ।।6.91.82।।
output: Pained by Vanaras, some fearful entered Lanka, few had fallen in the ocean and some sought refuge in the mountain.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
हतमिन्द्रजितंदृष्टवाशयानं च रणक्षितौ । राक्षसानांसहस्रेषु न कश्चित्प्रत्यदृश्यत ।।6.91.83।।
output: Indrajith was lying, having fallen on the ground, and not even one of the thousands of Rakshasas was present there to see.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
यथास्तङ्गतआदित्येनावतिष्ठन्तिरश्मयः । तथातस्मिन्निपतितेराक्षसास्तेगतादिशः ।।6.91.84।।
output: Just as Sun rays go away as soon as the Sun sets in the evening, the Rakshasas also went in all directions seeing Indrajith fallen.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
शान्तरश्मिरिवादित्योनिर्वाणइवपावकः । बभूव स महाबाहुर्व्यपास्तगतजीवितः ।।6.91.85।।
output: Shorn of life, the broad shouldered Indrajith remained on the ground like the Sun whose rays have become cool, after death.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:
प्रशान्तपीडाबहुलोविनष्टारिःप्रहर्षवान् । बभूवलोकःपतितेराक्षसेन्द्रसुतोतदा ।।6.91.86।।
output: Then many were at peace and rejoiced in the world, being relieved, when Ravana's son dropped dead.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
हर्षं च शक्रोभगवान् सहसर्वैर्महर्षिभिः । जगामनिहतेतस्मिन्राक्षसेपापकर्मणि ।।6.91.87।।
output: पापकर्मणि of sinful deeds, तस्मिन् राक्षसे that Rakshasa, निहते killed, भगवान् glorious, शक्रःIndra, सर्वैःall, महर्षिभिःसह including great sages, हर्षम् rejoiced, जगाम felt

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
आकाशेचापिदेवानांशुश्रुवेदुन्दुभिस्वनः । नृत्यद्भिरप्सरोभिश्चगन्धर्वैश्चमहात्मभिः ।।6.91.88।।
output: आकाशे in the heaven, देवानाम् Devas, दुन्दुभिस्वनः sounds of drums, नृत्यद्भिः dance also, अप्सरोभिः of Apsaras, महात्मभिः of great souls, गन्धर्वैश्च Gandharvas, शुश्रुवे was heard

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ववर्षुःपुष्पवर्षाणितदद्भुतमिवाभवत् । प्रशशंसुर्हतेतस्मिन्राक्षसेक्रूरकर्मणि ।।6.91.89।।
output: With cruel minded Rakshasa killed, celebrities showered rain of flowers praising the wonderful deed.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:

output: As the terror of all worlds had fallen and the water from the sky became pure, Devas and Danavas rejoiced and came there.

instruction:

output: Devas, Danavas and Ghandharvas arrived there and said, "Let the Brahmins be without anxiety and move about without fear."

instruction:

output: Vibheeshana and Hanuman, leader of Bears Jambavan praised Lakshmana and greeted him for his victory.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 91:

output: Having accomplished their goal, monkeys roaring, playing, surrounded Lakshmana, and stood.

instruction:

लाङ्गूलानिप्रविध्यन्तस्स्फोटयन्तश्चवानराः । लक्ष्मणोजयतीत्येवंवाक्यंविश्रावयंस्तदा ।।6.91.95।।
output: Then Vanaras wagging their tails and lashing them announced slogans saying," Lakshmana is winning."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
अन्योन्यं च समालशिष्यहरयोहृष्टमानसाः । चक्रुरुच्चावगुणाराघवाश्रयसजा: कथा: ।।6.91.96।।
output: The monkeys feeling very happy embraced one another singing in praise of Lakshmana saying" Lakshmana has won"and stories related to Lakshmana

output: रुधिरक्लिन्नगात्रः body smeared with blood, शुभलक्षणः auspicious marks, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, आहवे in battle, तम् him, शक्रजेतारम् one who won Indra, हत्वा killing, हृष्टः joyful, बभूव experienced

output: Then Valiant and mighty Lakshmana called Jambavantha, Hanumantha, all the Vanaras, following Vibheeshana and Hanuman quickly reached Sugriva and Raghava.

instruction:

output: तदा then, वीरः heroic, आगत्य coming close, महात्मने great soul, राघवाय to Raghava, निष्टनन्निव being tired in, इन्द्रजितःIndrajith, घोरम् terrific, वधम् killed, आचचक्षे reported

instruction:

output: Then Vibheeshana gladly informed Rama that Ravana's son's head had been severed by great Lakshmana.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 92:
श्रुत्वैवतुमहावीर्योलक्षणनेन्द्रजिद्वधम् । प्रहर्षमतुलंलेभेवाक्यंचेदमुवाच ह ।।6.92.7।।
output: As soon as Lakshmana said that Indrajith was killed, Rama was very glad and immediately spoke as follows.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 92:
साधुलक्ष्मणतुष्टोऽस्मिकर्मचासुकरंकृतम् । रावणेर्हिविनाशेनजितमुत्यपधारय ।।6.92.8।।
output: "Well done, Lakshmana! I am glad. A difficult deed has been done. By the fall of Indrajith success has been achieved."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 92:
स तंशिरस्युपाघ्रायलक्ष्मणंकीर्तिवर्धनम् । लज्जमानंबलात्स्नेहादङ्गमारोप्यवीर्यवान् ।।6.92.9।। उपवेश्यतमुत्सङ्गेपरिष्वज्यावपीडितम् । भ्रातरंलक्ष्मणंस्निग्धंपुनःपुनरुदैक्षत ।।6.92.10।।
output: Bending the head of Lakshmana, a valiant one and enhancer of glory, who was shy of praising him, Rama lovingly, forcibly drawing him onto his lap and making him sit on examined again and again the wounded body and looked at him.

instruction:

output: Bending the head of Lakshmana, a valiant one and enhancer of glory, who was shy of praising him, Rama lovingly, forcibly drawing him onto his lap and making him sit on examined again and again the wounded body and looked at him.

instruction:

शल्यसंपीडितंशस्तंनिःश्वसन्तंतुंलक्ष्मणम् । रामस्तुदुःखसन्तप्तंतंतुनिःश्वासपीडितम् ।।6.92.11।। मूर्ध्निचैनमुपाघ्रायभूयःसंस्पृश्य च त्वरन् । उवाचलक्ष्मणंवाक्यमाश्वास्यपुरुषर्षभः ।।6.92.12।।
output: Lakshmana, a bull among men, body tormented by arrows, immersed in pain, breathing heavily. Rama stroking him, restoring his confidence, quickly spoke as follows.

instruction:

output: Lakshmana, a bull among men, body tormented by arrows, immersed in pain, breathing heavily. Rama stroking him, restoring his confidence, quickly spoke as follows.

output: दुष्करकर्मणा one who does What is difficult for others, परमकळ्याणम् deed which is extremely auspicious (beneficial), कर्म action, कृतम् done, अद्य now, पुत्रे son, हते killed, युधि in battle, रावणम् Ravana, निहतम् also killed, मन्ये think

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 92:
अद्याहंविजयीशत्रौहतेतस्मिन् दुरात्मनि । रावणस्यनृशंसस्यदिष्ट्यावीरत्वयारणे ।।6.92.14।। छिन्नोहिदक्षिणोबाहुः स हितस्यव्यपाश्रयः । विभीषणहनूमद्भ्यांकृतंकर्ममहद्रणे ।।6.92.15।।
output: 'Ravana was depending on Indrajith indeed. Now by that a great action of severing his right hand in comb at by Vibheeshana and Hanuman, I consider victorious.'

instruction:

output: 'Ravana was depending on Indrajith indeed. Now by that a great action of severing his right hand in comb at by Vibheeshana and Hanuman, I consider victorious.'

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 92:
अहोरात्रैस्त्रिभिर्वीरःकथञ्चितवन्दिपातितः । विरमित्रःकृतोऽस्म्यद्यनिर्यास्यतिहिरावणः ।।6.92.16।। बलव्यूहेनमहताश्रुत्वापुत्त्रंनिपातितम् ।
output: 'Hero! In three days and nights indeed, you have made short of Indrajith. Hearing that Ravana's son has been made short of, Ravana will come now with large army troops.'

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तंपुत्रवधसन्तप्तंनिर्यान्तंराक्षसाधिपम् ।।6.92.17।। बलेनावृत्यमहतानिहनिष्यामिदुर्जयम् ।
output: 'On hearing of his son's death, the Rakshasa Lord will come forth with a huge army. Turning towards him I will put an end to him.'

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
त्वयालक्ष्मणनाथेनसीता च पृथिवी च मे ।।6.92.18।। न दुष्प्रापाहतेतस्मिन् शक्रजेतरिचाहवे ।
output: Lakshmana, with you as my protector and Indra's enemy killed, neither Sita nor earth will be difficult to get back.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सतंभ्रातरमाश्वास्यपरिष्वज्य च राघवः ।।6.92.19।। रामःसुषेणंमुदितस्समाभाष्येदमब्रवीत् ।
output: Rama, the celebrated scion of Raghu dynasty, restored the confidence of Lakshmana and embraced him happily. He invited Sushena and spoke as follows.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
सशल्योऽयंमहाप्राज्ञस्सौमित्रिर्मित्रवत्सलः ।।6.92.20।। यथाभवतिसुस्वस्थस्तथात्वंसमुपाचर ।
output: "O very wise Sushena! Treat Saumithri in such a way that this Lakshmana, loved by friends pained by the arrows pierced, will be relieved."

instruction:

विशल्यःक्रियतांक्षिप्रंसौमित्रिस्सविभीषणः ।।6.92.21।। ऋक्ष्वानरसैन्यानांशूराणांद्रुमयोधिनाम् । येचाप्यन्येऽत्रयुध्यन्तिसशल्याव्रणिनस्तथा ।।6.92.22।। तेऽपिसर्वेप्रयत्नेनक्रियन्तांसुखिनस्तथा ।
output: सविभीषणः that Vibheeshana, सौमित्रिः Saumithri, क्षिप्रम् quickly, विशल्यः, क्रियताम् be treated, ऋक्ष्वानरसैन्यानाम् army of Bears, द्रुमयोधिनाम् who fight with trees, शूराणाम् heroes, ये च they also, अन्ये others, अत्र there, युध्यन्ति in the battle, सशल्याः the arrows, तथा so also, व्रणिनः wounds, तेसर्वेऽपि of all also, तथा so also, प्रयत्नेन by effort, सुखिनः make happy, क्रियन्ताम् healed

instruction:

विशल्यःक्रियतांक्षिप्रंसौमित्रिस्सविभीषणः ।।6.92.21।। ऋक्ष्वानरसैन्यानांशूराणांद्रुमयोधिनाम् । येचाप्यन्येऽत्रयुध्यन्तिसशल्याव्रणिनस्तथा ।।6.92.22।। तेऽपिसर्वेप्रयत्नेनक्रियन्तांसुखिनस्तथा ।
output: "Let Vibheeshana and Saumithri be treated quickly. Let all the army of Bears and others who fought with trees, and the heroes be treated. Let all others who fought in the battlefield and wounded be also healed by your effort and make them happy."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
एवमुक्तस्तुरामेणमहात्माहरियूथपः ।।6.92.23।। लक्ष्मणायदरौनस्तस्सुषेणःपरमौषधम् ।
output: Spoken by Rama in that manner, the great Vanara leader, Sushena gave supreme medicine to Lakshman through his nose.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स तस्यगन्धमाघ्रायविशल्यस्समपद्यत ।।6.92.24।। तदानिर्वेदनश्चैवसंरूढव्रणएव च ।
output: सः he, तदा then, तस्य his, गन्धम् fragrance, आघ्राय breathing in, विशल्यः, निर्वेदनश्चैव freed from arrows, संरूढव्रणएव च rid of pain from wounds, समपद्यत restored to normal state

instruction:

output: तदा then, राघवाज्ञज्नाया by Rama's order, विभीषणमुखानाम् Vibheeshana and other leaders, सुहृदाम् friends, सर्ववानरमुख्यानाम् all Vanara leaders, चिकित्साम् having treated, अकरोत् performed

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 92:
ततःप्रकृतिमापन्नोहृतशल्योगतव्यथ: ।।6.92.26।। सौमित्रिर्मुदितस्तत्र क्षणेन विगतज्वरः ।
output: Then Saumithri, freed from arrows, relieved from pain, anguish gone in a moment, and naturally restored, was happy.

instruction:

output: At that time, Rama, also the monkey leader, and Vibheeshana, Jambavan with their army seeing Lakshmana getting up, free from wounds were full of joy.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:

output: ततः then, पौलस्त्यसचिवाः ministers of Paulastya (Ravana of Paulastya dynasty), इन्द्रजितःIndrajith, वधम् killed, श्रुत्वा hearing, सव्यथा: distressing, अभिज्ञाय having known, दशग्रीवाय to tenheaded Ravana, आचचक्षुः reported

instruction:

युद्धेहतोमहाराजलक्ष्मणेनतवात्मजः । विभीषणसहायेनमिषतांनोमहाद्युतिः ।।6.93.2।।
output: "O King! Your glorious son was killed by Lakshmana with the assistance of Vibheeshana, as we were witnessing."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 93:
शूरंशूरेणसम्गम्यसम्युगेष्वपराजितः । लक्ष्मणेनहतश्शूरःपुत्रस्तेमहेन्द्रजित् ।।6.93.3।। गतस्सपरमान्लोकान्शरैस्सन्ताप्यलक्ष्मणम् ।
output: "Your son who has never been defeated in war, who won Indra, the ruler of gods, after fighting and fighting was killed by Lakshmana's arrows. He has ascended to the higher world."

instruction:

instruction:

output: हा ha, राक्षसचमूमुख्य Rakshasa army chief, ममवत्स my son, महाबल might, इन्द्रम् Indra, जित्वा had won, त्वम् such, अद्य now, कथम् how, लक्ष्मणस्य Lakshmana's, वशंगतः was a victim

instruction:

output: 'When angry, you could pierce with arrows even the time spirit or peak of Mandara mountain, why to speak of Lakshmana again'?

instruction:

output: महाबाहो mightyarmed, येन by this, अद्य today, त्वम् you, कालधर्मणा by virtue of Time, संयुक्तः joining, वैवस्वतः Yama, राजा king, मम my, अद्य today, भूयः become, बहुमतः esteemed

output: सर्वामरगणेष्वपि noble warriors, सुयोधानाम् path trodden, एषःin that way, पन्थाः path, यः that which, भर्तुःकृते for the king, हन्यते is killed, सःपुमान् man, स्वर्गम् heaven, ऋच्छति attains

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 93:
अद्यदेवगणास्सर्वेलोकपालामहर्षयः ।।6.93.10।। हतमिन्द्रजितंदृष्टवासुखंस्वप्स्यन्तिनिर्भयाः ।
output: 'Today, seeing Indrajith killed, Devatas in heaven, guardians of the worlds, great sages would be fearless and be happy and comfortable'.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 93:

output: Today without Indrajith alone the three worlds (earth, heaven, and underworld) including forests are desolate, dark, and lustreless to me.

instruction:

output: 'Today in the gynaecium we will hear the cries of Rakshasa maidens like the roaring of elephants in the cave'.

instruction:

output: परन्तप scourge of enemies, यौवराज्यं च prince regent, लङ्कां च from Lanka, रक्षांसि च Rakshasas of Lanka, मातरम् mother, मां च me also, भार्याश्च wife also, नःविहाय left, क्व why, गतःwent असि you

instruction:

output: 'O hero! My obsequies should have been done by you. It is peculiar that I have to perform'.

instruction:

output: सःत्वम् you, सुग्रीवे Sugriva, जीवति living, लक्ष्मणेन Lakshmana, राघवे Raghava, मम me, शल्यम् arrow, अनुद्धृत्य deserting, नः not, विहाय doing, क्व where, गतःअसि have you gone

output: Distressed Ravana was lamenting in this way on account of his son deserting, as anger had taken over him.

instruction:

output: By nature, he is angry. Now with the loss of his son, he was glowing like the Sun that shines brighter by the rays in summer.

instruction:

instruction:

output: As Ravana yawned in anger, fire with smoke burst forth from his mouth like Vrtra'.

instruction:

instruction:

तस्यप्रकृत्यारक्ते च रक्तेक्रोथानगिनापि च ।।6.93.21।। रावणस्यमहाघोरेदीप्तेनेत्रेबभूवतुः ।
output: By nature, Ravana's eyes are red, through the fire of anger it was even more red glowing and very dreadful.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
घोरंप्रकृत्यारूपंतत्तस्यक्रोधाग्निमूर्छितम् ।।6.93.22।। बभूवरूपंक्रुद्धस्यरुद्रस्येवदुरासदम् ।
output: His eyes are naturally dreadful, deluded with fire of anger his form was like Rudra's and threatening.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 93:
तस्यक्रुद्धस्यनेत्राभ्यांप्रापतन्नाश्रृबिन्दवः ।।6.93.23।। दीपाभ्यामिवदीप्ताभ्यांसार्चिषस्स्नेहबिन्दवः ।
output: Just as drops of oil drop from flaming lamps, tears dropped from his enraged flaming eyes.

instruction:

output: When he was biting on his teeth (enraged), the sound from his teeth resembled the sound of a grinder revolved round by Danavas.

instruction:

output: The Rakshasas could not go near Ravana who was moving in anger in all directions like the moving and unmoving creations move when chased by the god of death.

instruction:

output: ततः then, परमसङ्क्रुद्धः very angry, राक्षसाधिपः Rakshasa king, रावणः Ravana, आहवे battle, संस्तंभयिषुः provoke, रक्षसाम् Rakshasas, मध्ये midst, अब्रवीत् spoke

instruction:

मयावर्षसहस्राणिचरित्वापरमंतपः ।।6.93.28।। तेषुतेष्ववकाशेषुस्वयम्भूःपरितोषितः ।
output: 'I have done penance for thousands of years several times and am a pleased selfborn creator'.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तस्यैवतपसोव्युष्ट्याप्रसादाच्छस्वयम्भुवः ।।6.93.29।। नासुरेभ्यो न देवेभ्योभयंममकदाचन ।
output: 'By the power of the penancedone by me once, creator Brahma has given me reward, pleased with my penance. I have no fear of Asuras or Devas'.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
कवचंब्रह्मदत्तंमेयदादित्यसमप्रभम् ।।6.93.30।। देवासुरविमर्धेषु न भिन्नंवज्रमुष्टिभिः ।
output: 'I was given a shield by Brahma, effulgent like the Sun which the Devas or Danavas could not break with their thunderbolt fists'.

instruction:

output: 'Today if I, with that shield mounted the chariot go for battle, who can dare to withstand me openly? Even Indra can't'.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 93:
त्तदातिप्रसन्नेनसशरंकार्मुकंमहत् ।।6.93.32।। देवासुरविमर्धेषुममदत्तंस्वयम्भुवा । अद्यतूर्यशतैर्भीमंधनुरुत्थाप्यतांमम ।।6.93.33।। रामलक्ष्मणयोरेववधायपरमाहवे ।
output: 'Let that supreme bow and the great arrows bestowed to me, by Brahma the creator who was pleased, when I fought in battle between Devas and Asuras, be brought to destroy Rama and Lakshmana today accompanied by hundreds of trumpets.'

instruction:

output: 'Let that supreme bow and the great arrows bestowed to me, by Brahma the creator who was pleased, when I fought in battle between Devas and Asuras, be brought to destroy Rama and Lakshmana today accompanied by hundreds of trumpets.'

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 93:
स पुत्रवधसन्तप्तःक्रूरःक्रोधवशंगतः ।।6.93.34।। समीक्ष्यरावणोबुद्ध्यासीतांहन्तुंव्यवस्यत ।
output: Feeling very sad about the death of his son, cruel Ravana overpowered by anger went thinking to destroy Sita.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 93:

output: Redeyed Ravana, looking dreadful with a frightening face, desperate, spoke in a low voice to all Rakshasas as follows.

instruction:

output: 'My son showed the Vanaras there something which had been killed there to hoodwink as Sita."

instruction:

output: "I myself will rejoice now in the same way (as Indarjith had done for cheating) making it true. I will destroy that lowly kshatriya, Rama's very dear Vaidehi". Having spoken like that to the ministers he took up the sword."

instruction:

output: In a totally confused state on account of the death of his son, he went to Mythili taking the excellent sword, which was shining resembling pure sky, feeling enraged, accompanied by his wife, and surrounded by the ministers.

instruction:

output: व्रजन्तम् in the abode, राक्षसम् Rakshasas, प्रेक्ष्य observing, सिंहनादम् lion roar, विचुक्रुशुः emitted,, संक्रुद्धम् very furious, राक्षसम् Rakshasa, प्रेक्ष्य seeing, अन्योन्यम् one another, आलिङ्ग्य embracing, ऊचुश्च spoke to one another

instruction:

output: "Seeing Ravana, the two brothers will tremble. By Ravana's fury all the four rulers of the world (Indra, Yama, Varuna, Kubera), would have disappeared. He has struck down many other enemies in wars."

output: Just as created beings experience their senses and do not perceive their soul, the army experienced the hitting of Raghava by their senses but were not able to perceive him who was hitting them.

Rama was seen as a wheel of time spirit by the people.

output: Rakshasa women lament over the death of Rakshasas in war.

Thousands of warriors sent by king Ravana, mounted on chariots, yoked to horses, of the colour of fire, thousands of warriors who could wage with iron bars, decked in gold, mounted on colourful chariots of golden colour pictures and Rakshasas who can change their form at will, were destroyed by Sri Rama."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 95:
दृष्टवाश्रुत्वा च सम्भ्रान्ताहतशेषानिशाचराः । राक्षसीश्चसमागम्यदीनाश्चिन्तापरिप्लुताः ।।6.95.4।। विधवाहतपुत्राश्चक्रोशन्त्योहतबान्दवाः । राक्षस्यःसहसङ्गम्यदुःखार्ताःपर्यदेवयन् ।।6.95.5।।
output: "On seeing and hearing of the others left over, the night rangers felt bewildered and piteous with agony coming together, moving in groups, those who lost husband, son, kin and protectors along with associates crying, stricken with grief."

output: "On seeing and hearing of the others left over, the night rangers felt bewildered and piteous with agony coming together, moving in groups, those who lost husband, son, kin and protectors along with associates crying, stricken with grief."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 95:
कथंशूर्पणखावृद्धाकरालानिर्णतोदरी । आससादवनेरामंकन्दर्पमिवरूपिणम् ।।6.95.6।।
output: "How did that old, dreadful and hideous Surpanakha approach Rama, whose form is charming like the god of love, in the forest?"

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 95:
सुकुमारंमहासत्त्वंसर्वभूतहितेरतम् । तंदृष्टवालोकनिन्द्यासाहीनरूपाप्रकामिता ।।6.95.7।।
output: "That woman of ugly appearance deserves to be killed. How is it that she was stung with love with that delicate Rama, a well wisher of all beings?"

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 95:
कथंसर्वगुणैर्हीनागुणवन्तंमहौजसम् । सुमुखंदुर्मुखीरामंकामयामासराक्षसी ।।6.95.8।।
output: "How did that rakshasi of terrible appearance dare to love that virtuous Rama?"

instruction:

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तन्निमित्तमिदंवैरंरावणेनकृतंमहत् । वधायसीतासासीतादशग्रीवेणरक्षसा ।।6.95.11।।
output: "For that reason of Surpanakha, this enmity has been conceived by Ravana and Sita was borne away by the ten headed Rakshasa."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 95:
न च सीतांदशग्रीवःप्राप्नोतिजनकात्मजाम् । बद्धंबलवतावैरमक्षयंराघवेण च ।।6.95.12।।
output: "Hope the ten headed Ravana will not touch Sita forcibly, by which undying enmity has been contracted already."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
वैदेहींप्रार्थयानंतंविराधंप्रेक्षयराक्षसम् । हतमेकेनरामेणपर्याप्तंतन्निदर्शनम् ।।6.95.13।।
output: "On perceiving that Viradha solicitous of Vaidehi, the Rakshasa was killed by Rama with one arrow. That is sufficient proof (of Rama's valour)."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 95:
चतुर्धशसहस्राणिरक्षसांभीमकर्मणाम् । निहतानिजनस्थानेशरैरग्निशिखोपमैः ।।6.95.14।।
output: " At Janasthana fourteen thousand Rakshasas have been destroyed with his arrows like peaks of fire."

instruction:

खरश्चनिहतःसङ्ख्येदूषणस्त्रिशिरास्तथा । शरैरादितसङ्काशैःपर्याप्तंतन्निदर्शनम् ।।6.95.15।।
output: सङ्ख्ये in combat, आदित्यसङ्काशैःsun like, शरैः arrows, खरश्च Khara, निहतः killed, दूषणः Dooshana, तथा so also, त्रिशिराः Trisira, तत् that, पर्याप्तम् example, निदर्शनम् sufficient proof

instruction:

हतोयोजनबाहुश्चकबन्दोरुदिराशनः । क्रोधान्नादंनदन् सोऽथपर्याप्तंतन्निदर्शनम् ।।6.95.16।।
output: "Kabhanda who lived on blood came roaring, enraged, whose arms were eight meters long was also killed and that is a sufficient example."

instruction:

जघानबलिनंरामस्सहस्रनयनात्मजम् । वालिनंमेरुसङ्काशंपर्याप्तंतन्निदर्शनम् ।।6.95.17।।
output: रामः Rama, बलिनम्mighty, सहस्रनयनात्मजम् son of thousand eyed Indra, मेरुसङ्काशम् resembled mountain Meru, वालिनम् Vali, जघान killed, तत् that, पर्याप्तम् sufficient, निदर्शनम् example

output: ऋष्यमूके Rishyamukha, वसन् living, दीनःdejected, भग्नमनोरथः disconsolate, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, राज्यम् kingdom, प्रापितः restored, तत् his, पर्याप्तम् sufficient, निदर्शनम् example

instruction:

धर्मार्थसहितंवाक्यंसर्वेषांरक्षसांहितम् । युक्तंविभीषणेनोक्तंमोहत्तस्य न रोचते ।।6.95.19।।
output: "Good advice given by Vibheeshana in accordance with righteousness was not liked by him in delusion."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
विभीषणवचःकुर्याद्यदिस्मधनदानुजः । श्मशानभूतादुःखार्तानेयंलङ्काभविष्यति ।।6.95.20।।
output: धनदानुजः younger brother of Kubera, विभीषणवचः Vibheeshana's words, कुर्यात् स्मयदि had followed, इयम् this, लङ्का Lanka, श्मशानभूता crematorium, दुःखार्ता stricken with grief, न भविष्यति would not have become

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 95:
कुम्भकर्णंहतंश्रुत्वाराघवेणमहाबलम् । अतिकायं च दुर्मर्षंलक्ष्मणेनहतंतदा ।।6.95.21।। प्रियंचेन्द्रजितंपुत्रंरावणोनावबुध्यते ।
output: "Kumbhakarna of extraordinary strength having been killed by Raghava, and even on hearing that Atikaya who is difficult to disregard, and Indrajith, dear son killed by Lakshmana also, Ravana has not realised."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ममपुत्रोममभ्राताममभर्तारणेहतः ।।6.95.22।। इत्येषश्रूयतेशब्दोराक्षसीनांकुलेकुले ।
output: "My son is killed, my brother is killed, my husband is killed," was the sound heard from every family.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 95:
रथश्चाश्वाश्चनागाश्चहताःशतसहस्रशः ।।6.95.23।। रणेरामेणशूरेणहताश्चापिपदातयः ।
output: "Horses, elephants, warriors, even foot soldiers were killed, chariots were destroyed, and hundreds and thousands struck down in war by Rama."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
रुद्रोवायदिवाविष्णुर्महेन्द्रोवाशतक्रतुः ।।6.95.24।। हन्तिनोरामरूपेणयदिवास्वयमन्तकः ।
output: रुद्रोवा by Rudra, यदिवा is it, विष्णुः Lord Vishnu, शतक्रतुः who has done a hundred sacrifices, महेन्द्रोवा by Mahendra, यदिवा is it, स्वयम् himself, अन्तकः god of death, रामरूपेण in the form of Rama, नः is it, हन्ति killing

instruction:

हतप्रवीरारामेणनिराशाजीवितेवयम् ।।6.95.25।। अपश्य्नत्योभयस्यान्तमनाथाविलपामहे ।
output: रामेण by Rama, हतप्रवीराः eminent heroes, वयम् we, जीविते life, निराशाः lost, भयस्य with fear, अन्तम् end, अपश्यन्तः not able to see, अनाथाः orphans, विलपामहे weeping

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 95:
रामहस्ताद्धशग्रीवश्शूरोदत्तमहावरः ।।6.95.26।। इदंभयंमहाघोरंसमुत्पन्नं न बुध्यते ।
output: "Graced with the boon of arrows the tenheaded Ravana has not realised the appalling danger to him from Rama."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तं न देवा न गन्धर्वा न पिशाचा न राक्षसाः ।।6.95.27।। उपसृष्टंपरित्रातुंशक्तारामेणसम्युगे ।
output: "Neither gods nor Gandharvas, not even fiends will be able to protect, struck by Rama in war."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
त्पताश्चापिदृश्यन्तेरावणस्यरणेरणे ।।6.95.28।। कथयन्तिहिरामेणरावणस्यनिबर्हणम् ।
output: "In every war evil portents are noticed rising up, of Rama destroying Ravana. How much more to say?"

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
पितामहेनप्रीतेनदेवदानवराक्षसैः ।।6.95.29।। रावणस्याभयंदत्तंमनुष्येभ्यो न याचितम् ।
output: प्रीतेन lovingly, पितामहेन by Brahma, रावणस्य Ravana's, देवदानवराक्षसैः Devas Danavas and Rakshasas, अभयम् protection, दत्तम् provided, मनुष्येभ्यःfrom humans, न याचितम् not sought

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तदिदंमानुषंमन्येप्राप्तंनिःसंशयंभयम् ।।6.95.30।। जीवितान्तकंघोरंरक्षसांरावणस्य च ।
output: "Fearlessness of death from human beings attained by Ravana in this way was no doubt terrific to Rakshasas and Ravana."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
पीड्यमानास्तुबलिनावरदानेनरक्षसा ।।6.95.31।। दीप्स्सैस्तपोभिर्विबुधाःपितामहमपूजयन् ।
output: "Tormented by the oppression of Ravana, on account of the boon (given to him by the creator) and intensity of his austerities, the learned worshipped Brahma."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 95:
देवतानांहितार्थायमहात्मावैपितामहः ।।6.95.32।। उवाचदेवताःसर्वाइदंतुष्टोमहद्वचः ।
output: "Gratified by the worship of Devatas, wishing them good, Brahma spoke these words."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 95:
अद्यप्रभृतिलोकांस्त्रीन् सर्वेदानवराक्षसाः ।।6.95.33।। भयेनप्रावृतानित्यंविचरिष्यन्तिशाश्वतम् ।
output: "From now ,all Danavas and Rakshasas will range the three worlds every day permanently in fear."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
दैवतैस्तुसमागम्यसर्वैश्चेन्द्रपुरोगमैः ।।6.95.34।। वृषध्वजस्त्रिपुरहामहादेवःप्रसादितः ।
output: इन्द्रपुरोगमैः marching towards Indra, सर्वैः all, दैवतैः Devatas, समागम्य getting together, वृषध्वजः device of bull, त्रिपुरहा Tripura, महादेवः Lord MahaDeva, प्रसादितःpropitiated

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 95:
प्रसन्नस्तुमहादेवोदेवानेतद्वचोऽब्रवीत् ।।6.95.35।। उत्पत्स्यतिहितार्थंवोनारीरक्षःक्षयावहा ।
output: MahaDeva was pleased by the Devatas and spoke these words for their benefit," a woman will be born for the destruction of Rakshasas."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 95:
एषादेवैःप्रयुक्तातुक्षुद्यथादानवान् पुरा ।।6.95.36।। भक्षयिष्यतिनःसीताराक्षसघ्नीसरावणान् ।
output: "Just as hunger consumed Danavas earlier, this woman, instigated (by Devatas) will consume all Rakshasas and Ravana."

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
रावणस्यापनीतेनदुर्विनीतस्यदुर्मतेः ।।6.95.37।। अयंनिष्टानकोघोरंशोकेनसमभिप्लुतः ।
output: दुर्विनीतस्य misconduct, दुर्मतेः evil minded, रावणस्य Ravana's, अपनीतेन immoral action, शोकेन in grief, समभिप्लुतः attended by, घोरः terrific, अयम् us, निष्टानकः stares at us

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 95:
तंन पश्यामहेलोकेयोनःशरणदोभवेत् ।।6.95.38।। राघवेणोपसृष्टानां कालेनेव युगक्षये ।
output: "Threatened like this by Raghava, we cannot perceive anyone in this world who can protect us now. Just as beings are threatened by the time spirit at the end of the destruction of this world, we are threatened."

महेन्द्राशनिकल्पेनतलेनाभिहतःक्षितौ ।।6.97.31।। पपातरुधिरक्लिन्नश्शोणितंसमुद्यमन् । स्रोतोभ्यस्तुविरूपाक्षोजलंप्रस्रवणादिव ।।6.97.32।।
output: Hurt by the palm which resembled Indra's weapon, blood started flowing from Virupaksha's body just like water flowed from waterfalls. Bathed in blood, vomiting blood, Virupaksha fell on the ground.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
महेन्द्राशनिकल्पेनतलेनाभिहतःक्षितौ ।।6.97.31।। पपातरुधिरक्लिन्नश्शोणितंसमुद्यमन् । स्रोतोभ्यस्तुविरूपाक्षोजलंप्रस्रवणादिव ।।6.97.32।।
output: महेन्द्राशनिकल्पेन resembling Indra's weapon, तलेन by that palm, अभिहतः hurt, विरूपाक्षःVirupaksha, प्रस्रवणात् flowing from water falls, जलमिव like water, स्रोतोभ्यः from the body, बहु much, शोणितम् blood, समुगदिरन् vomiting, रुधिरक्लिन्नःbathed in blood, क्षितौ on the ground, पपात fell

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
विवृत्तनयनंक्रोधात्सफेनंरुधिराप्लुतम् । ददृशुस्तेविरूपाक्षंविरूपाक्षतरंकृतम् ।।6.97.33।।
output: The Vanaras witnessed Virupaksha who had misshapen eyes, turning his eyeballs in anger, foaming blood flowing from nostrils.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स्फुरन्तंपरिवर्तन्तंपार्श्वेनरुधिरोक्षितम् । करुणं च विनर्दन्तंददृशुःकपयोरिपुम् ।।6.97.34।।
output: कपयः monkeys, स्फुरन्तम् rolling by, पार्श्वेन sides, परिवर्तनम् changing sides, रुधिरोक्षितम् bathed in blood, करुणम् compassion, विनर्दन्तम् causing sorrow, रिपुम् enemy, ददृशुः witnessed,

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 97:
तथातुतौसंम्यतिसम्प्रयुक्तौ । तरस्विनौवानरराक्षसानाम् ।।6.97.35।।
output: Thus, both close to each other, both redoubtable armies, of Vanaras and Rakshasas, both powerful and terrific, both mighty, roared as if the great ocean had burst.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
हन्यमानेबलेतूर्णमन्योन्यंतेमहामृथे । सरसीवमहाघर्मेसोपक्षीणेबभूवतुः ।।6.98.1।।
output: Major conflict between Sugriva and Mahodara, minister of Ravana. Death of Mahodara in the hands of Sugriva.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
स्वबलस्यविघातेनविरूपाक्ष्वधेन च । बभूवद्विगुणंक्रुद्धोरावणोराक्षसाधिपः ।।6.98.2।।
output: राक्षसाधिपः Lord of Rakshasas, रावणः Ravana, स्वबलस्य his army, घातेन destruction, विरूपाक्ष्वधेन च fall of Virupaksha, द्विगुणम् doubly, क्रुद्धः angry, बभूव became

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
प्रक्षीणंतुबलंदृष्टवावध्यमानंवलीमुखैः । बभूवास्यव्यथायुद्धेप्रेक्ष्यदैवविपर्ययम् ।।6.98.3।।
output: Rakshasa's army was killed by Vanaras and drastically reduced. Seeing the adversary of God's grace, Ravana was agonized on witnessing it.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
उवाच च समीपस्थंमहोदरमरिन्दमम् । अस्मिन्कालेमहाबाहोजयाशात्वयिमेस्थिता ।।6.98.4।।
output: And then Ravana spoke to Mahodara who was close by, one who is difficult to encounter, saying " At this time the hope for my victory is centered in you."

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
जहिशत्रुचमूंवीरदर्शयाद्यपराक्रमम् । भर्तृपिण्डस्यकालोऽऽयंनिर्देष्टुंसाधुयुध्यताम् ।।6.98.5।।
output: "O heroic Mahodara! Today, exhibit your valour by destroying the enemy army. Having received my subsistence, this is the time to repay. Fight well in war."

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
एवमुक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वाराक्षसेन्द्रोमहोदरः । प्रविवेशारिसेनांतांपतङ्गइवपावकम् ।।6.98.6।।
output: Having spoken like that by the king of Rakshasas, Mahodara entered the army of the enemy like a moth enters fire.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
ततस्सकदनंचक्रेवानराणांमहाबलः । भर्तृवाक्येनतेजस्वीस्वेनवीर्येणचोदितः ।।6.98.7।।
output: Thereafter, the mighty and brilliant Mahodara, in obedience to the word of the king, inspired by his own valour, went to fight with Vanaras.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
वानराश्चमहासत्त्वाःप्रगृह्वःविपुलाशशिलाः । प्रविश्यारिबलंभीमंजघ्नुस्तेरजनीचरान् ।।6.98.8।।
output: The mighty Vanaras also seizing huge rocks entered into the frightening enemy army of the Rakshasas.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
महोदरस्तुसङ्कृद्धश्शरैःकाञ्चनभूषणैः । चिच्छेदपाणिपादोरुन्वानराणांमहाहवे ।।6.98.9।।
output: महाहवे great war, सुसङ्कृद्धः highly enraged, महोदरः Mahodara, काञ्चनभूषणैःdecked with gold शरैः arrows, वानराणाम् Vanaras, पाणिपादोरु hands legs and thighs, चिच्छेद shattered

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
ततस्तेवानरास्सर्वेराक्षसैरर्दिताभृशम् । दिशोदशद्रुताःकेचित्केचित्सुग्रीवमाश्रिताः ।।6.98.10।।
output: Thereafter, unable to bear the pain, those Vanaras hit by Rakshasas, went in ten directions and some went to Sugriva for refuge.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
प्रभग्नांसमरेदृष्टवावानराणांमहाचमूम् । अभिदुद्रावसुग्रीवोमहोदरमनन्तरम् ।।6.98.11।।
output: Seeing the great army of Vanaras defeated in the conflict, Sugriva rushed towards Mahodara.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
प्रगृह्यविपुलांघोरांमहीधरसमांशिलाम् । चिक्षेप स महातेजास्तद्वधायहरीश्वरः ।।6.98.12।।
output: Endowed with great energy, Sugriva, the monkey Lord, seizing a huge mountain like dreadful rock, hurled to kill Mahodara.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
तामापततनींसहसाशिलांदृष्टवामहोदरः । असम्भ्रान्तस्ततोबाणैर्निर्बिभेददुरासदाम् ।।6.98.13।।
output: ततः then, महोदरःMahodara, सहसा immediately, आपतन्तीम् coming towards him, दुरासदाम् difficult to break, तांशिलाम् that rock, दृष्टवा seeing, असम्भ्रान्तः not bewildered, बाणैः arrows, निर्बिभेद struck and broke

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
रक्षसातेनबाणौघैर्निकृत्तासासहस्रधा । निपपातशिलाभूमौगृध्रचक्रमिवाकुलम् ।।6.98.14।।
output: That rock, struck by Mahodara fell on the ground shattered and broken into a thousand pieces.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तांतुभिन्नांशिलांदृष्टवासुग्रीवःक्रोधमूर्छितः । सालमुत्पाट्यचिक्षेपराक्षसेरणमूर्थनि ।।6.98.15।।
output: Seeing the fragmented rock, Sugriva was deluded with anger, and tearing up a sala tree, he shattered on the Rakshasa (Mahodara) in the battlefield.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
शरैश्चविददारैनंशूरःपरपुरञ्जयः । स ददर्शततःक्रुद्धःपरिघंपतितंभुवि ।।6.98.16।।
output: Mahodara, a scourge of enemy forces, who lacerated Sugriva in that manner, angry, made the tree fall on the ground.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
आविध्यतु स तंदीप्तंपरिघंतस्यदर्शयन् । परिघाग्रेणवेगेनजघानास्यहयोत्तमान् ।6.98.17।।
output: Sugriva, picking up that glowing iron bar, exhibiting its top, whirling it around, struck the best of horses of Mahodara.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
तस्माद्धतहयावदीरःसोऽऽवप्लुत्यमहारथात् । गदांजग्राहसंक्रुद्धोराक्षसोऽऽथमहोदरः ।।6.98.18।।
output: Then the hero, Mahodara, his horses destroyed, jumped from the great chariot, and took hold of a mace.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
गदापरिघहस्तौतौयुधिवीरौसमीयतुः । नर्दन्तौगोवृषप्रख्यौघनाविवसविद्युतौ ।।6.98.19।।
output: Both the heroes, Mahodara and Sugriva like two bulls holding mace and iron bar respectively, like clouds charged with lightning came roaring in the battlefield.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
ततःक्रुद्धोगदांतस्यैचिक्षेपरजनीचरः । ज्वलतनींभास्कराभासांसुग्रीवायमहोदरः ।।6.98.20।।
output: Then provoked by anger, the night ranger, Mahodara flung his mace at Sugriva which shone like the Sun.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
गदांतांसुमहाघोरामापततनींमहाबलः । सुग्रीवोरोषताम्राक्षस्समुद्यम्यमहाहवे ।।6.98.21।। आजघानगदांतस्यपरिघेणहरीश्वर । पपात स गदोद्भिन्नःपरिघस्तस्यभूतले ।।6.98.22।।
output: महाहवे terrible conflict, आपतन्तीम् falling, सुमहाघोराम् very dreadful, तांगदाम् that mace, महाबलः mighty, रोषताम्राक्षः eyes turned red in anger, हरीश्वरः Lord of monkeys, सुग्रीवःSugriva, समुद्यम्य struck, तस्य his, गदाम् mace, आजघान hit, गदोद्भिन्नः mace broken into pieces, तस्य his, परिघःiron bar, भूतले on the ground, पपात fell.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
गदांतांसुमहाघोरामापततनींमहाबलः । सुग्रीवोरोषताम्राक्षस्समुद्यम्यमहाहवे ।।6.98.21।। आजघानगदांतस्यपरिघेणहरीश्वर । पपात स गदोद्भिन्नःपरिघस्तस्यभूतले ।।6.98.22।।
output: In that terrible conflict, seeing the mace broken and falling, mighty Sugriva, whose eyes turned red in anger, lifted up his iron bar, struck at the mace of the Rakshasa. The mace fell on the ground and broke into pieces.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
ततोजग्राहतेजस्वीसुग्रीवोवसुधातलात् । आयसंमुसलंघोरंसर्वतोहेमभूषितम् ।।6.98.23।।
output: Then, energetic Sugriva picked from the ground a frightening steel club encrusted with gold on all sides.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
स तमुद्यम्यचिक्षेपसोऽऽप्यन्यांव्याक्षिपद्गदाम् । भिन्नावन्योन्यमासाद्यपेततुद्दरणीतले ।।6.98.24।।
output: Sugriva took up the steel club and hurled at Mahodara who took another mace and hit back. Both collided with each other and shattered they fell down on the surface of the earth.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
ततोग्नप्रहरणौमुष्टिभ्यांतौसमीयतुः । तेजोबलसमाविष्टौदीप्ताविवहुताशनौ ।।6.98.25।।
output: ततः thereafter, तेजोबलसमाविष्टौ fully endowed with strength, तौ both, भिन्नप्रहरणौ weapons broken, दीप्तौ glowing, हुताशनौइव like fire, मुष्टिभ्याम् with their fists, समीयतुः fought

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
जघ्नतुस्तौतदान्योन्यंवेदतुश्चपुनःपुनः । तलैश्चान्योन्यमहत्यपेततुश्चमहीतले ।।6.98.26।।
output: Then both of them again and again striking each other slapping with palms fell down and rolled on the ground.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
उत्पेततुस्ततस्तूर्णंजघ्नतुश्चपरस्परम् । भुजैश्चिक्षिपतुर्वीरावन्योन्यमपराजितौ ।।6.98.27।।
output: Then quickly getting up striking one another, both the heroes who have never been defeated, pushed each other by their arms.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
जग्मतुस्तौश्रमंवीरौबाहुयुधेपरंतपौ । अजहारतदाखडगमदूरपरिवर्तिनम् ।।6.98.28।। राक्षसश्चर्मणासार्धंमहावेगोमहोदरः ।
output: Both being scourge of their enemies, both heroes wrestling were exhausted with fighting. Then the Rakshasa picked up a sword lying not far from there along with a shield.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
थैव च महाखडगंचर्मणापतितंसह ।।6.98.29।। जग्राहवानरश्रेष्ठस्सुग्रीवोवेगवत्तरः।।
output: Likewise, Sugriva endowed with speed, a champion of Vanaras, took up a huge sword fallen down with a shield.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
तौतुरोषपरीताङ्गौनर्दन्तावभ्यधावताम् ।।6.98.30।। उद्यतासीरणेहृष्टावुभौशस्त्रविशारदौ ।
output: Then the two, whose limbs ceased, who were knowledgeable in the use of weapons, furious, sprang forward in the battle, both with joy, roaring to destroy one another.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
दक्षिणंमण्डलंचोभौसुतूर्णंसम्परीयतुः ।।6.98.31।। अन्योन्यमभिसङ्कृद्धौ जये प्रणिहितावुभौ ।
output: Enraged at one another, intent to win, both stretched forth at great speed, going from left to right in circles and encountered each other.

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
तुशूरोमहावेगोवीर्यश्लाघीमहोदरः ।।6.98.32।। महाचर्मणितंखडगंपातयामासदुर्मतिः ।
output: Mahodara, a warrior, evil minded one, endowed with great speed, hurled the sword on the shield of Sugriva.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
लग्नमुत्कर्षतःखडगंखडगेनकपिकुञ्जरः ।।6.98.33।। जहारसशिरस्त्राणंकुण्डलोपहितंशिरः ।
output: कपिकुञ्जरः elephant of the monkeys, लग्नम् struck to, खडगम् sword, उत्कर्षतःextracting, सशिरस्त्राणम् head with helmet, कुण्डलोपगतम् decked with earrings, शिरःhead, खडगेन sword, जहारsevered

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 98:
निकृत्तशिरसस्तस्यपतितस्यमहीतले ।।6.98.34।। तद्बलंराक्षसेन्द्रस्यदृष्टवातत्र न तिष्टते ।
output: Mahodara's head severed and fell on the ground. Seeing that Rakshasa king's army ran from there.

instruction:
Summarize the key idea behind this verse:
हत्वांतंवानरैस्सार्धंननादमुदितोहरिः ।।6.98.35।। चुक्रोध च दशग्रीवोबभौहृष्टश्चराघवः ।
output: Sugriva, the monkey leader having killed Mahodara, the Vanaras shouted in joy. The ten headed Ravana became enraged. Raghava was glad.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
विषण्णवदनास्सर्वेराक्षसादीनचेतसः ।।6.98.36।। विद्रवन्तिततस्सर्वेभयवित्रस्तचेतसः ।
output: सर्वे all, राक्षसाः Rakshasas, विषण्णवदनाः sad face, दीनचेतसः dull and piteous, सर्वे all, भयवित्रस्तचेतसः out of fear, ततः there, विद्रवन्ति ran

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
महोदरंतंन्वििपात्यभूमौमहागिरेःकीर्णमिवैकदेशम् । सूर्यात्मजस्तत्ररराजलक्ष्म्यसूर्यस्स्वतेजोभिरिवाप्रधृष्यः ।।6.98.37।।
output: सूर्यात्मजः son of sun god, महागिरेः great mountain, कीर्णम् thrown, एकदेशम् इव one part, तंमहोदरम् Mahodara, भूमौ on the ground, न्वििपात्य broken, अप्रधृष्यःunassailable, सूर्यः Sun, स्वतेजोभिरिव by his radiance, तत्र there, लक्ष्म Lakshmi, रराज shone

instruction:
Explain this verse from Yuddha Kanda, Sarga 99:
महोदरेतुनिहतेमहापार्श्वोमहाबलः । सुग्रीवेणसमीक्ष्याथक्रोधात्सम्ररक्तलोचनः ।।6.99.1।। अङ्गदस्यचमूंभीमांक्षोभयामाससायकैः ।
output: Gazing at Mahodara killed by Sugriva, mighty Mahaparsva's eyes turned red in anger. He created a commotion in the army of Angada.

instruction:
Translate this Sanskrit verse to English:
सवानराणांमुख्यानामुत्तमाङ्गानिसर्वशः ।।6.99.2।। पातयामानकायेभ्यःफलंवृन्तादिवानिलः ।

instruction:

केषांचिदिषुभिर्बाहुन् स्कन्धांश्छिच्छेदराक्षसः च ।।6.99.3।। वानराणांसुङ्कृद्ध: पार्श्वंकेषांव्यदारयत् ।
output: Then with his arrows, that Rakshasa (Mahaparsva) shattered the arms of some, shoulders of some, sides, and ribs of some Vanaras.

instruction:

तेऽर्दिताबाणवर्षेणमहापार्श्वेनवानराः ।।6.99.4।। विषादविमुखाःसर्वेबभूवुर्गतचेतसः ।
output: महापार्श्वेन Mahaparsva, बाणवर्षेण rain of arrows, अर्दिताः dejected, तेवानराः those Vanaras, सर्वे all, विषादविमुखाःsad look, गतचेतसः lost senses, बभूवुः wore

instruction:

निरीक्ष्यबलमुद्विग्नमङ्गदोराक्षसार्दितम् ।।6.99.5।। वेगंचक्रेमहावेगमहाबाहुस्समुद्रइवपर्वणि ।
output: Observing the army oppressed by the Rakshasa leader, Angada, endowed with broad shoulders, exhibited his might speedily like the ocean on full moon days.

instruction:

आयसंपरिघंगृह्यसूर्यरमशिसमप्रभम् ।।6.99.6।। समरेवानरश्रेष्ठोमहापार्श्वेन्यपातयत् ।
output: The foremost of the Vanaras (Angada), taking an iron bar flung on Mahaparsva in the battlefield.

instruction:

स तुतेनप्रहारेणमहापार्श्वोविचेतनः ।।6.99.7।। ससूतस्स्यन्दनात्तस्माद्विसंज्ञश्चापतद्भुवि ।
output: By that hit, Mahaparsva became unconscious and fell on the ground, senseless, from the chariot along with the charioteer.

instruction:
